3:131: When God Almighty mentioned the righteous who pay expenses, give zakat, and give charity and charity to those in need and relatives in all circumstances and times, He began to mention those who consume usury and people's money unjustly and through all kinds of doubts. He informed about them on the day they emerge from their graves and rise from them, until their resurrection and resurrection. He said, Those who consume interest will not rise except as one rises who is being beaten by Satan into insanity. That is, they will not rise from their graves on the Day of Resurrection except as one who is being beaten by Satan into insanity rises while he is being beaten by Satan, and that is because he will rise in an abhorrent manner. Ibn Abbas said: The usurer will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection insane and choking. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. He said: It was narrated on the authority of Awf bin Malik, Saeed bin Jubayr, As-Suddi, Ar-Rabi bin Anas, Qatadah, and Muqatil bin Hayyan, something similar to that. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Muqatil bin Hayyan that they said regarding His statement, Those who consume interest will not stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity, meaning that they will not stand on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Nujayh said the same on the authority of Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Abu Bakr bin Abi Maryam on the authority of Damrah bin Hanif, on the authority of Abu Abdullah bin Masoud, on the authority of his father, that he used to recite, Those who consume interest will not stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity, and Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Rabi’ah bin Kulthum told us, my father told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It will be said on the Day of Resurrection to the usurer: Take your weapon for war, and he recited. Those who consume interest will not rise again except as one rises who is being beaten by Satan into insanity, that is, when he rises from his grave. In the hadith of Abu Saeed in Al-Isra’, as mentioned in Surah Subhan, that the Prophet (peace be upon him) passed by people that night who had interior spaces like houses, so he asked about them, and it was said: These are the ones who consume interest. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it at length, and Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Al-Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Abu Al-Salt, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: “On the night of my Isra’, I came upon people whose stomachs were like houses, in which were snakes running from outside their stomachs. I said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: These are the ones who consume interest.” Imam Ahmad narrated it, on the authority of Hasan and Affan, both of them on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, with it, and there is weakness in its chain of transmission. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Samura bin Jundub in the long hadith of the dream: So we came to a river, I thought he was saying: red like blood, and in the river there was a man swimming, and on the bank of the river there was a man who had collected many stones, and that swimmer was swimming, then the one who had collected the stones came, and he opened his mouth wide for him and fed him a stone, we mention in its interpretation that it is a usurer. And His statement, That is because they said, ‘Trade is only like usury.’ But God has permitted trade and forbidden usury, meaning that they only permitted this because they objected to the rulings of God in His law. This is not an analogy on their part between usury and trade, because the polytheists do not recognize the legitimacy of the principle of trade that God has permitted in the Qur’an. If this were a case of analogy, they would have said, ‘Usury is only like trade.’ Rather, they said, ‘Trade is only like usury,’ meaning it is its counterpart. So why was this forbidden and this permitted? This is an objection from them to the Shari’ah, that is, this is like that, and He has permitted this and forbidden that, and the saying of the Most High: And God has permitted trade and forbidden usury may be a complete response to them, that is, to what they said of the objection, despite their knowledge of God’s distinction between this and that in ruling, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, whose ruling cannot be questioned, and He is not asked about what He does, while they are asked, and He is the Knower of the truths of matters and their interests, and what benefits His servants, so He permits it for them, and what harms them, so He forbids them from it, and He is more merciful to them than a mother to her infant child, and for this reason He said: But whoever receives an admonition from his Lord and desists, then he shall have what is past, and his affair is with God, that is, whoever is informed of God’s prohibition of usury and desists when the Shari’ah reaches him, then he shall have what is past of the transaction, because of His saying: God has pardoned what is past, and as the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said on the day of the conquest of Mecca, And all usury in the Age of Ignorance is placed under these two feet of mine, and the first usury I will remove is the usury of Al-Abbas, and he did not command them to return the increases taken in the case of The pre-Islamic era, but rather he pardoned what was past, as God Almighty said: He shall have what is past, and his affair is with God. Saeed bin Jubair and As-Suddi said: He shall have what is past, what he had eaten of usury before it was forbidden. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was read to Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul-Hakam, Ibn Wahb told us, Jarir bin Hazim told me, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Umm Yunus, meaning his wife Al-Aliyah bint Aifa, that Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her, Umm Muhibbah, the mother of a child of Zaid bin Arqam: O Mother of the Believers, do you know Zaid bin Arqam? She said: Yes. She said: I sold him as a slave to Al-Ata for eight hundred, and I needed his price, so I bought him before the due date for six hundred. She said: What a bad purchase and what a bad purchase! Tell Zaid that his jihad with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has been nullified if he does not repent. He said: So I said: What if I leave the two hundred and take the six hundred? She said: Yes, But whoever receives an admonition from his Lord and desists, he will have what is past. This trace is well-known and is evidence for those who forbade the issue of ‘ayna, along with what came in it from the aforementioned hadiths established in the Book of Rulings, and praise and thanks be to God. Then God Almighty said: And whoever returns meaning to usury and does it after reaching the prohibition of God from it, then he deserves punishment, and the proof is established against him, and for this reason He said: Then those are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein eternally. Abu Dawud said: Yahya Abu Dawud told us, Yahya bin Ma’in told us, Abdullah bin Raja’ al-Makki told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Uthman Khathim, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: When the verse was revealed, Those who consume interest cannot stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Whoever does not give up usury, let him be warned of war from God and His Messenger. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Ibn Khathim, and he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of Muslim, and they did not include it. Rather, what was forbidden was usury, which is farming with some of what comes out of the land. Al-Muzabana: It is the purchase of fresh dates in the palm trees and dates on the ground, and Al-Muhaqala: It is the purchase of grain in its ear in the field with grain on the ground. These things and the like were forbidden to eliminate the source of usury, because the equality between two things is not known before drying. For this reason, the jurists said: Ignorance of similarity is like the reality of comparison. From this, they forbade things based on what they understood from the narrowing of the paths leading to usury and the means leading to it, and the difference in their view according to what God has given to each of them of knowledge. God Almighty said: And above every possessor of knowledge is the All-Knowing. The subject of usury is one of the most difficult subjects for many scholars. The Commander of the Faithful, Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: There are three things that I wish the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had entrusted us with a covenant in which we could adhere to them: the grandfather, the descendants of the deceased, and some of the subjects of usury - meaning by that some issues that have a taint of usury - and the Shariah bears witness that every forbidden thing has a means to it like it, because that which leads to the forbidden is forbidden, just as that which does not fulfill the duty except by it. It is obligatory. It has been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of An-Nu’man ibn Bashir, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “What is lawful is clear and what is unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters. So whoever avoids doubtful matters clears himself in regard to his religion and his honor, and whoever falls into doubtful matters falls into what is unlawful, like a shepherd who pastures his animals near a sanctuary, soon to graze them therein.” And in the Sunan on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Ali, may God be pleased with them both, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Leave that which makes you doubt for that which does not make you doubt. And in another hadith: Sin is that which troubles the heart, and the soul hesitates about it, and you hate for people to find out about it. And in another narration: Consult your heart, even if people give you a fatwa and give you a fatwa. And Ath-Thawri said on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ash-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The last thing that was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the verse on usury. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Qubaysah on his authority. Ahmad said on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab, that ‘Umar said: Among the last things that were revealed was the verse on usury, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He was arrested before he could explain it to us, so leave usury and suspicion. He said: It was narrated by Ibn Majah and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Hayaj bin Bastam, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said: Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, gave us a sermon and said: I may forbid you from things that are good for you, and I order you to do things that are not good for you. And the last verse of the Qur’an to be revealed was the verse on usury, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died without explaining it to us, so leave that which makes you doubt, for that which does not make you doubt. Ibn Abi Uday said with the chain of transmission that it was suspended, so he mentioned it and Al-Hakim rejected it in his Mustadrak. Ibn Majah said: Amr bin Ali Al-Sayrafi told us, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Masoud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Usury has seventy-three chapters. And Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak: on the authority of Amr bin Ali Al-Fallas with his chain of transmission similarly, and he added: The easiest of them is that… A man marries his mother, and if he commits usury, he will be punished for violating the honor of the Muslim man.” He said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, but they did not include it. Ibn Majah said: Abdullah bin Saeed told us, Abdullah bin Idris told us, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Saeed Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Usury has seventy parts, the easiest of which is for a man to marry his mother. Imam Ahmad said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibad bin Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Khaira, on the authority of Al-Hasan, about forty or fifty years ago, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A time will come upon the people when they will consume usury. He said: It was said to him: All the people? He said: Whoever among them does not consume it will be affected by its dust. Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah narrated it in the same way, through different chains of transmission, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Khaira, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on his authority. Of this type is the prohibition of means that lead to forbidden things, the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Muslim bin Subaih, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, who said: When the verses at the end of Surat Al-Baqarah were revealed about usury, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out. To the mosque and he recited them, and he forbade trade in alcohol. The group, except for Al-Tirmidhi, transmitted it through paths from Al-A’mash with it, and this is the wording of Al-Bukhari’s narration when interpreting this verse, so he forbade trade. In his wording from Aisha, she said: When the verses from the end of Surat Al-Baqarah were revealed about usury, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited them to the people, then he forbade trade in alcohol. Some of the imams who spoke about this hadith said: When he forbade usury and its means, he forbade alcohol and what leads to it from trade and the like, as he, peace be upon him, said in the agreed upon hadith: May God curse the Jews, fat was forbidden to them, so they rendered it and sold it and ate its price. And it was mentioned in the hadith of Ali, Ibn Mas’ud and others, when cursing the muhallil in the interpretation of his statement: Until she marries a husband other than him, his statement, may God bless him and grant him peace, May God curse the one who consumes usury, the one who gives it, its two witnesses, and its scribe. They said: And what witnesses to it and writes about it is only if it appears in the form of a legitimate contract, and its interior is corrupt, so the consideration is in its meaning, not its form, because the actions By intentions, and in the Sahih: God does not look at your appearances or your wealth, but rather He looks at your hearts and your deeds. The great Imam Abu al-Abbas Ibn Taymiyyah wrote a book on invalidating what is permissible, which included a prohibition on engaging in means that lead to all falsehood, and that was sufficient and healing, so may God have mercy on him and be pleased with him. The Almighty says, forbidding His believing servants from engaging in usury and consuming it in multiples, as they used to say in the days of ignorance: When the due date of a debt comes, either pay it or increase it. If he pays it, otherwise, he increases it in the period, and the other increases it in the amount, and so on every year, perhaps the little will be doubled until it becomes a lot multiplied. The Almighty commanded His servants to be pious, so that they may succeed in the first and the last, then He threatened them with the Fire and warned them against it, so the Almighty said: “And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers. And obey God and the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.” Then He urged them to hasten to do good deeds and hasten to attain the acts of worship, so the Almighty said: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous. That is, just as the Fire was prepared for the disbelievers. It has been said that the meaning of His saying its width is the heavens and the earth is an indication of the vastness of its length, as He said in describing the furnishings of Paradise: its linings are of brocade. That is, what do you think? By the backs? It was said: Rather, its width is like its length because it is a dome under the throne, and the domed and round thing is as wide as its length. This is indicated by what was established in the Sahih: “If you ask God for Paradise, then ask Him for Al-Firdaws, for it is the highest part of Paradise and the middle of Paradise, and from it the rivers of Paradise flow, and its roof is the Throne of the Most Merciful.” This verse is like the Almighty’s saying in Surat al-Hadid 57:Race one another to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth, the verse. We narrated in Musnad Al-Imam Ahmad that Heraclius wrote to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: You have invited me to a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God, so where is the night when the day comes? Ibn Jarir narrated it and said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Muslim bin Khalid told me on the authority of Abu Khathim, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Rashid, on the authority of Ya’la bin Murrah, who said: “I met Al-Tanukhi, the messenger of Heraclius to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Homs, an old man who had become corrupt. He said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the letter of Heraclius, so he handed the paper to a man on his left. He said: I said: Who is your companion who reads? They said: Mu’awiyah. Then it was the letter of my companion: You have written inviting me to a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous. So where is the Fire?” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God! Where is the night when the day comes? Al-A’mash, Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu’bah said on the authority of Qays ibn Muslim on the authority of Tariq ibn Shihab: Some Jews asked Umar ibn al-Khattab about a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? Umar said to them: Have you seen when the day comes, where is the night? And when the night comes, where is the day? They said: Something similar has been taken from the Torah. Ibn Jarir narrated it through three chains of transmission. Then he said: Ahmad ibn Hazim told us, Abu Nu’aym told us, Ja’far ibn Burqan told us, Yazid ibn al-A’sam told us: A man from the People of the Book said: They say, A Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Where is the night when the day comes, and where is the day when the night comes? This has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Mu’ammar told us, Al-Mughirah ibn Salamah Abu Hisham told us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn al-A’sam, on the authority of His uncle Yazid ibn al-Asamm, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, said: “A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘Have you seen the words of God the Almighty: “A Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth,” then where is the Fire? He said: ‘Have you seen that when the night comes it covers everything, so where is the day?’ He said: ‘Wherever God wills.’ He said: ‘And so the Fire will be wherever God the Almighty wills.’” This has two possible meanings one of them that the meaning in that is that it does not necessarily follow from our not seeing the night when the day comes that it is not in a place, even if we do not know it, and so the Fire will be wherever God the Almighty wills, and this is more apparent as mentioned previously in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of al-Bazzar. Second That the meaning is that if the day covers the face of the world from this side, then the night is from the other side, so likewise Paradise is in the highest of the high above the heavens under the Throne and its width, as God Almighty said like the width of the heaven and the earth and Hell is in the lowest of the low, so there is no contradiction between it being like the width of the heavens and the earth and the existence of Hell, and God knows best. Then God the Almighty mentioned the description of the people of Paradise, saying, Those who spend in ease and hardship, meaning in hardship and ease, in comfort and distress, in health and sickness, and in all circumstances, just as He said, Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, meaning that nothing distracts them from obeying God the Almighty and spending in what pleases Him, and doing good to His creation from their relatives and others with various types of righteousness. And God the Almighty said, And those who restrain anger and pardon the people, meaning that if anger arises in them, they restrain it, meaning they conceal it and do not act on it, and they pardon those who wrong them. It was mentioned in some of the narrations: “God the Most High says: O son of Adam, remember Me when you become angry, and I will remember you when you become angry, so that I will not destroy you among those whom I destroy.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Abu Ya’la said in his Musnad: Abu Musa al-Zaman told us, Isa bin Shu’aib al-Dareer Abu al-Fadl told us, al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman al-Jizi told me on the authority of Abu Amr bin Anas bin Malik, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever restrains his anger, God will restrain his punishment from him. Whoever guards his tongue, God will cover his faults. Whoever apologizes to God, God will accept his apology.” This is a strange hadith, and its chain of transmission is questionable. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, Malik told us on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa’id bin al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The strong man is not the one who wrestles, but the strong man is the one who controls himself when he is angry. The two sheikhs narrated it on the authority of Malik. Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taymi, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Suwaid, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Which of you would rather have the wealth of his heir than his own wealth? They said: O Messenger of God, there is none among us who does not love his wealth more than the wealth of his heir. He said: “Know that there is none among you who does not love the wealth of his heir more than his own wealth. Your wealth from your wealth is only what you have sent forward, and the wealth of your heir is what you have delayed.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you consider to be a wrestler among you? We said: The one who is not wrestled by men. He said: No, but the one who controls himself when he is angry. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you consider to be a slave among you? We said: The one who has no children. He said: No, but the slave is the one who has not sent forward any of his children. Al-Bukhari included the first chapter of it, and Muslim included the original of this hadith, on the authority of Al-A’mash. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, I heard Urwah ibn `Abdullah al-Ju`fi narrating on the authority of Hasbah or Ibn Abi Hasin, on the authority of a man who witnessed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, giving a sermon, and he said, Do you know what ruqūb is? We said, The one who has no children. He said, Ruqūb is all the ones who have children and then died without having given anything from them. He said, Do you know what sāluq is? They said, The one who has no wealth. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The sāluq is all the one who has wealth and then died without giving anything from it. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, What is sarā`? They said, The one who is struck down. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Sarā` is all the sarā`, the one who becomes angry and his anger becomes intense, his face turns red, and his hair stands up, so he is struck down by his anger. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr told us, Hisham ibn Urwah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, on the authority of his uncle called Jariyah ibn Qudamah Al-Sa’di, “that he asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, say to me something that will benefit me and make it short for me so that I may understand it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not get angry. So he repeated it to him until he repeated it to him many times, each time saying: Do not get angry.” And this is how he narrated it on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah on the authority of Hisham on his authority, and he also narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id Al-Qattan on the authority of Hisham on his authority, “that a man said: O Messenger of God, say to me something and make it short for me so that I may understand it. He said: Do not get angry.” The hadith is narrated only by Ahmad. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman, “On the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A man said: O Messenger of God, advise me. He said: Do not get angry. The man said: So I thought about it when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said what he said, and I saw that anger brings together all evil.” Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Abu Ibn Harb ibn Abi Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: He was watering from his cistern when some people came and said: Who among you will bring water to Abu Dharr and count the hairs from his head? A man said: I will. So the man came and brought water to him from the cistern and pounded it. Abu Dharr was standing, so he sat down and then lay down. It was said to him: O Abu Dharr, why did you sit down and then lie down? He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: If one of you becomes angry while standing, let him sit down. If the anger goes away from him, then all well and good, otherwise let him lie down.” Abu Dawood narrated it from Ahmad ibn Hanbal with his chain of transmission, except that it was included in his narration on the authority of Abu Harb on the authority of Abu Dharr. The correct version is Ibn Abi Harb on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Dharr, as Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated it on the authority of his father. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim bin Khalid told us, Abu Wa’il al-San’ani told us: We were sitting with Urwah bin Muhammad when a man entered and said to him words that angered him. When he angered him, he stood up and came back to us after having performed ablution. He said: My father told me on the authority of my grandfather Atiyah - he is Ibn Sa’d al-Sa’di - and he was a companion - he said: “The Messenger of God said: Anger is from the devil, and the devil was created from fire, and fire is extinguished only with water. So when one of you becomes angry, let him perform ablution.” And this is how Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Ibrahim bin Khalid al-San’ani on the authority of Abu Wa’il al-Qass al-Muradi al-San’ani. Abu Dawud said: I think he was Abdullah bin Buhair. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Noah bin Ja’una al-Salami told us, on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever gives respite to someone in difficulty or forgives him, God will protect him from the heat of Hell. Indeed, the work of Paradise is made difficult by a hill - three times - Indeed, the work of Hell is made easy by a slip. And the happy one is the one who is protected from trials, and there is no sip more beloved to God than a sip of anger that a servant swallows. No servant of God swallows it except that it fills his stomach with faith.’” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it, and its chain of transmission is good, with no one who is wounded in it, and its text is good. Another hadith with the same meaning - Abu Dawud said: Uqbah bin Makram told us, Abd al-Rahman, meaning Ibn Mahdi, told us, on the authority of Bishr, meaning Ibn Mansur, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ajlan, on the authority of Suwaid bin Wahb, on the authority of a man from the sons of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever suppresses anger when he is able to vent it, God will fill him with security and faith. Whoever refrains from wearing a beautiful garment when he is able to do so - Bishr said: I think he said: out of humility - God will clothe him with the garment of honor. Whoever marries for God, God will clothe him with the crown of kingship.” Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Yazid told us: Saeed told us, Abu Marhum told me on the authority of Sahl bin Muadh bin Anas, on the authority of his father, “The Messenger of God said: Whoever suppresses his anger when he is able to vent it, God will call him in front of all creation and let him choose from any of the houris he wants.” Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Ayoub, and Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Gharib. Another hadith - Abd al-Razzaq said: Dawud ibn Qays informed us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of a man from the people of Ash-Sham called Abd al-Jalil, on the authority of his uncle, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, regarding the words of God Almighty: And those who restrain anger, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever restrains anger when he is able to give vent to it, God will fill him with security and faith. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Another hadith - Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad told us, Yahya ibn Abi Talib told us, Ali ibn Asim told us, Yunus ibn Ubayd told me on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘A servant has not taken a sip of food that is better in reward than a sip of anger that he swallows seeking the face of God.’” And Ibn Majah narrated it likewise on the authority of Bishr ibn Umar, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd, with the same chain of transmission. So God Almighty’s statement: And those who restrain anger means that they do not act out their anger on people, but rather they restrain their evil from them, and they seek reward for that from God Almighty. Then God the Almighty said: And those who pardon people meaning, while refraining from evil, they pardon those who wronged them in their souls, so that no grudge remains in their souls against anyone, and this is the most perfect state, and for this reason He said: And God loves the doers of good so this is from the stations of goodness, and in the hadith: “There are three things that I swear by: no wealth is diminished by charity, and God does not increase a servant through forgiveness except in honor, and whoever humbles himself before God, God will raise him up.” Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Musa bin Uqbah from Ishaq bin Yahya bin Talhah Al-Qurashi, from Ubadah bin As-Samit, from Ubayy bin Ka’b that the Messenger of God, “said: Whoever is pleased to have a lofty building and be raised in status, let him pardon those who wronged him, give to those who deprived him, and connect with those who severed ties with him.” Then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it. Ibn Mardawayh included it from the hadith of Ali, Ka’b bin Ujrah, Abu Hurayrah, and Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with them, in a similar manner. It was narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, a crier will call out, saying: Where are those who pardoned people? Come to your Lord and take your rewards. It is the right of every Muslim man, if he pardons, to enter Paradise.” And God Almighty said: And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins. That is, if they commit a sin, they follow it up with repentance and seeking forgiveness. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Hammam bin Yahya told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Abdullah bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He said: A man committed a sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant committed a sin and knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant. Then he committed another sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant. Then he committed another sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant.” With it, I bear witness that I have forgiven my servant, so let him do whatever he wants.” It was included in Sahih from the hadith of Ishaq bin Abi Talha, in a similar manner. Another Hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr and Abu Amir told us: Zuhair told us: Saad al-Ta’i told us: Abu al-Mudallah, the freed slave of the Mother of the Believers, heard Abu Hurairah, we said: O Messenger of God, when we see you, our hearts soften, and we are from the people of the Hereafter, and when we leave you, the world pleases us, and we smell women and children. He said: “If you were to be in every state in the state you are in with me, the angels would shake your hands with their palms, and visit you in your homes. And if you did not sin, God would bring people who would sin so that He would forgive them.” We said: O Messenger of God, tell us about Paradise, what is its structure? He said: A brick of gold and a brick of silver, its mortar is the most fragrant musk, its pebbles are pearls and rubies, and its soil is saffron. Whoever enters it will be blessed and will not be miserable, and will live forever and will not die. His clothes will not wear out, and his youth will not fade. There are three whose supplications will not be rejected: the just ruler, the fasting person until he breaks his fast, and the supplication of the one who is not fasting until he breaks his fast.” The oppressed person is carried on the clouds and the gates of heaven are opened for him, and the Lord says: By My glory, I will surely aid you, even if after a while. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from another chain of transmission on the authority of Sa`d. Ablution and two rak`ahs of prayer are confirmed upon repentance, as narrated by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal: Waki` told us, Mis`ar and Sufyan Al-Thawri told us on the authority of Uthman ibn Al-Maghbarah Al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Ali ibn Rabi`ah, on the authority of Asma` ibn Al-Hakam Al-Fazari, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: Whenever I heard a hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God would benefit me with whatever He willed from it. And if someone else tells me about it, I make him swear, and if he swears to me, I believe him. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, told me - and Abu Bakr spoke the truth - that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There is no man who commits a sin, then performs ablution and does it well - Misa’ar said - then prays - Sufyan said - then prays two rak’ahs, and seeks forgiveness from God Almighty, except that He forgives him.” And thus it was narrated by Ali ibn al-Madini, al-Humaidi, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, the people of the Sunan, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, al-Bazzar, and al-Daraqutni through various chains of transmission on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Mughira with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is a good hadith, and we have mentioned its chains of transmission, and the discussion of it is complete in Musnad Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him. In short, it is a good hadith, and it is narrated by the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, on the authority of the Prophet’s successor, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with them both. What bears witness to the authenticity of this hadith is what Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is none among you who performs ablution and completes it, then says: I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, except that the eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and he may enter through whichever one he wishes.” And in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, that he performed ablution for them as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, then said: “I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then prays two rak’ahs in which he does not think, his previous sins will be forgiven.” This hadith has been proven from the narration of the four Imams, the Rightly-Guided Caliphs, on the authority of the Master of the First and the Last, and the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds, as indicated by the clear Book, that seeking forgiveness for sins benefits sinners. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Ja’far ibn Sulayman informed us on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: It has been reported to me that when this verse was revealed, And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins, the verse, Satan wept. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Mahraz bin Awn told us, Uthman bin Matar told us, Abdul Ghafoor told us, on the authority of Abu Nasirah, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He said, ‘Upon you is saying ‘There is no god but God’ and seeking forgiveness, so do a lot of them, for Satan said, ‘I have destroyed people with sins and they have destroyed me with ‘There is no god but God’ and seeking forgiveness. So when I saw that, I have destroyed them with desires, and they think that they are guided.’” Uthman bin Matar and his sheikh are weak. Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Amr and Abu Al-Haitham Al-Atwari on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Satan said: O Lord, by Your glory, I will continue to mislead Your servants as long as their souls are in their bodies. God Almighty said: By My glory and majesty, I will continue to forgive them as long as they seek My forgiveness.” Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Umar ibn Abi Khalifa told us, I heard Abu Badr narrating on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: “A man came and said: O Messenger of God, I have committed a sin. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you sin, seek forgiveness from your Lord. He said: I seek forgiveness, then I sin again. He said: If you sin again, seek forgiveness from your Lord. He said it the fourth time, seek forgiveness from your Lord, until Satan is the one who regrets.” This is a strange hadith from this source. And the Almighty’s saying: And who forgives sins except God? means that no one forgives them except Him, as Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Mus’ab told us, Salam ibn Maskeen and al-Mubarak told us on the authority of al-Hasan on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Sari’ that a prisoner was brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: O God, I repent to You and I do not repent to Muhammad. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The truth has been made known to its people. And His saying: And they did not persist in what they did while they knew means that they repented from their sins and returned to God soon, and they did not continue in the sin and persist in it without giving it up. And if the sin was repeated from them, they would repent from it, as al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Ishaq ibn Abi Isra’il and others told us, they said: Abu Yahya Abd al-Hamid al-Hammani told us on the authority of Uthman ibn Waqid, on the authority of Abu Nasirah, on the authority of a freed slave of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He who seeks forgiveness will not persist, even if he returns seventy times a day.” And Abu Dawud narrated it. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Bazzar in his Musnad from the hadith of Uthman bin Waqid - and Yahya bin Ma'een authenticated him with it - and his Sheikh Abu Nasirah Al-Wasiti, whose name is Muslim bin Ubaid, who was authenticated by Imam Ahmad and Ibn Hibban. Ali bin Al-Madini and Al-Tirmidhi said: The chain of transmission of this hadith is not that good. It appears that it is due to the ignorance of the client of Abu Bakr, but the ignorance of someone like him does not harm because he is a great follower, and it is sufficient for him to attribute it to Abu Bakr, so it is a good hadith, and God knows best. And his statement, and they know, Mujahid and Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair said, and they know, that whoever repents, God will accept his repentance. This is like the statement of God, the Most High, Do they not know that God accepts repentance from His servants? and His statement, And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful. And there are many similar examples to this. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Jarir told us, Habban - he is Ibn Zaid Al-Sharabi - told us, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “that he said while he was on the pulpit: ‘Be merciful and you will be shown mercy, and forgive and you will be forgiven. Woe to those who defy speech, woe to those who persist in what they have done while they know.’” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. Then God the Almighty said after describing them with what He described them with: Their reward is forgiveness from their Lord meaning their reward for these attributes is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow meaning of various types of drinks abiding therein meaning abiding therein and excellent is the reward of the workers God the Almighty praises Paradise.
3:1: We have mentioned the hadith that states that the greatest name of God is in these two verses, God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, and “Alif, Lam, Meem. God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining,” when interpreting the Throne Verse. We have already discussed His statement, Alif, Lam, Meem, at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah, in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it. We have already discussed His statement, God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, in the interpretation of the Throne Verse. God the Almighty says: The Book has been sent down to you in truth meaning the Qur’an has been sent down to you, O Muhammad, in truth, meaning there is no doubt or suspicion about it, rather it is revealed from God. He sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness, and sufficient is God as a witness. His statement: Confirming what was before it means of the books sent down before it from the heaven to God’s servants, the prophets. They confirm what they have informed him of, and they have given good tidings in ancient times, and he confirms them because it matches what they have informed him of, and they have given good tidings of the promise from God to send Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to send down the great Qur’an upon him. His statement: And He sent down the Torah meaning to Moses, son of Imran, and the Gospel meaning to Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon them, before meaning before this Qur’an, as guidance for mankind meaning in their time. And He sent down the Criterion which is the difference between guidance and misguidance. Truth and falsehood, error and guidance, with what God the Most High mentions of arguments, evidence, clear proofs, and conclusive evidence, and He explains it, clarifies it, interprets it, establishes it, guides to it, and draws attention to it from that. Qatada and Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas said: The Criterion here is the Qur’an. Ibn Jarir chose that it is a source here because the Qur’an was mentioned before in His statement: He has sent down to you the Book in truth, which is the Qur’an. As for what Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Salih, that what is meant by the Criterion here is the Torah, it is also weak because the Torah was mentioned before, and God knows best. And the Almighty says: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of God meaning they denied them, rejected them, and rejected them falsely, for them is a severe punishment meaning on the Day of Resurrection, and God is Exalted in Might meaning invincible in status and great in power, possessor of vengeance meaning of those who denied His verses and disobeyed His noble messengers and great prophets.

3:5: The Almighty informs us that He knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, nothing of that is hidden from Him, It is He who shapes you in the wombs as He wills meaning He creates you in the wombs as He wills, male and female, good and bad, miserable and happy, There is no god but He, the Almighty, the Wise meaning He is the One who created, and He alone deserves divinity, with no partner, and to Him belongs the glory that cannot be reached, and the wisdom and the judgments. This verse contains an allusion, or rather an explicit statement, that Jesus, son of Mary, is a created servant, as God created all other human beings, because God shaped him in the womb and created him as He willed. So how can he be a god as the Christians claim, may God's curses be upon them, when he has turned over in the wombs and moved from one state to another? As God Almighty said: He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, within three darknesses.

3:7: God the Almighty informs us that in the Qur’an there are clear verses, they are the foundation of the Book, that is, clear evidence with clear meanings that are not ambiguous to anyone, and there are other verses in which the meaning is ambiguous to many people or some of them, so whoever refers what is ambiguous to what is clear from it and rules its clear verses over its ambiguous verses for him has been guided, and whoever reverses it will be reversed, and for this reason God the Almighty said, They are the foundation of the Book, that is, its origin to which one can refer when in doubt, and others are ambiguous, that is, their meaning may agree with the clear verses or may mean something else in terms of wording and structure, but not in terms of what is intended. They differed regarding the clear and ambiguous verses, and many expressions were narrated from the predecessors. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: The clear verses abrogate it, its lawful and unlawful verses, its rulings, its limits, its obligations, what is commanded and acted upon. And Ibn Abbas also said that the clear verses are the words of God the Almighty: Say, ‘Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you - that you not associate anything with Him.’ and the verses after it. And the Almighty’s saying: And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him to three verses after it. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and he narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: My father told us, Sulayman bin Harb told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Suwayd, that Yahya bin Ya’mar and Abu Fakhita discussed this verse, which is: They are the foundations of the Book and others are unspecific. Abu Fakhita said: The openings of the surahs. Yahya bin Ya’mar said: The obligations, the commands and prohibitions, the lawful and the unlawful. Ibn Lahi’ah said on the authority of Ata’ bin Dinar on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: They are the foundations of the Book because they are written in all the books. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: Because there is no one of the people of religion who does not accept them. It was said about the unspecific: the abrogated, the earlier and later, the examples in it, the sections, and what is believed in but not acted upon. It was narrated by Ali bin Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was said that they are the disconnected letters at the beginning of the surahs, as stated by Muqatil bin Hayyan, and from Mujahid, the ambiguous verses confirm each other, and this is in the interpretation of His statement, A Book similar and repeated. There they mentioned that the similar is the speech that is in one context, and the repeated is the speech about two opposite things, such as the description of Paradise and the description of Hell, and the mention of the state of the righteous and the state of the wicked, and the like. As for here, the ambiguous is that which is opposite to the decisive, and the best that has been said about it is what we have presented, and it is what Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar, may God have mercy on him, stated, where he said: Among them are the decisive verses, so they are the proof of the Lord and the protection of the servants and the repelling of falsehood by opponents, and they have no change from what they were placed upon. He said: And the ambiguous verses in truth have no change, distortion, or interpretation. God has tested the servants with them as He tested them with regard to the lawful and the unlawful, so that they are not diverted to falsehood and distorted from the truth. That is why God Almighty said: But as for those in whose hearts is deviation meaning misguidance and deviation from the truth to falsehood they follow that which is ambiguous of it meaning they only take from it that which is ambiguous which they can distort to suit their corrupt purposes and apply it to them because its wording is likely to be what they are interpreting. As for the decisive verses, they have no share in them because it is a defense for them and an argument against them. That is why God Almighty said: Seeking to cause discord meaning to mislead their followers, making them think that they are using the Qur’an as evidence for their innovation, while it is an argument against them and not for them, just as if the Christians argued that the Qur’an had stated that Jesus was the spirit of God and His word which He bestowed upon Mary and a spirit from Him, and they abandoned the argument of His statement He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favor and His statement “Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is as the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust and then said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was” and other decisive verses that clearly state that he was created from God’s creations and a servant and messenger from God’s messengers. And the Almighty’s saying, and seeking its interpretation, meaning to distort it as they want. Muqatil ibn Hayyan and al-Suddi said, They seek to know what will be and what are the consequences of things from the Qur’an. Imam Ahmad said, Ismail told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited, “It is He who has sent down to you the Book. In it are verses that are precise, they are the foundation of the Book, and others that are unspecific,” until His saying, people of understanding. Then he said, So when you see those who dispute therein, they are the ones God meant, so beware of them. This is how the hadith was found in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, with no one between them. This is how Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Ismail ibn Ulayyah and Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi, both of them on the authority of Ayoub, on his authority. Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Abdi narrated it in his Musnad on the authority of Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi on the authority of Ayoub, on his authority. And Abd al-Razzaq narrated it on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Ayoub, and more than one person narrated it on the authority of Ayoub. Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih on the authority of Ayyub narrated it, and Abu Bakr ibn al-Mundhir narrated it in his interpretation through two chains of transmission on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Sadosi, whose nickname was A’rim: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aishah, on his authority. Abu ‘Amir al-Kharraz and others followed Ayyub on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, on the authority of Abu ‘Amir al-Kharraz, and he mentioned it. And thus Sa’id ibn Mansur narrated it in his Sunan on the authority of Hammad ibn Yahya al-Abbah, on the authority of ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aishah. And Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Ruh ibn al-Qasim and Nafi’ ibn ‘Umar al-Jumahi, both of them on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aishah, on his authority. Nafi’ said in his narration on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah: Aishah told me, and he mentioned it. This hadith was narrated by Al-Bukhari when interpreting this verse, and by Muslim in the Book of Al-Qadar in his Sahih, and by Abu Dawud in Al-Sunnah in his Sunan, all three of them on the authority of Al-Qa’nabi, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ibrahim Al-Tustari, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book; in it are verses that are precise until His saying: And none will remember except those of understanding. She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: So when you see those who follow that of it which is ambiguous, then those are the ones whom God has named, so beware of them. The wording of Al-Bukhari. And Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it likewise, on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ibrahim, and he said: It is good and authentic. He mentioned that Yazid ibn Ibrahim Al-Tustari was the only one to mention Al-Qasim in this chain of narration. More than one person narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah on the authority of Aisha, but he did not mention Al-Qasim, that is what he said. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it and said: My father told us, Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi told us, Yazid ibn Ibrahim al-Tastari and Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the statement of God Almighty: But as for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow that of it which is ambiguous, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When you see those who follow that of it which is ambiguous, then those are the ones whom God has named, so beware of them. Ibn Jarir said: Ali ibn Sahl told us, al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: They follow that of it which is ambiguous, seeking discord, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has warned you, so when you see them, recognize them. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through another chain of transmission on the authority of al-Qasim on the authority of Aisha, and he said: Imam Ahmad. Abu Kamil told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Abu Ghalib, who said: I heard Abu Umamah telling the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the words of God Almighty: But as for those in whose hearts is deviation, they will follow that of it which is ambiguous, he said: They are the Khawarij. And about the words of God Almighty: The Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black, he said: They are the Khawarij. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from more than one source, on the authority of Abu Ghalib. On the authority of Abu Umamah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who mentioned it. The least of these hadiths is that they are attributed to the Companions, but their meaning is correct. The first innovation that occurred in Islam was the Khawarij tribulation, and their beginning was because of this world when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided the spoils of Hunayn. It was as if they saw in their corrupt minds that he was not just in the division, so they surprised him with this statement. Their speaker, Dhu al-Khuwaysira - may God rip his side open - said: Be just, for you have not been just. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “You have failed and lost if I am not just. Does he trust me with the people of the earth and you do not trust me?” When the man turned back, Omar ibn al-Khattab, and in the narration of Khalid ibn al-Walid, asked permission from the Messenger of God to kill him. He said, “Leave him, for from the offspring of this man, that is, from his kind, will emerge a people who will consider your prayer insignificant compared to their prayer, your fasting insignificant compared to their fasting, and your recitation insignificant compared to their recitation. They will depart from the religion as an arrow departs from its target. So wherever you find them, kill them, for in killing them there is a reward for whoever kills them.” Then they appeared during the days of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and they killed them at Nahrawan. Then peoples, tribes, opinions, whims, articles, and many widespread sects branched out from them. Then the Qadariyyah emerged, then the Mu’tazila, then the Jahmites, and other innovations that the Truthful, the Trusted One, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us about in his saying, And this nation will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in Hell except one. They said, Who are they, O Messenger of God? He said, Those who are on what I and my companions are on. Al-Hakim included this addition in his Mustadrak. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Abu Musa told us, Amr bin Asim told us, Al-Mu`tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Jundub bin Abdullah, that it reached him on the authority of Hudhayfah, or he heard it from him, narrating on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said, Indeed, among my nation are people who recite the Qur’an, scattering it like scattering dates, and interpreting it in a way other than its interpretation. They did not include it. And the Almighty’s saying, And none knows its interpretation except God, the reciters differed regarding the pause here. It was said: On the majesty, as was mentioned previously on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Interpretation is of four types: an interpretation that no one is excused for understanding, an interpretation that the Arabs know from their languages, an interpretation that those firmly grounded in knowledge know, and an interpretation that none knows except God. This statement is narrated on the authority of Aisha, Urwah, Abu al-Sha’tha’, Abu Nahik, and others. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim said in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Hashim bin Muzayd told us, Muhammad bin Ismail bin Ayyash told us, my father told me, Damdam bin Zar'ah told me, on the authority of Shuraih bin Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, "I do not fear for my nation except three things: that their wealth will increase and they will become envious and fight each other; that the Book will be opened to them and the believer will take it seeking its interpretation. 'None knows its interpretation except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge who say, 'We believe in it,'" the verse; and that their knowledge will increase and they will waste it and not care about it. Very strange. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim told us, Ahmad ibn Amr told us, Hisham ibn Ammar told us, Ibn Abi Hatim told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn al-`As, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The Qur’an was not revealed for some parts to contradict others. So whatever you recognize of it, act upon it, and whatever is ambiguous, believe in it.” Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, who said: Ibn Abbas used to recite: “None knows its interpretation except God. And those firmly rooted in knowledge say, ‘We believe in it.’” Ibn Jarir narrated it likewise on the authority of `Umar ibn `Abd al-`Aziz and Malik ibn Anas that they believed in it but did not know its interpretation. Ibn Jarir narrated that in the recitation of `Abdullah ibn Mas`ud: “Its interpretation is only with amusement. And those firmly rooted in knowledge say, ‘We believe in it.’” And likewise on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b, Ibn Jarir chose this statement. Some of them stopped at his saying: and those firmly rooted in knowledge, and many of the commentators and scholars of the principles followed them, and said: Addressing what is not understood is far-fetched. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: I am from those firmly rooted who know its interpretation. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: And those firmly rooted in knowledge know its interpretation and say, We believe in it. And so said al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ja’far al-Zubayr: And none knows its interpretation he meant what he meant except God, and those firmly rooted in knowledge say, “We believe in it. Then they returned the interpretation of the ambiguous verses to what they knew of the interpretation of the decisive verses in which no one has an interpretation except one interpretation, so the Book was consistent with their saying and some of it confirmed some of it, so the argument was implemented, and the excuse became apparent, and falsehood was removed, and disbelief was repelled. And in the hadith, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed for Ibn Abbas, and said, O God, give him understanding in the religion and teach him the interpretation. And from Scholars have separated this matter and said: Interpretation is used, and it is intended by it in the Qur’an in two meanings: One of them is interpretation in the sense of the reality of the thing and what its matter leads to, and from it is the saying of the Most High: And he said, O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision of before and His saying, Do they await except its interpretation on the Day its interpretation comes? meaning the reality of what they were informed of regarding the matter of the Resurrection. If this is what is meant by interpretation, then the pause is at the majesty because the realities of matters and their essence are not known clearly except by God Almighty, and His saying, And those firmly rooted in knowledge is the subject and They say, ‘We believe in it’ is its predicate. However, if the other meaning is meant by interpretation, which is explanation, clarification, and expression of the thing, like His saying, Inform us of its interpretation, meaning its explanation, if this meaning is meant by it, then the pause is at And those firmly rooted in knowledge because they know and understand what they were addressed with in this regard, even if they do not encompass knowledge of the realities of things as they are. Based on this, His saying, They say, ‘We believe in it’ is a state of them, and this is permissible, and it is from The conjoined without the conjoined to it, like his saying: For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their wealth until his saying: “They say: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers” and the verse, and the Almighty’s saying: And your Lord will come and the angels, rank upon rank meaning: And the angels will come, rank upon rank. And His statement, informing about them, “They say: We believe in it,” meaning the ambiguous, All of it is from our Lord, meaning all of the decisive and the ambiguous are true and correct, and each one of them confirms the other and testifies to it, because all of it is from God and nothing from God is different or contradictory, as He says: Do they not then consider the Qur’an? Had it been from other than God, they would have found therein much discrepancy, and for this reason the Most High said: And none will remember except those of understanding, meaning only those with sound minds and upright understandings understand, comprehend, and contemplate the meanings in their proper manner. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Awf al-Himsi told us, Na’eem ibn Hammad told us, Fayyad al-Raqi told us, Abdullah ibn Yazid told us, and he had met the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Anas, Abu Umamah, and Abu al-Darda’, may God be pleased with them, said: Abu al-Darda’ told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about those firmly grounded in knowledge, so he said: He whose oath is true, whose tongue is truthful, and whose heart is upright, and he who… Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard some people arguing, so he said: “Those who came before you were destroyed because of this. They struck some parts of the Book of God with others. The Book of God was revealed to confirm some parts of it, so do not deny some parts of it with others. So whatever you know of it, say, and whatever you do not know, leave it to its scholar.” Ibn Mardawayh’s narration of this hadith was presented on the authority of Hisham ibn `Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Hazim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of `Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on his authority. Abu Ya`la al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Zuhair ibn Harb told us, Anas ibn `Iyad told us, on the authority of Abi Hazim, on the authority of Abi Salamah, who said: I do not know it except from Abi Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Qur’an was revealed in seven letters, and arguing about the Qur’an is disbelief. He said it. Three - what you know of it, then act upon it, and what you do not know of it, then refer it to its Knower, the Most High, the Majestic. This is a sound chain of transmission, but it has a defect because of the narrator’s statement, I do not know it except from Abu Hurairah. Ibn al-Mundhir said in his interpretation: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told us, Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Nafi’ ibn Yazid told me, he said: It is said: Those who are firmly grounded in knowledge are humble before God, humble themselves before God in His pleasure, they do not act arrogantly towards those above them nor do they belittle those below them. Then God the Almighty said, informing us that they called upon their Lord, saying: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, meaning do not make them deviate from guidance after You have established them upon it, and do not make us like those in whose hearts is deviation, who seek what is ambiguous in the Qur’an, but establish us on Your straight path and Your upright religion, and grant us from Yourself, meaning from You, mercy with which You will establish our hearts and unite us, and increase our faith and certainty. You are the Giver. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Amr ibn Abdullah al-Awdi told us, and Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, they both said: Wakee’ told us on the authority of Abdul Hameed ibn Bahram, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Umm Salamah, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. Then he recited: “Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bakkar, on the authority of Abdul Hameed ibn Bahram, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Umm Salamah, who is Asma’ bint Yazid ibn al-Sakn, who heard her narrating: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to frequently supplicate: O God, Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. I said: O Messenger of God, does the heart fluctuate? He said: Yes, God did not create any human being from the children of Adam except that his heart is between two fingers of God Almighty, so if He wills, He makes him steadfast, and if He wills, He makes him deviate.” So we ask God Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after He has guided us, and we ask Him to grant us mercy from Him, for He is the Bestower. And thus Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Asad ibn Musa, on the authority of Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, with a similar chain of transmission. He also narrated it on the authority of al-Muthanna, on the authority of al-Hajjaj ibn Munhal, on the authority of Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, with a similar chain of transmission, and he added: I said, O Messenger of God, will you not teach me a supplication that I can make for myself? He said, Yes, say, ‘O God, Lord of the Prophet Muhammad, forgive my sin, remove the anger in my heart, and save me from the misleading trials.’ Then Ibn Mardawayh said: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Harun ibn Bakkar al-Dimashqi narrated to us, al-Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Khalal narrated to us, Yazid ibn Yahya ibn Ubaydullah informed us, Saeed ibn Bashir informed us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Hassan al-A’raj, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, often supplicated, O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. I said, “O Messenger of God, God, how often you supplicate with this supplication, and He said: There is no heart but that it is between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful. If He wills to make it straight, He makes it straight, and if He wills to make it deviate, He makes it deviate. Have you not heard His saying: “Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.” Strange in this regard, but its origin is proven in the two Sahihs and others through many chains of narration without the addition of this noble verse. Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri. Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Hibban, and Abdullah ibn Wahb both added on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abi Ayyub: Abdullah ibn al-Waleed al-Tujibi told me on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her. That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he woke up at night would say, “There is no god but You, glory be to You, O God, I seek Your forgiveness for my sin, and I ask You for mercy, O God, increase me in knowledge and do not let my heart deviate after You have guided me, and grant me mercy from You, for You are the Bestower.” The wording of Ibn Mardawayh. Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Abu Ubayd, the freed slave of Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Ubadah ibn Nassi, that he told him that he heard Qays ibn al-Harith say: Abu Abdullah al-Sunabhi told me that he prayed the Maghrib prayer behind Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, and Abu Bakr recited in the first two rak’ahs the Mother of the Qur’an and two short surahs from al-Mufassal, and he recited in the third rak’ah. He said: So I came close to him until my clothes almost touched his clothes, and I heard him recite the Mother of the Qur’an and this verse: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us al-An’am 2:17. Abu Ubaid said: Ubadah bin Nassi informed me that he was with Umar bin Abdul Aziz during his caliphate, and Umar said to Qais: How did you tell me about Abu Abdullah? Umar said: We have not abandoned it since we heard it from him, although before that I was on something else. A man said to him: What was the Commander of the Faithful on before that? He said: I used to recite “Say: He is God, the One.” This trace was narrated by Al-Walid bin Muslim on the authority of Malik and Al-Awza’i, both on the authority of Abu Ubaid. This trace was also narrated by Al-Walid on the authority of Ibn Jaber, on the authority of Yahya bin Yahya Al-Ghassani, on the authority of Mahmud bin Labid, on the authority of Al-Sunabhi, that he prayed behind Abu Bakr the Maghrib prayer, and in the first two he recited Surat Al-Fatihah and a short surah, reciting aloud. When he stood up for the third, he began to recite, so I came close to him until my clothes touched his clothes, and he recited this verse: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate. And His saying, Our Lord, You will surely gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt, meaning they say in their supplication: “O our Lord, You will surely gather Your creation on the Day of Resurrection, and You will separate between them and judge between them in that over which they differed, and You will reward each one according to his deeds and what he was upon in this world of good and evil.”
3:8: God the Almighty informs us that in the Qur’an there are clear verses, they are the foundation of the Book, that is, clear evidence with clear meanings that are not ambiguous to anyone, and there are other verses in which the meaning is ambiguous to many people or some of them, so whoever refers what is ambiguous to what is clear from it and rules its clear verses over its ambiguous verses for him has been guided, and whoever reverses it will be reversed, and for this reason God the Almighty said, They are the foundation of the Book, that is, its origin to which one can refer when in doubt, and others are ambiguous, that is, their meaning may agree with the clear verses or may mean something else in terms of wording and structure, but not in terms of what is intended. They differed regarding the clear and ambiguous verses, and many expressions were narrated from the predecessors. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: The clear verses abrogate it, its lawful and unlawful verses, its rulings, its limits, its obligations, what is commanded and acted upon. And Ibn Abbas also said that the clear verses are the words of God the Almighty: Say, ‘Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you - that you not associate anything with Him.’ and the verses after it. And the Almighty’s saying: And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him to three verses after it. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and he narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: My father told us, Sulayman bin Harb told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Suwayd, that Yahya bin Ya’mar and Abu Fakhita discussed this verse, which is: They are the foundations of the Book and others are unspecific. Abu Fakhita said: The openings of the surahs. Yahya bin Ya’mar said: The obligations, the commands and prohibitions, the lawful and the unlawful.
