Ibn Lahi’ah said on the authority of Ata’ bin Dinar on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: They are the foundations of the Book because they are written in all the books. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: Because there is no one of the people of religion who does not accept them. It was said about the unspecific: the abrogated, the earlier and later, the examples in it, the sections, and what is believed in but not acted upon. It was narrated by Ali bin Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was said that they are the disconnected letters at the beginning of the surahs, as stated by Muqatil bin Hayyan, and from Mujahid, the ambiguous verses confirm each other, and this is in the interpretation of His statement, A Book similar and repeated. There they mentioned that the similar is the speech that is in one context, and the repeated is the speech about two opposite things, such as the description of Paradise and the description of Hell, and the mention of the state of the righteous and the state of the wicked, and the like. As for here, the ambiguous is that which is opposite to the decisive, and the best that has been said about it is what we have presented, and it is what Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar, may God have mercy on him, stated, where he said: Among them are the decisive verses, so they are the proof of the Lord and the protection of the servants and the repelling of falsehood by opponents, and they have no change from what they were placed upon. He said: And the ambiguous verses in truth have no change, distortion, or interpretation. God has tested the servants with them as He tested them with regard to the lawful and the unlawful, so that they are not diverted to falsehood and distorted from the truth. That is why God Almighty said: But as for those in whose hearts is deviation meaning misguidance and deviation from the truth to falsehood they follow that which is ambiguous of it meaning they only take from it that which is ambiguous which they can distort to suit their corrupt purposes and apply it to them because its wording is likely to be what they are interpreting. As for the decisive verses, they have no share in them because it is a defense for them and an argument against them. That is why God Almighty said: Seeking to cause discord meaning to mislead their followers, making them think that they are using the Qur’an as evidence for their innovation, while it is an argument against them and not for them, just as if the Christians argued that the Qur’an had stated that Jesus was the spirit of God and His word which He bestowed upon Mary and a spirit from Him, and they abandoned the argument of His statement He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favor and His statement “Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is as the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust and then said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was” and other decisive verses that clearly state that he was created from God’s creations and a servant and messenger from God’s messengers. And the Almighty’s saying, and seeking its interpretation, meaning to distort it as they want. Muqatil ibn Hayyan and al-Suddi said, They seek to know what will be and what are the consequences of things from the Qur’an. Imam Ahmad said, Ismail told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited, “It is He who has sent down to you the Book. In it are verses that are precise, they are the foundation of the Book, and others that are unspecific,” until His saying, people of understanding. Then he said, So when you see those who dispute therein, they are the ones God meant, so beware of them. This is how the hadith was found in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, with no one between them. This is how Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Ismail ibn Ulayyah and Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi, both of them on the authority of Ayoub, on his authority. Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Abdi narrated it in his Musnad on the authority of Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi on the authority of Ayoub, on his authority. And Abd al-Razzaq narrated it on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Ayoub, and more than one person narrated it on the authority of Ayoub. Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih on the authority of Ayyub narrated it, and Abu Bakr ibn al-Mundhir narrated it in his interpretation through two chains of transmission on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Sadosi, whose nickname was A’rim: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aishah, on his authority. Abu ‘Amir al-Kharraz and others followed Ayyub on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, on the authority of Abu ‘Amir al-Kharraz, and he mentioned it. And thus Sa’id ibn Mansur narrated it in his Sunan on the authority of Hammad ibn Yahya al-Abbah, on the authority of ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aishah. And Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Ruh ibn al-Qasim and Nafi’ ibn ‘Umar al-Jumahi, both of them on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aishah, on his authority. Nafi’ said in his narration on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah: Aishah told me, and he mentioned it. This hadith was narrated by Al-Bukhari when interpreting this verse, and by Muslim in the Book of Al-Qadar in his Sahih, and by Abu Dawud in Al-Sunnah in his Sunan, all three of them on the authority of Al-Qa’nabi, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ibrahim Al-Tustari, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book; in it are verses that are precise until His saying: And none will remember except those of understanding. She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: So when you see those who follow that of it which is ambiguous, then those are the ones whom God has named, so beware of them. The wording of Al-Bukhari. And Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it likewise, on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ibrahim, and he said: It is good and authentic. He mentioned that Yazid ibn Ibrahim Al-Tustari was the only one to mention Al-Qasim in this chain of narration. More than one person narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah on the authority of Aisha, but he did not mention Al-Qasim, that is what he said. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it and said: My father told us, Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi told us, Yazid ibn Ibrahim al-Tastari and Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the statement of God Almighty: But as for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow that of it which is ambiguous, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When you see those who follow that of it which is ambiguous, then those are the ones whom God has named, so beware of them. Ibn Jarir said: Ali ibn Sahl told us, al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: They follow that of it which is ambiguous, seeking discord, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has warned you, so when you see them, recognize them. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through another chain of transmission on the authority of al-Qasim on the authority of Aisha, and he said: Imam Ahmad. Abu Kamil told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Abu Ghalib, who said: I heard Abu Umamah telling the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the words of God Almighty: But as for those in whose hearts is deviation, they will follow that of it which is ambiguous, he said: They are the Khawarij. And about the words of God Almighty: The Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black, he said: They are the Khawarij. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from more than one source, on the authority of Abu Ghalib. On the authority of Abu Umamah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who mentioned it. The least of these hadiths is that they are attributed to the Companions, but their meaning is correct. The first innovation that occurred in Islam was the Khawarij tribulation, and their beginning was because of this world when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided the spoils of Hunayn. It was as if they saw in their corrupt minds that he was not just in the division, so they surprised him with this statement. Their speaker, Dhu al-Khuwaysira - may God rip his side open - said: Be just, for you have not been just. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “You have failed and lost if I am not just. Does he trust me with the people of the earth and you do not trust me?” When the man turned back, Omar ibn al-Khattab, and in the narration of Khalid ibn al-Walid, asked permission from the Messenger of God to kill him. He said, “Leave him, for from the offspring of this man, that is, from his kind, will emerge a people who will consider your prayer insignificant compared to their prayer, your fasting insignificant compared to their fasting, and your recitation insignificant compared to their recitation. They will depart from the religion as an arrow departs from its target. So wherever you find them, kill them, for in killing them there is a reward for whoever kills them.” Then they appeared during the days of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and they killed them at Nahrawan. Then peoples, tribes, opinions, whims, articles, and many widespread sects branched out from them. Then the Qadariyyah emerged, then the Mu’tazila, then the Jahmites, and other innovations that the Truthful, the Trusted One, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us about in his saying, And this nation will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in Hell except one. They said, Who are they, O Messenger of God? He said, Those who are on what I and my companions are on. Al-Hakim included this addition in his Mustadrak. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Abu Musa told us, Amr bin Asim told us, Al-Mu`tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Jundub bin Abdullah, that it reached him on the authority of Hudhayfah, or he heard it from him, narrating on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said, Indeed, among my nation are people who recite the Qur’an, scattering it like scattering dates, and interpreting it in a way other than its interpretation. They did not include it. And the Almighty’s saying, And none knows its interpretation except God, the reciters differed regarding the pause here. It was said: On the majesty, as was mentioned previously on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Interpretation is of four types: an interpretation that no one is excused for understanding, an interpretation that the Arabs know from their languages, an interpretation that those firmly grounded in knowledge know, and an interpretation that none knows except God. This statement is narrated on the authority of Aisha, Urwah, Abu al-Sha’tha’, Abu Nahik, and others. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim said in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Hashim bin Muzayd told us, Muhammad bin Ismail bin Ayyash told us, my father told me, Damdam bin Zar'ah told me, on the authority of Shuraih bin Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, "I do not fear for my nation except three things: that their wealth will increase and they will become envious and fight each other; that the Book will be opened to them and the believer will take it seeking its interpretation. 'None knows its interpretation except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge who say, 'We believe in it,'" the verse; and that their knowledge will increase and they will waste it and not care about it. Very strange. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim told us, Ahmad ibn Amr told us, Hisham ibn Ammar told us, Ibn Abi Hatim told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn al-`As, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The Qur’an was not revealed for some parts to contradict others. So whatever you recognize of it, act upon it, and whatever is ambiguous, believe in it.” Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, who said: Ibn Abbas used to recite: “None knows its interpretation except God. And those firmly rooted in knowledge say, ‘We believe in it.’” Ibn Jarir narrated it likewise on the authority of `Umar ibn `Abd al-`Aziz and Malik ibn Anas that they believed in it but did not know its interpretation. Ibn Jarir narrated that in the recitation of `Abdullah ibn Mas`ud: “Its interpretation is only with amusement. And those firmly rooted in knowledge say, ‘We believe in it.’” And likewise on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b, Ibn Jarir chose this statement. Some of them stopped at his saying: and those firmly rooted in knowledge, and many of the commentators and scholars of the principles followed them, and said: Addressing what is not understood is far-fetched. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: I am from those firmly rooted who know its interpretation. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: And those firmly rooted in knowledge know its interpretation and say, We believe in it. And so said al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ja’far al-Zubayr: And none knows its interpretation he meant what he meant except God, and those firmly rooted in knowledge say, “We believe in it. Then they returned the interpretation of the ambiguous verses to what they knew of the interpretation of the decisive verses in which no one has an interpretation except one interpretation, so the Book was consistent with their saying and some of it confirmed some of it, so the argument was implemented, and the excuse became apparent, and falsehood was removed, and disbelief was repelled. And in the hadith, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed for Ibn Abbas, and said, O God, give him understanding in the religion and teach him the interpretation. And from Scholars have separated this matter and said: Interpretation is used, and it is intended by it in the Qur’an in two meanings: One of them is interpretation in the sense of the reality of the thing and what its matter leads to, and from it is the saying of the Most High: And he said, O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision of before and His saying, Do they await except its interpretation on the Day its interpretation comes? meaning the reality of what they were informed of regarding the matter of the Resurrection. If this is what is meant by interpretation, then the pause is at the majesty because the realities of matters and their essence are not known clearly except by God Almighty, and His saying, And those firmly rooted in knowledge is the subject and They say, ‘We believe in it’ is its predicate. However, if the other meaning is meant by interpretation, which is explanation, clarification, and expression of the thing, like His saying, Inform us of its interpretation, meaning its explanation, if this meaning is meant by it, then the pause is at And those firmly rooted in knowledge because they know and understand what they were addressed with in this regard, even if they do not encompass knowledge of the realities of things as they are. Based on this, His saying, They say, ‘We believe in it’ is a state of them, and this is permissible, and it is from The conjoined without the conjoined to it, like his saying: For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their wealth until his saying: “They say: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers” and the verse, and the Almighty’s saying: And your Lord will come and the angels, rank upon rank meaning: And the angels will come, rank upon rank. And His statement, informing about them, “They say: We believe in it,” meaning the ambiguous, All of it is from our Lord, meaning all of the decisive and the ambiguous are true and correct, and each one of them confirms the other and testifies to it, because all of it is from God and nothing from God is different or contradictory, as He says: Do they not then consider the Qur’an? Had it been from other than God, they would have found therein much discrepancy, and for this reason the Most High said: And none will remember except those of understanding, meaning only those with sound minds and upright understandings understand, comprehend, and contemplate the meanings in their proper manner. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Awf al-Himsi told us, Na’eem ibn Hammad told us, Fayyad al-Raqi told us, Abdullah ibn Yazid told us, and he had met the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Anas, Abu Umamah, and Abu al-Darda’, may God be pleased with them, said: Abu al-Darda’ told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about those firmly grounded in knowledge, so he said: He whose oath is true, whose tongue is truthful, and whose heart is upright, and he who… Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard some people arguing, so he said: “Those who came before you were destroyed because of this. They struck some parts of the Book of God with others. The Book of God was revealed to confirm some parts of it, so do not deny some parts of it with others. So whatever you know of it, say, and whatever you do not know, leave it to its scholar.” Ibn Mardawayh’s narration of this hadith was presented on the authority of Hisham ibn `Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Hazim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of `Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on his authority. Abu Ya`la al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Zuhair ibn Harb told us, Anas ibn `Iyad told us, on the authority of Abi Hazim, on the authority of Abi Salamah, who said: I do not know it except from Abi Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Qur’an was revealed in seven letters, and arguing about the Qur’an is disbelief. He said it. Three - what you know of it, then act upon it, and what you do not know of it, then refer it to its Knower, the Most High, the Majestic. This is a sound chain of transmission, but it has a defect because of the narrator’s statement, I do not know it except from Abu Hurairah. Ibn al-Mundhir said in his interpretation: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told us, Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Nafi’ ibn Yazid told me, he said: It is said: Those who are firmly grounded in knowledge are humble before God, humble themselves before God in His pleasure, they do not act arrogantly towards those above them nor do they belittle those below them. Then God the Almighty said, informing us that they called upon their Lord, saying: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, meaning do not make them deviate from guidance after You have established them upon it, and do not make us like those in whose hearts is deviation, who seek what is ambiguous in the Qur’an, but establish us on Your straight path and Your upright religion, and grant us from Yourself, meaning from You, mercy with which You will establish our hearts and unite us, and increase our faith and certainty. You are the Giver. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Amr ibn Abdullah al-Awdi told us, and Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, they both said: Wakee’ told us on the authority of Abdul Hameed ibn Bahram, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Umm Salamah, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. Then he recited: “Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bakkar, on the authority of Abdul Hameed ibn Bahram, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Umm Salamah, who is Asma’ bint Yazid ibn al-Sakn, who heard her narrating: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to frequently supplicate: O God, Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. I said: O Messenger of God, does the heart fluctuate? He said: Yes, God did not create any human being from the children of Adam except that his heart is between two fingers of God Almighty, so if He wills, He makes him steadfast, and if He wills, He makes him deviate.” So we ask God Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after He has guided us, and we ask Him to grant us mercy from Him, for He is the Bestower. And thus Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Asad ibn Musa, on the authority of Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, with a similar chain of transmission. He also narrated it on the authority of al-Muthanna, on the authority of al-Hajjaj ibn Munhal, on the authority of Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, with a similar chain of transmission, and he added: I said, O Messenger of God, will you not teach me a supplication that I can make for myself? He said, Yes, say, ‘O God, Lord of the Prophet Muhammad, forgive my sin, remove the anger in my heart, and save me from the misleading trials.’ Then Ibn Mardawayh said: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Harun ibn Bakkar al-Dimashqi narrated to us, al-Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Khalal narrated to us, Yazid ibn Yahya ibn Ubaydullah informed us, Saeed ibn Bashir informed us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Hassan al-A’raj, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, often supplicated, O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. I said, “O Messenger of God, God, how often you supplicate with this supplication, and He said: There is no heart but that it is between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful. If He wills to make it straight, He makes it straight, and if He wills to make it deviate, He makes it deviate. Have you not heard His saying: “Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.” Strange in this regard, but its origin is proven in the two Sahihs and others through many chains of narration without the addition of this noble verse. Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri. Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Hibban, and Abdullah ibn Wahb both added on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abi Ayyub: Abdullah ibn al-Waleed al-Tujibi told me on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her. That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he woke up at night would say, “There is no god but You, glory be to You, O God, I seek Your forgiveness for my sin, and I ask You for mercy, O God, increase me in knowledge and do not let my heart deviate after You have guided me, and grant me mercy from You, for You are the Bestower.” The wording of Ibn Mardawayh. Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Abu Ubayd, the freed slave of Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Ubadah ibn Nassi, that he told him that he heard Qays ibn al-Harith say: Abu Abdullah al-Sunabhi told me that he prayed the Maghrib prayer behind Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, and Abu Bakr recited in the first two rak’ahs the Mother of the Qur’an and two short surahs from al-Mufassal, and he recited in the third rak’ah. He said: So I came close to him until my clothes almost touched his clothes, and I heard him recite the Mother of the Qur’an and this verse: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us al-An’am 2:17. Abu Ubaid said: Ubadah bin Nassi informed me that he was with Umar bin Abdul Aziz during his caliphate, and Umar said to Qais: How did you tell me about Abu Abdullah? Umar said: We have not abandoned it since we heard it from him, although before that I was on something else. A man said to him: What was the Commander of the Faithful on before that? He said: I used to recite “Say: He is God, the One.” This trace was narrated by Al-Walid bin Muslim on the authority of Malik and Al-Awza’i, both on the authority of Abu Ubaid. This trace was also narrated by Al-Walid on the authority of Ibn Jaber, on the authority of Yahya bin Yahya Al-Ghassani, on the authority of Mahmud bin Labid, on the authority of Al-Sunabhi, that he prayed behind Abu Bakr the Maghrib prayer, and in the first two he recited Surat Al-Fatihah and a short surah, reciting aloud. When he stood up for the third, he began to recite, so I came close to him until my clothes touched his clothes, and he recited this verse: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate. And His saying, Our Lord, You will surely gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt, meaning they say in their supplication: “O our Lord, You will surely gather Your creation on the Day of Resurrection, and You will separate between them and judge between them in that over which they differed, and You will reward each one according to his deeds and what he was upon in this world of good and evil.”
3:9: God the Almighty informs us that in the Qur’an there are clear verses, they are the foundation of the Book, that is, clear evidence with clear meanings that are not ambiguous to anyone, and there are other verses in which the meaning is ambiguous to many people or some of them, so whoever refers what is ambiguous to what is clear from it and rules its clear verses over its ambiguous verses for him has been guided, and whoever reverses it will be reversed, and for this reason God the Almighty said, They are the foundation of the Book, that is, its origin to which one can refer when in doubt, and others are ambiguous, that is, their meaning may agree with the clear verses or may mean something else in terms of wording and structure, but not in terms of what is intended. They differed regarding the clear and ambiguous verses, and many expressions were narrated from the predecessors. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: The clear verses abrogate it, its lawful and unlawful verses, its rulings, its limits, its obligations, what is commanded and acted upon. And Ibn Abbas also said that the clear verses are the words of God the Almighty: Say, ‘Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you - that you not associate anything with Him.’ and the verses after it. And the Almighty’s saying: And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him to three verses after it. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and he narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: My father told us, Sulayman bin Harb told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Suwayd, that Yahya bin Ya’mar and Abu Fakhita discussed this verse, which is: They are the foundations of the Book and others are unspecific. Abu Fakhita said: The openings of the surahs. Yahya bin Ya’mar said: The obligations, the commands and prohibitions, the lawful and the unlawful. Ibn Lahi’ah said on the authority of Ata’ bin Dinar on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: They are the foundations of the Book because they are written in all the books. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: Because there is no one of the people of religion who does not accept them. It was said about the unspecific: the abrogated, the earlier and later, the examples in it, the sections, and what is believed in but not acted upon. It was narrated by Ali bin Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was said that they are the disconnected letters at the beginning of the surahs, as stated by Muqatil bin Hayyan, and from Mujahid, the ambiguous verses confirm each other, and this is in the interpretation of His statement, A Book similar and repeated. There they mentioned that the similar is the speech that is in one context, and the repeated is the speech about two opposite things, such as the description of Paradise and the description of Hell, and the mention of the state of the righteous and the state of the wicked, and the like. As for here, the ambiguous is that which is opposite to the decisive, and the best that has been said about it is what we have presented, and it is what Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar, may God have mercy on him, stated, where he said: Among them are the decisive verses, so they are the proof of the Lord and the protection of the servants and the repelling of falsehood by opponents, and they have no change from what they were placed upon. He said: And the ambiguous verses in truth have no change, distortion, or interpretation. God has tested the servants with them as He tested them with regard to the lawful and the unlawful, so that they are not diverted to falsehood and distorted from the truth. That is why God Almighty said: But as for those in whose hearts is deviation meaning misguidance and deviation from the truth to falsehood they follow that which is ambiguous of it meaning they only take from it that which is ambiguous which they can distort to suit their corrupt purposes and apply it to them because its wording is likely to be what they are interpreting. As for the decisive verses, they have no share in them because it is a defense for them and an argument against them. That is why God Almighty said: Seeking to cause discord meaning to mislead their followers, making them think that they are using the Qur’an as evidence for their innovation, while it is an argument against them and not for them, just as if the Christians argued that the Qur’an had stated that Jesus was the spirit of God and His word which He bestowed upon Mary and a spirit from Him, and they abandoned the argument of His statement He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favor and His statement “Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is as the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust and then said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was” and other decisive verses that clearly state that he was created from God’s creations and a servant and messenger from God’s messengers. And the Almighty’s saying, and seeking its interpretation, meaning to distort it as they want. Muqatil ibn Hayyan and al-Suddi said, They seek to know what will be and what are the consequences of things from the Qur’an. Imam Ahmad said, Ismail told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited, “It is He who has sent down to you the Book. In it are verses that are precise, they are the foundation of the Book, and others that are unspecific,” until His saying, people of understanding. Then he said, So when you see those who dispute therein, they are the ones God meant, so beware of them. This is how the hadith was found in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, with no one between them. This is how Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Ismail ibn Ulayyah and Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi, both of them on the authority of Ayoub, on his authority. Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Abdi narrated it in his Musnad on the authority of Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi on the authority of Ayoub, on his authority. And Abd al-Razzaq narrated it on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Ayoub, and more than one person narrated it on the authority of Ayoub. Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih on the authority of Ayyub narrated it, and Abu Bakr ibn al-Mundhir narrated it in his interpretation through two chains of transmission on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Sadosi, whose nickname was A’rim: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aishah, on his authority. Abu ‘Amir al-Kharraz and others followed Ayyub on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, on the authority of Abu ‘Amir al-Kharraz, and he mentioned it. And thus Sa’id ibn Mansur narrated it in his Sunan on the authority of Hammad ibn Yahya al-Abbah, on the authority of ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aishah. And Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Ruh ibn al-Qasim and Nafi’ ibn ‘Umar al-Jumahi, both of them on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aishah, on his authority. Nafi’ said in his narration on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah: Aishah told me, and he mentioned it. This hadith was narrated by Al-Bukhari when interpreting this verse, and by Muslim in the Book of Al-Qadar in his Sahih, and by Abu Dawud in Al-Sunnah in his Sunan, all three of them on the authority of Al-Qa’nabi, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ibrahim Al-Tustari, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book; in it are verses that are precise until His saying: And none will remember except those of understanding. She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: So when you see those who follow that of it which is ambiguous, then those are the ones whom God has named, so beware of them. The wording of Al-Bukhari. And Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it likewise, on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ibrahim, and he said: It is good and authentic. He mentioned that Yazid ibn Ibrahim Al-Tustari was the only one to mention Al-Qasim in this chain of narration. More than one person narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah on the authority of Aisha, but he did not mention Al-Qasim, that is what he said. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it and said: My father told us, Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi told us, Yazid ibn Ibrahim al-Tastari and Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the statement of God Almighty: But as for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow that of it which is ambiguous, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When you see those who follow that of it which is ambiguous, then those are the ones whom God has named, so beware of them. Ibn Jarir said: Ali ibn Sahl told us, al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: They follow that of it which is ambiguous, seeking discord, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has warned you, so when you see them, recognize them. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through another chain of transmission on the authority of al-Qasim on the authority of Aisha, and he said: Imam Ahmad. Abu Kamil told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Abu Ghalib, who said: I heard Abu Umamah telling the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the words of God Almighty: But as for those in whose hearts is deviation, they will follow that of it which is ambiguous, he said: They are the Khawarij. And about the words of God Almighty: The Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black, he said: They are the Khawarij. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from more than one source, on the authority of Abu Ghalib. On the authority of Abu Umamah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who mentioned it. The least of these hadiths is that they are attributed to the Companions, but their meaning is correct. The first innovation that occurred in Islam was the Khawarij tribulation, and their beginning was because of this world when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided the spoils of Hunayn. It was as if they saw in their corrupt minds that he was not just in the division, so they surprised him with this statement. Their speaker, Dhu al-Khuwaysira - may God rip his side open - said: Be just, for you have not been just. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “You have failed and lost if I am not just. Does he trust me with the people of the earth and you do not trust me?” When the man turned back, Omar ibn al-Khattab, and in the narration of Khalid ibn al-Walid, asked permission from the Messenger of God to kill him. He said, “Leave him, for from the offspring of this man, that is, from his kind, will emerge a people who will consider your prayer insignificant compared to their prayer, your fasting insignificant compared to their fasting, and your recitation insignificant compared to their recitation. They will depart from the religion as an arrow departs from its target. So wherever you find them, kill them, for in killing them there is a reward for whoever kills them.” Then they appeared during the days of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and they killed them at Nahrawan. Then peoples, tribes, opinions, whims, articles, and many widespread sects branched out from them. Then the Qadariyyah emerged, then the Mu’tazila, then the Jahmites, and other innovations that the Truthful, the Trusted One, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us about in his saying, And this nation will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in Hell except one. They said, Who are they, O Messenger of God? He said, Those who are on what I and my companions are on. Al-Hakim included this addition in his Mustadrak. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Abu Musa told us, Amr bin Asim told us, Al-Mu`tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Jundub bin Abdullah, that it reached him on the authority of Hudhayfah, or he heard it from him, narrating on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said, Indeed, among my nation are people who recite the Qur’an, scattering it like scattering dates, and interpreting it in a way other than its interpretation. They did not include it. And the Almighty’s saying, And none knows its interpretation except God, the reciters differed regarding the pause here. It was said: On the majesty, as was mentioned previously on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Interpretation is of four types: an interpretation that no one is excused for understanding, an interpretation that the Arabs know from their languages, an interpretation that those firmly grounded in knowledge know, and an interpretation that none knows except God. This statement is narrated on the authority of Aisha, Urwah, Abu al-Sha’tha’, Abu Nahik, and others. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim said in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: Hashim bin Muzayd told us, Muhammad bin Ismail bin Ayyash told us, my father told me, Damdam bin Zar'ah told me, on the authority of Shuraih bin Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, "I do not fear for my nation except three things: that their wealth will increase and they will become envious and fight each other; that the Book will be opened to them and the believer will take it seeking its interpretation. 'None knows its interpretation except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge who say, 'We believe in it,'" the verse; and that their knowledge will increase and they will waste it and not care about it. Very strange. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim told us, Ahmad ibn Amr told us, Hisham ibn Ammar told us, Ibn Abi Hatim told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn al-`As, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The Qur’an was not revealed for some parts to contradict others. So whatever you recognize of it, act upon it, and whatever is ambiguous, believe in it.” Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, who said: Ibn Abbas used to recite: “None knows its interpretation except God. And those firmly rooted in knowledge say, ‘We believe in it.’” Ibn Jarir narrated it likewise on the authority of `Umar ibn `Abd al-`Aziz and Malik ibn Anas that they believed in it but did not know its interpretation. Ibn Jarir narrated that in the recitation of `Abdullah ibn Mas`ud: “Its interpretation is only with amusement. And those firmly rooted in knowledge say, ‘We believe in it.’” And likewise on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b, Ibn Jarir chose this statement. Some of them stopped at his saying: and those firmly rooted in knowledge, and many of the commentators and scholars of the principles followed them, and said: Addressing what is not understood is far-fetched. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: I am from those firmly rooted who know its interpretation. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: And those firmly rooted in knowledge know its interpretation and say, We believe in it. And so said al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ja’far al-Zubayr: And none knows its interpretation he meant what he meant except God, and those firmly rooted in knowledge say, “We believe in it. Then they returned the interpretation of the ambiguous verses to what they knew of the interpretation of the decisive verses in which no one has an interpretation except one interpretation, so the Book was consistent with their saying and some of it confirmed some of it, so the argument was implemented, and the excuse became apparent, and falsehood was removed, and disbelief was repelled. And in the hadith, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed for Ibn Abbas, and said, O God, give him understanding in the religion and teach him the interpretation. And from Scholars have separated this matter and said: Interpretation is used, and it is intended by it in the Qur’an in two meanings: One of them is interpretation in the sense of the reality of the thing and what its matter leads to, and from it is the saying of the Most High: And he said, O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision of before and His saying, Do they await except its interpretation on the Day its interpretation comes? meaning the reality of what they were informed of regarding the matter of the Resurrection. If this is what is meant by interpretation, then the pause is at the majesty because the realities of matters and their essence are not known clearly except by God Almighty, and His saying, And those firmly rooted in knowledge is the subject and They say, ‘We believe in it’ is its predicate. However, if the other meaning is meant by interpretation, which is explanation, clarification, and expression of the thing, like His saying, Inform us of its interpretation, meaning its explanation, if this meaning is meant by it, then the pause is at And those firmly rooted in knowledge because they know and understand what they were addressed with in this regard, even if they do not encompass knowledge of the realities of things as they are. Based on this, His saying, They say, ‘We believe in it’ is a state of them, and this is permissible, and it is from The conjoined without the conjoined to it, like his saying: For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their wealth until his saying: “They say: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers” and the verse, and the Almighty’s saying: And your Lord will come and the angels, rank upon rank meaning: And the angels will come, rank upon rank. And His statement, informing about them, “They say: We believe in it,” meaning the ambiguous, All of it is from our Lord, meaning all of the decisive and the ambiguous are true and correct, and each one of them confirms the other and testifies to it, because all of it is from God and nothing from God is different or contradictory, as He says: Do they not then consider the Qur’an? Had it been from other than God, they would have found therein much discrepancy, and for this reason the Most High said: And none will remember except those of understanding, meaning only those with sound minds and upright understandings understand, comprehend, and contemplate the meanings in their proper manner. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Awf al-Himsi told us, Na’eem ibn Hammad told us, Fayyad al-Raqi told us, Abdullah ibn Yazid told us, and he had met the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Anas, Abu Umamah, and Abu al-Darda’, may God be pleased with them, said: Abu al-Darda’ told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about those firmly grounded in knowledge, so he said: He whose oath is true, whose tongue is truthful, and whose heart is upright, and he who… Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard some people arguing, so he said: “Those who came before you were destroyed because of this. They struck some parts of the Book of God with others. The Book of God was revealed to confirm some parts of it, so do not deny some parts of it with others. So whatever you know of it, say, and whatever you do not know, leave it to its scholar.” Ibn Mardawayh’s narration of this hadith was presented on the authority of Hisham ibn `Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Hazim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of `Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on his authority. Abu Ya`la al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Zuhair ibn Harb told us, Anas ibn `Iyad told us, on the authority of Abi Hazim, on the authority of Abi Salamah, who said: I do not know it except from Abi Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Qur’an was revealed in seven letters, and arguing about the Qur’an is disbelief. He said it. Three - what you know of it, then act upon it, and what you do not know of it, then refer it to its Knower, the Most High, the Majestic. This is a sound chain of transmission, but it has a defect because of the narrator’s statement, I do not know it except from Abu Hurairah. Ibn al-Mundhir said in his interpretation: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told us, Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Nafi’ ibn Yazid told me, he said: It is said: Those who are firmly grounded in knowledge are humble before God, humble themselves before God in His pleasure, they do not act arrogantly towards those above them nor do they belittle those below them. Then God the Almighty said, informing us that they called upon their Lord, saying: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, meaning do not make them deviate from guidance after You have established them upon it, and do not make us like those in whose hearts is deviation, who seek what is ambiguous in the Qur’an, but establish us on Your straight path and Your upright religion, and grant us from Yourself, meaning from You, mercy with which You will establish our hearts and unite us, and increase our faith and certainty. You are the Giver. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Amr ibn Abdullah al-Awdi told us, and Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, they both said: Wakee’ told us on the authority of Abdul Hameed ibn Bahram, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Umm Salamah, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. Then he recited: “Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bakkar, on the authority of Abdul Hameed ibn Bahram, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Umm Salamah, who is Asma’ bint Yazid ibn al-Sakn, who heard her narrating: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to frequently supplicate: O God, Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. I said: O Messenger of God, does the heart fluctuate? He said: Yes, God did not create any human being from the children of Adam except that his heart is between two fingers of God Almighty, so if He wills, He makes him steadfast, and if He wills, He makes him deviate.” So we ask God Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after He has guided us, and we ask Him to grant us mercy from Him, for He is the Bestower. And thus Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Asad ibn Musa, on the authority of Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, with a similar chain of transmission. He also narrated it on the authority of al-Muthanna, on the authority of al-Hajjaj ibn Munhal, on the authority of Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, with a similar chain of transmission, and he added: I said, O Messenger of God, will you not teach me a supplication that I can make for myself? He said, Yes, say, ‘O God, Lord of the Prophet Muhammad, forgive my sin, remove the anger in my heart, and save me from the misleading trials.’ Then Ibn Mardawayh said: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Harun ibn Bakkar al-Dimashqi narrated to us, al-Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Khalal narrated to us, Yazid ibn Yahya ibn Ubaydullah informed us, Saeed ibn Bashir informed us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Hassan al-A’raj, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, often supplicated, O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. I said, “O Messenger of God, God, how often you supplicate with this supplication, and He said: There is no heart but that it is between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful. If He wills to make it straight, He makes it straight, and if He wills to make it deviate, He makes it deviate. Have you not heard His saying: “Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.” Strange in this regard, but its origin is proven in the two Sahihs and others through many chains of narration without the addition of this noble verse. Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri. Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Hibban, and Abdullah ibn Wahb both added on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abi Ayyub: Abdullah ibn al-Waleed al-Tujibi told me on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her. That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he woke up at night would say, “There is no god but You, glory be to You, O God, I seek Your forgiveness for my sin, and I ask You for mercy, O God, increase me in knowledge and do not let my heart deviate after You have guided me, and grant me mercy from You, for You are the Bestower.” The wording of Ibn Mardawayh. Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Abu Ubayd, the freed slave of Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Ubadah ibn Nassi, that he told him that he heard Qays ibn al-Harith say: Abu Abdullah al-Sunabhi told me that he prayed the Maghrib prayer behind Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, and Abu Bakr recited in the first two rak’ahs the Mother of the Qur’an and two short surahs from al-Mufassal, and he recited in the third rak’ah. He said: So I came close to him until my clothes almost touched his clothes, and I heard him recite the Mother of the Qur’an and this verse: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us al-An’am 2:17. Abu Ubaid said: Ubadah bin Nassi informed me that he was with Umar bin Abdul Aziz during his caliphate, and Umar said to Qais: How did you tell me about Abu Abdullah? Umar said: We have not abandoned it since we heard it from him, although before that I was on something else. A man said to him: What was the Commander of the Faithful on before that? He said: I used to recite “Say: He is God, the One.” This trace was narrated by Al-Walid bin Muslim on the authority of Malik and Al-Awza’i, both on the authority of Abu Ubaid. This trace was also narrated by Al-Walid on the authority of Ibn Jaber, on the authority of Yahya bin Yahya Al-Ghassani, on the authority of Mahmud bin Labid, on the authority of Al-Sunabhi, that he prayed behind Abu Bakr the Maghrib prayer, and in the first two he recited Surat Al-Fatihah and a short surah, reciting aloud. When he stood up for the third, he began to recite, so I came close to him until my clothes touched his clothes, and he recited this verse: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate. And His saying, Our Lord, You will surely gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt, meaning they say in their supplication: “O our Lord, You will surely gather Your creation on the Day of Resurrection, and You will separate between them and judge between them in that over which they differed, and You will reward each one according to his deeds and what he was upon in this world of good and evil.”
3:10: God Almighty tells us about the disbelievers that they are fuel for the Fire On the Day when their excuses will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse, and for them is the worst home. And what they were given in this world of wealth and children will not benefit them with God, nor will it save them from His punishment and painful chastisement, as God Almighty said: “So do not be impressed by their wealth or their children. God only intends to punish them thereby in the life of this world, and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers.” And God Almighty said: “Do not be deceived by the movement of those who disbelieve throughout the land. A brief enjoyment. Then their refuge is Hell, and an evil resting place.” And He said here: Indeed, those who disbelieve meaning in God’s signs, and denied His messengers, and disobeyed His book, and did not benefit from His revelation to His prophets, “Never will their wealth or their children avail them against God at all. And those are the fuel for the Fire” meaning its wood with which it is lit and kindled, as He said: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell. The verse. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Ibn Al-Haad told me on the authority of Hind bint Al-Harith, on the authority of Umm Al-Fadl, the mother of Abdullah bin Abbas, who said: While we were in Mecca, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, got up at night and called out, Have I conveyed the message? O God, have I conveyed the message? three times. Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, got up and said, Yes. Then morning came and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Islam will prevail until disbelief returns to its places. People will cross the seas with Islam. A time will come upon the people when they will learn the Qur’an and recite it, then they will say, ‘We have recited and taught. So who is this who is better than us?’ Is there any good in those people? They said, ‘O Messenger of God, who are those people?’ He said, ‘Those are from you, and those are the fuel of the Fire.’” And this is how I saw it with this wording. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Yazid bin Abdullah bin Al-Haad, on the authority of Hind bint Al-Harith, the wife of Abdullah bin Shaddad, on the authority of Umm Al-Fadl, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, got up one night in Mecca and said, Have I conveyed the message? He said it three times. Then Umar ibn al-Khattab, who was the most patient, stood up and said: O God, yes, I was keen, I tried hard, and I advised, so be patient. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Faith will prevail until disbelief is returned to its places. Men will cross the seas with Islam. A time will come upon the people when they will read the Qur’an, and they will read it and teach it, and they will say: We have read and we have taught, so who is this who is better than us? There is no good in those people.” They said: O Messenger of God, who are those people? He said: Those people are from you, and those people are the fuel of the Fire.” Then he narrated it via Musa ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Bint al-Haad, on the authority of al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, in a similar manner. And the Almighty’s saying: Like the way of Pharaoh’s family. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Like the actions of Pharaoh’s family. This was also narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, Mujahid, Abu Malik, Ad-Dahhak, and more than one person. Some of them say: Like the way of Pharaoh’s family, and like the actions of Pharaoh’s family, and like the likeness of Pharaoh’s family. The words are similar, and dāb with sukūn and ḥarā’ like nahr and nahr, is the action, state, affair, matter, and habit, just as it is said: This will not cease to be my habit and your habit. Imru’ al-Qays said: My companions standing there on their mounts said, Don’t be sad, be kind. As usual, from Umm Al-Huwairith before her and her neighbor Umm Al-Rabab in Masal The meaning is as you usually do with Umm al-Huwayrith when you destroyed yourself in your love for her and cried over her house and her image. The meaning of the verse is that neither wealth nor children will avail the disbelievers, rather they will perish and be tormented as happened to the people of Pharaoh and those before them who denied the messengers in what they brought of God’s signs and proofs. And God is severe in penalty, meaning severe in punishment, painful in torment, no one can avoid it and nothing escapes Him. Rather, He is the doer of whatever He wills, the One who has overcome everything and everything has been humbled to Him. There is no god but Him and no lord but Him.

The meaning of the verse is that neither wealth nor children will avail the disbelievers, rather they will perish and be tormented as happened to the people of Pharaoh and those before them who denied the messengers in what they brought of God’s signs and proofs. And God is severe in penalty, meaning severe in punishment, painful in torment, no one can avoid it and nothing escapes Him. Rather, He is the doer of whatever He wills, the One who has overcome everything and everything has been humbled to Him. There is no god but Him and no lord but Him.
3:12: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to the disbelievers, You will be overcome, that is, in this world, and you will be herded, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, to Hell, and an evil resting place. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar reported on the authority of Asim bin Umar bin Qatada that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had afflicted the people of Badr with what he had afflicted, and returned to Medina, he gathered the Jews in the market of Banu Qaynuqa', and said, O group of Jews, become Muslims before God afflicts you with what afflicted the Quraysh. They said, "O Muhammad, do not be deceived by yourselves because you killed a group of Quraysh who were ignorant and did not know how to fight. By God, if you had fought us, you would have known that we are the people, and that you have not encountered the likes of us." So God revealed about that His statement, Say to those who disbelieve, You will be overcome and herded to Hell, and an evil resting place." There was a sign for you in the two companies that met. One company was fighting in the cause of God, and the other was disbelieving. They saw them twice their number, with their own eyes. And God supports with His victory whom He wills." Indeed in that is a lesson for those of insight. Muhammad ibn Ishaq also narrated it, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Saeed or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned it. For this reason, the Almighty said: There has certainly been for you a sign, meaning, there has certainly been for you, O Jews who say what you say, a sign, meaning, an indication that God is the One who strengthens His religion, supports His Messenger, manifests His word, and upholds His command. In two companies, meaning, two groups, that met, meaning to fight. One company fighting in the way of God and the other disbelieving, and they were the polytheists of Quraysh on the day of Badr. And His statement: They will see them twice their number, with their own eyes, some scholars said, as narrated by Ibn Jarir: The polytheists on the day of Badr will see the Muslims twice their number, with their own eyes, meaning, God made that in what they saw a reason for Islam’s victory over them. There is no problem with this except for one aspect, which is that the polytheists sent Umar ibn Sa’d on that day before the fighting to estimate the number of Muslims for them, so he informed them that they were three hundred, a little more or less, and that is how it was. They were three hundred and some men, then when the battle took place, God supported them with a thousand of the special angels and their leaders. The second opinion is that the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: They will see them twice as many as they are, with their own eyes is that the Muslim group will see the disbelieving group twice as many as they are, that is, twice as many in number, and despite this, God will grant them victory over them. There is no problem with this according to what Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: that the believers on the day of Badr were three hundred and thirteen men, and the polytheists were six hundred and twenty-six men. It is as if this opinion was taken from the apparent meaning of this verse, but it is contrary to what is well-known among the people of history, biographies, and the days of the people, and contrary to what is known among the majority that the polytheists were between nine hundred and a thousand, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman, on the authority of Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr, that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked that black slave of Banu Al-Hajjaj about the number of Quraysh, he said: Many. He said: How many do they slaughter every day? He said: One day nine and one day ten. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people are between nine hundred and a thousand. Abu Ishaq al-Sabi’i narrated on the authority of Haritha, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: They were a thousand, and Ibn Mas’ud said the same. It is well-known that they were between nine hundred and a thousand, and in any case they were three times the number of Muslims, and on this basis this statement is problematic, and God knows best, but Ibn Jarir explained this and made it correct as you say: I have a thousand, and I need twice that, and you need three thousand, so he said, and on this basis there is no problem, but another question remains which is applicable to both statements, which is to say: What is the connection between this verse and the Almighty’s statement in the story of Badr And when He showed them to you when you met in your eyes as few and made you as few in their eyes that God might accomplish a matter which was to be done? The answer is that this was in one case and the other was in another case, as al-Suddi said on the authority of al-Tayyib on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud in the Almighty’s statement: There was for you a sign in the two companies that met al-Badr, he said: This is the day of Badr, Abdullah Ibn Mas’ud said: We looked at the polytheists and saw them weakening against us, then we looked at them and did not see them increase against us by a single man, and that is the Almighty’s statement: And when He showed them to you when you met in your eyes “A little and they will make you seem small in their eyes. The verse. Abu Ishaq said on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: They seemed small in our eyes until I said to a man next to me: Do you think they are seventy? He said: I think they are a hundred. He said: So we captured one of them and said: How many were you? He said: One thousand. So when each of the two groups saw the other, the Muslims saw the polytheists twice as many as they were, that is, twice as many as they were, so that they would trust and turn to and seek help from their Lord, the Almighty, the Majestic. And the polytheists saw the believers likewise, so that they would feel terror, fear, panic, and panic. Then, when the two groups faced each other, God made these few in the eyes of the others, and those few in the eyes of the others, so that each of them would advance over the other, so that God may accomplish a matter that was to be done, that is, to differentiate between truth and falsehood, so that the word of faith would prevail over disbelief and tyranny, and the believers would be honored and the disbelievers would be humiliated, as God Almighty said: And God certainly gave you victory at Badr, when you were weak. And He said here: “And God supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those of vision.” That is, indeed in that is a lesson for whoever has insight and understanding, by which he is guided to God’s wisdom, actions, and decree, which is to grant victory to His believing servants in this worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand.

3:14: The Almighty tells us about the types of pleasures that have been made attractive to people in this worldly life, such as women and children. He began with women, because the temptation caused by them is more severe, as it was proven in the Sahih that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, I have not left behind me any temptation more harmful to men than women. But if the intention behind them is chastity and many children, then this is desired and recommended, as the hadiths have been reported encouraging marriage and increasing it, The best of this nation is the one who has the most women, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “The world is a provision, and the best provision of it is the righteous woman. If he looks at her, she pleases him, and if he commands her, she obeys him, and if he is away from her, she protects herself and his wealth.” And his saying in another hadith, Women and perfume have been made beloved to me, and the delight of my eyes has been made in prayer. Aisha may God be pleased with her said: Nothing was dearer to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) than women except horses, and in another narration: From horses except women. The love of children is sometimes for boasting and adornment, so it is included in this, and sometimes it is to increase offspring and increase the nation of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from those who worship God alone with no partner, so this is praiseworthy and commendable as is proven in the hadith: Marry the loving and fertile, for I will outnumber the nations with you on the Day of Resurrection. Likewise, the love of money is sometimes for boasting, conceit, and haughtiness towards the weak and oppression towards the poor, so this is reprehensible, and sometimes it is for spending on acts of worship, maintaining kinship ties and relatives, and forms of righteousness and obedience, so this is praiseworthy and commendable in Islamic law. The commentators differed regarding the amount of a qintar in statements, and the gist of them is that it is a large sum of money as Ad-Dahhak and others said, and it was said: a thousand dinars, and it was said: one thousand two hundred dinars, and it was said: twelve thousand, and it was said: forty thousand, and it was said: sixty thousand, and it was said: seventy thousand. It was said: Eighty thousand, and other things were said. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A qintar is twelve thousand awqiyah, each awqiyah is better than what is between the heavens and the earth. Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on his authority. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Ibn Mahdi, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Asim ibn Bahdalah, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, with a chain of transmission ending with him, and this is more authentic. This is how Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal and Ibn Umar, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Abu Hurairah and Abu al-Darda’, that they said: A qintar is one thousand two hundred awqiyah. Then Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: Zakariya ibn Yahya al-Dareer told us, Shababah told us, Mukhallad ibn Abd al-Wahid told us. On the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Maimouna, on the authority of Zur bin Habish, on the authority of Abi bin Kaab, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A qintar is one thousand and two hundred ounces. This is also a rejected hadith, and it is more likely that it was attributed to Abi bin Kaab like other companions. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah al-Rabdhi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Yahnash Abu Musa, on the authority of Umm al-Darda’, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever recites one hundred verses will not be recorded among the heedless, and whoever recites one hundred verses to a thousand, will have a qintar of reward with God, a qintar of which is like a huge mountain.” And Wakee’ narrated it on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah with a similar meaning. Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ya’qub told us, Ahmad bin Isa bin Zaid al-Lakhmi told us in Tanis, Amr bin Abi Salamah told us, Zuhair bin Muhammad told us, Hamid al-Tawil and another man told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the statement of God Almighty: And the heaped up qintars? He said: The qintar is two thousand ounces. It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, but they did not include it. This is how al-Hakim narrated it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it with another wording, saying: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Raqi informed us, Amr ibn Abi Salamah informed us, Zuhair, meaning Ibn Muhammad, informed us, Hamid al-Tawil, and another man whom he named, meaning Yazid al-Raqashi, informed us, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: A qintar means a thousand dinars. This is how Ibn Mardawayh and al-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Maryam, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Salamah, so he mentioned the same with his chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Hasan al-Basri, on his authority, in a mursal and attributing it to him: A qintar is one thousand two hundred dinars. This is the narration of al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ad-Dahhak said: Some Arabs say: A qintar is one thousand dinars, and some say: twelve thousand. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Arim told us on the authority of Hammad on the authority of Saeed. Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, said: A qintar is a bull’s musk filled with gold. Abu Muhammad said: Muhammad bin Musa Al-Harashi narrated it on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, and the chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet is more authentic. And the love of horses is divided into three categories: Sometimes their owners tie them up, preparing them for the path of God whenever they need them to fight on them, so these are rewarded, and sometimes they tie them up as a source of pride and a warning to the people of Islam, so this is a burden on their owner, and sometimes for chastity and the acquisition of their offspring, and God’s right in their necks is not forgotten, so this is a cover for their owner, as will come in the hadith about that, God willing, when God says: And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war verse. As for the branded, it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: the branded is the shepherd, and the branded is the beautiful, and likewise it was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Abd al-Rahman bin Abdullah bin Abza, al-Suddi, al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Abu Sinan, and others. Makhul said: the branded is the forelock and the hooves, and it was said: other than that. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told us on the authority of Abd al-Hamid bin Ja’far, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, on the authority of Suwaid bin Qais, on the authority of Mu’awiyah bin Hudayj, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him. On his authority, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no Arabian horse except that it is permitted to call out with two supplications at every dawn, saying: ‘O God, You have given me authority over the children of Adam, so make me among those whose wealth and family are most beloved to him, or whose wealth and family are most beloved to him.’” And the Almighty’s statement, and the livestock, means camels, cows, and sheep, and and the tillage, means the land used for planting and farming. Imam Ahmad said: Ruh bin Ubadah told us, Abu Na’amah al-Adawi told us, on the authority of Muslim bin Badil, on the authority of Iyas bin Zuhair, on the authority of Suwaid bin Hubairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, who said: The best wealth of a man is a well-trained mare or a well-fertilized field. Well-trained means those with many offspring, and the field is the arranged palm tree, and well-fertilized means the pollinated. Then God Almighty said: That is the enjoyment of worldly life, meaning that this is only the flower of worldly life and its fleeting, transient adornment. And with God is the best return, meaning the best return and reward. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Hafs bin Omar bin Saad. He said: Omar bin Al-Khattab said when the verse The love of desires has been made fair-seeming to people was revealed, I said: Now, O Lord, when You have made it fair-seeming to us, then the verse “Say: Shall I inform you of something better than that for those who fear God” was revealed. For this reason, the Almighty said: “Say: Shall I inform you of something better than that?” That is, say, O Muhammad, to the al-Nas 114:Shall I inform you of something better than what has been made fair-seeming to people in this worldly life of its adornments and pleasures, which will inevitably vanish? Then He informed about that and said: For those who fear God are gardens with their Lord beneath which rivers flow. That is, rivers of various kinds of drinks flow between its sides and corners, such as honey, milk, wine, water, and other things that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Abiding therein that is, remaining therein forever, not seeking to change from it. And purified spouses that is, free from filth, impurity, harm, menstruation, postpartum bleeding, and other things that befall the women of this world. And pleasure from God that is, His pleasure will be upon them, so He will never be angry with them after that. For this reason, the Almighty said in the other verse in Bara’ah: And the pleasure of God is greater, meaning greater than what He gave them of eternal bliss. Then God Almighty said: And God is Seeing of His servants, meaning He gives each one according to what he deserves of giving.
