Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of al-Hasan al-Basri, on his authority, in a mursal and attributing it to him: A qintar is one thousand two hundred dinars. This is the narration of al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ad-Dahhak said: Some Arabs say: A qintar is one thousand dinars, and some say: twelve thousand. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Arim told us on the authority of Hammad on the authority of Saeed. Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, said: A qintar is a bull’s musk filled with gold. Abu Muhammad said: Muhammad bin Musa Al-Harashi narrated it on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, and the chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet is more authentic. And the love of horses is divided into three categories: Sometimes their owners tie them up, preparing them for the path of God whenever they need them to fight on them, so these are rewarded, and sometimes they tie them up as a source of pride and a warning to the people of Islam, so this is a burden on their owner, and sometimes for chastity and the acquisition of their offspring, and God’s right in their necks is not forgotten, so this is a cover for their owner, as will come in the hadith about that, God willing, when God says: And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war verse. As for the branded, it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: the branded is the shepherd, and the branded is the beautiful, and likewise it was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Abd al-Rahman bin Abdullah bin Abza, al-Suddi, al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Abu Sinan, and others. Makhul said: the branded is the forelock and the hooves, and it was said: other than that. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told us on the authority of Abd al-Hamid bin Ja’far, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, on the authority of Suwaid bin Qais, on the authority of Mu’awiyah bin Hudayj, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him. On his authority, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no Arabian horse except that it is permitted to call out with two supplications at every dawn, saying: ‘O God, You have given me authority over the children of Adam, so make me among those whose wealth and family are most beloved to him, or whose wealth and family are most beloved to him.’” And the Almighty’s statement, and the livestock, means camels, cows, and sheep, and and the tillage, means the land used for planting and farming. Imam Ahmad said: Ruh bin Ubadah told us, Abu Na’amah al-Adawi told us, on the authority of Muslim bin Badil, on the authority of Iyas bin Zuhair, on the authority of Suwaid bin Hubairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, who said: The best wealth of a man is a well-trained mare or a well-fertilized field. Well-trained means those with many offspring, and the field is the arranged palm tree, and well-fertilized means the pollinated. Then God Almighty said: That is the enjoyment of worldly life, meaning that this is only the flower of worldly life and its fleeting, transient adornment. And with God is the best return, meaning the best return and reward. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Hafs bin Omar bin Saad. He said: Omar bin Al-Khattab said when the verse The love of desires has been made fair-seeming to people was revealed, I said: Now, O Lord, when You have made it fair-seeming to us, then the verse “Say: Shall I inform you of something better than that for those who fear God” was revealed. For this reason, the Almighty said: “Say: Shall I inform you of something better than that?” That is, say, O Muhammad, to the al-Nas 114:Shall I inform you of something better than what has been made fair-seeming to people in this worldly life of its adornments and pleasures, which will inevitably vanish? Then He informed about that and said: For those who fear God are gardens with their Lord beneath which rivers flow. That is, rivers of various kinds of drinks flow between its sides and corners, such as honey, milk, wine, water, and other things that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Abiding therein that is, remaining therein forever, not seeking to change from it. And purified spouses that is, free from filth, impurity, harm, menstruation, postpartum bleeding, and other things that befall the women of this world. And pleasure from God that is, His pleasure will be upon them, so He will never be angry with them after that. For this reason, the Almighty said in the other verse in Bara’ah: And the pleasure of God is greater, meaning greater than what He gave them of eternal bliss. Then God Almighty said: And God is Seeing of His servants, meaning He gives each one according to what he deserves of giving.
3:16: The Blessed and Exalted describes His pious servants whom He has promised a great reward, saying: “Those who say, ‘Our Lord, we have believed,’ meaning in You and in Your Book and in Your Messenger, ‘so forgive us our sins,’ meaning in our belief in You and in what You have prescribed for us, so forgive us our sins and our shortcomings in our affairs by Your grace and mercy, ‘and protect us from the punishment of the Fire,’” then the Almighty said: The patient ones, meaning in their performance of acts of obedience and their abandonment of forbidden acts, and the truthful ones, in what they have reported of their faith in the hard work they are committed to, and the obedient ones, and obedience means obedience and submission, “and those who spend,’ meaning from their wealth in all the acts of obedience they are commanded to do, and maintaining ties of kinship and relatives, and filling gaps, and helping those in need, “and those who seek forgiveness in the hours of the pre-dawn hours,” indicating the virtue of seeking forgiveness at the time of the pre-dawn hours. It has been said that when Jacob, peace be upon him, said to his sons, I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, he delayed them until The time of dawn. It was proven in the two Sahihs and other Musnads and Sunnahs from more than one source on the authority of a group of the Companions that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, the Blessed and Exalted, descends every night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains, and says: ‘Is there anyone who asks so that I may give him? Is there anyone who calls so that I may answer him? Is there anyone who seeks forgiveness so that I may forgive him?’” The hadith. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Hasan al-Daraqutni devoted a separate section to this, and narrated it through multiple chains of transmission. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed the witr prayer throughout the night from the beginning, middle, and end, and his witr prayer ended at dawn.” Abdullah ibn Umar used to pray at night, then he would say: O Nafi’, has dawn come? If he says: Yes, he should turn to supplication and seeking forgiveness until morning. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, my father told us, on the authority of Harith ibn Abi Matar, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Hatib, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard a man in the early hours of the morning in a corner of the mosque saying: O Lord, You commanded me and I obeyed You, and this is the early hours of the morning, so forgive me. I looked and saw that he was Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: We were commanded when we prayed at night to seek forgiveness at the end of the early hours of the morning seventy times.

3:18: God Almighty has testified, and He is sufficient as a witness, and He is the most truthful and just of witnesses, and the most truthful of those who say, There is no god but He, meaning He is the One who is unique in divinity for all creation, and that all are His servants and creation and are in need of Him, and He is independent of anything other than Him, as God Almighty said: But God bears witness to what He has revealed to you, the verse, then He linked the testimony of His angels and those of knowledge with His testimony, saying, God bears witness that there is no god but He, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge, and this is a great distinction for scholars in this situation. Upholding justice is in the accusative case as a state, and it is like that in all cases. There is no god but He is an emphasis on what came before, The Almighty, the Wise, the Almighty whose majesty and pride cannot be challenged, the Wise in His words and actions, His law and His decree. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Abd Rabbih told us, Baqiyah ibn al-Waleed told us, Jubayr ibn Amr al-Qurashi told us, Abu Saeed al-Ansari told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, the client of the family of al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, on the authority of al-Zubayr Ibn al-Awwam said: “I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Arafat reciting this verse: ‘God bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels and those of knowledge upholding justice. There is no god but He, the Almighty, the Wise.’ And I am of that, O Lord.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from another chain of transmission, saying: Ali ibn Husayn told us, Muhammad ibn al-Mutawakkil al-Asqalani told us, Umar ibn Hafs ibn Thabit Abu Sa’id al-Ansari told us, Abd al-Malik ibn Yahya ibn Ibad ibn Abd God ibn al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of al-Zubayr, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he recited this verse: ‘God bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels.’ He said: ‘And I bear witness, O Lord.’” Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said in al-Mu’jam al-Kabir: Abdun ibn Ahmad and Ali ibn Sa’id al-Razi told us, they said: ‘Ammar ibn Umar ibn al-Mukhtar told us, my father told me, Ghalib al-Qattan told me, he said: I came to Kufa for business, and I stopped near al-A’mash, and when it was night I wanted to go down. He got up and prayed at night and came across this verse: “God bears witness that there is no god except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge - maintaining justice. There is no god except Him - the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam.” Then Al-A’mash said: “And I bear witness to what God bears witness to, and I entrust this testimony to God, which is a trust for me with God. Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam.” He said it repeatedly. I said: He heard something in it. So I went to him and said farewell to him, then I said: O Abu Muhammad, I heard you repeating this verse. He said: Have you not heard what is in it? I said: I have been with you for a month and you have not spoken to me. He said: By God, I will not tell you about it until a year has passed. So I stayed for a year, and I was at his door. When the year had passed, I said: O Abu Muhammad, the year has passed. He said: Abu Wa’il told me on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Its owner will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and God Almighty will say: My servant made a covenant with Me, and I am the most deserving of fulfilling the covenant. Admit My servant into Paradise.” And the Almighty’s saying, Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam is a statement from Him, the Almighty, that there is no religion in His sight that He accepts from anyone except Islam, and it is following the messengers in what God sent them with at all times until they were sealed with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who blocked all paths to Him except from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So whoever meets God after the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a religion other than His law, it will not be accepted, as God Almighty said: And whoever desires other than Islam as religion, it will never be accepted from him (al-Baqarah 2:17). And he said in this verse, informing that the religion that is acceptable to him is limited to Islam, Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam. And Ibn Jarir mentioned that Ibn Abbas read, God bears witness that there is no god but God. He and the angels and those of knowledge uphold justice. There is no god except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam. The majority read it with the kasra as a report, and both meanings are correct, but this is more apparent according to the majority, and God knows best. Then God the Almighty informed us that those who were given the first Book only differed after the proof had been established against them by sending messengers to them and revealing books to them, so He said: And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. That is, some of them transgressed against one another, so they differed about the truth due to their envy, hatred, and animosity, so some of them led the hatred of others to oppose him in all his words and actions, even if they were true. Then God the Almighty said: And whoever disbelieves in the verses of God, that is, whoever denies what God revealed in His Book, then indeed, God is swift in account. That is, God will reward him for that and hold him accountable for his denial, and punish him for his opposition to His Book. Then the Almighty said: If they dispute with you meaning they argue with you about monotheism “say: I have submitted myself to God, and so do those who follow me” meaning say: I have devoted my worship to God alone, with no partner or equal, no son or wife, and those who follow me meaning on my religion, he says the same as I say, as the Almighty said: “Say: This is my way; I invite to God with insight, I and those who follow me” the verse, then the Almighty said, commanding His servant and Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to call to his way and religion and to enter into his law and what God sent him with, the People of the Book from the two religions and the illiterate polytheists, so the Almighty said: “And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered ones, ‘Have you submitted?’ If they have submitted, then they have been guided. But if they turn away, then upon you is only the conveyance” meaning, God is responsible for their reckoning, and to Him is their return and their final destination, and He is the One who guides whomever He wills and misguides whomever He wills, and He has the perfect wisdom and the conclusive proof. For this reason the Almighty said: And God is Seeing of His servants meaning, He is All-Knowing of who deserves guidance from whomever deserves it. Misguidance, and He is the One who is not asked about what He does, but they will be asked. This is only due to His wisdom and mercy. This verse and others like it are among the clearest indications of the universality of his mission, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him, to all of creation, as is necessarily known from his religion, and as indicated by the Book and the Sunnah in more than one verse and hadith. Among these is the saying of God Almighty: Say, ‘O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all.’ And God Almighty said: Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His Servant that he may be to the worlds a warner. And in the two Sahihs and others, which have been proven to be transmitted by multiple events, that he, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him, sent his letters calling to God the kings of the horizons and the groups of the children of Adam, from their Arabs and non-Arabs, their People of the Book and their illiterate ones, in compliance with God’s command to him to do so. And Abd al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him, that he said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, no one from this nation hears of me, whether Jewish or Christian, and dies without believing in what I was sent with, except that he will be among the people of the Fire.” Narrated by Muslim. And he, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him, said: I was sent to the red and the black, he said, The Prophet was sent to his people in particular, and I was sent to all people. Imam Ahmad said: Muammil told us, Hammad told us, Thabit told us on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him: A Jewish boy used to make ablution water for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and hand him his shoes. He fell ill, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him and entered upon him while his father was sitting at his head. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “O so-and-so, say ‘There is no god but God.’ He looked at his father and his father remained silent. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, repeated it to him, and he looked at his father. His father said: ‘Obey Abu al-Qasim.’ The boy said: ‘I bear witness that there is no god but God and that you are the Messenger of God.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out saying: ‘Praise be to God who brought him out of the Fire through me.’” Narrated by al-Bukhari in Sahih, and other verses and hadiths.

3:20: God Almighty has testified, and He is sufficient as a witness, and He is the most truthful and just of witnesses, and the most truthful of those who say, There is no god but He, meaning He is the One who is unique in divinity for all creation, and that all are His servants and creation and are in need of Him, and He is independent of anything other than Him, as God Almighty said: But God bears witness to what He has revealed to you, the verse, then He linked the testimony of His angels and those of knowledge with His testimony, saying, God bears witness that there is no god but He, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge, and this is a great distinction for scholars in this situation. Upholding justice is in the accusative case as a state, and it is like that in all cases. There is no god but He is an emphasis on what came before, The Almighty, the Wise, the Almighty whose majesty and pride cannot be challenged, the Wise in His words and actions, His law and His decree. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Abd Rabbih told us, Baqiyah ibn al-Waleed told us, Jubayr ibn Amr al-Qurashi told us, Abu Saeed al-Ansari told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, the client of the family of al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, on the authority of al-Zubayr Ibn al-Awwam said: “I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Arafat reciting this verse: ‘God bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels and those of knowledge upholding justice. There is no god but He, the Almighty, the Wise.’ And I am of that, O Lord.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from another chain of transmission, saying: Ali ibn Husayn told us, Muhammad ibn al-Mutawakkil al-Asqalani told us, Umar ibn Hafs ibn Thabit Abu Sa’id al-Ansari told us, Abd al-Malik ibn Yahya ibn Ibad ibn Abd God ibn al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of al-Zubayr, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he recited this verse: ‘God bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels.’ He said: ‘And I bear witness, O Lord.’” Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said in al-Mu’jam al-Kabir: Abdun ibn Ahmad and Ali ibn Sa’id al-Razi told us, they said: ‘Ammar ibn Umar ibn al-Mukhtar told us, my father told me, Ghalib al-Qattan told me, he said: I came to Kufa for business, and I stopped near al-A’mash, and when it was night I wanted to go down. He got up and prayed at night and came across this verse: “God bears witness that there is no god except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge - maintaining justice. There is no god except Him - the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam.” Then Al-A’mash said: “And I bear witness to what God bears witness to, and I entrust this testimony to God, which is a trust for me with God. Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam.” He said it repeatedly. I said: He heard something in it. So I went to him and said farewell to him, then I said: O Abu Muhammad, I heard you repeating this verse. He said: Have you not heard what is in it? I said: I have been with you for a month and you have not spoken to me. He said: By God, I will not tell you about it until a year has passed. So I stayed for a year, and I was at his door. When the year had passed, I said: O Abu Muhammad, the year has passed. He said: Abu Wa’il told me on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Its owner will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and God Almighty will say: My servant made a covenant with Me, and I am the most deserving of fulfilling the covenant. Admit My servant into Paradise.” And the Almighty’s saying, Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam is a statement from Him, the Almighty, that there is no religion in His sight that He accepts from anyone except Islam, and it is following the messengers in what God sent them with at all times until they were sealed with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who blocked all paths to Him except from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So whoever meets God after the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a religion other than His law, it will not be accepted, as God Almighty said: And whoever desires other than Islam as religion, it will never be accepted from him (al-Baqarah 2:17). And he said in this verse, informing that the religion that is acceptable to him is limited to Islam, Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam. And Ibn Jarir mentioned that Ibn Abbas read, God bears witness that there is no god but God. He and the angels and those of knowledge uphold justice. There is no god except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam. The majority read it with the kasra as a report, and both meanings are correct, but this is more apparent according to the majority, and God knows best. Then God the Almighty informed us that those who were given the first Book only differed after the proof had been established against them by sending messengers to them and revealing books to them, so He said: And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. That is, some of them transgressed against one another, so they differed about the truth due to their envy, hatred, and animosity, so some of them led the hatred of others to oppose him in all his words and actions, even if they were true. Then God the Almighty said: And whoever disbelieves in the verses of God, that is, whoever denies what God revealed in His Book, then indeed, God is swift in account. That is, God will reward him for that and hold him accountable for his denial, and punish him for his opposition to His Book. Then the Almighty said: If they dispute with you meaning they argue with you about monotheism “say: I have submitted myself to God, and so do those who follow me” meaning say: I have devoted my worship to God alone, with no partner or equal, no son or wife, and those who follow me meaning on my religion, he says the same as I say, as the Almighty said: “Say: This is my way; I invite to God with insight, I and those who follow me” the verse, then the Almighty said, commanding His servant and Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to call to his way and religion and to enter into his law and what God sent him with, the People of the Book from the two religions and the illiterate polytheists, so the Almighty said: “And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered ones, ‘Have you submitted?’ If they have submitted, then they have been guided. But if they turn away, then upon you is only the conveyance” meaning, God is responsible for their reckoning, and to Him is their return and their final destination, and He is the One who guides whomever He wills and misguides whomever He wills, and He has the perfect wisdom and the conclusive proof. For this reason the Almighty said: And God is Seeing of His servants meaning, He is All-Knowing of who deserves guidance from whomever deserves it. Misguidance, and He is the One who is not asked about what He does, but they will be asked. This is only due to His wisdom and mercy. This verse and others like it are among the clearest indications of the universality of his mission, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him, to all of creation, as is necessarily known from his religion, and as indicated by the Book and the Sunnah in more than one verse and hadith. Among these is the saying of God Almighty: Say, ‘O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all.’ And God Almighty said: Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His Servant that he may be to the worlds a warner. And in the two Sahihs and others, which have been proven to be transmitted by multiple events, that he, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him, sent his letters calling to God the kings of the horizons and the groups of the children of Adam, from their Arabs and non-Arabs, their People of the Book and their illiterate ones, in compliance with God’s command to him to do so. And Abd al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him, that he said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, no one from this nation hears of me, whether Jewish or Christian, and dies without believing in what I was sent with, except that he will be among the people of the Fire.” Narrated by Muslim. And he, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him, said: I was sent to the red and the black, he said, The Prophet was sent to his people in particular, and I was sent to all people. Imam Ahmad said: Muammil told us, Hammad told us, Thabit told us on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him: A Jewish boy used to make ablution water for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and hand him his shoes. He fell ill, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him and entered upon him while his father was sitting at his head. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “O so-and-so, say ‘There is no god but God.’ He looked at his father and his father remained silent. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, repeated it to him, and he looked at his father. His father said: ‘Obey Abu al-Qasim.’ The boy said: ‘I bear witness that there is no god but God and that you are the Messenger of God.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out saying: ‘Praise be to God who brought him out of the Fire through me.’” Narrated by al-Bukhari in Sahih, and other verses and hadiths.
3:21: This is a censure from God the Most High for the People of the Book for the sins and forbidden acts they committed in their denial of God’s verses, in the past and present, which the Messengers conveyed to them out of arrogance towards them, and out of stubbornness towards them, and insolence towards the truth, and in disdain for following it. Despite this, they killed those of the Prophets whom they killed when they conveyed to them God’s law without reason or crime on their part towards them, except for the fact that they called them to the truth. And they kill those among the people who enjoin justice. This is the height of arrogance, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Arrogance is rejecting the truth and belittling people. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu al-Zubayr al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muslim al-Naysaburi, a resident of Mecca, told us. Abu Hafs Umar ibn Hafs, meaning Ibn Thabit ibn Zararah al-Ansari, told us. Muhammad ibn Hamza told us. Abu al-Hasan, a client of Banu Asad, told us, on the authority of Makhul, on the authority of Abu Qubaysah ibn Dhu’ayb al-Khuza’i, on the authority of Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah., may God be pleased with him, said: “I said: O Messenger of God, which people will be most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection? He said: A man who killed a prophet or one who enjoined what is right and forbade what is wrong. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of God and kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among the people - give them tidings of a painful punishment.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu Ubaidah, the Children of Israel killed forty-three prophets at the beginning of the day in one hour. Then one hundred and seventy men from the Children of Israel stood up and enjoined what is right upon those they killed and forbade them from what is wrong. They killed them all at the end of the day on that day. They are the ones whom God, the Almighty, mentioned.” And thus it was narrated by Ibn Jarir on the authority of Abu Ubaid al-Wasabi Muhammad ibn Hafs, on the authority of Ibn Himyar, on the authority of Abu al-Hasan, a client of Banu Asad, on the authority of Makhul, and on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Children of Israel killed three hundred prophets at the beginning of the day, and they held a market for their vegetables at the end of it. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. That is why when they were too arrogant to accept the truth and acted arrogantly towards people, God met them with humiliation and degradation in this world and a humiliating punishment in the Hereafter. God Almighty said: Then give them tidings of a painful punishment. That is, painful and humiliating. Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.

3:23: God Almighty says, denouncing the Jews and Christians who cling to what they claim to their two books that are in their hands, which are the Torah and the Gospel, and when they are called to judge by what is in them of obeying God in what He commanded them to do in them of following Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they turn away and turn away from them, and this is the most extreme form of censuring them and mentioning them for their opposition and stubbornness, then God Almighty says: That is because they said, ‘The Fire will not touch us except for a few days’ meaning that what led them and emboldened them to oppose the truth was their fabrication against God in what they claimed for themselves that they would only be tormented in the Fire for seven days for every thousand years in this world, one day, and the explanation of that was presented in Surat Al-Baqarah. Then God the Almighty said: And they were deceived in their religion by what they used to invent. That is, He made them steadfast in their false religion, by what they deceived themselves with, by claiming that the Fire would not touch them because of their sins except for a few days. They are the ones who invented this of their own accord and fabricated it, and God did not send down any authority for it. God the Almighty said, threatening and warning them: How then will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt? That is, how will their situation be when they have inventing lies about God, belied His Messengers, killed His Prophets, and the scholars of their people, who enjoined what is right and forbade what is wrong, and God the Almighty will ask them about all of that and hold them accountable for it and reward them for it. For this reason God the Almighty said: How then will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt? That is, there is no doubt about its occurrence and existence, And every soul will be fully compensated for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.

3:26: The Blessed and Most High says: Say O Muhammad, glorifying your Lord, thanking Him, entrusting Him and relying on Him, O God, Owner of the Kingdom meaning, all the Kingdom is Yours, "You give the Kingdom to whomever You will and take the Kingdom away from whomever You will. You honor whomever You will and abase whomever You will" meaning, You are the Giver and the Withholder, and You are the One Who wills what is, and what You do not will is not. In this verse, there is a warning and guidance to thank God Almighty for His Messenger's blessing upon him and this nation, because God Almighty transferred the prophethood from the Children of Israel to the Arab Qurayshite Prophet, the unlettered Meccan, the Seal of the Prophets, and the Messenger of God to all of mankind and jinn, in whom God combined the virtues of those who came before him, and He distinguished him with characteristics that He did not give to any prophet or messenger in knowledge of God and His law, and his knowledge of the past and future unseen, and His revelation to him of the truths of the Hereafter, and the spreading of his nation in the horizons in the easts of the earth. And its wests, and the manifestation of his religion and law over all other religions and laws, so may the prayers and peace of God be upon him forever until the Day of Judgment, as long as night and day follow one another. That is why God the Almighty said: “Say: O God, Owner of the Kingdom” verse, meaning You are the One who controls Your creation and does what You will, just as God the Almighty responded to those who judge Him in His affairs when He said: “And they say: Why was this Qur’an not sent down to a great man from the two cities?” God the Almighty said in response to them: Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord? verse, meaning we dispose of what We have created as we wish without any hindrance or resistance, and We have the perfect wisdom and complete proof in that, and thus He gives prophethood to whomever He wills, just as God the Almighty said: God knows best where to place His message verse, and God the Almighty said: See how We have favored some of them over others verse. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated in the biography of Ishaq bin Ahmad in his history, on the authority of Al-Ma’mun the Caliph, that he saw written in a palace in the land of the Romans in Himyaritic, so he translated it for him, and it was: In the name of God, the night and day do not differ, nor do the stars of the sky revolve in the heavens except by the transfer of blessings from a king whose authority has passed to another king. And the kingdom of the Lord of the Throne is eternal, it is not perishable nor shared. And the Almighty’s saying: You cause the night to enter the day and cause the day to enter the night means that You take from the length of this and add to the shortness of this, so they become equal, then You take from this to this and they differ, then they become equal, and so on in the seasons of the year, spring, summer, autumn and winter. And the Almighty’s saying: And You bring forth the living from the dead and You bring forth the dead from the living means that You bring forth the crop from the seed, and the seed from the crop, and the palm tree from the pit, and the pit from the palm tree, and the believer from the disbeliever, and the disbeliever from the believer, and the chicken from the egg, and the egg from the chicken, and what follows this course of all things, And You provide for whomever You will without account means that You give whomever You will of wealth that cannot be counted or calculated, and You withhold from others because of Your wisdom, will, desire and justice in that. Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Ghalabi told us, Ja’far ibn Jisr ibn Farqad told us, my father told us on the authority of Amr ibn Malik, on the authority of Abu al-Jawza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “The greatest name of God, by which if He is called upon, He answers, is in this verse from Al Imran 3:‘Say, O God, Owner of the Kingdom, You give the kingdom to whom You will and You take the kingdom away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and You abase whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Indeed, You are over all things competent.’”

That is why God the Almighty said: “Say: O God, Owner of the Kingdom” verse, meaning You are the One who controls Your creation and does what You will, just as God the Almighty responded to those who judge Him in His affairs when He said: “And they say: Why was this Qur’an not sent down to a great man from the two cities?” God the Almighty said in response to them: Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord? verse, meaning we dispose of what We have created as we wish without any hindrance or resistance, and We have the perfect wisdom and complete proof in that, and thus He gives prophethood to whomever He wills, just as God the Almighty said: God knows best where to place His message verse, and God the Almighty said: See how We have favored some of them over others verse. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated in the biography of Ishaq bin Ahmad in his history, on the authority of Al-Ma’mun the Caliph, that he saw written in a palace in the land of the Romans in Himyaritic, so he translated it for him, and it was: In the name of God, the night and day do not differ, nor do the stars of the sky revolve in the heavens except by the transfer of blessings from a king whose authority has passed to another king. And the kingdom of the Lord of the Throne is eternal, it is not perishable nor shared. And the Almighty’s saying: You cause the night to enter the day and cause the day to enter the night means that You take from the length of this and add to the shortness of this, so they become equal, then You take from this to this and they differ, then they become equal, and so on in the seasons of the year, spring, summer, autumn and winter. And the Almighty’s saying: And You bring forth the living from the dead and You bring forth the dead from the living means that You bring forth the crop from the seed, and the seed from the crop, and the palm tree from the pit, and the pit from the palm tree, and the believer from the disbeliever, and the disbeliever from the believer, and the chicken from the egg, and the egg from the chicken, and what follows this course of all things, And You provide for whomever You will without account means that You give whomever You will of wealth that cannot be counted or calculated, and You withhold from others because of Your wisdom, will, desire and justice in that. Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Ghalabi told us, Ja’far ibn Jisr ibn Farqad told us, my father told us on the authority of Amr ibn Malik, on the authority of Abu al-Jawza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “The greatest name of God, by which if He is called upon, He answers, is in this verse from Al Imran 3:‘Say, O God, Owner of the Kingdom, You give the kingdom to whom You will and You take the kingdom away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and You abase whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Indeed, You are over all things competent.’”
3:29: The Blessed and Exalted forbade His believing servants from befriending the disbelievers, and from taking them as allies, secretly showing them affection, instead of the believers. Then He threatened for that, saying, And whoever does that has nothing to do with God. That is, whoever commits what God has forbidden in this, has disavowed God, as God the Almighty said, “O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, extending to them affection while they have disbelieved in what came to you of the truth, expelling the Messenger and yourselves, [and] beware of believing in God, your Lord. If you have come out [to fight] in My cause and seeking My pleasure, secretly showing them affection, and I know what you have concealed and what you have declared. And whoever does that among you has certainly strayed from the right path.” And God the Almighty said, “O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you want to make for God a clear authority over you?” And God the Almighty said, “O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever is an ally to them among you - then indeed, he is of them.” And He said, God the Almighty said after mentioning the friendship of the believers from the Muhajireen, Ansar and Bedouins: “And those who disbelieve are allies of one another. If you do not do so, there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption.” God the Almighty said: Except that you guard yourselves against them with a precaution. That is, except for those who fear their evil in some countries or times, then he may guard hisselves against them outwardly, not inwardly and intentionally, as Al-Bukhari said on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’: He said: We smile in the faces of people while our hearts curse them. Al-Thawri said: Ibn Abbas said: Taqiyyah is not in action, rather taqiyyah is in the tongue. Al-Awfi narrated the same on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Taqiyyah is in the tongue. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Abu Al-Sha’tha’, Ad-Dahhak and Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas also said this. What they said is supported by God’s statement: Whoever disbelieves in God after his belief, except for one who is forced thereto [while] his heart is at rest with faith. Al-Bukhari said: Al-Hasan said: Taqiyya is until the Day of Judgment. Then God the Almighty said: And God warns you of Himself meaning He warns you of His vengeance for opposing Him, His power and His punishment for those who befriend His enemies and oppose His allies. Then God the Almighty said: And to God is the destination meaning to Him is the return and the turning back, so that He may reward every worker for his deeds. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Suwaid bin Saeed told us, Muslim bin Khalid told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Hussain, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Sabit, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun, who said: Muadh bin Jabal stood up among us and said: “O my sons, I am the Messenger of God to you. Do you know that the return is to Paradise or to Hell?”
3:30: The Blessed and Exalted informs His servants that He knows the secrets, the consciences and the outward appearances, and that nothing of theirs is hidden from Him. Rather, His knowledge encompasses them in all conditions, times, days, moments and all times, and everything on earth and in the heavens, not even the weight of an atom is hidden from Him, nor anything smaller than that in all regions of the earth, seas and mountains. And God is over all things competent. That is, His power is effective in all of that. This is a warning from Him to His servants to fear and dread Him lest they commit what He has forbidden and what He hates from them, for He is All-Knowing of all their affairs, and He is Able to hasten their punishment. And if He delays those among them, He grants respite, then He takes the grip of the Mighty, the Powerful. For this reason, He said after this, On the Day every soul will find present what it has done of good, the verse, meaning on the Day of Resurrection, all of the servant’s deeds, good and evil, will be presented to him, as the Almighty said, On that Day man will be informed of what he has sent forth and what he has left behind. So whatever he sees of his good deeds, that will please him and make him happy, and whatever he sees of It was ugly and made him angry and he wished that he would disown him and that there would be a long period between them, as was said to his devil who was associated with him in this world, and who had emboldened him to do evil: Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts, what an evil companion! Then the Almighty said, confirming, threatening and warning: And God warns you of Himself. That is, He frightens you with His punishment. Then the Almighty said, giving hope to His servants so that they would not despair of His mercy and lose hope in His kindness: And God is Kind to the servants. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: Out of His kindness to them, He warns them of Himself. Another said: That is, He is Merciful to His creation and loves for them to adhere to His straight path and His upright religion and to follow His noble Messenger.

3:32: This noble verse is a ruling on everyone who claims to love God but is not on the Muhammadan way, for he is a liar in his claim in the same matter until he follows the Muhammadan law and the prophetic religion in all his words, actions and conditions, as it was proven in the Sahih from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said, Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our command, it will be rejected. For this reason he said, Say, ‘If you love God, then follow me, and God will love you.’ That is, you will obtain more than what you asked for from your love for Him, which is His love for you, and it is greater than the first, as some of the wise scholars said: The matter is not that you love, but rather the matter is that you love. Al-Hasan al-Basri and others from the Salaf said: Some people claimed that they loved God, so God tested them with this verse, saying: “Say: If you should love God, then follow me, and God will love you.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, Ubayd God ibn Musa told us, on the authority of Abd al-A’la ibn A’yan, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Is religion anything but love and hatred? God the Most High said: “Say: If you should love God, then follow me.” Abu Zur’ah Abd al-A’la said: This hadith is fabricated. Then the Almighty said: And He will forgive you your sins, and God is Forgiving and Merciful. That is, by following the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, you will obtain all of this from the blessing of his embassy. Then the Almighty said, commanding everyone, both private and public, “Say: Obey God and the Messenger. But if they turn away,” that is, disobey his command, then indeed, God does not like the disbelievers. This indicates that disobeying him in the way is disbelief, and God does not like those who are described by that, even if he claims and alleges in himself that he loves God and draws near to Him until he follows the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, the Seal of the Messengers and the Messenger of God to all of mankind: the jinn and mankind, who, if the prophets, or even the messengers, or even those of them who are determined, were in his time, they would have no choice but to follow him, enter into his obedience, and follow his law, as will be explained in the Almighty’s statement: And when God took the covenant of the prophets, the verse, God willing.

3:34: God Almighty tells us that He chose these houses over all the people of the earth, so He chose Adam, peace be upon him, created them with His hand, breathed into him from His spirit, made His angels prostrate to him, taught him the names of everything, and settled him in Paradise, then sent him down from it because of His wisdom in that. He chose Noah, peace be upon him, and made him the first messenger He sent to the people of the earth, when people worshipped idols and associated with God what He had not sent down as authority, and He took revenge for him when he spent a long time among his people calling them to God night and day, secretly and openly, but that only made them flee more, so He called down a curse upon them, so God drowned them all, and none of them were saved except those who followed him in the religion with which God sent him. He chose the family of Abraham, among them the master of mankind and the seal of the prophets, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the family of Imran, and what is meant by this Imran is the father of Mary, daughter of Imran, the mother of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar, may God have mercy on him, said: He is Imran bin Yashim bin Amon Misha bin Hezekiah bin Ahrik bin Yoim bin Azariah bin Amaziah bin Yaush bin Agrihu bin Yazem bin Yahafshat bin Insha bin Abian bin Rakhim bin Solomon bin David, peace be upon them. So Jesus, peace be upon him, is from the descendants of Abraham, as will be explained in Surat Al-An’am, God willing, and he is trustworthy.

3:36: This Imran woman is the mother of Mary, peace be upon her, and she is Hannah bint Faqud. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: She was a woman who could not bear children. One day, she saw a bird feeding its chicks, and she desired a child. She called upon God Almighty to grant her a child, and God answered her prayer. Her husband had intercourse with her, and she became pregnant from him. When she was certain of the pregnancy, she vowed that it would be dedicated, that is, purely devoted to worship and service of the Holy House. She said: “My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated, so accept it from me. Indeed, You are the Hearer, the Knower.” That is, the Hearer of my prayer and the Knower of my intention. She did not know what was in her womb: a male or a female? And when she delivered her, she said, ‘My Lord, indeed I have delivered a female, and God knows best what I have delivered.’ It was read with the ta’ raised, as it is the ta’ of the speaker, and that this is part of her statement. It was read with the ta’ silent, as it is part of the statement of God Almighty, And the male is not like the female, meaning in strength and endurance in worship and service to the Al-Aqsa Mosque. And indeed, I have named her Mary. This is evidence of the permissibility of naming on the day of birth, as is apparent from the context, because it was legislated before us, and it was reported as established. Thus, the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was established, when he said, A son was born to me tonight, and I named him after my father, Ibrahim. They both reported it. It was also established in them: “That Anas bin Malik went with his brother when his mother gave birth to him to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he gave him a chin-tip and named him Abdullah.” In Sahih Al-Bukhari: A man said, ‘O Messenger of God, a son was born to me tonight, so what should I name him?’ He said, ‘The name of your son is Abd Al-Rahman.’ It was also established in Sahih: When Abu Usaid came to him with his son to give him a chin-tip, he forgot about him, so his father ordered him to be returned to their home. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was mentioned in the assembly, he named him Al-Mundhir. As for the hadith of Qatada on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri on the authority of Samurah bin Jundub, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Every boy is in pledge for his ‘aqeeqah, which is slaughtered on his seventh day, and he is named and his head is shaved. Ahmad and the people of Sunan narrated it, and Al-Tirmidhi authenticated it with this wording. It was narrated: and he is made to bleed, which is more authentic and more reliable, and God knows best. And likewise what was narrated by Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar in the Book of Genealogy: “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed the ‘aqeeqah for his son Ibrahim on the seventh day and named him Ibrahim.” Its chain of transmission is not proven, and it contradicts what is in the Sahih. Even if it were authentic, it would be interpreted as meaning that he made his name known that day, and God knows best. And his statement, reporting on the authority of the mother of Mary, that she said, And I seek refuge for her and her offspring with You from the accursed Satan, means that she sought refuge for her with God Almighty from the evil of Satan, and she sought refuge for her offspring, who was her son Jesus, peace be upon him, and God answered her, as Abd al-Razzaq said: “Muammar informed us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ibn Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God said: No child is born except that Satan touches him when he is born, and he cries out crying out from his touch, except for Mary and her son.” Then Abu Hurayrah says: Read if you wish, And I seek refuge for her and her offspring with You from the accursed Satan. They both included it on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq, and Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Al-Faraj, on the authority of Baqiyah, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. It was narrated from the hadith of Qays, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘There is no newborn child but that Satan squeezes him once or twice, except for Jesus, son of Mary, and Mary.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘And I seek refuge for her and her offspring in You from Satan, the accursed.’” And from the hadith of Al-Ala’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Abu Al-Tahir, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Amr ibn Al-Harith, on the authority of Abu Yunus, on the authority of Abu Hurairah. Ibn Wahb also narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Ajlan, the freed slave of Al-Mishma’il, on the authority of Abu Hurairah. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated it on the authority of Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Qusayt, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the original hadith. And thus it was narrated by Al-Layth bin Saad, on the authority of Ja`far bin Rabi`ah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Harmaz al-A`raj, who said: Abu Hurayrah said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The devil stabs every son of Adam in the side when his mother gives birth to him, except for Jesus, son of Mary. He went to stab him, but he stabs the veil.’”

3:38: Our Lord tells us that He accepted her as a vow from her mother, and that He made her grow well, meaning He made her beautiful in appearance and a cheerful appearance, and made the reasons for acceptance easy for her, and paired her with the righteous among His servants so that she would learn from them knowledge, goodness and religion. That is why He said, And Zakariya took care of her. Another reading is, And Zakariya took care of her with emphasis on the fa, and Zakariya is in the accusative case as a direct object, meaning He made him her guardian. Ibn Ishaq said: That was only because she was an orphan. Another mentioned: That the Children of Israel were afflicted with a drought, so Zakariya took care of Mary for that reason. There is no contradiction between the two statements, and God knows best. God decreed that Zakariya would be her guardian for her happiness, so that she would acquire from him a great deal of beneficial knowledge and righteous deeds, and because he was the husband of her maternal aunt, as mentioned by Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir and others. It was also said: the husband of her sister, as mentioned in the Sahih. Then there were Yahya and Isa, who were the sons of the maternal aunt. What Ibn Ishaq mentioned may also be applied to that by extension. Based on this, she was in the custody of her maternal aunt. It was established in the Sahih that “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled that Ammarah bint Hamzah should be in the custody of her maternal aunt, the wife of Ja’far ibn Abi Talib. He said that the maternal aunt is like the mother.” Then God, the Almighty, informed about her sovereignty and majesty in her place of worship, saying: Whenever Zakariya entered upon her in the prayer chamber, he found with her provision. Mujahid, Ikrimah, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-Sha’tha’, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, Atiyah al-Awfi and al-Suddi said: meaning that he found with her summer fruits in the winter, and winter fruits in the summer. On the authority of Mujahid, He found with her provision, meaning knowledge, or he said: scrolls in which there was knowledge. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. The first is more correct and indicates the miracles of the saints. There are many similar versions of this in the Sunnah. So when Zachariah saw this with her, He said, ‘O Mary, from where did you get this?’ That is, he said, From where did you get this? “She said, ‘It is from God. Indeed, God provides for whom He wills without account.’” Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Sahl bin Zangala told us, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, Abdullah bin Lahi`ah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir, “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stayed for days without eating food until it became difficult for him, so he went around the houses of his wives, and he did not find anything with any of them, so he came to Fatima and said: O my daughter, do you have anything for me to eat, for I am hungry? She said: No, by God - may my father and mother be sacrificed for you - so when he left her, a neighbor of hers sent her two loaves of bread and a piece of meat, so she took it from her and put it in a bowl of hers, and said: By God, I will give this to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, over myself and from me, and they were all in need of a full meal, so she sent Hasan or Husayn to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he returned to her, and she said to him: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, God has brought something and I have hidden it for you. He said: Come here, my daughter. She said: So I brought him the bowl, So he uncovered it, and it was filled with bread and meat. When she looked at it, she was amazed and knew that it was a blessing from God. So she praised God and sent blessings upon His Prophet and presented it to the Messenger of God. When he saw it, he praised God and said: Where did you get this, my daughter? She said: O father, “It is from God. God provides for whomever He wills without account.” So he praised God and said: Praise be to God who made you, my daughter, similar to the lady of the women of the Children of Israel. When God provided her with something and she was asked about it, she would say: It is from God. God provides for whomever He wills without account. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for Ali. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ate, and Ali, Fatima, Hasan, Husayn, and all the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his family ate until they were all full. She said: The bowl remained as it was. She said: So she gave the rest of it to all the neighbors, and God made it a blessing and much good. As for the discussion of the disconnected letters, it was mentioned at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah, and His saying, mention the mercy of your Lord, meaning this is a mention of God’s mercy to His servant Zachariah. Yahya bin Ya’mar read, mention the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zachariah, and Zachariah is lengthened and shortened, two well-known readings. He was a great prophet from the prophets of the Children of Israel, and in Sahih Al-Bukhari it is mentioned that he was a carpenter who ate from the work of his hand in carpentry. And his saying, When he called upon his Lord, a secret call, some of the commentators said: He only concealed his supplication so that he would not be accused of being reckless in his request for a child due to his old age. Al-Mawardi narrated it. Others said: He only concealed it because it was dearer to God, as Qatada said about this verse, When he called upon his Lord, a secret call, that God knows the pious heart and hears the secret voice. Some of the predecessors said: He, peace be upon him, got up at night and his companions were asleep, so he began to call out to his Lord, saying secretly: O Lord, O Lord, O Lord, so God said to him: At your service, at your service, at your service. He said, O Lord, indeed my bones have grown feeble, meaning I have become weak and my strength has failed, and my head is ablaze with gray hair, meaning the gray hair has burned into the blackness, as Ibn Duraid said in his book, Al-Maqsura: Don't you see that my head is the color of a morning's forehead under the covers of darkness? The ovary caught fire in a draft like the burning of embers of the ghada tree. What is meant by this is to inform about weakness and arrogance and their apparent and hidden signs. And his saying, And I have never been unhappy in my supplication to You, my Lord, means, I have never known from You anything but an answer to my supplication, and You have never turned me away from what I asked of You. And his saying, And I feared my relatives after me, most of them read the ya’ of mawali in the accusative case as if it were a direct object. According to Al-Kisa’i, he made the ya’ sukoon, as the poet said: As if their hands in the bottom of the tinkling floor were the hands of maids dealing paper The other said: A young man who, if he could compete with the sun, would throw off its mask, or the moon, would throw off its necklace. And from it is the saying of Abu Tammam Habib bin Aws al-Ta’i: His poetry was so different that I stayed up all night to recite it, I thought his rhymes would fight. Mujahid, Qatada and As-Suddi said: By mawali he meant the agnates. Abu Salih said: Kalalah. It was narrated on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, that he used to recite it, And indeed, I feared my agnates after me, with a shaddah on the fa, meaning I said, My agnates after me. According to the first reading, the reason for his fear was that he feared that they would treat people badly after him, so he asked God for a son who would be a prophet after him to govern them with his prophethood as He revealed to him. He was answered in that, not that he feared that they would inherit his money, for a prophet is of a greater status and greater rank than to fear for his money to this extent, or to be disgusted by his agnates’ inheritance of him, and to ask to have a son so that he could take his inheritance without them. This is one reason. Second It was not mentioned that he had money, but rather that he was a carpenter who ate from the earnings of his hands, and such a person does not accumulate money, especially the prophets, for they were the most ascetic in this world. Third It has been proven in the two Sahihs from more than one source that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, We do not inherit, what we leave behind is charity. And in a narration by al-Tirmidhi with a sound chain of transmission, We, the community of prophets, do not inherit. Based on this, it is necessary to interpret his statement, Then grant me from Yourself an heir who will inherit me, as referring to the inheritance of prophethood. For this reason, he said, And he inherits from the family of Jacob, like his statement, And Solomon inherited from David, meaning in prophethood, because if it had been in wealth, he would not have singled him out from among his brothers for that, and there would not have been much benefit in informing about that, since it is well-known and established in all laws and religions that the son inherits from his father. If it were not a special inheritance, he would not have informed about it. All of this is confirmed and proven by what is authentic in the hadith, We, the community of prophets, do not inherit, what we leave behind is charity. Mujahid said about his statement, He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, his inheritance was knowledge, and Zakariya was from the descendants of Jacob. Hisham said: Ismail bin Abi Khalid informed us on the authority of Abu Salih on his statement, He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, he said: He will be a prophet as his fathers were prophets. Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of al-Hasan, he will inherit his prophethood and his knowledge. Al-Suddi said: He will inherit my prophethood and the prophethood of the family of Jacob. Malik on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, And he will inherit from the family of Jacob, he said: Their prophethood. Jabir bin Nuh and Yazid bin Harun both said on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih on his statement, He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, he said: He will inherit my money and inherit the prophethood from the family of Jacob. This is the choice of Ibn Jarir in his interpretation. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Qatada that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God have mercy on Zachariah and what he had to do with inheriting his wealth, and may God have mercy on Lot, for he used to take refuge in a strong support. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Jabir bin Nuh told us on the authority of Mubarak, who is Ibn Fadala, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God have mercy on my brother Zachariah and what he had to do with inheriting his wealth when he said: ‘Grant me from Yourself an heir who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob.’” These are mursal hadiths that do not contradict the sahih hadiths, and God knows best. His statement, And make him, my Lord, pleasing means pleasing to You and to Your creation, You love him and make him beloved to Your creation in his religion and his character.
3:39: When Zachariah, peace be upon him, saw that God would provide Mary, peace be upon her, with winter fruits in the summer and summer fruits in the winter, he desired a child at that time. He was a very old man whose bones had weakened and whose hair was covered with gray hair, and his wife was also old and barren. However, despite all this, he asked his Lord and called out to Him in a secret call, saying, "My Lord, grant me from Yourself meaning from You a good offspring meaning a righteous son for You are the Hearer of supplication. God the Almighty said, Then the angels called to him while he was standing praying in the sanctuary" meaning the angels addressed him verbally, making him hear while he was standing praying in the sanctuary of his worship, the place of his seclusion and the place of his supplication and prayer. Then God the Almighty informed him of what the angels had given him the good report of, "God gives you good tidings of John" meaning a son from your loins whose name will be John. Qatada and others said: He was only called John because God revived him through faith. And his saying, Confirming a word from God. Al-Awfi and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Abu Al-Sha’tha’, As-Suddi, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, Ad-Dahhak and others said about this verse, Confirming a word from God, meaning Jesus, son of Mary. Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas said: He was the first to believe in Jesus, son of Mary. Qatadah said: And according to his Sunnah and method. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said about his saying, Confirming a word from God, he said: Yahya and Jesus were maternal cousins, and Yahya’s mother used to say to Maryam 19:I find that which is in my womb prostrating to that which is in your womb. So that is his belief in Jesus, his belief in him in his mother’s womb, and he was the first to believe in Jesus, and the word of God is Jesus, and he is greater than Jesus, peace be upon him. And this is what As-Suddi also said. His saying: And a master. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, Qatadah, Saeed bin Jubair and others said: The wise. Qatadah said: A master in knowledge and worship. Ibn Abbas, Ath-Thawri and Ad-Dahhak said: The master is the wise and pious. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: He is the knowledgeable jurist. Atiyah said: The master in his character and religion. Ikrimah said: He is the one who is not overcome by anger. Ibn Zayd said: He is the noble. Mujahid and others said: He is the generous to God Almighty. His saying: And chaste. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubair, Abu Al-Shathaa, and Atiyah Al-Awfi, that they said: The one who does not have intercourse with women. And on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas: He is the one who does not have children. And Ad-Dahhak said: He is the one who has no children and no water. And Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Yahya bin Al-Mughirah told us, Jarir told us on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding chaste: The one who does not have water. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated a very strange hadith about this, saying: Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn Ghalib al-Baghdadi told us, Sa`id ibn Sulayman told us, `Ibad, meaning ibn al-`Awwam, told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa`id, on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Ibn al-`As - he does not know whether it was `Abdullah or `Amr - “on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: ‘and a master and chaste,’ he said: Then he took something from the ground and said: His penis was like this.” Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us, Yahya ibn Sa`id al-Qattan told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa`id al-Ansari, that he heard Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Amr ibn al-`As say: There is no one among God’s creation who does not meet Him with a sin except Yahya ibn Zakariya. Then Sa`id recited: ‘and a master and chaste,’ then he took something from the ground and said: The chaste is he whose penis is like this. Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan pointed with the tip of his index finger. This is a hadith that is more authentic in its chain of transmission than the hadith that is attributed to the Prophet. Indeed, there is doubt about the authenticity of the hadith that is attributed to the Prophet. And God knows best. And Ibn al-Mundhir narrated in his interpretation: Ahmad ibn Dawud al-Samnani told us, Suwaid ibn Saeed told us, Ali ibn Musahhar told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Saeed, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-Aas say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘No servant meets God except with a sin, except John ibn Zakariya, for God says: “And a master and chaste.” He said: He only mentioned him like the hem of a garment, and he pointed with his fingertip.” And Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Isa ibn Hammad and Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Muradi told us, they said: Hajjaj ibn Sulayman al-Muqri told us, on the authority of al-Layth ibn Saad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ajlan, on the authority of al-Qa’qa’, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, “that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Every son of Adam meets God with a sin, for which He will punish him if He wills, or have mercy on him, except John ibn Zakariya, for he was a master, chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell down.” To a speck of earth, so he took it and said: His penis was like this speck. Judge Iyad said in his book Al-Shifa: Know that God Almighty’s praise of Yahya that he was chaste is not as some of them said that he was fearful or not mentioned, but rather the most skilled commentators and critics of scholars denied this and said: This is a shortcoming and a defect, and is not befitting of the prophets, peace be upon them, but rather its meaning is that he is protected from sins, i.e. he does not commit them as if he was restrained from them. And it was said that he prevented himself from desires. It was said that he has no desire for women, and it has become clear to you from this that the inability to marry is a deficiency, and the virtue is in its existence, then he prevents it either by striving like Jesus, or by sufficiency from God Almighty like John, peace be upon him, then it is for the one who is able to have it, and does what is required in it, and it does not distract him from his Lord, a higher degree, and it is the degree of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who was not distracted by their large number from the worship of his Lord, rather it increased his worship by protecting them and taking care of them and earning them and guiding them, rather he stated that it is not from the fortunes of his world, even if it is from the fortunes of the world of others, so he said: Some of your world has been made beloved to me. This is his wording. What is meant is that he praised Yahya for being chaste, not that he did not come to women. Rather, its meaning, as he and others have said, is that he was protected from indecencies and filth. This does not prevent him from marrying lawful women, having intercourse with them, and having children with them. Rather, the existence of offspring for him may be understood from the supplication of Zachariah that came before, where he said: Grant me from Yourself good offspring, as if he said: a child who has offspring, lineage, and descendants. And God Almighty knows best. And His saying: And a prophet from among the righteous This is a second glad tiding of the prophethood of John after the glad tiding of his birth, and it is higher than the first, like His saying to Moses’ mother: Indeed, We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers. When Zachariah, peace be upon him, realized this glad tiding, he began to wonder about having a son from him after his old age. He said, ‘My Lord, how can I have a boy when old age has overtaken me and my wife is barren?’ He said, ‘Thus does God do what He wills.’ That is, God’s command is great, nothing is beyond His power, and no matter is too great for Him. He said, ‘My Lord, make for me a sign.’ That is, a sign by which I can prove that I have a son. He said, ‘Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days except by gesture.’ That is, a sign that you cannot speak, even though you are sound and healthy, as in His saying: three nights together. Then He commanded frequent remembrance, glorification, and praise in this state, so God the Almighty said: And remember your Lord often and glorify Him in the evening and the morning. Another part of expanding on this matter will come at the beginning of Surah Maryam, God willing.
