Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Abu Al-Sha’tha’, As-Suddi, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, Ad-Dahhak and others said about this verse, Confirming a word from God, meaning Jesus, son of Mary. Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas said: He was the first to believe in Jesus, son of Mary. Qatadah said: And according to his Sunnah and method. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said about his saying, Confirming a word from God, he said: Yahya and Jesus were maternal cousins, and Yahya’s mother used to say to Maryam 19:I find that which is in my womb prostrating to that which is in your womb. So that is his belief in Jesus, his belief in him in his mother’s womb, and he was the first to believe in Jesus, and the word of God is Jesus, and he is greater than Jesus, peace be upon him. And this is what As-Suddi also said. His saying: And a master. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, Qatadah, Saeed bin Jubair and others said: The wise. Qatadah said: A master in knowledge and worship. Ibn Abbas, Ath-Thawri and Ad-Dahhak said: The master is the wise and pious. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: He is the knowledgeable jurist. Atiyah said: The master in his character and religion. Ikrimah said: He is the one who is not overcome by anger. Ibn Zayd said: He is the noble. Mujahid and others said: He is the generous to God Almighty. His saying: And chaste. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubair, Abu Al-Shathaa, and Atiyah Al-Awfi, that they said: The one who does not have intercourse with women. And on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas: He is the one who does not have children. And Ad-Dahhak said: He is the one who has no children and no water. And Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Yahya bin Al-Mughirah told us, Jarir told us on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding chaste: The one who does not have water. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated a very strange hadith about this, saying: Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn Ghalib al-Baghdadi told us, Sa`id ibn Sulayman told us, `Ibad, meaning ibn al-`Awwam, told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa`id, on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Ibn al-`As - he does not know whether it was `Abdullah or `Amr - “on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: ‘and a master and chaste,’ he said: Then he took something from the ground and said: His penis was like this.” Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us, Yahya ibn Sa`id al-Qattan told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa`id al-Ansari, that he heard Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Amr ibn al-`As say: There is no one among God’s creation who does not meet Him with a sin except Yahya ibn Zakariya. Then Sa`id recited: ‘and a master and chaste,’ then he took something from the ground and said: The chaste is he whose penis is like this. Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan pointed with the tip of his index finger. This is a hadith that is more authentic in its chain of transmission than the hadith that is attributed to the Prophet. Indeed, there is doubt about the authenticity of the hadith that is attributed to the Prophet. And God knows best. And Ibn al-Mundhir narrated in his interpretation: Ahmad ibn Dawud al-Samnani told us, Suwaid ibn Saeed told us, Ali ibn Musahhar told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Saeed, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-Aas say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘No servant meets God except with a sin, except John ibn Zakariya, for God says: “And a master and chaste.” He said: He only mentioned him like the hem of a garment, and he pointed with his fingertip.” And Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Isa ibn Hammad and Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Muradi told us, they said: Hajjaj ibn Sulayman al-Muqri told us, on the authority of al-Layth ibn Saad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ajlan, on the authority of al-Qa’qa’, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, “that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Every son of Adam meets God with a sin, for which He will punish him if He wills, or have mercy on him, except John ibn Zakariya, for he was a master, chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell down.” To a speck of earth, so he took it and said: His penis was like this speck. Judge Iyad said in his book Al-Shifa: Know that God Almighty’s praise of Yahya that he was chaste is not as some of them said that he was fearful or not mentioned, but rather the most skilled commentators and critics of scholars denied this and said: This is a shortcoming and a defect, and is not befitting of the prophets, peace be upon them, but rather its meaning is that he is protected from sins, i.e. he does not commit them as if he was restrained from them. And it was said that he prevented himself from desires. It was said that he has no desire for women, and it has become clear to you from this that the inability to marry is a deficiency, and the virtue is in its existence, then he prevents it either by striving like Jesus, or by sufficiency from God Almighty like John, peace be upon him, then it is for the one who is able to have it, and does what is required in it, and it does not distract him from his Lord, a higher degree, and it is the degree of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who was not distracted by their large number from the worship of his Lord, rather it increased his worship by protecting them and taking care of them and earning them and guiding them, rather he stated that it is not from the fortunes of his world, even if it is from the fortunes of the world of others, so he said: Some of your world has been made beloved to me. This is his wording. What is meant is that he praised Yahya for being chaste, not that he did not come to women. Rather, its meaning, as he and others have said, is that he was protected from indecencies and filth. This does not prevent him from marrying lawful women, having intercourse with them, and having children with them. Rather, the existence of offspring for him may be understood from the supplication of Zachariah that came before, where he said: Grant me from Yourself good offspring, as if he said: a child who has offspring, lineage, and descendants. And God Almighty knows best. When Zachariah, peace be upon him, realized this glad tiding, he began to wonder about having a son from him after his old age. He said, ‘My Lord, how can I have a boy when old age has overtaken me and my wife is barren?’ He said, ‘Thus does God do what He wills.’ That is, God’s command is great, nothing is beyond His power, and no matter is too great for Him. He said, ‘My Lord, make for me a sign.’ That is, a sign by which I can prove that I have a son. He said, ‘Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days except by gesture.’ That is, a sign that you cannot speak, even though you are sound and healthy, as in His saying: three nights together. Then He commanded frequent remembrance, glorification, and praise in this state, so God the Almighty said: And remember your Lord often and glorify Him in the evening and the morning. Another part of expanding on this matter will come at the beginning of Surah Maryam, God willing.

3:43: This is a report from God the Most High about what the angels addressed to Mary, peace be upon her, about God’s command to them to do so, that God had chosen her, that is, He had selected her for her great worship, asceticism, honor, and purity from impurities and whispers, and He chose her a second time after another for her majesty over the women of the worlds. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar informed us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, regarding the words of God the Most High: Indeed, God has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds, he said: Abu Hurayrah used to narrate from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “The best women who rode camels are the women of Quraysh, tender to their children in their youth, and guardians of their husbands in their possessions. Mary, daughter of Imran, never rode a camel.” Only Muslim narrated it from this source, for he narrated it from Muhammad ibn Rafi’ and Abd ibn Hamid, both of them from Abd al-Razzaq with it, and Hisham ibn Urwah said, from his father, from Abdullah. Ibn Ja`far, on the authority of `Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘The best of its women is Mary, daughter of `Imran, and the best of its women is Khadija, daughter of Khuwaylid.’” They included it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Hisham, with a similar chain of transmission. Al-Tirmidhi said: Abu Bakr ibn Zanjawayh told us, `Abd al-Razzaq told us, Mu`ammar told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Sufficient for you from the women of the worlds are Mary, daughter of `Imran, Khadija, daughter of Khuwaylid, Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, and Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh. Al-Tirmidhi was the only one to narrate it and authenticated it. `Abdullah ibn Abi Ja`far al-Razi said, on the authority of his father, who said: Thabit al-Bunani used to narrate on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The best of the women of the worlds are four: Mary, daughter of `Imran, Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh, Khadija, daughter of Khuwaylid, and Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of God.’” Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from The path of Shu'bah, on the authority of Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, on the authority of his father, who said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'Many men have attained perfection, but none among women have attained perfection except three: Mary, daughter of Imran, Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh, and Khadijah, daughter of Khuwaylid. The superiority of Aisha over women is like the superiority of tharid over all other foods.'" Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Adam Al-Asqalani told us, Shu'bah told us, Amr ibn Murrah told us, I heard Murrah Al-Hamadani narrating on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari, who said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'Many men have attained perfection, but none among women have attained perfection except Mary, daughter of Imran, and Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh.'" It was narrated by all except Abu Dawud through various chains of narration on the authority of Shu'bah, and the wording of Al-Bukhari is: "Many men have attained perfection, but none among women have attained perfection except Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh, and Mary, daughter of Imran. The superiority of Aisha over women is like the superiority of tharid over all other foods." I have investigated the paths and wording of this hadith in the story of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, in our book, Al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya, and all praise and thanks be to God. Then God the Almighty informed us about the angels that they ordered them to worship frequently, be humble, bow, prostrate, and persevere in work, for what God wants for her of the matter that God has decreed and decided, which is a trial for her, and elevation in both worlds by what God has shown in her of His great power, as He created from her a son without a father, so God the Almighty said: O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, and prostrate and bow with those who bow. As for qunut, it is obedience in humility, as God the Almighty said: “Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. All are devoutly obedient to Him.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr ibn al-Harith told me, that Diraaj Abu al-Samh told him on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Every letter in the Qur’an in which qunut is mentioned is obedience. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ibn Lahi'ah on the authority of Darraj, and it contains something strange. Mujahid said: Mary, peace be upon her, would stand until her heels would swell. Qunut is the prolonged standing in prayer, meaning in compliance with the words of God the Most High: O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord. Al-Hasan said: It means worship your Lord, and prostrate and bow with those who bow. That is, be among them. Al-Awza'i said: She stood in her prayer niche, bowing, prostrating, and standing, until yellow water came down from her feet, may God be pleased with her and satisfy her. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned in her biography on the authority of Muhammad bin Yunus Al-Kadimi, and it contains something wrong: Ali bin Bahr bin Barri narrated to us, Al-Walid bin Muslim narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Awza'i, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, regarding His words: O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord and prostrate. He said: She prostrated until yellow water came down from her eyes. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya said: Al-Hasan bin Abdul Aziz told us, Damrah told us, on the authority of Ibn Shawdhab, who said: Mary, peace be upon her, used to bathe every night. Then God Almighty said to His Messenger after He informed him of the clear details of the matter: This is from the report of the unseen which We reveal to you, meaning, We relate it to you. And you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should be responsible for Mary, nor were you with them when they disputed, meaning, you were not with them, O Muhammad, to tell them directly about what happened. Rather, God informed you of that as if you were present and a witness to what happened when they drew lots concerning Mary as to which of them should be responsible for her, and that was because of their desire for reward. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, that he informed him on the authority of Ikrimah, and Abu Bakr on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Then she went out with her, meaning the mother of Mary, carrying Mary, in her rag to the sons of the priest, the son of Aaron, the brother of Moses, peace be upon them. He said: And on that day they were in the direction of the veil of the Kaaba in the Holy House, so she said to them: Here is this vowed woman, for I have set her free, and she is a female, and a menstruating woman does not enter the church, and I will not return her to my house, so they said: This is the daughter of our Imam, and Imran used to lead them in prayer, and he was the keeper of our sacrifice, so Zachariah said: Give her to me, for her maternal aunt is under me, so they said: We are not pleased, she is the daughter of our Imam, so that was when they drew lots for her with their pens with which they write the Torah, so Zachariah drew lots and took care of her. And Ikrimah also mentioned it, and Al-Suddi, Qatadah, Al-Riba’ bin Anas and others, and the hadith of some of them entered In some, they went to the Jordan River, and there they drew lots to throw their pens, and whoever of them remained in the flow of water would be its guarantor. So they threw their pens, and the water carried them away except for the pen of Zachariah, which remained. It is said that he went up, splitting the flow of water, and he was nevertheless their leader, their master, their scholar, their imam, and their prophet, may the prayers and peace of God be upon him and upon all the prophets.

He said: She prostrated until yellow water came down from her eyes. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya said: Al-Hasan bin Abdul Aziz told us, Damrah told us, on the authority of Ibn Shawdhab, who said: Mary, peace be upon her, used to bathe every night. Al-Tirmidhi said: Abu Bakr ibn Zanjawayh told us, `Abd al-Razzaq told us, Mu`ammar told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Sufficient for you from the women of the worlds are Mary, daughter of `Imran, Khadija, daughter of Khuwaylid, Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, and Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh. 3:46: This is good report from the angels to Mary, peace be upon her, that she will have a great son who will have great status. God the Almighty said: When the angels said, 'O Mary, indeed God gives you good tidings of a word from Him' meaning a son whose existence will be by a word from God, meaning He will say to him: Be, and he will be. This is the interpretation of His statement: Confirming a word from God as the majority mentioned based on what was previously explained. His name is the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary meaning he will be famous for this in this world, and the believers will know him by this. He was called the Messiah, some of the early Muslims said: because of his frequent travels. It was also said: because he had Messiah feet, without soles, and it was also said: because if he touched someone with a disability, he would be cured, by God's permission. His statement: Jesus, son of Mary is in reference to his mother, as he had no father. He will be honored in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near to God. That is, he will have honor and status with God in this world because of what God reveals to him of the Shari’ah and what He sends down to him of the Book and other things that God has granted him. And in the Hereafter, he will intercede with God for whomever He permits him to do so, and He will accept it from him, as is the case with his brothers of strong will. May God’s prayers and peace be upon him and them all. And His statement, And he will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity, that is, he will call to the worship of God alone, with no partner or associate, while he is young, as a miracle and a sign, and in his maturity when God reveals that to him, and he will be among the righteous, that is, in his words and deeds, he will have sound knowledge and righteous deeds. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: On the authority of Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Qusayt, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Shurahbil, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘No newborn spoke in his infancy except Jesus and the companion of Jurayj.’” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu al-Saqr Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Qaz’ah told us, al-Husayn, meaning al-Marwazi, told us, Jarir, meaning Ibn Hazim, told us, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “No one spoke in the cradle except three: Jesus, a boy who was in the time of Jurayj, and another boy.” So when she heard the angels’ glad tidings to her about that from God, the Almighty, she said in her supplication: My Lord, how can I have a child when no man has touched me? She said: How can this child come into being from me when I do not have a husband, nor do I intend to marry, and I am not unchaste, God forbid? The king said to her, on behalf of God Almighty, in answer to that question, Thus God creates what He wills. That is, God’s command is great and nothing is beyond His power. He stated here, He creates what He wills. He did not say, He does, as in the story of Zechariah. Rather, he stated here that He creates so that no doubt would remain for the falsifier. He confirmed that by saying, When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. That is, He does not delay anything, but rather He occurs immediately after the command without delay, as He said, And Our command is but one, like the twinkling of an eye. That is, We only command once, with no duality in it, so that thing is quick like the twinkling of an eye.

3:49: God Almighty says, informing about the completion of the angels' glad tidings to Mary about her son Jesus, peace be upon him: that God teaches him the Book and wisdom. It appears that what is meant by the Book here is writing, and wisdom is explained in Surat Al-Baqarah, and the Torah and the Gospel. The Torah is the Book that was sent down to Moses, son of Imran, and the Gospel that was sent down to Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon them. Jesus, peace be upon him, used to memorize this and that, and his saying: And a messenger to the Children of Israel means that he made him a messenger to the Children of Israel, saying to them Indeed, I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, that I create for you from clay, as it were, the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by God's permission. And that is what he used to do, he would form the shape of a bird from clay, then he would breathe into it and it would fly clearly by God's permission, the Almighty, who made this a miracle for him indicating that He sent him. And I heal the blind. It was said that he is the one who sees during the day but does not see at night, and the opposite was said. It was said: Al-A'sha. It was said: Al-A'mash. It was said: He is the one who is born blind, and this is more similar, because he is more eloquent in miracles and stronger in challenges. And the leper is well-known, And I bring the dead to life by God's permission. Many scholars said: God sent every prophet with what suited the people of his time. The prevailing thing in the time of Moses, peace be upon him, was magic and the glorification of magicians. So God sent him with a miracle that dazzled the eyes and confused every magician. When they were certain that it was from the Great, the Compeller, they submitted to Islam and became righteous servants of God. As for Jesus, peace be upon him, he was sent in the time of doctors and people of natural science, so he came to them with signs that no one could access except by being supported by the One who established the Sharia. So how could a doctor have the ability to bring inanimate objects to life, or to treat the blind and the leper, and to send someone who is in his grave, bound until the Day of Judgment? And likewise Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent in a time of eloquent and articulate people and the best of poets, so he brought them a book from God Almighty, if mankind and the jinn were to gather together to produce something like it, or ten surahs like it, or a surah like it, they would never be able to, even if they supported each other. And that is only because the speech of the Lord Almighty is never like the speech of creation. And His statement: And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses means I inform you of what one of you has eaten now, and what is stored for him in his house for tomorrow. Indeed in that meaning in all of that is a sign for you meaning of my truthfulness in what I have brought to you if you are believers * and confirming what came before me of the Torah meaning confirming and confirming it and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you in it is evidence that Jesus, peace be upon him, abrogated some of the law of the Torah, and this is the correct of the two opinions. Some scholars said: He did not abrogate anything of it, but rather made lawful for them some of what they were disputing about in error, so He revealed They have a cover for that, as He said in the other verse: And that I may make clear to you some of that over which you differ. And God knows best. Then He said: And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, meaning with an argument and proof of my truthfulness in what I say to you. “So fear God and obey me. Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him.” That is, I and you are equal in servitude to Him, submission and humility to Him. This is a straight path.

3:53: God the Almighty says: So when Jesus perceived meaning he sensed from them the determination to disbelieve and continue in misguidance, "he said: Who are my helpers for God?" Mujahid said: Who will follow me to God. Sufyan al-Thawri and others said: Who are my helpers with God? Mujahid said: Closest. It appears that he meant who are my helpers in calling to God? Just as "the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say during the Hajj seasons before he emigrated: Who will shelter me so that I may convey the words of my Lord? For the Quraysh prevented me from conveying the words of my Lord until he found the helpers, so they sheltered him and supported him and he emigrated to them, so they comforted him and protected him from the black and the red, may God be pleased with them and satisfy them." Thus, Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, was assigned to a group of the Children of Israel, so they believed in him, supported him, aided him, and followed the light that was sent down with him. For this reason, God Almighty said, informing about them, “The disciples said, ‘We are supporters of God. We have believed in God, and bear witness that we are Muslims. Our Lord, we have believed in what You revealed and have followed the Messenger, so register us among the witnesses.’” It was said that the disciples were short-skinned, and it was said that they were called that because of the whiteness of their clothes, and it was said that they were hunters. The correct view is that the Helper disciple, as proven in the two Sahihs, is that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, summoned the people on the Day of the Confederates, Az-Zubayr volunteered, then he summoned them, and Az-Zubayr, may God be pleased with him, volunteered, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every prophet has a disciple, and my disciple is Az-Zubayr. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Waki’ told us, Isra’il told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding his statement, Then write us down with the witnesses, he said: With the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is a good chain of transmission. Then the Almighty said, informing about the leaders of the Children of Israel, regarding their intention to kill Jesus, peace be upon him, and their desire to harm him and crucify him when they conspired against him and slandered him to the king of that time, and he was an unbeliever, that here is a man who misleads people and turns them away from obeying the king and corrupts the subjects and separates father from son, and other things that they hung around their necks and accused him of as lies, and that he was born of fornication until they provoked the anger of the king, so he sent someone to search for him to take him and crucify him and torture him, and when they surrounded his house and thought that they had captured him, God Almighty saved him from among them and raised him from the window of that house to the heavens, and God cast his likeness on a man who was with him in the house, and when those entered they thought he was Jesus in the darkness of the night, so they took him and humiliated him and crucified him, and they put thorns on his head, and this was from God’s deception with them, for He saved His Prophet and raised him from among them and left them in their misguidance, thinking that they had They achieved their goal, but God placed in their hearts cruelty and stubbornness towards the truth, which remained with them, and He caused them to be humiliated and not leave them until the Day of Judgment. That is why God Almighty said: And they plotted, and God plotted, and God is the best of plotters.

3:56: The commentators differed regarding the words of God the Almighty: Indeed, I will take you and raise you up to Me. Qatada and others said: This is from the first and last, meaning that I will raise you up to Me and take you up, meaning after that. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: I will take you up, meaning I will cause you to die. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, who said: God caused him to die three hours at the beginning of the day when He raised him up to Me. Ibn Ishaq said: The Christians claim that God caused him to die for seven hours, then brought him back to life. Ishaq bin Bishr said, on the authority of Idris, on the authority of Wahb: God caused him to die for three days, then resurrected him, then raised him up. Matar al-Warraq said: I will cause you to die from this world, but it is not a death, and Ibn Jarir said the same: He caused him to die is he raised him up. The majority said: What is meant by death here is sleep, as God the Almighty said: And it is He who takes you by night (al-Baqarah 2:17). God the Almighty said: God takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die during their sleep [al-Anbiya’], and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “used to say when he awoke from sleep: ‘Praise be to God who has given us life after He caused us to die’” [al-Hadith]. God the Almighty said: “And because of their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander * And their saying, ‘We killed the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, the Messenger of God.’ But they killed him not, nor crucified him, but it appeared so to them. And those who differ therein are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumptions. And they killed him not, for certain. Rather, God raised him up to Himself. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise. * And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will believe in him before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them.” [al-Anbiya’] The pronoun in His statement before his death refers to Jesus, peace be upon him, meaning there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will believe in Jesus before Jesus’ death, and that is when he descends to earth before the Day of Resurrection, as will be explained. At that time, all the People of the Scripture will believe in him, because he imposes the jizya and does not accept anything but Islam. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman told us, Abdullah ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, al-Rabi` ibn Anas told us, on the authority of al-Hasan that he said regarding the words of God Almighty: I will cause you to die meaning the death of a dream, God raised him up in his dream. Al-Hasan said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the Jews: Jesus did not die, and he will return to you before the Day of Resurrection.” And the words of God Almighty: And purify you from those who disbelieve meaning by raising you up to heaven, and make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. And this is how it happened, for when God raised the Messiah, peace be upon him, to heaven, his companions split into sects after him. Some of them believed in what God sent him with, that he was the servant and messenger of God and the son of His female servant, and some of them went to extremes and made him the son of God, and others said: He is God, and still others said: He is the third of three. God has narrated their statements in the Qur’an and responded to each group, so they continued in that for nearly three hundred years, then a king from the Greek kings appeared to them called Constantine, so he entered the religion of Christianity, it was said: a trick to corrupt it, because he was a philosopher, and it was said: out of ignorance on his part, except that he changed the religion of Christ for them and distorted it, and added to it and subtracted from it, and laws were established for him, and the great trust which is the contemptible betrayal, and pork was permitted in his time, and they reached the East for him, and depicted for him churches, temples and monasteries, and he increased their fasting by ten days because of a sin he committed, as they claim, and the religion of Christ became the religion of Constantine, except that he built for them churches, temples, monasteries and monasteries more than twelve thousand temples, and he built the city attributed to him, and the royal group followed him, and in all of this they were victorious over the Jews, God supported them against them, because they were closer to the truth than them, even though all of them were infidels upon them, the curses of God, so when God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, it was Whoever believes in him believes in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers in the true manner. They were the followers of every prophet on the face of the earth, since they believed in the Messenger, the unlettered Arab prophet, the Seal of the Messengers and the Master of the children of Adam in general, who called them to believe in all the truth. They were more deserving of every prophet than his nation, who claimed to be on his religion and path, with what they had distorted and changed. Then, if none of that had happened, God would have abrogated the law of all the messengers with what God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the true religion that will not be changed or altered until the Day of Judgment, and will continue to exist, victorious, and apparent over every religion. For this reason, God opened for his companions the easts and wests of the earth, and they crossed all the kingdoms, and all the countries submitted to them, and they defeated Khosrau, and conquered Caesar and took their treasures, and they were spent in the way of God, as their prophet informed them of that from their Lord, the Almighty, in His saying: “God has promised those who believe among you and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, just as He made those before them successors, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has revealed to them.” He was pleased with them and will surely substitute for them, after their fear, security, they will worship Me, not associating anything with Me. This is why, since they were the true believers in Christ, they took over the lands of the Levant from the Christians and forced them to flee to the Romans, so they fled to their city of Constantinople, and Islam and its people will remain above them until the Day of Resurrection. The truthful and trustworthy, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed his nation that the last of them will conquer Constantinople and take possession of its wealth, and will kill the Romans in a very great slaughter, the likes of which people have never seen nor will they see anything like it after it. I have collected this in a separate section, and for this reason God Almighty said: “And I will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ. As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.” And He did the same with those Jews who disbelieved in Christ or exaggerated or praised him from among the Christians. He punished them in this world by killing and capturing, and seizing wealth and removing hands from the kingdoms. In the Hereafter, their punishment will be more severe and more difficult. And they will have no protector from God. “And as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will pay them their rewards in full,” meaning in this world and the Hereafter, in this world with victory and triumph, and in the Hereafter with the highest gardens. And God does not love the wrongdoers. Then the Almighty said: This is what We recite to you of the verses and the wise remembrance. That is, this is what We have narrated to you, O Muhammad, regarding the matter of Jesus, the beginning of his birth and the manner of his affair, and it is among what the Almighty said and revealed to you and sent down to you from the Preserved Tablet, so there is no doubt or suspicion in it, as the Almighty said in Surat Maryam 19:“That is Jesus, the son of Mary - the word of truth about which they are in dispute. It is not for God to take a son. Glory be to Him! When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is.” And here the Almighty said:

God has narrated their statements in the Qur’an and responded to each group, so they continued in that for nearly three hundred years, then a king from the Greek kings appeared to them called Constantine, so he entered the religion of Christianity, it was said: a trick to corrupt it, because he was a philosopher, and it was said: out of ignorance on his part, except that he changed the religion of Christ for them and distorted it, and added to it and subtracted from it, and laws were established for him, and the great trust which is the contemptible betrayal, and pork was permitted in his time, and they reached the East for him, and depicted for him churches, temples and monasteries, and he increased their fasting by ten days because of a sin he committed, as they claim, and the religion of Christ became the religion of Constantine, except that he built for them churches, temples, monasteries and monasteries more than twelve thousand temples, and he built the city attributed to him, and the royal group followed him, and in all of this they were victorious over the Jews, God supported them against them, because they were closer to the truth than them, even though all of them were infidels upon them, the curses of God, so when God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, it was Whoever believes in him believes in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers in the true manner. They were the followers of every prophet on the face of the earth, since they believed in the Messenger, the unlettered Arab prophet, the Seal of the Messengers and the Master of the children of Adam in general, who called them to believe in all the truth. They were more deserving of every prophet than his nation, who claimed to be on his religion and path, with what they had distorted and changed. Then, if none of that had happened, God would have abrogated the law of all the messengers with what God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the true religion that will not be changed or altered until the Day of Judgment, and will continue to exist, victorious, and apparent over every religion. For this reason, God opened for his companions the easts and wests of the earth, and they crossed all the kingdoms, and all the countries submitted to them, and they defeated Khosrau, and conquered Caesar and took their treasures, and they were spent in the way of God, as their prophet informed them of that from their Lord, the Almighty, in His saying: “God has promised those who believe among you and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, just as He made those before them successors, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has revealed to them.” He was pleased with them and will surely substitute for them, after their fear, security, they will worship Me, not associating anything with Me. This is why, since they were the true believers in Christ, they took over the lands of the Levant from the Christians and forced them to flee to the Romans, so they fled to their city of Constantinople, and Islam and its people will remain above them until the Day of Resurrection. The truthful and trustworthy, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed his nation that the last of them will conquer Constantinople and take possession of its wealth, and will kill the Romans in a very great slaughter, the likes of which people have never seen nor will they see anything like it after it. I have collected this in a separate section, and for this reason God Almighty said: “And I will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ. As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.” And He did the same with those Jews who disbelieved in Christ or exaggerated or praised him from among the Christians. He punished them in this world by killing and capturing, and seizing wealth and removing hands from the kingdoms. In the Hereafter, their punishment will be more severe and more difficult. And they will have no protector from God. “And as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will pay them their rewards in full,” meaning in this world and the Hereafter, in this world with victory and triumph, and in the Hereafter with the highest gardens. And God does not love the wrongdoers. Then the Almighty said: This is what We recite to you of the verses and the wise remembrance. That is, this is what We have narrated to you, O Muhammad, regarding the matter of Jesus, the beginning of his birth and the manner of his affair, and it is among what the Almighty said and revealed to you and sent down to you from the Preserved Tablet, so there is no doubt or suspicion in it, as the Almighty said in Surat Maryam 19:“That is Jesus, the son of Mary - the word of truth about which they are in dispute. It is not for God to take a son. Glory be to Him! When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is.” And here the Almighty said:
3:58: The commentators differed regarding the words of God the Almighty: Indeed, I will take you and raise you up to Me. Qatada and others said: This is from the first and last, meaning that I will raise you up to Me and take you up, meaning after that. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: I will take you up, meaning I will cause you to die. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, who said: God caused him to die three hours at the beginning of the day when He raised him up to Me. Ibn Ishaq said: The Christians claim that God caused him to die for seven hours, then brought him back to life. Ishaq bin Bishr said, on the authority of Idris, on the authority of Wahb: God caused him to die for three days, then resurrected him, then raised him up. Matar al-Warraq said: I will cause you to die from this world, but it is not a death, and Ibn Jarir said the same: He caused him to die is he raised him up. The majority said: What is meant by death here is sleep, as God the Almighty said: And it is He who takes you by night (al-Baqarah 2:17). God the Almighty said: God takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die during their sleep [al-Anbiya’], and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “used to say when he awoke from sleep: ‘Praise be to God who has given us life after He caused us to die’” [al-Hadith]. God the Almighty said: “And because of their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander * And their saying, ‘We killed the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, the Messenger of God.’ But they killed him not, nor crucified him, but it appeared so to them. And those who differ therein are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumptions. And they killed him not, for certain. Rather, God raised him up to Himself. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise. * And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will believe in him before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them.” [al-Anbiya’] The pronoun in His statement before his death refers to Jesus, peace be upon him, meaning there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will believe in Jesus before Jesus’ death, and that is when he descends to earth before the Day of Resurrection, as will be explained. At that time, all the People of the Scripture will believe in him, because he imposes the jizya and does not accept anything but Islam. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman told us, Abdullah ibn Abi Ja`far told us, on the authority of his father, al-Rabi` ibn Anas told us, on the authority of al-Hasan that he said regarding the words of God Almighty: I will cause you to die meaning the death of a dream, God raised him up in his dream. Al-Hasan said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the Jews: Jesus did not die, and he will return to you before the Day of Resurrection.” And the words of God Almighty: And purify you from those who disbelieve meaning by raising you up to heaven, and make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. 3:59: The Almighty says: The likeness of Jesus before God in God's power, as He created him without a father, is like the likeness of Adam, as He created him without a father or mother, but He created him from dust and then said to him, 'Be,' and he was. So the One who created Adam without a father is able to create Jesus by a fortiori and more appropriate way, and if it is permissible to claim sonship in Jesus because he was created without a father, then it is permissible in Adam by a fortiori way, and it is known by consensus that this is false, so claiming it in Jesus is even more false and more clearly corrupt, but the Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, wanted to show His power to His creation when He created Adam from neither a male nor a female, and created Eve from a male without a female, and created Jesus from a female without a male, just as He created the rest of creation from a male and a female, and for this reason the Almighty said in Surah Maryam, And We will make him a sign for mankind and He said here, The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters meaning this is the true statement about Jesus from which there is no escape and no truth other than it, and what is after the truth except misguidance. Then the Almighty said, commanding His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to challenge those who opposed the truth regarding the matter of Jesus after the revelation of the proof: “But whoever disputes with you concerning him after what has come to you of knowledge, say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us supplicate earnestly, and invoke the curse of God upon the liars, whether from us or from you.” The reason for the revelation of this Mubahala and the ones before it from the beginning of the Surah to here about the delegation of Najran is that when the Christians came and began to argue about Jesus and claim what they claim about his sonship and divinity, God revealed the beginning of this Surah in response to them. Ibn Ishaq said in his famous biography and others: A delegation of Christians from Najran came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sixty riders, among them fourteen men from their nobles to whom their affairs would be referred, and they are: Al-Aqib, whose name is Abdul-Masih; Al-Sayyid, who is Al-Ayham; Abu Haritha bin Alqamah, the brother of Bakr bin Wa’il; Uways bin Al-Harith; Zaid; Qais; Yazid and his Nabih; Khuwaylid; Amr; Khalid; Abdullah; and Yahanis. The affairs of these people would be referred to three of them, and they are Al-Aqib, who was the leader of the people and had their opinion and their advisor, and they would not act except according to his opinion; Al-Sayyid, who was their scholar and the owner of their travels and their community; and Abu Haritha bin Alqamah, who was their bishop. Their rabbi, imam and head of their schools, was a man from the Arabs of Banu Bakr ibn Wa’il, but he converted to Christianity and the Romans and their kings honored him and built churches for him and served him because they knew of his steadfastness in their religion. He knew the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, his description and his status from what he learned from the previous books, but his ignorance led him to continue in Christianity because of what he saw of his veneration there and his prestige among its people. Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Ja’far ibn al-Zubayr told me, he said: They came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina, and entered his mosque when he prayed the afternoon prayer, wearing the clothes of the rabbis, cloaks and robes as beautiful as the men of Banu al-Harith ibn Ka’b. He said: Those of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who saw them said: We have not seen a delegation like them after them. And the time for their prayer came, so they stood in the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Leave them and pray facing the east. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke to Abu Haritha ibn Alqamah and Al-Aqib Abd al-Rahman from among them. Christ and Mr. Ayham, who are Christians of the religion of the king, although their matter differs, say: He is God, and they say: He is the son of God, and they say: He is the third of three. God is far above what they say. And so is the saying of the Christians, for they argue in their saying that He is God, that He used to bring the dead back to life, and heal the blind, the lepers, and those with diseases, and tell the unseen, and create from clay the form of a bird, then breathe into it and it becomes a bird, and all of that is by the command of God. And that God may make him a sign for the people, and they argue for their saying that he is the son of God, saying: He had no father who knew, and he spoke in the cradle with something that no one from the children of Adam had heard before him, and they argue for their saying that he is the third of three with the saying of God the Most High: We did, We commanded, We created, and We decreed, and they say: If he were one, he would not have said anything except I did, I commanded, I decreed, and I created, but he and Jesus and Mary - God is exalted and sanctified and is far above what the wrongdoers and deniers say - and in all of that from their saying: The Qur’an has been revealed, so when the two rabbis spoke to him, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Become Muslims, they said: We have already become Muslims, he said: You have not become Muslims, so become Muslims. They said: Yes, we became Muslims before you. He said: You have lied, what prevents you from becoming Muslims is your calling a son for God, your worship of the cross, and your eating pork. They said: Who is his father, O Muhammad? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent about them and did not answer them. Then God revealed about that of their saying and the difference in their affair the beginning of Surat Al Imran up to eighty-some verses of it. Then Ibn Ishaq spoke about its interpretation until he said: When the report from God and the final judgment between Him and them came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he ordered what he ordered of cursing them if they rejected that to him, he called them to that, and they said: O Abu al-Qasim, let us consider our affair and then we will come to you with what we want to do with what you called us to. Then they turned away from him, then they were alone with the one who came after, and that was their opinion. They said: O Abd al-Masih, what do you think? He said: By God, O Christians, you have known that Muhammad is a prophet sent, and he has brought you the final word about your companion. You have known that no people have ever cursed a prophet, and their elders remained, nor their young ones grew up. If you do this, it will be your extermination. If you insist on following your religion and remaining as you say about your companion, then say farewell to the man and return to your country. They came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Abu al-Qasim, we have decided not to curse you and leave you in your religion and return to our religion. But send with us a man from your companions whom you are pleased with to judge between us in matters in which we differed regarding our wealth, for you are content with us. Muhammad ibn Ja`far said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Come to me in the evening, and I will send with you the strong and trustworthy one. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, used to say: I have never loved leadership as much as I loved it on that day, hoping that I would be its owner. I went to the noon prayer in the early morning. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the noon prayer, he said the greeting of peace and then looked away. “I began to stretch out my legs for him to see me, but he kept looking until he saw Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah, so he called him and said: ‘Go out with them and judge between them with justice in what they differed over.’” ‘Umar said: So Abu Ubaidah, may God be pleased with him, went with her. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of ‘Asim ibn ‘Umar ibn Qatada, on the authority of Mahmud ibn Labid, on the authority of Rafi’ ibn Khadij: That the delegation of the people of Najran came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said about the nobles: They were twelve, and he mentioned the rest of it in a longer context than this, and other additions. Al-Bukhari said: Abbas bin Al-Hussein told us, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Silah bin Zafar, on the authority of Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “Al-Aqib and Al-Sayyid, the two rulers of Najran, came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanting to perform the Li’an. He said: One of them said to the other: Do not do it, for by God, if he is a prophet and we perform the Li’an, neither we nor our descendants after us will succeed. They said: We will give you what you asked of us, but send with us a trustworthy man, and do not send with us anyone but a trustworthy person. He said: I will send with you a trustworthy man, truly trustworthy. The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were eager to do so, so he said: Get up, O Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah. When he got up, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is the trustworthy one of this nation.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah through various chains of narration on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Sabi’i on the authority of Silah, on the authority of Hudhayfah, in a similar manner. Ahmad, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Israel on the authority of Abu Ishaq. On the authority of Silah, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, similarly. Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Walid told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, He said, ‘Every nation has a trustee, and the trustee of this nation is Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah.’ Imam Ahmad said: Ismail ibn Yazid al-Ruqi Abu Yazid told us, Furat told us, on the authority of `Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, on the authority of `Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: Abu Jahl, may God curse him, said, ‘If I see Muhammad praying at the Ka`bah, I will come to him and step on his neck.’ He said: ‘If he did, the angels would seize him in person. If the Jews wished for death, they would die and see their seats in Hell. If those who challenged the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to mubahala went out, they would return without finding any wealth or family.’ Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of `Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Mu`ammar, on the authority of `Abd al-Karim, on its authority. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dala’il al-Nubuwwah a very long story of the Najran delegation, and let us mention it, for it contains many benefits, and it contains strangeness, and it is appropriate for this occasion. Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah al-Hafiz and Abu Saeed Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Fadl told us: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya’qub told us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar told us, Yunus ibn Bakir told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Abd Yusoo’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, Yunus said - and he was a Christian who converted to Islam - that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to the people of Najran before the Book of Solomon was revealed to him: “In the name of the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, from Muhammad the Prophet, the Messenger of God, to the Bishop of Najran and the people of Najran, you have converted to Islam, for I praise to you the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. As for what follows, I call you to the worship of God from the worship of servants, and I call you to the guardianship of God from the guardianship of servants. If you refuse, then pay the jizya, and if you refuse, then I have declared war on you, and peace.” When the bishop received the letter and read it, he was horrified by it and was extremely frightened. He sent for a man from Najran called Shurahbil ibn Wada’ah, who was from Hamdan. No one was called before him when a difficult matter arose, neither al-Ayham, nor al-Sayyid, nor al-Aqib. So the bishop gave the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Shurahbil, who read it. The bishop said: O Abu Maryam, what do you think? Shurahbil said: I know what God promised Abraham in the descendants of Ishmael of prophethood, so how can I believe that this is that man? I have no opinion in the matter of prophethood, and if it were in a worldly matter I would have advised you about it with my opinion and made an effort for you. The bishop said: Step aside and sit down. Shurahbil stepped aside and sat to one side. The bishop sent to a man from Najran called Abdullah bin Shurahbil, who was from Dhi Asbah of Himyar. He read the letter to him and asked him about his opinion on it. He said to him the same as Shurahbil had said. The bishop said to him: Step aside and sit down. Abdullah stepped aside and sat to one side. The bishop sent to a man from Najran called Jabbar bin Fayd from Banu al-Harith bin Ka’b, one of Banu al-Hamas. He read the letter to him and asked him about his opinion on it. He said to him the same as Shurahbil and Abdullah had said, so the bishop ordered him to step aside and sit aside. When they all agreed on that statement, the bishop ordered the bell to be rung and the fires and sackcloth were raised in the monasteries. This is what they used to do when they were frightened during the day, and when they were frightened at night, they would ring the bell and the fires were raised in the monasteries. When the bell was rung and the sackcloth was raised, the people of the valley, both above and below, gathered together. The length of the valley is a day’s journey for a fast rider, and it contains seventy-three villages and one hundred and twenty thousand fighters. He read to them the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked them about their opinion on it. The opinion of the people of opinion among them was unanimous that they should send Shurahbil ibn Wada’ah al-Hamdani, Abdullah ibn Shurahbil al-Asbahi, and Jabbar ibn Fayd al-Harithi to bring them report of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The delegation set out until they were in Medina, where they removed their travel clothes and put on their garments made of silk and gold rings. Then they set out until they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and greeted him, but he did not respond to them. They remained silent for a long day, but he did not speak to them, and they were wearing those garments and gold rings. Then they set out following Uthman ibn Affan and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, who were acquainted with them. They found them among some of the Muhajireen and Ansar in a gathering. They said: O Uthman and Abd al-Rahman, your Prophet wrote us a letter, so we came to him in response. We came to him and greeted him. He did not return our greetings, and we kept talking to him for a long day, until we were exhausted from talking to him. What do you think, should we go back? They said to Ali ibn Abi Talib, who was with the al-Nas 114:What do you think, O Abu al-Hasan, about these people? Then Ali said to Uthman and Abd al-Rahman: I think they should put off their clothes and rings, and wear their travelling clothes, then return to him. So they did and greeted him, and he returned their greeting. Then he said: By Him Who sent me with the truth, they came to me the first time and Iblis was with them. Then he asked them, and they kept asking him and them until they said to him: What do you say about Jesus? We are returning to our people and we are Christians. If you are a prophet, we would be pleased to hear what you say about him? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have nothing about him today, so stay until I tell you what my Lord says to me about Jesus. Then the next morning God revealed this verse: “Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is as that of Adam. He created him from dust and then said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was. The truth is from your Lord, so be not among the doubters. But whoever disputes with you about him after what has come to you of knowledge, say: ‘Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us supplicate earnestly and invoke the curse of God upon the liars.’” But they refused to acknowledge it. Thus, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came the next day after he had informed them of the report, he came with al-Hasan and al-Husayn in his tent, and Fatima was walking behind him to curse, and he had several wives at that time. Shurahbil said to his two companions: You know that when the top and bottom of a valley meet, they will not return or depart except according to my opinion, and by God I see a heavy matter. By God, if this man is a king sent, then we will be the first Arabs to stab him in the eyes and reject his command. It will not go away from his chest or the chests of his companions until they afflict us with a calamity, and we are the closest Arabs to them in neighborliness. And if this man is a prophet sent, then we will curse him, and there will not remain from us on the face of the earth a hair or a nail except that it will perish. His two companions said to him: What is the opinion, O Abu Maryam? He said: I see that I should rule on it, for I see a man who never rules excessively. They said to him: You and that. Shurahbil met the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: I have seen something better than your cursing. He said: What is it? He said: Your ruling today until night and your night until morning, so whatever you rule on us is permissible. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Is there someone behind you who will curse you? Shurahbil said: Ask my companion. So he asked them and they said: It does not come to the valley and does not proceed except from Shurahbil’s opinion. Then the Almighty said, commanding His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to challenge those who opposed the truth regarding the matter of Jesus after the revelation of the proof: “But whoever disputes with you concerning him after what has come to you of knowledge, say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us supplicate earnestly, and invoke the curse of God upon the liars, whether from us or from you.” The reason for the revelation of this Mubahala and the ones before it from the beginning of the Surah to here about the delegation of Najran is that when the Christians came and began to argue about Jesus and claim what they claim about his sonship and divinity, God revealed the beginning of this Surah in response to them. Ibn Ishaq said in his famous biography and others: A delegation of Christians from Najran came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sixty riders, among them fourteen men from their nobles to whom their affairs would be referred, and they are: Al-Aqib, whose name is Abdul-Masih; Al-Sayyid, who is Al-Ayham; Abu Haritha bin Alqamah, the brother of Bakr bin Wa’il; Uways bin Al-Harith; Zaid; Qais; Yazid and his Nabih; Khuwaylid; Amr; Khalid; Abdullah; and Yahanis. The affairs of these people would be referred to three of them, and they are Al-Aqib, who was the leader of the people and had their opinion and their advisor, and they would not act except according to his opinion; Al-Sayyid, who was their scholar and the owner of their travels and their community; and Abu Haritha bin Alqamah, who was their bishop. Their rabbi, imam and head of their schools, was a man from the Arabs of Banu Bakr ibn Wa’il, but he converted to Christianity and the Romans and their kings honored him and built churches for him and served him because they knew of his steadfastness in their religion. He knew the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, his description and his status from what he learned from the previous books, but his ignorance led him to continue in Christianity because of what he saw of his veneration there and his prestige among its people. Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Ja’far ibn al-Zubayr told me, he said: They came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina, and entered his mosque when he prayed the afternoon prayer, wearing the clothes of the rabbis, cloaks and robes as beautiful as the men of Banu al-Harith ibn Ka’b. He said: Those of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who saw them said: We have not seen a delegation like them after them. And the time for their prayer came, so they stood in the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Leave them and pray facing the east. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke to Abu Haritha ibn Alqamah and Al-Aqib Abd al-Rahman from among them. Christ and Mr. Ayham, who are Christians of the religion of the king, although their matter differs, say: He is God, and they say: He is the son of God, and they say: He is the third of three. God is far above what they say. And so is the saying of the Christians, for they argue in their saying that He is God, that He used to bring the dead back to life, and heal the blind, the lepers, and those with diseases, and tell the unseen, and create from clay the form of a bird, then breathe into it and it becomes a bird, and all of that is by the command of God. And that God may make him a sign for the people, and they argue for their saying that he is the son of God, saying: He had no father who knew, and he spoke in the cradle with something that no one from the children of Adam had heard before him, and they argue for their saying that he is the third of three with the saying of God the Most High: We did, We commanded, We created, and We decreed, and they say: If he were one, he would not have said anything except I did, I commanded, I decreed, and I created, but he and Jesus and Mary - God is exalted and sanctified and is far above what the wrongdoers and deniers say - and in all of that from their saying: The Qur’an has been revealed, so when the two rabbis spoke to him, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Become Muslims, they said: We have already become Muslims, he said: You have not become Muslims, so become Muslims. They said: Yes, we became Muslims before you. He said: You have lied, what prevents you from becoming Muslims is your calling a son for God, your worship of the cross, and your eating pork. They said: Who is his father, O Muhammad? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent about them and did not answer them. Then God revealed about that of their saying and the difference in their affair the beginning of Surat Al Imran up to eighty-some verses of it. Then Ibn Ishaq spoke about its interpretation until he said: When the report from God and the final judgment between Him and them came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he ordered what he ordered of cursing them if they rejected that to him, he called them to that, and they said: O Abu al-Qasim, let us consider our affair and then we will come to you with what we want to do with what you called us to. Then they turned away from him, then they were alone with the one who came after, and that was their opinion. They said: O Abd al-Masih, what do you think? He said: By God, O Christians, you have known that Muhammad is a prophet sent, and he has brought you the final word about your companion. You have known that no people have ever cursed a prophet, and their elders remained, nor their young ones grew up. If you do this, it will be your extermination. If you insist on following your religion and remaining as you say about your companion, then say farewell to the man and return to your country. They came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Abu al-Qasim, we have decided not to curse you and leave you in your religion and return to our religion. But send with us a man from your companions whom you are pleased with to judge between us in matters in which we differed regarding our wealth, for you are content with us. Muhammad ibn Ja`far said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Come to me in the evening, and I will send with you the strong and trustworthy one. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, used to say: I have never loved leadership as much as I loved it on that day, hoping that I would be its owner. I went to the noon prayer in the early morning. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the noon prayer, he said the greeting of peace and then looked away. “I began to stretch out my legs for him to see me, but he kept looking until he saw Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah, so he called him and said: ‘Go out with them and judge between them with justice in what they differed over.’” ‘Umar said: So Abu Ubaidah, may God be pleased with him, went with her. Al-Bukhari said: Abbas bin Al-Hussein told us, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Silah bin Zafar, on the authority of Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “Al-Aqib and Al-Sayyid, the two rulers of Najran, came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanting to perform the Li’an. He said: One of them said to the other: Do not do it, for by God, if he is a prophet and we perform the Li’an, neither we nor our descendants after us will succeed. They said: We will give you what you asked of us, but send with us a trustworthy man, and do not send with us anyone but a trustworthy person. He said: I will send with you a trustworthy man, truly trustworthy. The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were eager to do so, so he said: Get up, O Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah. When he got up, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is the trustworthy one of this nation.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah through various chains of narration on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Sabi’i on the authority of Silah, on the authority of Hudhayfah, in a similar manner. Ahmad, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Israel on the authority of Abu Ishaq. On the authority of Silah, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, similarly. Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Walid told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, He said, ‘Every nation has a trustee, and the trustee of this nation is Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah.’ Imam Ahmad said: Ismail ibn Yazid al-Ruqi Abu Yazid told us, Furat told us, on the authority of `Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, on the authority of `Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: Abu Jahl, may God curse him, said, ‘If I see Muhammad praying at the Ka`bah, I will come to him and step on his neck.’ He said: ‘If he did, the angels would seize him in person. If the Jews wished for death, they would die and see their seats in Hell. If those who challenged the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to mubahala went out, they would return without finding any wealth or family.’ Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of `Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Mu`ammar, on the authority of `Abd al-Karim, on its authority. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dala’il al-Nubuwwah a very long story of the Najran delegation, and let us mention it, for it contains many benefits, and it contains strangeness, and it is appropriate for this occasion. Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah al-Hafiz and Abu Saeed Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Fadl told us: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya’qub told us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar told us, Yunus ibn Bakir told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Abd Yusoo’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, Yunus said - and he was a Christian who converted to Islam - that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to the people of Najran before the Book of Solomon was revealed to him: “In the name of the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, from Muhammad the Prophet, the Messenger of God, to the Bishop of Najran and the people of Najran, you have converted to Islam, for I praise to you the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. As for what follows, I call you to the worship of God from the worship of servants, and I call you to the guardianship of God from the guardianship of servants. If you refuse, then pay the jizya, and if you refuse, then I have declared war on you, and peace.” When the bishop received the letter and read it, he was horrified by it and was extremely frightened. He sent for a man from Najran called Shurahbil ibn Wada’ah, who was from Hamdan. No one was called before him when a difficult matter arose, neither al-Ayham, nor al-Sayyid, nor al-Aqib. So the bishop gave the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Shurahbil, who read it. The bishop said: O Abu Maryam, what do you think? Shurahbil said: I know what God promised Abraham in the descendants of Ishmael of prophethood, so how can I believe that this is that man? I have no opinion in the matter of prophethood, and if it were in a worldly matter I would have advised you about it with my opinion and made an effort for you. The bishop said: Step aside and sit down. Shurahbil stepped aside and sat to one side. The bishop sent to a man from Najran called Abdullah bin Shurahbil, who was from Dhi Asbah of Himyar. He read the letter to him and asked him about his opinion on it. He said to him the same as Shurahbil had said. The bishop said to him: Step aside and sit down. Abdullah stepped aside and sat to one side. The bishop sent to a man from Najran called Jabbar bin Fayd from Banu al-Harith bin Ka’b, one of Banu al-Hamas. He read the letter to him and asked him about his opinion on it. He said to him the same as Shurahbil and Abdullah had said, so the bishop ordered him to step aside and sit aside. When they all agreed on that statement, the bishop ordered the bell to be rung and the fires and sackcloth were raised in the monasteries. This is what they used to do when they were frightened during the day, and when they were frightened at night, they would ring the bell and the fires were raised in the monasteries. When the bell was rung and the sackcloth was raised, the people of the valley, both above and below, gathered together. The length of the valley is a day’s journey for a fast rider, and it contains seventy-three villages and one hundred and twenty thousand fighters. He read to them the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked them about their opinion on it. The opinion of the people of opinion among them was unanimous that they should send Shurahbil ibn Wada’ah al-Hamdani, Abdullah ibn Shurahbil al-Asbahi, and Jabbar ibn Fayd al-Harithi to bring them report of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The delegation set out until they were in Medina, where they removed their travel clothes and put on their garments made of silk and gold rings. Then they set out until they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and greeted him, but he did not respond to them. They remained silent for a long day, but he did not speak to them, and they were wearing those garments and gold rings. Then they set out following Uthman ibn Affan and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, who were acquainted with them. They found them among some of the Muhajireen and Ansar in a gathering. They said: O Uthman and Abd al-Rahman, your Prophet wrote us a letter, so we came to him in response. We came to him and greeted him. He did not return our greetings, and we kept talking to him for a long day, until we were exhausted from talking to him. What do you think, should we go back? They said to Ali ibn Abi Talib, who was with the al-Nas 114:What do you think, O Abu al-Hasan, about these people? Then Ali said to Uthman and Abd al-Rahman: I think they should put off their clothes and rings, and wear their travelling clothes, then return to him. So they did and greeted him, and he returned their greeting. Then he said: By Him Who sent me with the truth, they came to me the first time and Iblis was with them. Then he asked them, and they kept asking him and them until they said to him: What do you say about Jesus? We are returning to our people and we are Christians. If you are a prophet, we would be pleased to hear what you say about him? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have nothing about him today, so stay until I tell you what my Lord says to me about Jesus. Shurahbil said to his two companions: You know that when the top and bottom of a valley meet, they will not return or depart except according to my opinion, and by God I see a heavy matter.
