Christ and Mr. Ayham, who are Christians of the religion of the king, although their matter differs, say: He is God, and they say: He is the son of God, and they say: He is the third of three. God is far above what they say. And so is the saying of the Christians, for they argue in their saying that He is God, that He used to bring the dead back to life, and heal the blind, the lepers, and those with diseases, and tell the unseen, and create from clay the form of a bird, then breathe into it and it becomes a bird, and all of that is by the command of God. And that God may make him a sign for the people, and they argue for their saying that he is the son of God, saying: He had no father who knew, and he spoke in the cradle with something that no one from the children of Adam had heard before him, and they argue for their saying that he is the third of three with the saying of God the Most High: We did, We commanded, We created, and We decreed, and they say: If he were one, he would not have said anything except I did, I commanded, I decreed, and I created, but he and Jesus and Mary - God is exalted and sanctified and is far above what the wrongdoers and deniers say - and in all of that from their saying: The Qur’an has been revealed, so when the two rabbis spoke to him, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Become Muslims, they said: We have already become Muslims, he said: You have not become Muslims, so become Muslims. They said: Yes, we became Muslims before you. He said: You have lied, what prevents you from becoming Muslims is your calling a son for God, your worship of the cross, and your eating pork. They said: Who is his father, O Muhammad? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent about them and did not answer them. Then God revealed about that of their saying and the difference in their affair the beginning of Surat Al Imran up to eighty-some verses of it. Then Ibn Ishaq spoke about its interpretation until he said: When the report from God and the final judgment between Him and them came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he ordered what he ordered of cursing them if they rejected that to him, he called them to that, and they said: O Abu al-Qasim, let us consider our affair and then we will come to you with what we want to do with what you called us to. Then they turned away from him, then they were alone with the one who came after, and that was their opinion. They said: O Abd al-Masih, what do you think? He said: By God, O Christians, you have known that Muhammad is a prophet sent, and he has brought you the final word about your companion. You have known that no people have ever cursed a prophet, and their elders remained, nor their young ones grew up. If you do this, it will be your extermination. If you insist on following your religion and remaining as you say about your companion, then say farewell to the man and return to your country. They came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Abu al-Qasim, we have decided not to curse you and leave you in your religion and return to our religion. But send with us a man from your companions whom you are pleased with to judge between us in matters in which we differed regarding our wealth, for you are content with us. Muhammad ibn Ja`far said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Come to me in the evening, and I will send with you the strong and trustworthy one. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, used to say: I have never loved leadership as much as I loved it on that day, hoping that I would be its owner. I went to the noon prayer in the early morning. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the noon prayer, he said the greeting of peace and then looked away. “I began to stretch out my legs for him to see me, but he kept looking until he saw Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah, so he called him and said: ‘Go out with them and judge between them with justice in what they differed over.’” ‘Umar said: So Abu Ubaidah, may God be pleased with him, went with her. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of ‘Asim ibn ‘Umar ibn Qatada, on the authority of Mahmud ibn Labid, on the authority of Rafi’ ibn Khadij: That the delegation of the people of Najran came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said about the nobles: They were twelve, and he mentioned the rest of it in a longer context than this, and other additions. Al-Bukhari said: Abbas bin Al-Hussein told us, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Silah bin Zafar, on the authority of Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “Al-Aqib and Al-Sayyid, the two rulers of Najran, came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanting to perform the Li’an. He said: One of them said to the other: Do not do it, for by God, if he is a prophet and we perform the Li’an, neither we nor our descendants after us will succeed. They said: We will give you what you asked of us, but send with us a trustworthy man, and do not send with us anyone but a trustworthy person. He said: I will send with you a trustworthy man, truly trustworthy. The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were eager to do so, so he said: Get up, O Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah. When he got up, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is the trustworthy one of this nation.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah through various chains of narration on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Sabi’i on the authority of Silah, on the authority of Hudhayfah, in a similar manner. Ahmad, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Israel on the authority of Abu Ishaq. On the authority of Silah, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, similarly. Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Walid told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, He said, ‘Every nation has a trustee, and the trustee of this nation is Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah.’ Imam Ahmad said: Ismail ibn Yazid al-Ruqi Abu Yazid told us, Furat told us, on the authority of `Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, on the authority of `Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: Abu Jahl, may God curse him, said, ‘If I see Muhammad praying at the Ka`bah, I will come to him and step on his neck.’ He said: ‘If he did, the angels would seize him in person. If the Jews wished for death, they would die and see their seats in Hell. If those who challenged the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to mubahala went out, they would return without finding any wealth or family.’ Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of `Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Mu`ammar, on the authority of `Abd al-Karim, on its authority. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dala’il al-Nubuwwah a very long story of the Najran delegation, and let us mention it, for it contains many benefits, and it contains strangeness, and it is appropriate for this occasion. Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah al-Hafiz and Abu Saeed Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Fadl told us: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya’qub told us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar told us, Yunus ibn Bakir told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Abd Yusoo’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, Yunus said - and he was a Christian who converted to Islam - that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to the people of Najran before the Book of Solomon was revealed to him: “In the name of the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, from Muhammad the Prophet, the Messenger of God, to the Bishop of Najran and the people of Najran, you have converted to Islam, for I praise to you the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. As for what follows, I call you to the worship of God from the worship of servants, and I call you to the guardianship of God from the guardianship of servants. If you refuse, then pay the jizya, and if you refuse, then I have declared war on you, and peace.” When the bishop received the letter and read it, he was horrified by it and was extremely frightened. He sent for a man from Najran called Shurahbil ibn Wada’ah, who was from Hamdan. No one was called before him when a difficult matter arose, neither al-Ayham, nor al-Sayyid, nor al-Aqib. So the bishop gave the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Shurahbil, who read it. The bishop said: O Abu Maryam, what do you think? Shurahbil said: I know what God promised Abraham in the descendants of Ishmael of prophethood, so how can I believe that this is that man? I have no opinion in the matter of prophethood, and if it were in a worldly matter I would have advised you about it with my opinion and made an effort for you. The bishop said: Step aside and sit down. Shurahbil stepped aside and sat to one side. The bishop sent to a man from Najran called Abdullah bin Shurahbil, who was from Dhi Asbah of Himyar. He read the letter to him and asked him about his opinion on it. He said to him the same as Shurahbil had said. The bishop said to him: Step aside and sit down. Abdullah stepped aside and sat to one side. The bishop sent to a man from Najran called Jabbar bin Fayd from Banu al-Harith bin Ka’b, one of Banu al-Hamas. He read the letter to him and asked him about his opinion on it. He said to him the same as Shurahbil and Abdullah had said, so the bishop ordered him to step aside and sit aside. When they all agreed on that statement, the bishop ordered the bell to be rung and the fires and sackcloth were raised in the monasteries. This is what they used to do when they were frightened during the day, and when they were frightened at night, they would ring the bell and the fires were raised in the monasteries. When the bell was rung and the sackcloth was raised, the people of the valley, both above and below, gathered together. The length of the valley is a day’s journey for a fast rider, and it contains seventy-three villages and one hundred and twenty thousand fighters. He read to them the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked them about their opinion on it. The opinion of the people of opinion among them was unanimous that they should send Shurahbil ibn Wada’ah al-Hamdani, Abdullah ibn Shurahbil al-Asbahi, and Jabbar ibn Fayd al-Harithi to bring them report of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The delegation set out until they were in Medina, where they removed their travel clothes and put on their garments made of silk and gold rings. Then they set out until they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and greeted him, but he did not respond to them. They remained silent for a long day, but he did not speak to them, and they were wearing those garments and gold rings. Then they set out following Uthman ibn Affan and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, who were acquainted with them. They found them among some of the Muhajireen and Ansar in a gathering. They said: O Uthman and Abd al-Rahman, your Prophet wrote us a letter, so we came to him in response. We came to him and greeted him. He did not return our greetings, and we kept talking to him for a long day, until we were exhausted from talking to him. What do you think, should we go back? They said to Ali ibn Abi Talib, who was with the al-Nas 114:What do you think, O Abu al-Hasan, about these people? Then Ali said to Uthman and Abd al-Rahman: I think they should put off their clothes and rings, and wear their travelling clothes, then return to him. So they did and greeted him, and he returned their greeting. Then he said: By Him Who sent me with the truth, they came to me the first time and Iblis was with them. Then he asked them, and they kept asking him and them until they said to him: What do you say about Jesus? We are returning to our people and we are Christians. If you are a prophet, we would be pleased to hear what you say about him? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have nothing about him today, so stay until I tell you what my Lord says to me about Jesus. Then the next morning God revealed this verse: “Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is as that of Adam. He created him from dust and then said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was. The truth is from your Lord, so be not among the doubters. But whoever disputes with you about him after what has come to you of knowledge, say: ‘Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us supplicate earnestly and invoke the curse of God upon the liars.’” But they refused to acknowledge it. Thus, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came the next day after he had informed them of the report, he came with al-Hasan and al-Husayn in his tent, and Fatima was walking behind him to curse, and he had several wives at that time. Shurahbil said to his two companions: You know that when the top and bottom of a valley meet, they will not return or depart except according to my opinion, and by God I see a heavy matter. By God, if this man is a king sent, then we will be the first Arabs to stab him in the eyes and reject his command. It will not go away from his chest or the chests of his companions until they afflict us with a calamity, and we are the closest Arabs to them in neighborliness. And if this man is a prophet sent, then we will curse him, and there will not remain from us on the face of the earth a hair or a nail except that it will perish. His two companions said to him: What is the opinion, O Abu Maryam? He said: I see that I should rule on it, for I see a man who never rules excessively. They said to him: You and that. Shurahbil met the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: I have seen something better than your cursing. He said: What is it? He said: Your ruling today until night and your night until morning, so whatever you rule on us is permissible. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Is there someone behind you who will curse you? Shurahbil said: Ask my companion. So he asked them and they said: It does not come to the valley and does not proceed except from Shurahbil’s opinion. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned and did not curse them until the next day, and they came to him. He wrote this document for them: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This is what the Prophet Muhammad, the Messenger of God, wrote for Najran - if they are to rule on it - regarding every fruit, every yellow, white, and black animal, and the slaves that are in excess of them, and he left all of that for them for two thousand garments, in every Rajab a thousand garments, and in every Safar a thousand garments. He mentioned all the conditions and the rest of the context. The point is that their delegations were in the year nine, because Al-Zuhri said: The people of Najran were the first to pay the jizya to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the verse of the jizya was only revealed after the conquest, and it is the Almighty’s saying: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day 3:10. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Sulayman bin Ahmad told us, Ahmad bin Dawud Al-Makki told us, Bishr bin Mihran told us, Muhammad bin Dinar told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir, who said: Al-Aqib and Al-Tayyib came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he called them to curse, so they promised him that they would curse him in the morning. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went in the morning, and took the hand of Ali, Fatima, Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn, then he sent for them, but they refused to respond and acknowledged the tax to him. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One Who sent me with the truth, if they had said: No, I would have rained fire upon them in the valley.” Jabir said: And regarding them was revealed: We will call our sons and your sons. Our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves.” Jabir said, Our selves and yourselves means the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Ali ibn Abi Talib. Our sons means Al-Hassan and Al-Hussein. Our women means Fatima. And thus Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Ali bin Isa, on the authority of Ahmad bin Muhammad Al-Azhari, on the authority of Ali bin Hajar, on the authority of Ali bin Masahr, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, with the same meaning, then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of Muslim, and they did not narrate it like this. He said, and Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi narrated it on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, with a mursal, and this is more authentic. Something similar has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Al-Bara’, then God Almighty said: Indeed, this is the true story, meaning, what We have narrated to you, O Muhammad, regarding Jesus is the truth from which there is no deviation or escape. “And there is no god except God, and indeed, God is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. But if they turn away,” meaning from this to something else, then indeed, God is Knowing of the corrupters, meaning, whoever turns away from the truth to falsehood, then he is the corrupter, and God is Knowing of him, and He will reward him for that with the worst reward, and He is the Able, from whom nothing escapes, glory and praise be to Him, and we seek refuge in Him from the arrival of His vengeance.
3:62: The Almighty says: The likeness of Jesus before God in God's power, as He created him without a father, is like the likeness of Adam, as He created him without a father or mother, but He created him from dust and then said to him, 'Be,' and he was. So the One who created Adam without a father is able to create Jesus by a fortiori and more appropriate way, and if it is permissible to claim sonship in Jesus because he was created without a father, then it is permissible in Adam by a fortiori way, and it is known by consensus that this is false, so claiming it in Jesus is even more false and more clearly corrupt, but the Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, wanted to show His power to His creation when He created Adam from neither a male nor a female, and created Eve from a male without a female, and created Jesus from a female without a male, just as He created the rest of creation from a male and a female, and for this reason the Almighty said in Surah Maryam, And We will make him a sign for mankind and He said here, The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters meaning this is the true statement about Jesus from which there is no escape and no truth other than it, and what is after the truth except misguidance. Then the Almighty said, commanding His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to challenge those who opposed the truth regarding the matter of Jesus after the revelation of the proof: “But whoever disputes with you concerning him after what has come to you of knowledge, say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us supplicate earnestly, and invoke the curse of God upon the liars, whether from us or from you.” The reason for the revelation of this Mubahala and the ones before it from the beginning of the Surah to here about the delegation of Najran is that when the Christians came and began to argue about Jesus and claim what they claim about his sonship and divinity, God revealed the beginning of this Surah in response to them. Ibn Ishaq said in his famous biography and others: A delegation of Christians from Najran came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sixty riders, among them fourteen men from their nobles to whom their affairs would be referred, and they are: Al-Aqib, whose name is Abdul-Masih; Al-Sayyid, who is Al-Ayham; Abu Haritha bin Alqamah, the brother of Bakr bin Wa’il; Uways bin Al-Harith; Zaid; Qais; Yazid and his Nabih; Khuwaylid; Amr; Khalid; Abdullah; and Yahanis. Their rabbi, imam and head of their schools, was a man from the Arabs of Banu Bakr ibn Wa’il, but he converted to Christianity and the Romans and their kings honored him and built churches for him and served him because they knew of his steadfastness in their religion. He knew the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, his description and his status from what he learned from the previous books, but his ignorance led him to continue in Christianity because of what he saw of his veneration there and his prestige among its people. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dala’il al-Nubuwwah a very long story of the Najran delegation, and let us mention it, for it contains many benefits, and it contains strangeness, and it is appropriate for this occasion. Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah al-Hafiz and Abu Saeed Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Fadl told us: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya’qub told us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar told us, Yunus ibn Bakir told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Abd Yusoo’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, Yunus said - and he was a Christian who converted to Islam - that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to the people of Najran before the Book of Solomon was revealed to him: “In the name of the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, from Muhammad the Prophet, the Messenger of God, to the Bishop of Najran and the people of Najran, you have converted to Islam, for I praise to you the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. As for what follows, I call you to the worship of God from the worship of servants, and I call you to the guardianship of God from the guardianship of servants. If you refuse, then pay the jizya, and if you refuse, then I have declared war on you, and peace.” When the bishop received the letter and read it, he was horrified by it and was extremely frightened. He sent for a man from Najran called Shurahbil ibn Wada’ah, who was from Hamdan. No one was called before him when a difficult matter arose, neither al-Ayham, nor al-Sayyid, nor al-Aqib. So the bishop gave the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Shurahbil, who read it. The bishop said: O Abu Maryam, what do you think? Shurahbil said: I know what God promised Abraham in the descendants of Ishmael of prophethood, so how can I believe that this is that man? I have no opinion in the matter of prophethood, and if it were in a worldly matter I would have advised you about it with my opinion and made an effort for you. The bishop said: Step aside and sit down. Shurahbil stepped aside and sat to one side. The bishop sent to a man from Najran called Abdullah bin Shurahbil, who was from Dhi Asbah of Himyar. He read the letter to him and asked him about his opinion on it. He said to him the same as Shurahbil had said. The bishop said to him: Step aside and sit down. Abdullah stepped aside and sat to one side. The bishop sent to a man from Najran called Jabbar bin Fayd from Banu al-Harith bin Ka’b, one of Banu al-Hamas. He read the letter to him and asked him about his opinion on it. He said to him the same as Shurahbil and Abdullah had said, so the bishop ordered him to step aside and sit aside. When they all agreed on that statement, the bishop ordered the bell to be rung and the fires and sackcloth were raised in the monasteries. This is what they used to do when they were frightened during the day, and when they were frightened at night, they would ring the bell and the fires were raised in the monasteries. When the bell was rung and the sackcloth was raised, the people of the valley, both above and below, gathered together. The length of the valley is a day’s journey for a fast rider, and it contains seventy-three villages and one hundred and twenty thousand fighters. He read to them the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked them about their opinion on it. The opinion of the people of opinion among them was unanimous that they should send Shurahbil ibn Wada’ah al-Hamdani, Abdullah ibn Shurahbil al-Asbahi, and Jabbar ibn Fayd al-Harithi to bring them report of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The delegation set out until they were in Medina, where they removed their travel clothes and put on their garments made of silk and gold rings. Then they set out until they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and greeted him, but he did not respond to them. They remained silent for a long day, but he did not speak to them, and they were wearing those garments and gold rings. Then they set out following Uthman ibn Affan and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, who were acquainted with them. They found them among some of the Muhajireen and Ansar in a gathering. They said: O Uthman and Abd al-Rahman, your Prophet wrote us a letter, so we came to him in response. We came to him and greeted him. He did not return our greetings, and we kept talking to him for a long day, until we were exhausted from talking to him. What do you think, should we go back? They said to Ali ibn Abi Talib, who was with the al-Nas 114:What do you think, O Abu al-Hasan, about these people? Then Ali said to Uthman and Abd al-Rahman: I think they should put off their clothes and rings, and wear their travelling clothes, then return to him. So they did and greeted him, and he returned their greeting. Then he said: By Him Who sent me with the truth, they came to me the first time and Iblis was with them. Then he asked them, and they kept asking him and them until they said to him: What do you say about Jesus? We are returning to our people and we are Christians. If you are a prophet, we would be pleased to hear what you say about him? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have nothing about him today, so stay until I tell you what my Lord says to me about Jesus. Then the next morning God revealed this verse: “Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is as that of Adam. He created him from dust and then said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was. The truth is from your Lord, so be not among the doubters. But whoever disputes with you about him after what has come to you of knowledge, say: ‘Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us supplicate earnestly and invoke the curse of God upon the liars.’” But they refused to acknowledge it. Thus, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came the next day after he had informed them of the report, he came with al-Hasan and al-Husayn in his tent, and Fatima was walking behind him to curse, and he had several wives at that time. Shurahbil said to his two companions: You know that when the top and bottom of a valley meet, they will not return or depart except according to my opinion, and by God I see a heavy matter. By God, if this man is a king sent, then we will be the first Arabs to stab him in the eyes and reject his command. It will not go away from his chest or the chests of his companions until they afflict us with a calamity, and we are the closest Arabs to them in neighborliness. And if this man is a prophet sent, then we will curse him, and there will not remain from us on the face of the earth a hair or a nail except that it will perish. His two companions said to him: What is the opinion, O Abu Maryam? He said: I see that I should rule on it, for I see a man who never rules excessively. They said to him: You and that. Shurahbil met the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: I have seen something better than your cursing. He said: What is it? He said: Your ruling today until night and your night until morning, so whatever you rule on us is permissible. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Is there someone behind you who will curse you? Shurahbil said: Ask my companion. So he asked them and they said: It does not come to the valley and does not proceed except from Shurahbil’s opinion. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned and did not curse them until the next day, and they came to him. He wrote this document for them: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This is what the Prophet Muhammad, the Messenger of God, wrote for Najran - if they are to rule on it - regarding every fruit, every yellow, white, and black animal, and the slaves that are in excess of them, and he left all of that for them for two thousand garments, in every Rajab a thousand garments, and in every Safar a thousand garments. He mentioned all the conditions and the rest of the context. The point is that their delegations were in the year nine, because Al-Zuhri said: The people of Najran were the first to pay the jizya to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the verse of the jizya was only revealed after the conquest, and it is the Almighty’s saying: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day 3:10. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Sulayman bin Ahmad told us, Ahmad bin Dawud Al-Makki told us, Bishr bin Mihran told us, Muhammad bin Dinar told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir, who said: Al-Aqib and Al-Tayyib came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he called them to curse, so they promised him that they would curse him in the morning. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went in the morning, and took the hand of Ali, Fatima, Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn, then he sent for them, but they refused to respond and acknowledged the tax to him. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One Who sent me with the truth, if they had said: No, I would have rained fire upon them in the valley.” Jabir said: And regarding them was revealed: We will call our sons and your sons. Our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves.” Jabir said, Our selves and yourselves means the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Ali ibn Abi Talib. Our sons means Al-Hassan and Al-Hussein. Our women means Fatima. And thus Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Ali bin Isa, on the authority of Ahmad bin Muhammad Al-Azhari, on the authority of Ali bin Hajar, on the authority of Ali bin Masahr, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, with the same meaning, then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of Muslim, and they did not narrate it like this. He said, and Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi narrated it on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, with a mursal, and this is more authentic. Something similar has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Al-Bara’, then God Almighty said: Indeed, this is the true story, meaning, what We have narrated to you, O Muhammad, regarding Jesus is the truth from which there is no deviation or escape. “And there is no god except God, and indeed, God is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. But if they turn away,” meaning from this to something else, then indeed, God is Knowing of the corrupters, meaning, whoever turns away from the truth to falsehood, then he is the corrupter, and God is Knowing of him, and He will reward him for that with the worst reward, and He is the Able, from whom nothing escapes, glory and praise be to Him, and we seek refuge in Him from the arrival of His vengeance.
3:63: The Almighty says: The likeness of Jesus before God in God's power, as He created him without a father, is like the likeness of Adam, as He created him without a father or mother, but He created him from dust and then said to him, 'Be,' and he was. So the One who created Adam without a father is able to create Jesus by a fortiori and more appropriate way, and if it is permissible to claim sonship in Jesus because he was created without a father, then it is permissible in Adam by a fortiori way, and it is known by consensus that this is false, so claiming it in Jesus is even more false and more clearly corrupt, but the Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, wanted to show His power to His creation when He created Adam from neither a male nor a female, and created Eve from a male without a female, and created Jesus from a female without a male, just as He created the rest of creation from a male and a female, and for this reason the Almighty said in Surah Maryam, And We will make him a sign for mankind and He said here, The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters meaning this is the true statement about Jesus from which there is no escape and no truth other than it, and what is after the truth except misguidance. Then the Almighty said, commanding His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to challenge those who opposed the truth regarding the matter of Jesus after the revelation of the proof: “But whoever disputes with you concerning him after what has come to you of knowledge, say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us supplicate earnestly, and invoke the curse of God upon the liars, whether from us or from you.” The reason for the revelation of this Mubahala and the ones before it from the beginning of the Surah to here about the delegation of Najran is that when the Christians came and began to argue about Jesus and claim what they claim about his sonship and divinity, God revealed the beginning of this Surah in response to them. Ibn Ishaq said in his famous biography and others: A delegation of Christians from Najran came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sixty riders, among them fourteen men from their nobles to whom their affairs would be referred, and they are: Al-Aqib, whose name is Abdul-Masih; Al-Sayyid, who is Al-Ayham; Abu Haritha bin Alqamah, the brother of Bakr bin Wa’il; Uways bin Al-Harith; Zaid; Qais; Yazid and his Nabih; Khuwaylid; Amr; Khalid; Abdullah; and Yahanis. The affairs of these people would be referred to three of them, and they are Al-Aqib, who was the leader of the people and had their opinion and their advisor, and they would not act except according to his opinion; Al-Sayyid, who was their scholar and the owner of their travels and their community; and Abu Haritha bin Alqamah, who was their bishop. Their rabbi, imam and head of their schools, was a man from the Arabs of Banu Bakr ibn Wa’il, but he converted to Christianity and the Romans and their kings honored him and built churches for him and served him because they knew of his steadfastness in their religion. He knew the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, his description and his status from what he learned from the previous books, but his ignorance led him to continue in Christianity because of what he saw of his veneration there and his prestige among its people. Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Ja’far ibn al-Zubayr told me, he said: They came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina, and entered his mosque when he prayed the afternoon prayer, wearing the clothes of the rabbis, cloaks and robes as beautiful as the men of Banu al-Harith ibn Ka’b. He said: Those of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who saw them said: We have not seen a delegation like them after them. And the time for their prayer came, so they stood in the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Leave them and pray facing the east. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke to Abu Haritha ibn Alqamah and Al-Aqib Abd al-Rahman from among them. Christ and Mr. Ayham, who are Christians of the religion of the king, although their matter differs, say: He is God, and they say: He is the son of God, and they say: He is the third of three. God is far above what they say. And so is the saying of the Christians, for they argue in their saying that He is God, that He used to bring the dead back to life, and heal the blind, the lepers, and those with diseases, and tell the unseen, and create from clay the form of a bird, then breathe into it and it becomes a bird, and all of that is by the command of God. And that God may make him a sign for the people, and they argue for their saying that he is the son of God, saying: He had no father who knew, and he spoke in the cradle with something that no one from the children of Adam had heard before him, and they argue for their saying that he is the third of three with the saying of God the Most High: We did, We commanded, We created, and We decreed, and they say: If he were one, he would not have said anything except I did, I commanded, I decreed, and I created, but he and Jesus and Mary - God is exalted and sanctified and is far above what the wrongdoers and deniers say - and in all of that from their saying: The Qur’an has been revealed, so when the two rabbis spoke to him, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Become Muslims, they said: We have already become Muslims, he said: You have not become Muslims, so become Muslims. They said: Yes, we became Muslims before you. He said: You have lied, what prevents you from becoming Muslims is your calling a son for God, your worship of the cross, and your eating pork. They said: Who is his father, O Muhammad? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent about them and did not answer them. Then God revealed about that of their saying and the difference in their affair the beginning of Surat Al Imran up to eighty-some verses of it. Then Ibn Ishaq spoke about its interpretation until he said: When the report from God and the final judgment between Him and them came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he ordered what he ordered of cursing them if they rejected that to him, he called them to that, and they said: O Abu al-Qasim, let us consider our affair and then we will come to you with what we want to do with what you called us to. Then they turned away from him, then they were alone with the one who came after, and that was their opinion. They said: O Abd al-Masih, what do you think? He said: By God, O Christians, you have known that Muhammad is a prophet sent, and he has brought you the final word about your companion. You have known that no people have ever cursed a prophet, and their elders remained, nor their young ones grew up. If you do this, it will be your extermination. If you insist on following your religion and remaining as you say about your companion, then say farewell to the man and return to your country. They came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Abu al-Qasim, we have decided not to curse you and leave you in your religion and return to our religion. But send with us a man from your companions whom you are pleased with to judge between us in matters in which we differed regarding our wealth, for you are content with us. Muhammad ibn Ja`far said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Come to me in the evening, and I will send with you the strong and trustworthy one. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, used to say: I have never loved leadership as much as I loved it on that day, hoping that I would be its owner. I went to the noon prayer in the early morning. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the noon prayer, he said the greeting of peace and then looked away. “I began to stretch out my legs for him to see me, but he kept looking until he saw Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah, so he called him and said: ‘Go out with them and judge between them with justice in what they differed over.’” ‘Umar said: So Abu Ubaidah, may God be pleased with him, went with her. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of ‘Asim ibn ‘Umar ibn Qatada, on the authority of Mahmud ibn Labid, on the authority of Rafi’ ibn Khadij: That the delegation of the people of Najran came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said about the nobles: They were twelve, and he mentioned the rest of it in a longer context than this, and other additions. Al-Bukhari said: Abbas bin Al-Hussein told us, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Silah bin Zafar, on the authority of Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “Al-Aqib and Al-Sayyid, the two rulers of Najran, came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanting to perform the Li’an. He said: One of them said to the other: Do not do it, for by God, if he is a prophet and we perform the Li’an, neither we nor our descendants after us will succeed. They said: We will give you what you asked of us, but send with us a trustworthy man, and do not send with us anyone but a trustworthy person. He said: I will send with you a trustworthy man, truly trustworthy. The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were eager to do so, so he said: Get up, O Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah. If the Jews wished for death, they would die and see their seats in Hell. If those who challenged the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to mubahala went out, they would return without finding any wealth or family.’ Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of `Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Mu`ammar, on the authority of `Abd al-Karim, on its authority. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Sulayman bin Ahmad told us, Ahmad bin Dawud Al-Makki told us, Bishr bin Mihran told us, Muhammad bin Dinar told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir, who said: Al-Aqib and Al-Tayyib came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he called them to curse, so they promised him that they would curse him in the morning. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went in the morning, and took the hand of Ali, Fatima, Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn, then he sent for them, but they refused to respond and acknowledged the tax to him. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One Who sent me with the truth, if they had said: No, I would have rained fire upon them in the valley.” Jabir said: And regarding them was revealed: We will call our sons and your sons. Our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves.” Jabir said, Our selves and yourselves means the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Ali ibn Abi Talib. Our sons means Al-Hassan and Al-Hussein. Our women means Fatima. And thus Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Ali bin Isa, on the authority of Ahmad bin Muhammad Al-Azhari, on the authority of Ali bin Hajar, on the authority of Ali bin Masahr, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, with the same meaning, then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of Muslim, and they did not narrate it like this. He said, and Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi narrated it on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, with a mursal, and this is more authentic. Something similar has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Al-Bara’, then God Almighty said: Indeed, this is the true story, meaning, what We have narrated to you, O Muhammad, regarding Jesus is the truth from which there is no deviation or escape. “And there is no god except God, and indeed, God is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. But if they turn away,” meaning from this to something else, then indeed, God is Knowing of the corrupters, meaning, whoever turns away from the truth to falsehood, then he is the corrupter, and God is Knowing of him, and He will reward him for that with the worst reward, and He is the Able, from whom nothing escapes, glory and praise be to Him, and we seek refuge in Him from the arrival of His vengeance.
3:64: This address includes the People of the Book, Jews, Christians, and others like them. Say, O People of the Book, come to a word. The word refers to a useful sentence, as He said here. Then He described it by saying, Equal between us and you, meaning justice and half, in which we and you are equal. Then He explained it by saying, That we worship none but God and associate nothing with Him, not an idol, nor a cross, nor a statue, nor a tyrant, nor fire, nor anything, but rather we devote worship to God alone, with no partner for Him. This is the call of all the messengers. God Almighty said, And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him, ‘There is no god except Me, so worship Me.’ And God Almighty said, And We have certainly sent to every nation a messenger, [saying], ‘Worship God and avoid false gods.’ Then God Almighty said, And let not some of us take others as lords besides God. Ibn Jurayj said, He means that some of us obey others in disobeying God. Ikrimah said, We prostrate to some of us. “But if they turn away, then say, ‘Bear witness that we are Muslims.’” That is, if they turn away from this half and this call, then bear witness to them yourselves. On your continuation in the Islam that God has prescribed for you. We have mentioned in the explanation of Al-Bukhari when he narrated it on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah bin Utbah bin Masoud, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Abu Sufyan in his story when he entered upon Caesar, and he asked him about the lineage of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and about his description and attributes and what he called for, so he informed him of all of that in plain terms, even though Abu Sufyan was at that time a polytheist who had not yet converted to Islam, and that was after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah and before the conquest, as is stated in the hadith, and because when he asked him: Will he betray? He said: I said: No, and we are in a period of time with him in which we do not know what he will do, he said: And I could not add anything to it except this, and the point is that he said: Then the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought and he read it and in it was: "In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. From Muhammad, the Messenger of God, to Heraclius, the Great of the Romans. Peace be upon him who follows the right guidance. As for what follows, submit and you will be safe, and submit and God will give you your reward twice. But if you turn away, then upon you is the sin of the Arians. And O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you - that we will not worship except God and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords besides God. But if they turn away, then say, Bear witness that we are Muslims [in submission]. Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others mentioned that the beginning of Surah Al Imran, up to eighty-some verses, was revealed about the delegation from Najran. Al-Zuhri said: They were the first to pay the jizya. There is no disagreement that the verse of the jizya was revealed after the conquest. So what is the connection between writing this verse before the conquest to Heraclius as part of the letter, and what Muhammad ibn Ishaq and Al-Zuhri mentioned? The answer is from several aspects. One of them It is possible that this verse was revealed twice, once before Al-Hudaybiyyah, and once after the conquest. Second It is possible that the beginning of Surah Al Imran was revealed about the delegation from Najran up to this verse, and this verse was revealed before that, and Ibn Ishaq’s statement: up to eighty-some verses, is not preserved due to the evidence of the hadith of Abu Sufyan. Third It is possible that the arrival of the Najran delegation was before Al-Hudaybiyyah, and that what they offered was a reconciliation for the Mubahalah, not in the form of a tribute, but rather in the form of a truce and reconciliation, and the revelation of the verse on the tribute after that was in accordance with that, just as the imposition of the fifth and the four-fifths came in accordance with what Abdullah bin Jahsh did in that expedition before Badr, then the imposition of the division was revealed in accordance with that. Fourth It is possible that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered this to be written in his letter to Heraclius, it had not been revealed yet, then the Qur’an was revealed in agreement with him, may God bless him and grant him peace, just as it was revealed in agreement with Umar bin Al-Khattab regarding the veil and the prisoners, and regarding not praying for the hypocrites, and in His statement: And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer and in His statement: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you verse.
3:65: God the Almighty denies the Jews and Christians in their argument about Abraham, peace be upon him, and the claim of each group that he was one of them, as Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit, told me, Saeed bin Jubair or Ikrimah told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Christians of Najran and the Jewish rabbis gathered in the presence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they disputed in his presence. The rabbis said: Abraham was nothing but a Jew, and the Christians said: Abraham was nothing but a Christian. So God the Almighty revealed: O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham? The verse, meaning how do you claim, O Jews, that he was a Jew, when his time was before God revealed the Torah to Moses? And how do you claim, O Christians, that he was a Christian, when Christianity only emerged after his time by a long time? That is why God the Almighty said: Do you not reason? Then He the Almighty said: “Here you are, you have argued about that of which you have knowledge. Why do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge?” The verse. This is a denial of those who argue about that of which they have no knowledge, for the Jews and Christians argued about Abraham without knowledge. If they had argued about that which they had knowledge of, which was related to their religions that were prescribed for them until the time of the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, it would have been more appropriate for them. They only spoke about that which they did not know, so God denounced them for that and ordered them to refer what they had no knowledge of to the Knower of the unseen and the seen, who knows all things in their true and clear aspects. That is why God the Almighty said: And God knows, while you do not know. Then He the Almighty said: Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was one inclining toward truth, a Muslim. That is, one who turned away from polytheism and intended to believe. And he was not of the polytheists. This verse is like the one that came before in Surat al-Baqarah 2:“And they said, ‘Be Jews or Christians [so] you will be guided. ’” The verse. Then God the Almighty said: “Indeed, those most deserving of Abraham are those who followed him and this Prophet and those who have believed. And God is the ally of the believers.” God the Almighty says: The people most deserving of following Abraham the Friend are those who followed him in his religion and this Prophet, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who believed from his companions, the Muhajireen and the Ansar, and those who followed them after them. Saeed bin Mansour said: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Masrouq, on the authority of Abu Ad-Dahha, on the authority of Masrouq, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, every prophet has guardians from among the prophets, and my guardian among them is my father and the Friend of my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. Then he recited: Indeed, those most deserving of Abraham are those who followed him, the verse. At-Tirmidhi and Al-Bazzar narrated it from the hadith of Abu Ahmad Az-Zubayri, on the authority of Sufyan Ath-Thawri, on the authority of his father, on his authority. Then Al-Bazzar said: And it was narrated by others besides Abu Ahmad, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ad-Dahha, on the authority of Abdullah, and he did not mention Masrouq. And likewise, Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Wakee’ on the authority of Sufyan, then he said: This is more authentic, but Wakee’ narrated it in his interpretation, and he said: Sufyan told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Every prophet has a guardianship from the prophets, and my guardian among them is my father and the friend of my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, Abraham, peace be upon him.” Then he recited: Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him and this Prophet and those who have believed the verse, His saying: And God is the Guardian of the believers meaning the Guardian of all believers in His Messengers.

3:69: The Almighty tells about the Jews’ envy of the believers, and their desire to mislead them, and He informed that the consequences of that only come back to themselves, and they do not realize that they are being tricked. Then the Almighty said, denouncing them, O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the verses of God while you witness it? That is, you know its truth and realize its truth. O People of the Scripture, why do you mix truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know? That is, you conceal what is in your books about the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, while you know that and realize it. “And a party of the People of the Scripture say, ‘Believe in that which has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at its end. ’” This is a plot they wanted to confuse the weak among the people about their religion, which is that they agreed among themselves to show faith at the beginning of the day, and to pray the dawn prayer with the Muslims, but when the day came, they would return to their religion so that the ignorant among the people would say: What brought them back to their religion was their discovery of a contradiction and a defect in the religion of the Muslims. For this reason they said, Perhaps they They return. Ibn Abi Nujayh said: On the authority of Mujahid, in the words of God Almighty, informing about the Jews in this verse, he means the Jews who prayed the dawn prayer with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and disbelieved at the end of the day, as a plot on their part, so that people would see that they had become misguided from him after they had followed him. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A group of the People of the Book said: When you met the companions of Muhammad at the beginning of the day, then believe, and when it is the end of it, then pray your prayers so that they may say, These are the People of the Book, and they are more knowledgeable than us. And this is how it was narrated on the authority of Qatada, Al-Suddi, Al-Rabi’, and Abu Malik. And the Almighty said: And do not believe except to him who follows your religion meaning do not be reassured or reveal your secret and what you have except to him who follows your religion, and do not reveal what is in your hands to the Muslims so that they believe in it and use it as evidence against you. God Almighty said: Say, ‘Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of God’ meaning He is the One who guides the hearts of the believers to the most perfect faith in what He sent down to His servant and Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, of clear signs, decisive evidence, and evident arguments, even if you, O Jews, conceal what is in your hands of the description of Muhammad, the unlettered prophet, in your books that you transmitted from the earlier prophets. And His saying, That someone should be given the like of what you have been given, or that they should argue with you before your Lord, they say: Do not show the knowledge you have to the Muslims, so that they learn it from you, and become equal to you in it and have an advantage over you because of the strength of their faith in it, or argue with you about it before your Lord, meaning that they take it as an argument against you with what is in your hands, so that evidence is established against you, and the argument is formed in this world and the hereafter. God Almighty said: “Say: Verily, bounty is in the hand of God. He gives it to whom He wills,” meaning that all matters are under His control, and He is the Giver and the Withholder. He bestows upon whomever He wills faith, knowledge, and perfect perception, and He misguides whomever He wills, blinding his sight and insight, and sealing his heart and hearing, and placing a veil over his vision. He has the perfect argument and conclusive wisdom. “And God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing. He singles out for His mercy whomever He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty,” meaning that He singled you out, O believers, with bounty that is limitless and indescribable, with which He honored your Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, over all the other prophets. And He guided you to the most perfect of laws.

3:75: God the Almighty tells us about the Jews, that among them are traitors, and He warns the believers against being deceived by them, for among them is one who, if you entrust him with a great amount of money, will return it to you meaning, money, and among them is one who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you unless you stand over it meaning, by demanding, persisting, and insisting on getting your right, and if this is what he does with the dinar or anything above it, then it is more likely that he will not return it to him. We have already discussed the great amount at the beginning of the surah, but as for the dinar, it is well-known. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told us, Baqiyah told us on the authority of Ziyad bin Al-Haitham, Malik bin Dinar told us, he said: The dinar was called so because it is a debt and a fire. It was said: Its meaning is that whoever takes it rightfully, it is his debt, and whoever takes it wrongfully, the fire is for him. It is appropriate to mention here the hadith that Al-Bukhari included in more than one place in his Sahih, and the best of them is its context in the Book of Guarantee, where he said: Al-Layth said: Ja`far bin Rabi`ah told me, on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman bin Harmaz al-A`raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “that he mentioned a man from the Children of Israel who asked some of the Children of Israel to lend him a thousand dinars. He said: Bring me witnesses so I may bear witness. He said: God is sufficient as a witness. He said: Bring me a guarantor. He said: God is sufficient as a guarantor. He said: You have spoken the truth. So he gave it to him for a specified period. He went out to sea and fulfilled his need, then looked for a ship to ride so that he could arrive at the specified period, but he did not find a ship. So he took a piece of wood and carved it, then put in it a thousand dinars and a document from him to its owner, then he pushed it in its place, then he brought it to the sea and said: O God, You know that I borrowed a thousand dinars from so-and-so, and he asked me for a witness, so I said: God is sufficient as a witness.” He asked me for a guarantor, so I said: God is sufficient as a guarantor. So he agreed to that, and I tried hard to find a ship to which I could send what he had, but I was unable to. So I entrusted it to you. So he threw it into the sea until it entered it, then he turned away while he was looking for a ship to go to his country. Then the man who had given him a loan went out to see if a ship might bring him his money, and there was the piece of wood in which the money was, so he took it for his family as firewood. When he broke it, he found the money and the paper. Then the man from whom he had given him a loan came and brought him a thousand dinars, and said: By God, I have not ceased to strive to find a ship to bring you your money, but I have not found a ship before the one I came in. He said: Did you send me anything? He said: Did I not tell you that I did not find a mount before this? He said: Then God has fulfilled for you what I sent in the wood, so go back with a thousand dinars, guided.” This is how Al-Bukhari narrated it in one place, suspended in the form of certainty, and he attributed it in some places in the Sahih on the authority of Abdullah bin Salih, the scribe of Al-Layth, on his authority. Imam Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad in this manner, at length, on the authority of Yunus bin Muhammad Al-Mu’addab on the authority of Al-Layth, and Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Mudrik on the authority of Yahya bin Hammad, on the authority of Abu Awanah, on the authority of Umar bin Abi Salamah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. Then he said: It is not narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, except from this source with this chain of transmission. This is what he said, and it is a mistake for what came before. And his saying: That is because they said, ‘We have no blame upon the unlettered ones’ means that what led them to deny the truth was that they said: There is no blame upon us in our religion for eating the wealth of the unlettered ones, who are the Arabs, for God has made it permissible for us. God the Most High said: And they tell lies about God while they know. That is, they fabricated this statement and came up with this misguidance. God has forbidden them to eat wealth except by right. They are only a people of slander. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar informed us on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Hamadani, on the authority of Sa’sa’ah ibn Yazid, that a man asked Ibn Abbas, saying: We take from the wealth of the People of the Covenant in warfare, chickens and sheep. Ibn Abbas said: So what do you say? He said: We say that there is no harm in that. He said this is like what the People of the Book said: We have no blame upon the unlettered ones, that is, if they pay the jizyah, their wealth is not permissible for you except with their consent. And thus, Ath-Thawri narrated it on the authority of Abu Ishaq in a similar manner. And Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, Abu al-Rabi’ al-Zahrani told us, Ya’qub told us, Ja’far told us on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said: When the People of the Book said: We have no blame upon the unlettered ones, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The enemies of God lied. There is nothing that existed in the Age of Ignorance except that it is under these two feet of mine except the trust, for it is given to the righteous and the wicked.” Then God Almighty said: Yes, whoever fulfills his covenant and fears God, meaning, whoever fulfills his covenant and fears God among you, O People of the Book, that God has made a covenant with you regarding faith in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he is sent, as He took the covenant and pledge from the prophets and their nations with that, and fears God’s prohibitions, and follows His obedience and His law with which He sent the Seal of His Messengers and their Master. For God loves the righteous.
