3:77: God the Almighty says: Indeed, those who exchange what they have pledged to God of following Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioning his description to the people and explaining his command, and their false, wicked, sinful oaths for small, insignificant prices, which are the goods of this fleeting, transient worldly life, they will have no portion in the Hereafter, meaning they will have no share in it or portion of it, nor will God speak to them or look at them on the Day of Resurrection, meaning with mercy from Him to them, meaning God will not speak to them with words of kindness to them nor will He look at them with an eye of mercy, nor will He purify them, meaning from sins and impurities, rather He will order them to the Fire, and they will have a painful punishment. There are hadiths related to this noble verse, so let us mention what is easy from them. The first hadith Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Shu’bah told us, Ali bin Mudrik told me, he said I heard Abu Zur’ah on the authority of Kharsha bin Al-Har, on the authority of Abu Dharr, he said the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There are three whom God will not speak to, nor look at on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and they will have a painful punishment. I said: O Messenger of God, who are they? They have lost and failed. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, repeated it three times, he said: The one who lets his garment trail, the one who sells his goods by swearing, the liar, and the one who boasts.” Muslim and the people of Sunan narrated it on the authority of Shu’bah with it. Another way Ahmad said: Ismail told us on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Al-Ala’ bin Al-Shakheer, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahmas, who said: I met Abu Dharr and said to him: I have heard from you that you narrate a hadith on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: As for him, he does not think that I would lie about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after I heard it from him. So what have you heard from me? I said: I have heard that you say: Three are those whom God loves, and three are those whom God hates. He said: I said it and heard it. I said: Who are these whom God loves? He said: “A man meets the enemy in a group and he sets his throat for them until he is killed or he conquers for his companions, and the people travel and their journey is prolonged until they want to touch the ground and then they stop, and one of them moves aside and prays until he wakes them up for their departure, and a man has a neighbor who annoys him and he endures his annoyance until death or departure separates them. I said: Who are these people whom God hates? He said: The merchant who swears - or he said: the seller who swears - and the poor who is arrogant, and the miser who boasts.” Strange from this aspect. The second hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Jarbar bin Hazim, Adi bin Adi told us, Raja bin Haywah and Al-Aras bin Umaira told me, on the authority of his father Adi, who is Ibn Umaira Al-Kindi, who said: A man from Kinda, whose name was Imru’ Al-Qais bin Abis, disputed with a man from Hadhramaut before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding a piece of land. He ruled against the Hadrami with evidence, but he had no evidence, so he ruled against Imru’ Al-Qais with an oath. The Hadrami said: If I allow him to swear, O Messenger of God? I swear by the Kaaba that I have left, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever swears a false oath to seize someone’s money will meet God Almighty while He is angry with him. Raja said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: Those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price. Imru’ al-Qais said: What is for the one who abandons it, O Messenger of God? He said: Paradise. He said: Then bear witness that I have abandoned it all for him. Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of ‘Adi ibn ‘Adi with it. The third hadith Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Shuqaiq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever swears an oath in which he is wicked, in order to seize the wealth of a Muslim, will meet God, the Almighty, while He is angry with him. Al-Ash’ath said: By God, that was the case. There was a land between me and a Jewish man, and he denied it. So I brought him to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Do you have proof? I said: No. So he said to the Jew: Swear. I said: O Messenger of God, then he will swear and my wealth will be lost. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price Al-Bukhari and Muslim. They both narrated it from the hadith of Al-A’mash. Another way Ahmad said: Yahya bin Adam told us, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Asim bin Abi Al-Najoud, on the authority of Shaqiq bin Salamah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever takes the property of a Muslim unjustly will meet God while He is angry with him. Al-Ash’ath bin Qais came and said: What is Abu Abd Al-Rahman telling you? So we told him, and he said: “This hadith was in effect. I argued with my cousin before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about a well that was in his possession, but he denied it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Your proof is that it is your well, otherwise his oath.” I said: “O Messenger of God, I have no proof, and if you make it his oath, my well will be gone. My opponent is a wicked man.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever takes the property of a Muslim unjustly will meet God while He is angry with him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price... The fourth hadith Ahmad said: Yahya bin Ghailan told us, he said: Rashdin told us on the authority of Zaban, on the authority of Sahl bin Muadh bin Anas, on the authority of his father, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty has servants whom He will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, nor will He look at them. It was said: Who are those, O Messenger of God? He said: One who disowns his parents and is unwilling to be with them, one who disowns his children, and a man upon whom people bestowed a favor, but he was ungrateful for their favor and disowned them.” The fifth hadith Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Arfa told us, Hisham told us, Al-Awam, meaning Ibn Hawshab, informed us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Abdul Rahman, meaning Al-Sakaski, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, that a man displayed his merchandise in the market, and swore by God that he had been given something for it that he had not been given, in order to cause a Muslim to fall into it, so this verse was revealed: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price Al-Bukhari. It was narrated by Al-Bukhari from more than one source on the authority of Al-Awam. The sixth hadith Imam Ahmad said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three whom God will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He look at them, nor will He purify them, and they will have a painful punishment: a man who prevents a wayfarer from having excess water with him, a man who swears an oath regarding a commodity after the afternoon prayer, meaning falsely, and a man who pledges allegiance to an imam, so if he gives him something he fulfills it for him, and if he does not give him something he does not fulfill it for him.” Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Wakee’, and Al-Tirmidhi said: A good and sound hadith.
3:78: The Almighty tells us about the Jews, upon them be the curses of God, that there is a group among them who distort words from their places, and change the words of God and remove them from what is intended, to make the ignorant think that it is in the Book of God as well, and they attribute it to God, which is a lie against God, and they know from themselves that they have lied and fabricated all of that, and for this reason God the Almighty said: And they speak lies about God while they know. Mujahid, Al-Sha'bi, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Al-Rabi' bin Anas said: They distort the Book with their tongues they distort it, and thus Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that they distort and add, and no one among God’s creation removes the wording of a Book from God’s Books, but they distort it and interpret it in a way other than its interpretation. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: The Torah and the Gospel are as God Almighty revealed them, not a single word of them was changed, but they go astray by distorting and interpreting, and books that they wrote from themselves and they say, ‘It is from God,’ but it is not from God. As for the Books of God, they are preserved and not changed. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. If Wahb meant what they have in their hands of that, then there is no doubt that it has been changed, distorted, added, and subtracted. As for translating that scene into Arabic, there is a great error in it and many additions, subtractions, and gross delusion, and it is from the category of the interpreter’s interpretation of the interpreter, and the understanding of many of them, rather most of them, rather all of them, is corrupt. But if he meant the Books of God, which are His Books with him, then those are as he said: preserved, nothing has entered them.
3:79: Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad told us, on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Rafi' al-Qurazi said: When the Jewish and Christian rabbis from Najran gathered at the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he called them to Islam: Do you want us, O Muhammad, to worship you as the Christians worship Jesus, son of Mary? A Christian man from Najran called al-Ra'is said: Is that what you want from us, O Muhammad, and to which you are calling us? Or as he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God forbid that we worship other than God, or that we command the worship of other than God, for this is not what He sent me for, nor did He command me for this. Or as he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: So God revealed regarding that from their saying: “It is not for a human being that God should give him the Book and wisdom and prophethood, then he should say to the people, ‘Be my servants instead of God. ’” That is, it is not appropriate for a human being to whom God has given the Book, wisdom and prophethood, to say to the people, ‘Worship me instead of God,’ meaning with God. So if this is not appropriate for a prophet or a messenger, then it is not appropriate for any other people except them, by a fortiori and more appropriate. For this reason, Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: This is not appropriate for a believer to command the people to worship him. He said: That is because the people used to worship each other, meaning the People of the Book used to worship their rabbis and monks, as God Almighty said: They took their rabbis and monks as lords instead of God. And in Al-Musnad and Al-Tirmidhi, as will come, it is narrated that Adi bin Hatim said: O Messenger of God, they did not worship them. He said: Yes, they did. They made lawful for them what is unlawful and made unlawful for them what is lawful, so follow them, and that is their worship of them.” So the ignorant rabbis, monks, and sheikhs of misguidance are included in this blame and rebuke, unlike the Messengers and their followers from the working scholars, for they only command what God commands, and His noble Messengers conveyed it to them, and they only forbid them from what God forbade them from and His noble Messengers conveyed it to them. The Messengers, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them all, are the ambassadors between God and His creation in carrying out what they were entrusted with of the message and conveying the trust, so they carried out that perfectly, and advised the creation, and conveyed the truth to them. And His statement: But be devout scholars because you have taught the Book and because you have studied it, meaning, but the Messenger says to the people, Be devout scholars. Ibn Abbas, Abu Razin, and more than one said: That is, wise scholars, forbearing. Al-Hasan and more than one said: Jurists. And this is also narrated from Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubayr, Qatadah, Ata’ al-Khurasani, Atiyah al-Awfi, and al-Rabi’ bin Anas, and from al-Hasan also: That is, people of worship. And people of piety. Ad-Dahhak said in his statement: Because you have taught the Book and studied it: It is the right of the one who has learned the Qur’an to be a jurist. You learn means you understand its meaning. You learn was read with emphasis from teaching. And because you have studied means you memorize its words. Then God the Most High said: And He does not command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords meaning, and He does not command you to worship anyone other than God: neither a sent prophet nor a close angel. Would He command you to disbelieve after you have been Muslims? meaning, no one would do that except the one who called to worship other than God. And whoever called to worship other than God has called to disbelief. The prophets only command faith, which is the worship of God alone, with no partner for Him, as God the Most High said: And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no god except Me, so worship Me. And God the Most High said: And We have certainly sent among every nation a messenger, [saying], ‘Worship God and avoid false deities’ verse, and He said: And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers. Have We made gods to be worshipped besides the Most Merciful?” And He said, informing us about the angels, “And whoever among them says, ‘I am a god besides Him,’ We will recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.”

3:81: God Almighty tells us that He took a covenant from every prophet He sent from Adam, peace be upon him, to Jesus, peace be upon him, that no matter what book and wisdom God gave to one of them, and he reached any level, then a messenger came to him after him, he would believe in him and support him, and what he had of knowledge and prophethood would not prevent him from following and supporting whoever was sent after him. For this reason, God Almighty said, “And when God took a covenant from the prophets, ‘Whatever I give you of the Book and wisdom, then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him. He said, ‘Have you acknowledged and taken upon yourself My burden?’” Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, Qatadah, and As-Suddi said, it means My covenant. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, My burden means the weight of what you have carried of My covenant, meaning My strong and confirmed covenant. They said, We have acknowledged it. He said, “Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses. But whoever turns away after that,” meaning from this covenant and covenant, then those are the wicked. Ali ibn Abu Talib and his cousin Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: God did not send a prophet from the prophets except that He took a covenant from him, that if God sent Muhammad while he was alive, they would believe in him and support him, and He ordered him to take a covenant from his nation, that if Muhammad was sent while they were alive, they would believe in him and support him. Tawus, Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Qatadah said: God took a covenant from the prophets that they would believe in each other, and this does not contradict what Ali and Ibn Abbas said nor does it negate it, rather it requires it and requires it, and for this reason Abd Al-Razzaq narrated from Muammar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, like the saying of Ali and Ibn Abbas. Imam Ahmad said: Abd Al-Razzaq told us, Sufyan told us, from Jabir, from Al-Sha’bi, from Abdullah bin Thabit, who said: “Umar came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I passed by a brother of mine who was a Jew from Qurayza, and he wrote for me comprehensive verses from the Torah. Should I not present them to you?” He said, so the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, changed. Abdullah bin Thabit said, I said to him: Do you not see what is on the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? Umar said: We are pleased with God as our Lord, with Islam as our religion, and with Muhammad as our Messenger. He said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was relieved and he said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if Moses, peace be upon him, were to appear among you and you were to follow him and abandon me, you would go astray. You are my portion among the nations, and I am your portion among the prophets. Another Hadith Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr said: Ishaq told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Do not ask the People of the Book about anything, for they will not guide you and they have gone astray. You will either believe in falsehood or deny the truth. By God, if Moses were alive among you, he would have no choice but to follow me.’” In some Hadiths it says: If Moses and Jesus were alive, they would have no choice but to follow me. So the Messenger Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, will always remain until the Day of Judgment. He is the greatest Imam, and if he had existed in any era, he would have been the one whose obedience is obligatory and who is preferred over all the Prophets. For this reason, he was their Imam on the Night of the Isra’ when they gathered in the Holy House. Likewise, he is the intercessor on the Day of Resurrection when the Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, comes to decide the judgment between His servants. He is the praised station that is only befitting of Him, and from which the resolute prophets and messengers deviate until the turn comes to Him, and he is the one singled out for it, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him.

3:83: The Almighty says, denying whoever wants a religion other than the religion of God, with which He sent His books and with which He sent His messengers, which is the worship of God alone, with no partner for Him, to whom everyone in the heavens and the earth submits, meaning everyone in them submits to Him willingly or unwillingly, as God the Almighty says: And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, the verse, and God the Almighty says: “Have they not seen what God has created of things? They turn their shadows to the right and the left, prostrating to God, and they are humbled. And to God prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures, and the angels, and they are not arrogant. They fear their Lord above them and do what they are commanded.” So the believer submits with his heart and body to God, and the disbeliever submits to God unwillingly, for he is under subjugation, coercion, and the great authority that does not oppose or resist. A hadith was reported in the interpretation of this verse with another meaning that is strange, so Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani said: Ahmad bin Al-Nadr Al-Askari told us, Saeed bin Hafs Al-Nufaili told us, Muhammad bin Muhsin Al-Akashi told us, Al-Awza’i told us, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, And to Him submits everyone in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly. “As for those in the heavens, they are the angels, and as for those on the earth, they are those who were born as Muslims, and as for those who were unwillingly, they are those who were brought from the captives of the nations in chains and shackles, they are led to Paradise unwillingly.” It was mentioned in Sahih: Your Lord is amazed at a people who are led to Paradise in chains. And there will be evidence for it from another source, but the first meaning of the verse is stronger. Waki’ said in his interpretation: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion. He said: It is like His saying: And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say, ‘God.’ He also said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion. He said: When the covenant was taken, And to Him they will be returned, meaning on the Day of Resurrection, when He will reward each one according to his deeds. Then God the Almighty said: Say, ‘We believe in God and what was revealed to us,’ meaning the Qur’an, “and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, and Jacob,’ meaning of the scriptures and revelation, “and the tribes, meaning the clans of the Children of Israel branching off from the twelve sons of Israel, who is Jacob, and what was given to Moses and Jesus, meaning by that the Torah. The Gospel, And the prophets are from their Lord, and this includes all the prophets. The phrase We make no distinction between any of them means: Rather, we believe in all of them, and we are Muslims to Him. So the believers of this nation believe in every prophet who was sent, and in every book that was revealed. They do not disbelieve in any of that, rather they believe in what was revealed from God, and in every prophet that God sent. Then God Almighty said: And whoever desires other than Islam as religion - never will it be accepted from him verse, meaning whoever follows a path other than what God has prescribed, it will not be accepted from him and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in the authentic hadith: Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our command, it will be rejected. And thus it was narrated, and its chain of transmission is good. Then God the Almighty said: Indeed, those who disbelieved and died… And they are disbelievers, so the earth full of gold will not be accepted from any of them, even if he ransomed himself with it. That is, whoever dies as a disbeliever, no good will ever be accepted from him. Even if he spent the earth full of gold in what he considered to be an act of devotion, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about Abdullah bin Jud’an, who used to host guests, free the captive, and feed the poor: Will that benefit him? He said, “No, he never said a single day in his life: ‘My Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment.’” Likewise, if he ransomed himself with the earth full of gold, it would not be accepted from him, as God Almighty said, And no compensation will be accepted from them, nor will intercession benefit them. And He said, There is no trade in it nor friendship. And He said, “Indeed, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is in the earth and the like thereof with it to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them, and they will have a painful punishment.” And for this reason the Almighty said here: Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers - never will it be accepted from one of them an earth full of gold, even if he were to ransom himself with it. So He connected even if he were to ransom himself with the first, so it indicates that he is not the same. And what we mentioned is better than saying that the waw is redundant, and God knows best. And that requires that nothing will save him from the punishment of God, even if he had spent the equivalent of the earth in gold, even if he ransomed himself from God with an earth full of gold, the weight of its mountains and hills, its soil and sand, its plains and rugged areas, its land and sea. And Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj told us, Shu’bah told me on the authority of Abu Imran al-Jawni, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A man from the people of Hell will be told on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Tell me, if you had everything on the earth, would you ransom yourself with it? He said: He will say: Yes. Then God will say: I wanted something easier from you than that. I took a covenant from you in the loins of your father Adam that you would not associate anything with Me, but you refused except to associate.” And so on. Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. Another way Imam Ahmad said: Ruh told us, Hammad told us on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A man from the people of Paradise will be brought and it will be said to him: O son of Adam, how did you find your home? He will say: O Lord, what is the best home? He will say: Ask and wish. He will say: I do not ask nor wish except that you return me to the world so that I may be killed in your path ten times, because of what he sees of the virtue of martyrdom. And a man from the people of Hell will be brought and it will be said to him: O son of Adam, how did you find your home? He will say: O Lord, what is the worst home. He will say: Will you ransom yourself from me with the weight of the earth in gold? He will say: O Lord, yes. He will say: You have lied. I asked you for less than that and easier and you did not do it, so he will be returned to Hell.” That is why He said: For those is a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers. That is, they will have no one to save them from the punishment of God or protect them from His painful chastisement.

Even if he spent the earth full of gold in what he considered to be an act of devotion, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about Abdullah bin Jud’an, who used to host guests, free the captive, and feed the poor: Will that benefit him? He said, “No, he never said a single day in his life: ‘My Lord, forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment.’” Likewise, if he ransomed himself with the earth full of gold, it would not be accepted from him, as God Almighty said, And no compensation will be accepted from them, nor will intercession benefit them. And He said, There is no trade in it nor friendship. And He said, “Indeed, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is in the earth and the like thereof with it to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them, and they will have a painful punishment.” And for this reason the Almighty said here: Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers - never will it be accepted from one of them an earth full of gold, even if he were to ransom himself with it. So He connected even if he were to ransom himself with the first, so it indicates that he is not the same. And what we mentioned is better than saying that the waw is redundant, and God knows best. And that requires that nothing will save him from the punishment of God, even if he had spent the equivalent of the earth in gold, even if he ransomed himself from God with an earth full of gold, the weight of its mountains and hills, its soil and sand, its plains and rugged areas, its land and sea. And Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj told us, Shu’bah told me on the authority of Abu Imran al-Jawni, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A man from the people of Hell will be told on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Tell me, if you had everything on the earth, would you ransom yourself with it? He said: He will say: Yes. Then God will say: I wanted something easier from you than that. I took a covenant from you in the loins of your father Adam that you would not associate anything with Me, but you refused except to associate.” And so on. Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. Another way Imam Ahmad said: Ruh told us, Hammad told us on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A man from the people of Paradise will be brought and it will be said to him: O son of Adam, how did you find your home? He will say: O Lord, what is the best home? He will say: Ask and wish. He will say: I do not ask nor wish except that you return me to the world so that I may be killed in your path ten times, because of what he sees of the virtue of martyrdom. And a man from the people of Hell will be brought and it will be said to him: O son of Adam, how did you find your home? He will say: O Lord, what is the worst home. He will say: Will you ransom yourself from me with the weight of the earth in gold? He will say: O Lord, yes. He will say: You have lied. I asked you for less than that and easier and you did not do it, so he will be returned to Hell.” That is why He said: For those is a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers. That is, they will have no one to save them from the punishment of God or protect them from His painful chastisement.
3:92: Waki' narrated in his interpretation on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, You will never attain righteousness, he said: Paradise. Imam Ahmad said: Ruh told us, Malik told us, on the authority of Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, he heard Anas ibn Malik say: Abu Talhah was the wealthiest of the Ansar in Medina, and the most beloved of his wealth to him was Bayra'a, which was facing the mosque. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to enter it and drink from its pure water. Anas said: When the verse, You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love, was revealed, Abu Talhah said: O Messenger of God, God says, You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love, and the most beloved of my wealth to me is Bayra'a, and it is a charity for God, and I hope for its righteousness and its storage with God Almighty, so put it, O Messenger of God, where God wills you to put it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, "Good, good, that is profitable wealth, that is profitable wealth, and I heard and I think that you should put it in The closest relatives, Abu Talha said, I will, O Messenger of God. So Abu Talha divided it among his relatives and cousins. They both narrated it. In the two Sahihs, it is narrated that Umar said, “O Messenger of God, I have never acquired wealth that is more precious to me than my share in Khaybar. What do you command me to do with it?” He said, Keep the principal and distribute the fruits. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Abu al-Khattab Ziyad ibn Yahya al-Hassani narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Amr ibn Hamas, on the authority of Hamza ibn Abdullah ibn Omar, who said: Abdullah said: This verse came to my mind: You will not attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. So I remembered what God had given me, and I did not find anything more beloved to me than a Roman slave girl of mine. I said: She is free for the sake of God. If I were to return to something that I had given to God, I would marry her, meaning I married her.
3:93: Imam Ahmad said: Hisham bin Al-Qasim told us, Abdul Hamid told us, Shahr told us, he said: Ibn Abbas said: “A group of Jews attended the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: Tell us about characteristics that we ask you about, which only a prophet knows. He said: Ask me about whatever you wish, but give me the protection of God, and what Jacob took from his sons, if I tell you something and you understand it, you will follow me in Islam. They said: That is for you. He said: Ask me about whatever you wish. They said: Tell us about four characteristics: Tell us what food Israel forbade himself? And how is the woman’s water and the man’s water? And how is the male and female from it? And tell us how this illiterate prophet sleeps, and who is his guardian from the angels? So he took a covenant from them that if he told them, they would follow him. He said: I ask you by the One who sent down the Torah to Moses, do you know that Israel fell seriously ill and his illness lasted a long time, so he made a vow to God that if God cured him of his illness To forbid the most beloved food and drink to him, while the most beloved food to him was camel meat, and the most beloved drink to him was camel milk? They said: O God, yes. He said: O God, bear witness against them. He said: I ask you by God, there is no god but Him, Who sent down the Torah to Moses, do you know that the man's semen is white and thick, and the woman's semen is yellow and thin, so whichever of them is higher will have the child, and the resemblance is by God's permission. If the man's semen rises above the woman's semen, it will be a boy, by God's permission, and if the woman's semen rises above the man's semen, it will be a girl, by God's permission? They said: Yes. He said: O God, bear witness against them. He said: I ask you by Him Who sent down the Torah to Moses, do you know that the eyes of this unlettered prophet sleep but his heart does not? They said: O God, yes. He said: O God, bear witness. They said: And you now, tell us who is your guardian among the angels? Then we will have intercourse with you and leave you. He said: My guardian is Gabriel, and God never sent a prophet except that he was his guardian. They said: Then we will leave you. If your guardian were other than him, we would have followed you. Then God Almighty said: “Say: Who is an enemy to Gabriel?” The verse, and Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Hussein bin Muhammad on the authority of Abdul Hamid on his authority. Another way Ahmad said: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us, Abdullah ibn al-Waleed al-Ajli told us, on the authority of Bakir ibn Shihab, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Jews came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Abu al-Qasim, we ask you about five things. If you inform us of them, we will know that you are a prophet and we will follow you. So he took from them what Israel took from his sons when he said: ‘And God is witness over what we say.’ He said: Bring them. They said: Tell us about the sign of the Prophet. He said: His eyes sleep but his heart does not sleep. They said: Tell us how a woman becomes feminine and how she becomes masculine? He said: The two waters meet, so if the man’s water rises above the woman’s water, she becomes masculine, and if the woman’s water rises above the woman’s water, she becomes feminine. They said: Tell us what Israel forbade himself? He said: He used to suffer from sciatica, and he did not find anything that suited him except the milk of such-and-such - Ahmad said: Some of them said: He meant camels - so he forbade their meat. They said: You have spoken the truth. They said: Tell us, what is this thunder? He said: An angel. From the angels of God, the Almighty, he is entrusted with the clouds. In his hand - or in his hands - is a whip of fire with which he drives the clouds, driving them where God, the Almighty, commands them. They said: What is this voice that is heard? He said: His voice. They said: You have spoken the truth. There is only one thing left, and it is the one that we will follow if you inform us of it. There is no prophet but that he has an angel who brings him report. So inform us who is your companion? He said: Gabriel, peace be upon him. They said: Gabriel, that one, descends with war, fighting and torment, our enemy. If you had said: Michael, who descends with mercy, plants and rain, it would have been... Then God Almighty revealed: “Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - for indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart by permission of God, confirming what was before it and as guidance and good tidings for the believers.” And the verse after it. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Abdullah bin Al-Waleed Al-Ajli, with a similar meaning. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is strange. Ibn Jurayj and Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Israel, peace be upon him - he is Jacob - was afflicted with sciatica at night, and it would disturb him and prevent him from sleeping, and the pain would go away from him during the day, so he vowed to God that if God healed him, he would not eat a vein nor would a child eat one that had a vein. And this is what Al-Dahhak and Al-Suddi said. This is how Ibn Jarir narrated it and related it in his interpretation. He said: His sons followed him in forbidding that, following his example and imitating his method. He said: And his saying before he… “The Torah was revealed” means that he forbade himself from that before the Torah was revealed. I said: This context, after it was presented, has two reasons: One of them is that Israel, peace be upon him, forbade the things he loved most and left them for God, and this was permissible in their law, so it has a reason after his saying: You will not attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. This is what is permissible according to us, which is spending in obedience to God from that which the servant loves and desires, as God Almighty said: And he gives wealth, in spite of his love for it. God Almighty also said: And they feed the poor, in spite of their love for it. The second occasion When the statement of the response to the Christians, their false belief in the Messiah, and the clarification of the falsehood of what they went to and the emergence of the truth and certainty in the matter of Jesus and his mother, how God created him with His power and will and sent him to the Children of Israel calling to the worship of His Lord, the Blessed and Most High, began to respond to the Jews, may God curse them, and to clarify that the abrogation that they denied had occurred and was permissible, for God Almighty stated in their book, the Torah, that when Noah, peace be upon him, left the ship, God permitted him to eat from all the animals of the earth, then after this Israel forbade himself the meat and milk of camels, and his sons followed him in that, and the Torah came with the prohibition of that, and other things in addition to that, and God Almighty had permitted Adam to marry his daughters to his sons, and He prohibited that after that, and taking a wife as a concubine was permissible in the law of Abraham, peace be upon him, and Abraham did it with Hagar when he took her as a concubine to Sarah, and something like this was prohibited for them in the Torah, and likewise the union of two sisters It is permissible, and Jacob, peace be upon him, did it, he married two sisters, then he forbade them that in the Torah, and all of this is stipulated in the Torah for them, and this is abrogation itself, so let what God legislated for Christ, peace be upon him, be like that, in his making permissible some of what was forbidden in the Torah, so why did they not follow him? Rather, they denied him and opposed him? And likewise what God sent Muhammad, peace be upon him, with of the true religion, the straight path, and the religion of his father Abraham, so why do they not believe? That is why God Almighty said: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel had forbidden to himself before the Torah was revealed. That is, all foods were lawful to them before the Torah was revealed except what Israel had forbidden. Then God Almighty said: “Say: ‘Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful. ’” For it speaks of what we have said. But whoever invents a lie against God after that, it is those who are the wrongdoers. That is, whoever lies about God and claims that He has prescribed for them the Sabbath and that they should always adhere to the Torah, and that He did not send another prophet to call to God with proofs and arguments after what we have explained of the occurrence of abrogation and the emergence of what we have mentioned. It is those who are the wrongdoers. Then God Almighty said: “Say: God has spoken the truth.” That is, say, O Muhammad, God has spoken the truth in what He has informed us of and in what He has prescribed in the Qur’an. So follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists. That is, follow the religion of Abraham that God prescribed in the Qur’an on the tongue of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for it is the truth about which there is no doubt or uncertainty, and it is the way that no prophet has come with anything more perfect or clearer than it. There is nothing clearer or more complete than what God Almighty said: Say, ‘Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a right religion, the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with God.’ God Almighty also said: Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], to follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with God.
