The second occasion When the statement of the response to the Christians, their false belief in the Messiah, and the clarification of the falsehood of what they went to and the emergence of the truth and certainty in the matter of Jesus and his mother, how God created him with His power and will and sent him to the Children of Israel calling to the worship of His Lord, the Blessed and Most High, began to respond to the Jews, may God curse them, and to clarify that the abrogation that they denied had occurred and was permissible, for God Almighty stated in their book, the Torah, that when Noah, peace be upon him, left the ship, God permitted him to eat from all the animals of the earth, then after this Israel forbade himself the meat and milk of camels, and his sons followed him in that, and the Torah came with the prohibition of that, and other things in addition to that, and God Almighty had permitted Adam to marry his daughters to his sons, and He prohibited that after that, and taking a wife as a concubine was permissible in the law of Abraham, peace be upon him, and Abraham did it with Hagar when he took her as a concubine to Sarah, and something like this was prohibited for them in the Torah, and likewise the union of two sisters It is permissible, and Jacob, peace be upon him, did it, he married two sisters, then he forbade them that in the Torah, and all of this is stipulated in the Torah for them, and this is abrogation itself, so let what God legislated for Christ, peace be upon him, be like that, in his making permissible some of what was forbidden in the Torah, so why did they not follow him? Rather, they denied him and opposed him? And likewise what God sent Muhammad, peace be upon him, with of the true religion, the straight path, and the religion of his father Abraham, so why do they not believe? That is why God Almighty said: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel had forbidden to himself before the Torah was revealed. That is, all foods were lawful to them before the Torah was revealed except what Israel had forbidden. Then God Almighty said: “Say: ‘Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful. ’” For it speaks of what we have said. But whoever invents a lie against God after that, it is those who are the wrongdoers. That is, whoever lies about God and claims that He has prescribed for them the Sabbath and that they should always adhere to the Torah, and that He did not send another prophet to call to God with proofs and arguments after what we have explained of the occurrence of abrogation and the emergence of what we have mentioned. It is those who are the wrongdoers. Then God Almighty said: “Say: God has spoken the truth.” That is, say, O Muhammad, God has spoken the truth in what He has informed us of and in what He has prescribed in the Qur’an. So follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists. That is, follow the religion of Abraham that God prescribed in the Qur’an on the tongue of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for it is the truth about which there is no doubt or uncertainty, and it is the way that no prophet has come with anything more perfect or clearer than it. There is nothing clearer or more complete than what God Almighty said: Say, ‘Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a right religion, the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with God.’ God Almighty also said: Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], to follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with God.
3:96: The Almighty informs us that the first House established for mankind, that is, for all people, for their worship and rituals, to circumambulate it, pray to it, and seclude themselves at it, was the one at Bakkah meaning the Kaaba that was built by Abraham, peace be upon him, whom both the Christian and Jewish sects claim to follow his religion and method, and they do not perform Hajj to the House that he built by God's command to him in that and called people to perform Hajj, and for this reason the Almighty said: Blessed meaning it was established blessedly and a guidance for the worlds. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taymi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: "I said, O Messenger of God, which mosque was established on earth first? He said, Al-Masjid Al-Haram. I said: Then which? He said, Al-Masjid Al-Aqsa. I said: How much time is between them? He said: Forty years. I said: Then which? He said: Then wherever you find the prayer, pray, for all of it is a mosque." Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Al-A'mash with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Saeed bin Sulaiman told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding the words of God Almighty: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah - blessed. He said: There were houses before it, but it was the first house established for the worship of God. My father told us, Al-Hasan bin Al-Rabi’ told us, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara, who said: A man stood up to Ali, may God be pleased with him, and said: Will you not tell me about the House? Was it the first house established on earth? He said: No, but it was the first house in which blessing was established, the Station of Abraham, and whoever entered it was safe. He mentioned the full story of how Abraham built the House, and we have mentioned that in detail at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah, so there is no need to repeat it here. Al-Suddi claimed that it was the first house established on the face of the earth absolutely, and the correct statement is that of Ali, may God be pleased with him. As for the hadith that Al-Bayhaqi narrated in the construction of the Kaaba in his book, Evidences of Prophethood, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Abu Al-Khair, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Al-Aas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that God sent Gabriel to Adam and Eve and commanded them to build the Kaaba. So Adam built it, then he was commanded to circumambulate it, and it was said to him: You are the first of mankind, and this is the first House established for mankind, then as you see it is from the individual hadiths of Ibn Lahi’ah, and he is weak. What is more likely, and God knows best, is that this is attributed to Abdullah ibn Amr, and it is from the two Zamilah that were afflicted on the Day of Yarmouk from the words of the People of the Book. God the Almighty said: For the one at Bakkah. Bakkah is one of the names of Mecca according to the well-known. It was said: It was named thus because it weeps the necks of the oppressors and tyrants, meaning that they are humiliated and submissive there. It was also said: Because people weep in it, meaning they crowd together. Qatada said: God has made all people in it, so women pray in front of men and He does not do that in any other city. This was also narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Amr bin Shuaib, and Muqatil bin Hayyan. Hammad bin Salamah narrated on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: Mecca is from Al-Faj to At-Tan’im, and Bakkah is from the House to Al-Batha’. Shu’bah said, on the authority of Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim: Bakkah is the House and the Mosque. Al-Zuhri said the same. Ikrimah said, in one narration, and Maymun bin Mihran: The House and what is around it is Bakkah, and what is beyond that is Mecca. Abu Saleh, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Atiyah Al-Awfi and Muqatil bin Hayyan said: Bakkah is the location of the House, and everything else is Mecca. They mentioned many names for Mecca: Mecca, Bakkah, the Ancient House, the Sacred House, the Safe City, Al-Ma’mun, Umm Rahm, Umm Al-Qura, Salah, the Throne on the same weight as Badr, Al-Qadis because it purifies from sins, Al-Muqaddasah, Al-Naasah with a nun, and also with a ba’, Al-Hatima, Al-Nasasa, Al-Ra’s, Kutha’, Al-Balda, Al-Bunya, and Al-Ka’bah. And the Almighty’s saying: In it are clear signs meaning clear evidence that it was built by Abraham, and that God made it great and honored. Then the Almighty said: The Station of Abraham meaning that when the building was raised, he used it to help raise its foundations and walls, where he used to stand and hand it to Ishmael. It was attached to the wall of the House until Omar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him moved it during his rule to the eastern side so that it would be possible to circumambulate it, and not disturb those praying at it after circumambulating, because God Almighty has commanded us to pray at it when He said: And take, [O Muhammad], the Station of Abraham as a place of prayer. We have already presented the hadiths on that, so there is no need to repeat them here. Praise and thanks be to God. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his saying: In it are clear signs, the Station of Abraham meaning that among them is the Station of Abraham and the Monument. Mujahid said: The trace of his feet in the Station is a clear sign. This was also narrated on the authority of Omar bin Abdul Aziz, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi, Muqatil bin Hayyan, and others. Abu Talib said in his famous poem, Al-Lamiyyah: And Abraham's footsteps in the rock were wet on his bare feet, without sandals. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed and Amr Al-Awdi told us: Waki’ told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God the Almighty: The Station of Abraham, he said: The entire Sanctuary is the Station of Abraham. Amr’s wording is: The entire Stone is the Station of Abraham. It was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that he said: The Hajj is the Station of Abraham. This is how I saw it in the copy, and perhaps the entire Stone is the Station of Abraham. Mujahid stated this explicitly. And the words of God the Almighty: And whoever enters it shall be safe, meaning the Sanctuary of Mecca. If the fearful enters it, he is safe from all harm. This was the case in the time of ignorance, as Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others said: A man would be killed and a wool would be placed around his neck and he would enter the Sanctuary, and the son of the murdered man would meet him and not disturb him until he came out. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashja told us, Abu Yahya Al-Taymi told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God Almighty: And whoever enters it shall be safe, he said: Whoever seeks refuge in the House, the House will protect him, but he shall not be sheltered, fed, or given water. So if he leaves, he will be seized for his sin. God Almighty said: Have they not seen that We have made a secure sanctuary, while people are being snatched away from all around them? The verse, and God Almighty said: So let them worship the Lord of this House, Who has fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear. And among its prohibitions is the prohibition of hunting its game and scaring it away from its nests, and the prohibition of cutting its trees and uprooting its grass, as the hadiths and reports on that have been proven from a group of the Companions, both with and without chains of transmission. In the two Sahihs, and the wording is from Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of the conquest of Mecca, ‘There is no migration, but jihad and intention, and if you are called to arms, then go out. ’ And he said on the day of the conquest of Mecca, ‘This country was made sacred by God on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by God’s sanctity until the Day of Resurrection. Fighting in it was not permitted for anyone before me, and it was not permitted for me except during one hour of the day, so it is sacred by God’s sanctity until the Day of Resurrection. Its thorns should not be cut, its game should not be frightened, its lost items should not be picked up except by one who recognizes them, and its solitude should not be taken away. ’ Al-Abbas said, ‘O Messenger of God, except for idhkhir, for it is their herb and for their houses. ’ He said, ‘Except idhkhir. ’” And they have a similar or similar narration from Abu Hurairah, and they have a similar narration from Abu Shuraih al-Adawi as well, that he said to Amr ibn Saeed while he was sending out the expeditions to Mecca, ‘Give me permission, O prince, to tell you a statement that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said the next day on the day of the conquest. My ears heard it and I remembered it. ’ My heart, and my eyes saw it when he spoke it, that he praised and extolled God, then he said: "God has made Mecca sacred, and people have not made it sacred. It is not permissible for a man who believes in God and the Last Day to shed blood there, or cut down a tree there. If someone seeks permission to fight the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, there, then say to him: God has given permission to His Messenger and has not given you permission. He has only given me permission there for an hour of a day, and its sanctity has returned today to what it was yesterday, so let the witness inform the absent." It was said to Abu Shuraih: What did Amr say to you? He said: I know that better than you, O Abu Shuraih. The sanctuary does not protect a sinner, nor one who flees with blood, nor one who flees with disgrace. Jabir, may God be pleased with him, said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: It is not permissible for any of you to carry weapons in Mecca. Narrated by Muslim. On the authority of Abdullah bin Adi bin Al-Hamra Al-Zuhri that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was standing in Al-Huzura in the market of Mecca, saying, “By God, you are the best land of God, and the most beloved land of God to God. Had I not been expelled from you, I would not have left.” Narrated by Imam Ahmad, and this is his wording, and by Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan sahih. He also authenticated a hadith similar to it from Ibn Abbas. Ahmad narrated a similar hadith from Abu Hurayrah. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Bishr bin Adam bin Bint Azhar Al-Samman told us, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Zuraiq bin Muslim Al-Ama, a client of Banu Makhzum, on the authority of Ziyad bin Abi Ayyash, on the authority of Yahya bin Ja’dah bin Hubaira, regarding the words of God the Almighty: And whoever enters it shall be safe, he said: Safe from the Fire. And in the meaning of this statement is the hadith narrated by Al-Bayhaqi: Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Ahmad bin Abdun told us, Ahmad bin Ubaid told us, Muhammad bin Sulayman Al-Wasiti told us, Saeed bin Sulayman told us, Ibn Al-Mu'ammil told us, on the authority of Ibn Muhaisin, on the authority of Ata', on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever enters the House, enters into a good deed, exits from a bad deed, and exits forgiven. Then he said: Abdullah bin Al-Mu'ammil is the only one who narrated it, and it is not strong. And his statement, And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God, those who can afford the expenses for the journey to it, this is a verse of the obligation of Hajj according to the majority of scholars. It was said: Rather, it is his statement, And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God, and the first is more apparent. Multiple hadiths have been reported that it is one of the pillars, foundations, and foundations of Islam, and the Muslims have unanimously agreed upon this, and it is only obligatory for the accountable person once in a lifetime, according to the text and consensus. Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Al-Rabi’ bin Muslim Al-Qurashi told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon to us and said: O people, Hajj has been made obligatory upon you, so perform Hajj. A man said: Every year, O Messenger of God? He was silent until he said it three times. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If I had said yes, it would have been obligatory and you would not have been able to do it. Then he said: “Leave me as I have left you, for those who came before you were destroyed because of their excessive questioning and disagreement with their prophets. If I command you to do something, do as much of it as you can, and if I forbid you from something, leave it.” Muslim narrated it similarly on the authority of Zuhair bin Harb on the authority of Yazid bin Harun. Sufyan bin Husayn, Sulayman bin Katheer, Abdul Jalil bin Hamid and Muhammad bin Abi Hafsah narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Sinan Al-Du’ali, whose name was Yazid bin Umayyah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon to us and said: O people, God has prescribed Hajj for you. Then Al-Aqra’ bin Habis stood up and said: O Messenger of God, is it every year? He said: “If I had said it, it would have been obligatory, and if it were obligatory, you would not have performed it and you would not have been able to perform it. Hajj is performed once, so whoever performs more than that, it is voluntary.” Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah and Al-Hakim from the hadith of Al-Zuhri with it. It was narrated by Sharik from Samak from Ikrimah from Ibn Abbas in a similar manner. It was narrated from the hadith of Usamah bin Yazid. Imam Ahmad said: Mansur bin Wardan narrated to us on the authority of Ali bin Abdul-Ala, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Al-Bukhtari, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the verse, And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God, those who can afford the expenses for one’s expenses, was revealed, they said, O Messenger of God, every year? He was silent. They said, O Messenger of God, every year? He said, No, and if I had said yes, it would have been obligatory. Then God Almighty revealed, O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are made known to you, may distress you. This is how Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, and Al-Hakim narrated it on the authority of Mansur bin Wardan. Then Al-Tirmidhi said, Hasan Gharib, and what he said is questionable, because Al-Bukhari said, Abu Al-Bukhtari did not hear it from Ali. Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Ubaydah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: They said: O Messenger of God, is Hajj every year? He said: If you had said yes, it would be obligatory, and if it were obligatory, you would not have performed it, and if you did not perform it, you would have been punished. And in the two Sahihs, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Suraqah ibn Malik, “He said: O Messenger of God, is this enjoyment of ours for this year, or forever?” He said: No, rather forever. And in another narration: Rather, forever and ever. In Musnad of Imam Ahmad and Sunan Abi Dawud, from the hadith of Waqid bin Abi Waqid Al-Laithi, from his father, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his wives during his Hajj: This is the time when the confinement will appear - meaning, then the time when the confinement will appear - and do not leave the houses. As for the ability, it is divided into sections: Sometimes a person is able to do it by himself, and sometimes by someone else, as is established in the books of rulings. Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi said: Abd bin Hamid told us, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, Ibrahim bin Yazid told us, he said: I heard Muhammad bin Ibad bin Ja’far narrating from Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, “He said: A man stood up to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Who is the pilgrim, O Messenger of God? He said: The disheveled one who has spitting. Another stood up and said: Which Hajj is best, O Messenger of God? He said: The one who is tired and has spitting. Another stood up and said: What is the way, O Messenger of God? He said: The provisions and the mount.” And Ibn Majah narrated it in this way from the hadith of Ibrahim bin Yazid, who is Al-Khawzi. Al-Tirmidhi said: We do not know it except from his hadith, and some scholars have spoken about it. Before he memorized it, he said here and he said in the Book of Hajj: This is a good hadith. There is no doubt that the men of this chain of transmission are all trustworthy except for this Al-Khawzi, and they spoke about him because of this hadith, but others followed him, so Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah Al-Amiri told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair Al-Laithi told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ibad bin Jaafar, he said: I sat with Abdullah bin Umar, he said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: What is the way? He said: Provisions and a mount.” And Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in this way from the narration of Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair with it. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, Anas, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ata’, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas and Qatadah something similar to that, and this hadith has been narrated from other paths from the hadith of Anas, Abdullah bin Abbas, Ibn Mas’ud and Aisha, all of them with chains of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, but there is a question about their chains of transmission as is established in the Book of Rulings, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh took care to collect the chains of transmission of this hadith. Al-Hakim narrated it from the hadith of Qatada on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the statement of God, the Almighty, Whoever can afford the expenses of making the journey to it. It was said: What is the expenses? He said: Provisions and a mount. Then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of Muslim, and they did not include it. Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, “He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to God by mankind, those who can afford the expenses of making the journey to it.” They said: O Messenger of God, what is the expenses of making the journey? He said: Provisions and a mount. Waki’ narrated it in his interpretation on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Yunus on his authority. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ismail, who is Abu Isra’il al-Mala’i, on the authority of Fadil, meaning Ibn Amr, on the authority of Sa’id Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Hasten to perform Hajj, for none of you knows what will happen to him.’” Ahmad also said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, al-Hasan Ibn Amr al-Faqimi told us, on the authority of Mihran Ibn Abi Safwan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever intends to perform Hajj should hasten.’” Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Musaddad on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah al-Dharee’ with it. Ibn Jubayr narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Whoever can afford it, he said: Whoever possesses three hundred dirhams has afforded it. And on the authority of his freed slave, Ikrimah, he said: The way is health. And Wakee’ ibn al-Jarrah narrated on the authority of Abu Janab, meaning al-Kalbi, on the authority of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Whoever can afford it, he said: provisions and a camel. And the statement of God Almighty, And whoever disbelieves, then indeed, God is independent of the worlds, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and more than one said: That is, whoever denies the obligation of Hajj has disbelieved, and God is independent of him. Saeed bin Mansour said on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: When the verse, And whoever desires other than Islam as religion - never will it be accepted from him, was revealed, the Jews said: We are Muslims. God Almighty said: So argue with them and make them fight, meaning, “Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: God has enjoined upon the Muslims the pilgrimage to the House, whoever is able to do so. They said: It is not prescribed for us, and they refused to make the pilgrimage.” God Almighty said: And whoever disbelieves - then indeed, God is free from need of the worlds. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Abdullah bin Jaafar told us, Ismail bin Abdullah bin Masoud told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim and Shadh bin Fayyad told us, they said: Hilal Abu Hashim Al-Khurasani told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Hamadani told us on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever owns provisions and a mount and does not perform Hajj to the House of God, it does not harm him if he dies a Jew or a Christian, because God said: ‘And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God, those who can afford the expenses for one’s expenses. But whoever disbelieves - then indeed, God is independent of the worlds.’” And Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Muslim bin Ibrahim, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in this way on the authority of Abu Zur’ah Al-Razi: Hilal bin Fayyad told us, Hilal Abu Hashim Al-Khurasani told us, and he mentioned it with his chain of transmission likewise, and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Yahya Al-Qat’i on the authority of Muslim bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Hilal bin Abdullah, the client of Rabi’ah bin Amr bin Muslim Al-Bahili, on his authority. He said: This is a strange hadith that we do not know except from this source, and there is talk about its chain of transmission, and Hilal is unknown, and Al-Harith is weak in hadith. Al-Bukhari said: This Hilal is a fabricator of hadith. Ibn Adi said: This hadith is not authentic. Abu Bakr Al-Ismaili Al-Hafiz narrated from the hadith of Abu Amr Al-Awza’i: Ismail bin Ubaidullah bin Abi Al-Muhajir told me, Abd Al-Rahman bin Ghanem told me that he heard Umar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him say: Whoever is able to perform Hajj but does not perform it, it is the same to him whether he dies a Jew or a Christian. This is a sound chain of transmission back to Umar may God be pleased with him. Saeed bin Mansour narrated in his Sunan from Al-Hasan Al-Basri, who said: Umar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him said: I was thinking of sending men to these regions to look for everyone who had a grandmother and did not perform Hajj, and impose the jizyah on them. They are not Muslims, they are not Muslims.
3:97: The Almighty informs us that the first House established for mankind, that is, for all people, for their worship and rituals, to circumambulate it, pray to it, and seclude themselves at it, was the one at Bakkah meaning the Kaaba that was built by Abraham, peace be upon him, whom both the Christian and Jewish sects claim to follow his religion and method, and they do not perform Hajj to the House that he built by God's command to him in that and called people to perform Hajj, and for this reason the Almighty said: Blessed meaning it was established blessedly and a guidance for the worlds. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taymi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: "I said, O Messenger of God, which mosque was established on earth first? He said, Al-Masjid Al-Haram. I said: Then which? He said, Al-Masjid Al-Aqsa. I said: How much time is between them? He said: Forty years. I said: Then which? He said: Then wherever you find the prayer, pray, for all of it is a mosque." Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Al-A'mash with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Saeed bin Sulaiman told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding the words of God Almighty: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah - blessed. He said: There were houses before it, but it was the first house established for the worship of God. My father told us, Al-Hasan bin Al-Rabi’ told us, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara, who said: A man stood up to Ali, may God be pleased with him, and said: Will you not tell me about the House? Was it the first house established on earth? He said: No, but it was the first house in which blessing was established, the Station of Abraham, and whoever entered it was safe. He mentioned the full story of how Abraham built the House, and we have mentioned that in detail at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah, so there is no need to repeat it here. Al-Suddi claimed that it was the first house established on the face of the earth absolutely, and the correct statement is that of Ali, may God be pleased with him. As for the hadith that Al-Bayhaqi narrated in the construction of the Kaaba in his book, Evidences of Prophethood, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Abu Al-Khair, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Al-Aas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that God sent Gabriel to Adam and Eve and commanded them to build the Kaaba. So Adam built it, then he was commanded to circumambulate it, and it was said to him: You are the first of mankind, and this is the first House established for mankind, then as you see it is from the individual hadiths of Ibn Lahi’ah, and he is weak. What is more likely, and God knows best, is that this is attributed to Abdullah ibn Amr, and it is from the two Zamilah that were afflicted on the Day of Yarmouk from the words of the People of the Book. God the Almighty said: For the one at Bakkah. Bakkah is one of the names of Mecca according to the well-known. It was said: It was named thus because it weeps the necks of the oppressors and tyrants, meaning that they are humiliated and submissive there. It was also said: Because people weep in it, meaning they crowd together. Qatada said: God has made all people in it, so women pray in front of men and He does not do that in any other city. This was also narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Amr bin Shuaib, and Muqatil bin Hayyan. Hammad bin Salamah narrated on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: Mecca is from Al-Faj to At-Tan’im, and Bakkah is from the House to Al-Batha’. Shu’bah said, on the authority of Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim: Bakkah is the House and the Mosque. Al-Zuhri said the same. Ikrimah said, in one narration, and Maymun bin Mihran: The House and what is around it is Bakkah, and what is beyond that is Mecca. Abu Saleh, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Atiyah Al-Awfi and Muqatil bin Hayyan said: Bakkah is the location of the House, and everything else is Mecca. They mentioned many names for Mecca: Mecca, Bakkah, the Ancient House, the Sacred House, the Safe City, Al-Ma’mun, Umm Rahm, Umm Al-Qura, Salah, the Throne on the same weight as Badr, Al-Qadis because it purifies from sins, Al-Muqaddasah, Al-Naasah with a nun, and also with a ba’, Al-Hatima, Al-Nasasa, Al-Ra’s, Kutha’, Al-Balda, Al-Bunya, and Al-Ka’bah. And the Almighty’s saying: In it are clear signs meaning clear evidence that it was built by Abraham, and that God made it great and honored. Then the Almighty said: The Station of Abraham meaning that when the building was raised, he used it to help raise its foundations and walls, where he used to stand and hand it to Ishmael. It was attached to the wall of the House until Omar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him moved it during his rule to the eastern side so that it would be possible to circumambulate it, and not disturb those praying at it after circumambulating, because God Almighty has commanded us to pray at it when He said: And take, [O Muhammad], the Station of Abraham as a place of prayer. We have already presented the hadiths on that, so there is no need to repeat them here. Praise and thanks be to God. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his saying: In it are clear signs, the Station of Abraham meaning that among them is the Station of Abraham and the Monument. Mujahid said: The trace of his feet in the Station is a clear sign. This was also narrated on the authority of Omar bin Abdul Aziz, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi, Muqatil bin Hayyan, and others. Abu Talib said in his famous poem, Al-Lamiyyah: And Abraham's footsteps in the rock were wet on his bare feet, without sandals. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed and Amr Al-Awdi told us: Waki’ told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God the Almighty: The Station of Abraham, he said: The entire Sanctuary is the Station of Abraham. Amr’s wording is: The entire Stone is the Station of Abraham. It was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that he said: The Hajj is the Station of Abraham. This is how I saw it in the copy, and perhaps the entire Stone is the Station of Abraham. Mujahid stated this explicitly. And the words of God the Almighty: And whoever enters it shall be safe, meaning the Sanctuary of Mecca. If the fearful enters it, he is safe from all harm. This was the case in the time of ignorance, as Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others said: A man would be killed and a wool would be placed around his neck and he would enter the Sanctuary, and the son of the murdered man would meet him and not disturb him until he came out. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashja told us, Abu Yahya Al-Taymi told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God Almighty: And whoever enters it shall be safe, he said: Whoever seeks refuge in the House, the House will protect him, but he shall not be sheltered, fed, or given water. So if he leaves, he will be seized for his sin. God Almighty said: Have they not seen that We have made a secure sanctuary, while people are being snatched away from all around them? The verse, and God Almighty said: So let them worship the Lord of this House, Who has fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear. And among its prohibitions is the prohibition of hunting its game and scaring it away from its nests, and the prohibition of cutting its trees and uprooting its grass, as the hadiths and reports on that have been proven from a group of the Companions, both with and without chains of transmission. In the two Sahihs, and the wording is from Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of the conquest of Mecca, ‘There is no migration, but jihad and intention, and if you are called to arms, then go out. ’ And he said on the day of the conquest of Mecca, ‘This country was made sacred by God on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by God’s sanctity until the Day of Resurrection. Fighting in it was not permitted for anyone before me, and it was not permitted for me except during one hour of the day, so it is sacred by God’s sanctity until the Day of Resurrection. Its thorns should not be cut, its game should not be frightened, its lost items should not be picked up except by one who recognizes them, and its solitude should not be taken away. ’ Al-Abbas said, ‘O Messenger of God, except for idhkhir, for it is their herb and for their houses. ’ He said, ‘Except idhkhir. ’” And they have a similar or similar narration from Abu Hurairah, and they have a similar narration from Abu Shuraih al-Adawi as well, that he said to Amr ibn Saeed while he was sending out the expeditions to Mecca, ‘Give me permission, O prince, to tell you a statement that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said the next day on the day of the conquest. My ears heard it and I remembered it. ’ My heart, and my eyes saw it when he spoke it, that he praised and extolled God, then he said: "God has made Mecca sacred, and people have not made it sacred. It is not permissible for a man who believes in God and the Last Day to shed blood there, or cut down a tree there. If someone seeks permission to fight the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, there, then say to him: God has given permission to His Messenger and has not given you permission. He has only given me permission there for an hour of a day, and its sanctity has returned today to what it was yesterday, so let the witness inform the absent." It was said to Abu Shuraih: What did Amr say to you? He said: I know that better than you, O Abu Shuraih. The sanctuary does not protect a sinner, nor one who flees with blood, nor one who flees with disgrace. Jabir, may God be pleased with him, said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: It is not permissible for any of you to carry weapons in Mecca. Narrated by Muslim. On the authority of Abdullah bin Adi bin Al-Hamra Al-Zuhri that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was standing in Al-Huzura in the market of Mecca, saying, “By God, you are the best land of God, and the most beloved land of God to God. Had I not been expelled from you, I would not have left.” Narrated by Imam Ahmad, and this is his wording, and by Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan sahih. He also authenticated a hadith similar to it from Ibn Abbas. Ahmad narrated a similar hadith from Abu Hurayrah. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Bishr bin Adam bin Bint Azhar Al-Samman told us, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Zuraiq bin Muslim Al-Ama, a client of Banu Makhzum, on the authority of Ziyad bin Abi Ayyash, on the authority of Yahya bin Ja’dah bin Hubaira, regarding the words of God the Almighty: And whoever enters it shall be safe, he said: Safe from the Fire. And in the meaning of this statement is the hadith narrated by Al-Bayhaqi: Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Ahmad bin Abdun told us, Ahmad bin Ubaid told us, Muhammad bin Sulayman Al-Wasiti told us, Saeed bin Sulayman told us, Ibn Al-Mu'ammil told us, on the authority of Ibn Muhaisin, on the authority of Ata', on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever enters the House, enters into a good deed, exits from a bad deed, and exits forgiven. Then he said: Abdullah bin Al-Mu'ammil is the only one who narrated it, and it is not strong. And his statement, And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God, those who can afford the expenses for the journey to it, this is a verse of the obligation of Hajj according to the majority of scholars. It was said: Rather, it is his statement, And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God, and the first is more apparent. Multiple hadiths have been reported that it is one of the pillars, foundations, and foundations of Islam, and the Muslims have unanimously agreed upon this, and it is only obligatory for the accountable person once in a lifetime, according to the text and consensus. Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Al-Rabi’ bin Muslim Al-Qurashi told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon to us and said: O people, Hajj has been made obligatory upon you, so perform Hajj. A man said: Every year, O Messenger of God? He was silent until he said it three times. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If I had said yes, it would have been obligatory and you would not have been able to do it. Then he said: “Leave me as I have left you, for those who came before you were destroyed because of their excessive questioning and disagreement with their prophets. If I command you to do something, do as much of it as you can, and if I forbid you from something, leave it.” Muslim narrated it similarly on the authority of Zuhair bin Harb on the authority of Yazid bin Harun. Sufyan bin Husayn, Sulayman bin Katheer, Abdul Jalil bin Hamid and Muhammad bin Abi Hafsah narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Sinan Al-Du’ali, whose name was Yazid bin Umayyah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon to us and said: O people, God has prescribed Hajj for you. Then Al-Aqra’ bin Habis stood up and said: O Messenger of God, is it every year? He said: “If I had said it, it would have been obligatory, and if it were obligatory, you would not have performed it and you would not have been able to perform it. Hajj is performed once, so whoever performs more than that, it is voluntary.” Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah and Al-Hakim from the hadith of Al-Zuhri with it. It was narrated by Sharik from Samak from Ikrimah from Ibn Abbas in a similar manner. It was narrated from the hadith of Usamah bin Yazid. Imam Ahmad said: Mansur bin Wardan narrated to us on the authority of Ali bin Abdul-Ala, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Al-Bukhtari, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the verse, And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God, those who can afford the expenses for one’s expenses, was revealed, they said, O Messenger of God, every year? He was silent. They said, O Messenger of God, every year? He said, No, and if I had said yes, it would have been obligatory. Then God Almighty revealed, O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are made known to you, may distress you. This is how Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, and Al-Hakim narrated it on the authority of Mansur bin Wardan. Then Al-Tirmidhi said, Hasan Gharib, and what he said is questionable, because Al-Bukhari said, Abu Al-Bukhtari did not hear it from Ali. Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Ubaydah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: They said: O Messenger of God, is Hajj every year? He said: If you had said yes, it would be obligatory, and if it were obligatory, you would not have performed it, and if you did not perform it, you would have been punished. And in the two Sahihs, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Suraqah ibn Malik, “He said: O Messenger of God, is this enjoyment of ours for this year, or forever?” He said: No, rather forever. And in another narration: Rather, forever and ever. In Musnad of Imam Ahmad and Sunan Abi Dawud, from the hadith of Waqid bin Abi Waqid Al-Laithi, from his father, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his wives during his Hajj: This is the time when the confinement will appear - meaning, then the time when the confinement will appear - and do not leave the houses. As for the ability, it is divided into sections: Sometimes a person is able to do it by himself, and sometimes by someone else, as is established in the books of rulings. Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi said: Abd bin Hamid told us, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, Ibrahim bin Yazid told us, he said: I heard Muhammad bin Ibad bin Ja’far narrating from Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, “He said: A man stood up to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Who is the pilgrim, O Messenger of God? He said: The disheveled one who has spitting. Another stood up and said: Which Hajj is best, O Messenger of God? He said: The one who is tired and has spitting. Another stood up and said: What is the way, O Messenger of God? He said: The provisions and the mount.” And Ibn Majah narrated it in this way from the hadith of Ibrahim bin Yazid, who is Al-Khawzi. Al-Tirmidhi said: We do not know it except from his hadith, and some scholars have spoken about it. Before he memorized it, he said here and he said in the Book of Hajj: This is a good hadith. There is no doubt that the men of this chain of transmission are all trustworthy except for this Al-Khawzi, and they spoke about him because of this hadith, but others followed him, so Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah Al-Amiri told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair Al-Laithi told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ibad bin Jaafar, he said: I sat with Abdullah bin Umar, he said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: What is the way? He said: Provisions and a mount.” And Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in this way from the narration of Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair with it. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, Anas, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ata’, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas and Qatadah something similar to that, and this hadith has been narrated from other paths from the hadith of Anas, Abdullah bin Abbas, Ibn Mas’ud and Aisha, all of them with chains of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, but there is a question about their chains of transmission as is established in the Book of Rulings, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh took care to collect the chains of transmission of this hadith. Al-Hakim narrated it from the hadith of Qatada on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the statement of God, the Almighty, Whoever can afford the expenses of making the journey to it. It was said: What is the expenses? He said: Provisions and a mount. Then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of Muslim, and they did not include it. Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, “He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to God by mankind, those who can afford the expenses of making the journey to it.” They said: O Messenger of God, what is the expenses of making the journey? He said: Provisions and a mount. Waki’ narrated it in his interpretation on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Yunus on his authority. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ismail, who is Abu Isra’il al-Mala’i, on the authority of Fadil, meaning Ibn Amr, on the authority of Sa’id Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Hasten to perform Hajj, for none of you knows what will happen to him.’” Ahmad also said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, al-Hasan Ibn Amr al-Faqimi told us, on the authority of Mihran Ibn Abi Safwan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever intends to perform Hajj should hasten.’” Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Musaddad on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah al-Dharee’ with it. Ibn Jubayr narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Whoever can afford it, he said: Whoever possesses three hundred dirhams has afforded it. And on the authority of his freed slave, Ikrimah, he said: The way is health. And Wakee’ ibn al-Jarrah narrated on the authority of Abu Janab, meaning al-Kalbi, on the authority of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Whoever can afford it, he said: provisions and a camel. And the statement of God Almighty, And whoever disbelieves, then indeed, God is independent of the worlds, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and more than one said: That is, whoever denies the obligation of Hajj has disbelieved, and God is independent of him. Saeed bin Mansour said on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: When the verse, And whoever desires other than Islam as religion - never will it be accepted from him, was revealed, the Jews said: We are Muslims. God Almighty said: So argue with them and make them fight, meaning, “Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: God has enjoined upon the Muslims the pilgrimage to the House, whoever is able to do so. They said: It is not prescribed for us, and they refused to make the pilgrimage.” God Almighty said: And whoever disbelieves - then indeed, God is free from need of the worlds. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Abdullah bin Jaafar told us, Ismail bin Abdullah bin Masoud told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim and Shadh bin Fayyad told us, they said: Hilal Abu Hashim Al-Khurasani told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Hamadani told us on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever owns provisions and a mount and does not perform Hajj to the House of God, it does not harm him if he dies a Jew or a Christian, because God said: ‘And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God, those who can afford the expenses for one’s expenses. But whoever disbelieves - then indeed, God is independent of the worlds.’” And Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Muslim bin Ibrahim, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in this way on the authority of Abu Zur’ah Al-Razi: Hilal bin Fayyad told us, Hilal Abu Hashim Al-Khurasani told us, and he mentioned it with his chain of transmission likewise, and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Yahya Al-Qat’i on the authority of Muslim bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Hilal bin Abdullah, the client of Rabi’ah bin Amr bin Muslim Al-Bahili, on his authority. He said: This is a strange hadith that we do not know except from this source, and there is talk about its chain of transmission, and Hilal is unknown, and Al-Harith is weak in hadith. Al-Bukhari said: This Hilal is a fabricator of hadith. Ibn Adi said: This hadith is not authentic. Abu Bakr Al-Ismaili Al-Hafiz narrated from the hadith of Abu Amr Al-Awza’i: Ismail bin Ubaidullah bin Abi Al-Muhajir told me, Abd Al-Rahman bin Ghanem told me that he heard Umar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him say: Whoever is able to perform Hajj but does not perform it, it is the same to him whether he dies a Jew or a Christian. This is a sound chain of transmission back to Umar may God be pleased with him. Saeed bin Mansour narrated in his Sunan from Al-Hasan Al-Basri, who said: Umar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him said: I was thinking of sending men to these regions to look for everyone who had a grandmother and did not perform Hajj, and impose the jizyah on them. They are not Muslims, they are not Muslims.
3:98: This is a rebuke from God Almighty to the infidels, the People of the Book, for their stubbornness towards the truth, their disbelief in the verses of God, and their turning away from the path of God whoever among the people of faith wanted it with their effort and energy, despite their knowledge that what the Messenger brought was the truth from God, with what they have of knowledge from the earlier prophets and master messengers, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them all, and what they gave glad tidings of and warned of from mentioning the unlettered Hashemite Arab Meccan Prophet, the master of the children of Adam, the Seal of the Prophets, and the Messenger of the Lord of the Earth and the Heavens. God has threatened them for that, and informed them that He is a witness to their actions because they have contradicted what they have in their hands from the prophets and their treatment of the Messenger who was given glad tidings with denial, ingratitude, and stubbornness. So God Almighty informed them that He is not unaware of what they do, meaning that He will reward them for that on the Day when neither wealth nor children will be of any benefit.
3:99: This is a rebuke from God Almighty to the infidels, the People of the Book, for their stubbornness towards the truth, their disbelief in the verses of God, and their turning away from the path of God whoever among the people of faith wanted it with their effort and energy, despite their knowledge that what the Messenger brought was the truth from God, with what they have of knowledge from the earlier prophets and master messengers, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them all, and what they gave glad tidings of and warned of from mentioning the unlettered Hashemite Arab Meccan Prophet, the master of the children of Adam, the Seal of the Prophets, and the Messenger of the Lord of the Earth and the Heavens. God has threatened them for that, and informed them that He is a witness to their actions because they have contradicted what they have in their hands from the prophets and their treatment of the Messenger who was given glad tidings with denial, ingratitude, and stubbornness. So God Almighty informed them that He is not unaware of what they do, meaning that He will reward them for that on the Day when neither wealth nor children will be of any benefit.
3:100: God the Almighty warns His believing servants against obeying a group of the People of the Book who envy the believers for what God has given them of His grace and what He has granted them by sending His Messenger, as God the Almighty said: Many of the People of the Scripture wish they could turn you back to disbelief after you have believed, out of envy from themselves verse, and likewise He said here: If you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they will turn you back to disbelief after your belief verse. Then God the Almighty said: And how can you disbelieve while the verses of God are recited to you and among you is His Messenger verse. Meaning that disbelief is far from you, and God is far from it, for the verses of God are revealed to His Messenger night and day, and he recites them to you and conveys them to you. This is like His saying the Almighty: And what is the matter with you that you do not believe in God while the Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord and He has taken your covenant, if you are believers verse after verse. As it was mentioned in the hadith, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions one day, ‘Which of the believers is most amazing to you in faith?’ They said, ‘The angels.’ He said, ‘How can they not believe when they are with their Lord?’ They mentioned the prophets. He said, ‘How can they not believe when the revelation is sent down to them?’ They said, ‘So we.’ He said, ‘How can you not believe when I am among you?’ They said, ‘Which of the people is most amazing in faith?’ He said, ‘A people who will come after you and will find scriptures in which they will believe.’” I mentioned the chain of transmission of this hadith and the discussion of it at the beginning of my commentary on Al-Bukhari, praise be to God. Then God Almighty said, And whoever holds fast to God has been guided to a straight path. That is, despite this, holding fast to God and relying on Him is the mainstay of guidance, the means to avoiding misguidance, the means to right guidance, the path to success, and the attainment of one’s goal.

That is, despite this, holding fast to God and relying on Him is the mainstay of guidance, the means to avoiding misguidance, the means to right guidance, the path to success, and the attainment of one’s goal.
3:102: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Sinan told us, Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Sufyan and Shu`bah, on the authority of Zubayd al-Yami, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas`ud, Fear God as He should be feared. He said: That He should be obeyed and not disobeyed, that He should be remembered and not forgotten, and that He should be thanked and not ungrateful. This is a sound, suspended chain of transmission. Marra was followed by `Amr bin Maymun on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Yunus bin `Abd al-`A`la, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Fear God as He should be feared: that He should be obeyed and not disobeyed, that He should be thanked and not ungrateful, and that He should be remembered and not forgotten.’” Al-Hakim also narrated it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Mus`ar, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He mentioned it, then said: It is sound according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, and it was not… They both narrated it, and this is what he said, and it is more apparent that it is suspended, and God knows best. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Something similar was narrated from Marra Al-Hamadani, Al-Rabi’ bin Khathim, Amr bin Maymun, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Tawus, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abu Sinan, and Al-Suddi, and something similar to that. It was narrated from Anas that he said: A servant does not fear God as He should be feared until he controls his tongue. Saeed bin Jubair, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Qatadah, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Zaid bin Aslam, Al-Suddi, and others said that this verse was abrogated by the words of God the Most High: So fear God as much as you are able. And Ali bin Abi Talhah said from Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God the Most High: Fear God as He should be feared, he said: It was not abrogated, but the right to fear Him is that they strive in His cause as He should be striven in, and the blame of a blamer should not deter them in God’s cause, and they stand up for justice even if it is against themselves, their fathers, and their children. And the Almighty’s saying: And do not die except as Muslims means, preserve Islam while you are healthy and safe so that you die upon it, for the Generous One has made it a habit in His generosity that whoever lives upon something dies upon it, and whoever dies upon something will be resurrected upon it, so we seek refuge in God from anything other than that. Imam Ahmad said: Ruh told us, Shu’bah told us, he said: I heard Sulayman from Mujahid: The people were circumambulating the House and Ibn Abbas was sitting with Muhajjan, so he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O you who believe! Fear God as He should be feared and do not die except as Muslims.’ If a drop of Zaqqum were to fall, it would make the lives of the people of the earth miserable, so how about someone who has no food except Zaqqum?” And thus it was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak through various chains of narration on the authority of Shu’bah. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih, and Al-Hakim said: It meets the conditions of the two sheikhs, but they did not include it. Imam Ahmad said: Waki` told us, Al-A`mash told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Wahb, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abd Rabb al-Ka`bah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever would like to be saved from the Fire and enter Paradise, let death overtake him while he believes in God and the Last Day, and he treats people as he would like to be treated.’” Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say three things before his death: ‘None of you should die except while having good thoughts about God, the Almighty.’” Muslim narrated it on the authority of Al-A’mash on his authority. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan bin Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Abu Yunus told us, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that “God said: ‘I am as My servant thinks I am. If he thinks good of Me, then he will have it, and if he thinks evil of Me, then he will have it.’” The origin of this hadith is proven in the two Sahihs from another chain of narration on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘God says: I am as My servant thinks I am.’” Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik al-Qurashi told us, Ja’far ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of Thabit, and I think it was on the authority of Anas, who said: “A man from the Ansar was sick, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to visit him. He met him in the market and greeted him. He said to him: How are you, so-and-so? He said: I am fine, O Messenger of God. I hope in God and I fear my sins. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: These two things do not come together in the heart of a servant in this situation except that God gives him what he hopes for and makes him safe from what he fears.” Then he said: We do not know of anyone who narrated it on the authority of Thabit other than Ja’far ibn Sulayman, and this is how al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah narrated it from his hadith. Then al-Tirmidhi said: It is strange, and some of them narrated it on the authority of Thabit as a mursal. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Yusuf ibn Mahak, on the authority of Hakim ibn Hizam, who said: I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that I would not delay except standing. And he narrated it. Al-Nasa’i in his Sunan on the authority of Ismail bin Masoud on the authority of Khalid bin Al-Harith on the authority of Shu’bah on his authority, and he translated it and said Chapter on how he prostrates, then he cited something similar to it and it was said: Its meaning is that I will not die except as a Muslim, and it was said: Its meaning is that I will not be killed except facing forward and not turning away, and it goes back to the first. And the Almighty’s saying: And hold fast, all together, to the rope of God and be not divided. It was said, by the rope of God, meaning by the covenant of God, as He said in the verse after it, Humiliation has been imposed upon them wherever they are found, except by a rope from God and a rope from the people, meaning by a covenant and protection. And it was said, by the rope of God, meaning the Qur’an, as in the hadith of Al-Harith Al-A’war on the authority of Ali, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, describing the Qur’an as the strong rope of God and His straight path. A specific hadith was reported regarding this meaning. Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Jaafar Al-Tabari said: Saeed bin Yahya Al-Umawi told us, Asbat bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulayman Al-Arzami, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Abu Saeed, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Book of God is the rope of God extended from the heavens to the earth.” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muslim Al-Hijri on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas on the authority of Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This Qur’an is the strong rope of God, and it is the clear light, and it is the beneficial healing, a protection for whoever holds fast to it, and salvation for whoever follows it.” He narrated something similar on the authority of Hudhayfah and Zayd bin Arqam. Waki’ said: Al-A’mash told us on the authority of Abu Wa’il who said: Abdullah said: This path is at risk and the devils visit it. O Abdullah, this is the path, come to the path and hold fast to the rope of God, for the rope of God is the Qur’an. And His saying: And do not be divided He ordered them to be united and forbade them from division. There are many hadiths that forbid division and command them to come together and unite, as in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God is pleased with you with three things and is displeased with you with three things. He is pleased with you that you worship Him and do not associate anything with Him, that you hold fast to the rope of God all together and do not become divided, and that you advise whomever God has appointed over you. And He is displeased with you with three things: gossip, asking too many questions, and wasting money.” And He guaranteed them infallibility when they agree from error, as also mentioned in many hadiths. And it was feared that they would separate and differ, and that happened in this nation, so they split into seventy-three sects, one of which is a sect that will be saved to Paradise and safe from the punishment of Hell, and they are those who follow what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were upon. And the Almighty said: And remember the favor of God upon you - when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together, and you became, by His favor, brothers to the end of the verse. This context is about the Aws and Khazraj, for there had been many wars between them in the pre-Islamic era, and intense enmity, grudges, hatred, and discord, because of which their fighting and incidents between them had been prolonged. Then when God brought Islam, and those of them who entered it entered it, they became brothers who loved one another for the glory of God, connected for the sake of God, cooperating in righteousness and piety. God the Almighty said: “It is He who supported you with His victory and with the believers * And brought their hearts together. Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have brought their hearts together, but God brought their hearts together” to the end of the verse. They were on the brink of a pit of fire because of their disbelief, so God saved them from it by guiding them to faith. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, bestowed this favor upon them on the day when he divided the spoils of Hunayn, so he rebuked those of them who rebuked him, because of what he had given them in the division, because of what God had shown him, so he addressed them. He said: "O group of Ansar, did I not find you astray and God guided you through me? And you were divided and God united you through me, and poor and God enriched you through me? So whenever he said something, they said: God and His Messenger believe." Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar and others mentioned that this verse was revealed regarding the Aws and Khazraj. A Jewish man passed by a group of Aws and Khazraj, and he was displeased with their agreement and harmony, so he sent a man with him and ordered him to sit among them and remind them of their wars on the day of Bu'ath and those wars. He did so, and that remained his habit until the people's souls became heated, and some of them became angry with each other, and they rebelled and called out their slogans and demanded their weapons and threatened to go to Al-Harrah. This reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he came to them and began to calm them down, saying: Is it the call of ignorance while I am among you? And he recited this verse to them, so they regretted what they had done and reconciled and embraced and laid down their weapons, may God be pleased with them. Ikrimah mentioned that this was revealed about them when they argued about the slander case, and God knows best.

3:104: God the Almighty says: And let there be from you a group standing up to carry out God's command in calling to goodness, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and those are the successful ones, Ad-Dahhak said: They are the special Companions and the special narrators, meaning the mujahideen and scholars. Abu Ja'far Al-Baqir said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: And let there be from you a group inviting to goodness then he said: Goodness is following the Quran and my Sunnah narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. What is meant by this verse is that there should be a group from this nation that stands up to this matter, even though this is obligatory upon each individual of the nation according to his ability, as proven in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he is unable to do so, then with his tongue; if he is unable to do so, then with his heart - and that is the weakest of faith", and in another narration: And beyond that there is not even a mustard seed of faith. Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman al-Hashimi told us, Ismail bin Ja`far told us, Amr bin Abi Amr told me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman al-Ashhali, on the authority of Hudhayfah bin al-Yaman, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, or God will soon send upon you a punishment from Him, and then you will call upon Him and He will not respond to you.” Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Abi Amr, and al-Tirmidhi said: It is good. There are many hadiths on this subject, along with the noble verses, as their interpretation will come in their places. Then God Almighty said: And do not be like those who became divided and differed after clear proofs had come to them al-Baqarah 2:177. God Almighty forbids this nation from being like the past nations in their division and differences and their abandonment of enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, despite the proof being established against them. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Al-Mughira told us, Safwan told us, Azhar bin Abdullah Al-Hawzani told me, on the authority of Abu Amir Abdullah bin Luhay, who said: We performed Hajj with Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan, and when we arrived in Mecca, he stood up after praying the noon prayer and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The People of the Book split into seventy-two sects in their religion, and this nation will split into seventy-three sects - meaning the desires - all of them will be in Hell except one - which is the group - and there will emerge in my nation people who will trade with those desires as a dog trades with its owner, and there will not remain a vein or joint of it except that it enters it. By God, O people of the Arabs, if you do not do what your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came with, then it is more likely that others will not do it.” And this is how Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Hanbal and Muhammad bin Yahya, both of them on the authority of Abu Al-Mughira, whose name is Abdul Quddus bin Al-Hajjaj Al-Shami, on his authority. This hadith has been transmitted through various chains of transmission. And the Almighty’s saying: On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black means the Day of Resurrection, when the faces of the people of Sunnah and Jama’ah will turn white, and the faces of the people of innovation and division will turn black. This was said by Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. As for those whose faces will turn black, did you disbelieve after your belief? Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: They are the hypocrites. Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve. This description includes every disbeliever. As for those whose faces will turn white, they will be in the mercy of God, abiding therein forever. Meaning, Paradise, they will remain therein forever, not seeking to move away from it. Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi said when interpreting this verse: Abu Kurayb told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Rabi’ bin Subaih and Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Abu Ghalib, who said: Abu Umamah saw heads erected on the steps of the mosque of Damascus, so Abu Umamah said: The dogs of Hell are the worst of those killed under the sky, and the best of those killed are those who killed him. Then he recited: On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black to the end of the verse. I said to Abu Umamah: Did you hear it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: If I only heard it once, twice, three times, or four times - until he counted seven - and I did not tell you about it. Then he said: This is a good hadith. Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah on the authority of Abu Ghalib, and Ahmad included it in his Musnad on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abu Ghalib, in a similar manner. Ibn Mardawayh narrated a long, strange, and very amazing hadith when interpreting this verse from Abu Dharr. Then God Almighty said: These are the verses of God which We recite to you, meaning these are the verses of God, His proofs and His evidences, which We recite to you, O Muhammad. In truth, meaning We reveal what the matter is in this world and the next. He said: The best of people for mankind, you bring them in chains around their necks until they enter Islam. And this is what Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Atiyah Al-Awfi, Ikrimah, Ata, and Al-Rabi bin Anas said: You are the best nation produced for mankind, meaning the best of people for mankind, and the meaning is that they are the best of nations and the most beneficial people to people, and for this reason He said: You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in God. Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad bin Abdul Malik told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umaira, on the authority of the husband of Durrah bint Abi Lahab, on the authority of Durrah bint Abi Lahab, who said: "A man stood up to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was on the pulpit, and said: O Messenger of God, which of the people is the best? He said: The best of people are those who recite the Qur’an the most, are those who fear God the most, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and maintain ties of kinship. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, and al-Nasa’i in his Sunan, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God the Almighty: You are the best nation produced for mankind. He said: They are those who migrated with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca to Medina. The correct view is that this verse is general for the entire nation, each generation according to its own circumstances, and the best of their generations are those among whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, then those who came after them, then those who came after them, as He said in the other verse: And thus We have made you a just community, meaning the best, that you will be witnesses over the people. In Musnad of Imam Ahmad, Jami` al-Tirmidhi, Sunan Ibn Majah and Mustadrak al-Hakim, on the authority of Hakim ibn Mu`awiyah ibn Haidah, on the authority of his father, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘You are the best of seventy nations, and you are the most honorable to God, the Almighty. ’” This is a well-known hadith, and al-Tirmidhi classified it as hasan. It is also narrated on the authority of Mu`adh ibn Jabal and Abu Sa`id, similar to it. This nation has achieved the lead in good deeds through its Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for he is the most honorable of God’s creation and the most honorable of the Messengers to God. God sent him with a complete and great law that no Prophet or Messenger before him was given. So, working according to his method and path is enough to replace a little of what a lot of work from others cannot replace, as Imam Ahmad said: ‘Abd al-Rahman told us, Ibn Zuhair told us, on the authority of Abdullah, meaning Ibn Muhammad ibn `Aqil, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Ali, who is Ibn al-Hanafiyyah, that he heard `Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, say: “The Messenger of God said: I have been given what none of the Prophets have been given.” We said, O Messenger of God, what is it? He said, I have been aided by terror, I have been given the keys to the earth, I have been named Ahmad, the earth has been made a means of purification for me, and my nation has been made the best of nations. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this source, and its chain of transmission is good.
