Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Al-Ala Al-Hasan bin Suwar told us, Laith told us, on the authority of Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Halbas Yazid bin Maysarah, who said: I heard Umm Al-Darda’, may God be pleased with her, say: I heard Abu Al-Darda’, may God be pleased with him, say: “I heard Abu Al-Qasim, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and I had never heard him use his kunya before or after that, saying: God Almighty says: O Jesus, I will send after you a nation who, if what they like befalls them, will praise and thank them, and if what they dislike befalls them, they will seek reward and be patient, but they have no patience or knowledge.” He said: O Lord, how can this be for them, and they have no patience or knowledge? He said: I will give them from My patience and knowledge. There are hadiths that are appropriate to mention here. Imam Ahmad said: Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, Al-Masoudi told us, Bakir bin Al-Akhns told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have been given seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being brought to account, their faces like the moon on the night of the full moon, their hearts like the heart of one man, so I asked my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, for more, and He increased me with each one by seventy thousand.” Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: I saw that this would come upon the people of the villages and would befall those on the edges of the deserts. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Bakr Al-Sahmi told us, Hisham bin Hassan told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Mihran, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaid, on the authority of Maimun bin Mihran, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Bakr: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: My Lord has given me seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being brought to account. Umar said: O Messenger of God, why didn’t you ask Him for more? He said: I asked Him for more, and He gave me seventy thousand with each man. Umar said: Why didn’t you ask Him for more? He said: I asked Him for more, and He gave me this much.” And Abdullah bin Bakr spread his hands apart, and Abdullah said: And he stretched out his arms, and Abdullah urged, and Hisham said: This is from God, and he does not know how many. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abu Al-Yaman told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Damdam bin Zur’ah, who said: Shureih bin Ubaid said: Thawban fell ill in Homs, and Abdullah bin Qurt Al-Azdi was in charge of it, so he did not visit him. Then a man from the Kalaa’in came to visit Thawban, and Thawban said to him: Will you write? He said: Yes. He said: Write. So he wrote to the emir Abdullah bin Qurt from Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: As for what follows, if Moses and Jesus, peace be upon them, had a servant in your presence, you would have visited him. Then he folded the letter and said to him: Will you deliver it to him? He said: Yes. So the man went with his letter and gave it to Ibn Qurt, and when he saw him, he stood up in a panic, and the people said: What is the matter with him? Has something happened? Then Thawban came until he entered upon him, visited him and sat with him for a while, then he stood up and Thawban took his cloak and said: Sit down until I tell you a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in which he said: Seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account or punished, and with every thousand there will be seventy thousand. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this source and its chain of transmission is all trustworthy men from Syria and Homs, so it is a sound hadith, praise and thanks be to God. Another path: Al-Tabarani said: Amr bin Ishaq bin Zubayriq Al-Himsi told us, Muhammad bin Ismail, meaning Ibn Ayyash, told us, my father told me, on the authority of Damdam bin Zar’ah, on the authority of Shureih bin Ubaid, on the authority of Abu Asma Al-Rahbi, on the authority of Thawban, may God be pleased with him, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘My Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, promised me seventy thousand of my nation who will not be held accountable, with every thousand seventy thousand.’” Perhaps this is what is preserved with the addition of Abu Asma Al-Rahbi between Shureih and Thawban, and God knows best. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: We talked most of the time with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, one night, then we went to him and he said: “The prophets were shown to me tonight with their nations. A prophet would pass by with three people, a prophet with a group, a prophet with a few people, and a prophet with no one with him, until Moses, peace be upon him, passed by with a large group of the Children of Israel. I was amazed and said: Who are these? It was said: This is your brother Moses with the Children of Israel. He said: I said: Where are my nation? It was said: Look to your right. I looked and saw that the curtains had been closed with the faces of men. Then it was said to me: Look to your left. I looked and saw that the horizon had been closed with the faces of men. It was said to me: Are you satisfied? I said: I am satisfied, O Lord. He said: It was said to me: There are seventy thousand with these who will enter Paradise without being brought to account. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And he said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, if you are able to be among the seventy thousand, then do so. If you fall short, then be among the people of the valley. If you fall short, then be among the people of the horizon, for I have seen people quarreling with one another. So Ukasha bin Muhsin stood up and said: O Messenger of God, pray to God to make me one of them, meaning one of the seventy. So he prayed for him, and another man stood up and said: Pray to God, O Messenger of God, to make me one of them. So he said: Ukasha has preceded you in that. He said: Then we talked and said: Who do you think these seventy thousand are? They are people who were born in Islam and did not associate anything with God until they died. So that reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “They are those who do not seek ruqyah, nor cauterize, nor take omens, and they put their trust in their Lord.” This is how Ahmad narrated it with this chain of transmission and this context. He also narrated it on the authority of Abd al-Samad on the authority of Hisham on the authority of Qatadah with his chain of transmission similarly, and he added after his saying: I am satisfied, O Lord, I am satisfied, O Lord. He said: I am satisfied. I said: Yes. He said: Look to your left. He said: So I looked and saw that the horizon was blocked by the faces of men. He said: Are you satisfied? I said: I am satisfied. This is a sound chain of transmission from this source, transmitted only by Ahmad, and they did not include it. Another hadith Ahmad ibn Mani’ said: Abd al-Malik ibn Abd al-Aziz told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The nations were presented to me with seasons, and my nation was pleased with me. Then I saw them and I was amazed by their large numbers and their appearance. They filled the plains and the mountains. He said: Are you satisfied, O Muhammad? I said: Yes. He said: With these are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being brought to account. They are those who do not seek incantations or cauterize, and they put their trust in their Lord. Then ‘Ukasha ibn Muhsin stood up and said: O Messenger of God, ask God to make me one of them. He said: You are one of them. Then another man stood up and said: Ask God to make me one of them. He said: ‘Ukasha beat you to it.” Narrated by al-Hafiz al-Dhiya’ al-Maqdisi, who said: This, in my opinion, meets the conditions of Muslim. Another hadith Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Al-Judhu’i Al-Qadi told us, Uqbah ibn Mukram told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hassan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account or punished. It was said: Who are they? He said: They are those who do not cauterize, nor seek omens, nor believe in omens, and they put their trust in their Lord. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Hisham ibn Hassan, and he mentioned Ukasha. Another hadith It was established in the two Sahihs on the authority of Az-Zuhri on the authority of Sa`id ibn Al-Musayyab that Abu Hurairah told him: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘A group of my nation will enter Paradise, and they will be seventy thousand, and their faces will shine like the moon on a full moon night.’ Abu Hurairah said: ‘Ukasha ibn Muhsin Al-Asadi stood up, raising his blanket and said: ‘O Messenger of God, pray to God to make me one of them.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O God, make him one of them.’ Then a man from the Ansar stood up and said the same thing, and he said: ‘Ukasha beat you to it.’” Another hadith Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Yahya ibn Uthman told us, Saeed ibn Abi Maryam told us, Abu Ghassan told us, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa`d, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Seventy thousand - or seven hundred thousand - of my nation will enter Paradise, some of them taking others, until the first of them and the last of them enter Paradise, and their faces will be like the moon on the night of the full moon.” Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of `Abd al-`Aziz ibn Abi Hazim on the authority of his father on the authority of Sahl on his authority. Another Hadith Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj said in his Sahih: Saeed bin Mansour told us, Hisham told us, Hiseen bin Abdul Rahman told us, he said: I was with Saeed bin Jubair and he said, Which of you saw the star that fell last night? I said: I did. Then I said: I was not praying, but I was stung. He said: So what did you do? I said: I sought ruqyah. He said: What made you do that? I said: A Hadith narrated to us by Al-Sha’bi. He said: And what did Al-Sha’bi tell you? I said: He told us on the authority of Buraydah ibn al-Husaib al-Aslami that he said: There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye or a fever. He said: He who has concluded what he heard has done well. However, Ibn Abbas told us on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “The nations were presented to me and I saw the Prophet with a group of people, the Prophet with one or two men, and the Prophet with no one with him. Then a great multitude was raised to me and I thought that they were my nation. Then it was said to me: This is Moses and his people, but look to the horizon. So I looked and saw a great multitude. Then it was said to me: Look to the other horizon and see a great multitude. Then it was said to me: This is your nation and with them are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being held accountable or punished. Then he got up and entered his house.” So the people began to argue about those who will enter Paradise without being held accountable or punished. Some of them said: Perhaps they are those who accompanied the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some of them said: Perhaps they are those who were born in Islam and did not associate anything with God. They mentioned things, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to them and said: What are you arguing about? So they told him. He said: They are those who do not perform ruqyah, nor seek ruqyah from others, nor take omens, and they put their trust in their Lord. Then Ukasha bin Muhsin stood up and said: Ask God to make me one of them. He said: You are one of them. Then another man stood up and said: Ask God to make me one of them. He said: Ukasha beat you to it. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Asid bin Zaid on the authority of Hisham, but he does not have: they do not perform ruqyah. Another hadith Ahmad said: Ruh ibn Ubadah told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, Abu al-Zubayr told me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mention a hadith, in which it says: The first group will be saved, their faces like the moon on the night of the full moon, seventy thousand who will not be held accountable, then those who follow them will be like the brightest star in the sky.” Then likewise, and he mentioned the rest of it. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Ruh, except that he did not mention the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Another hadith Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Abi Asim said in his book Al-Sunan: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad, I heard Abu Umamah Al-Bahili say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “My Lord promised me that seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise, with each thousand seventy thousand who will not be held accountable or punished, and three handfuls from the handfuls of my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic.” And this is how Al-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Hisham bin Ammar on the authority of Ismail bin Ayyash, and this is a good chain of transmission. Another way On the authority of Abu Umamah. Ibn Abi Asim said, Dahim told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us on the authority of Safwan bin Amr, on the authority of Salim bin Amir, on the authority of Abu Al-Yaman Al-Hawzani, whose name is Amir bin Abdullah bin Luhay, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, who said: “God promised me that seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account. Yazid bin Al-Akhns said: By God, those among your nation, O Messenger of God, are like a reddish fly among flies. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God promised me seventy thousand, with each thousand seventy thousand and He gave me three handfuls more.” This is also a good chain of transmission. Another hadith Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Khalid told us, Abu Tobah told us, Muawiyah ibn Salam told us on the authority of Zayd ibn Salam that he heard Abu Salam say: Aamer ibn Zayd al-Bakali told me that he heard Utbah ibn Abd al-Salami, may God be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My Lord, the Almighty, promised me that seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account, then every thousand will intercede for seventy thousand, then my Lord, the Almighty, will scoop up three handfuls of dust in His hands.” So Umar said: God will intercede for the first seventy for their fathers, sons, and clans, and I hope that God will make me one of the last handfuls of dust. Al-Hafiz al-Dhiya Abu Abdullah al-Maqdisi said in his book Sifat al-Jannah: I do not know of any defect in this chain of transmission, and God knows best. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told me, Hisham, meaning Al-Dastawai, told us, Yahya bin Abi Katheer told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Abi Maimouna, Ata bin Yasar told us that Rafa’ah Al-Juhani told him, he said: We set out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until we were at Al-Kadeed, or he said: at Qudayd, and he mentioned a hadith in which he said: “My Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, promised me that seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account, and I hope that they will not enter it until you and your righteous spouses and offspring have settled in dwellings in Paradise.” Al-Dhiya’ said: This, in my opinion, is in accordance with the conditions of Muslim. Another hadith Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma’mar informed us on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Nadr ibn Anas, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God promised me that He would admit four hundred thousand of my nation into Paradise. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: Give us more, O Messenger of God. He said: By God, this is it. Umar said: That is enough, O Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr said: Leave me alone, and what does it matter to you if God admits us all into Paradise? Umar said: God willing, He will admit His creation into Paradise with one hand. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Umar has spoken the truth. This hadith with this chain of transmission is unique to Abd al-Razzaq. Al-Dhiya’ said it and Al-Hafiz Abu Na’im Al-Isfahani narrated it. He said: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Mukhallad told us, Ibrahim bin Al-Haitham Al-Baldi told us, Sulayman bin Harb told us, Abu Hilal told us on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: My Lord promised me that He would admit one hundred thousand of my nation into Paradise. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, give us more. He said: And so it was, and Sulayman bin Harb pointed with his hand in the same manner. I said: O Messenger of God, give us more. Umar said: God is able to admit people into Paradise with a single handful. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Umar has spoken the truth. This is a strange hadith from this source. Abu Hilal’s name is Muhammad bin Salim Al-Rasibi, from Basra. Another chain of transmission on the authority of Anas. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr told us, `Abd al-Qahir ibn al-Sarri al-Sulami told us, Hamid told us on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise. They said: ‘Give us more, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘For every man there are seventy thousand.’ They said: ‘Give us more,’ and he was on a sand dune. He said like this and threw some with his hand. They said: ‘O Messenger of God, may God distance those who enter Hell after this.’” This is a good chain of transmission, and all of its men are trustworthy, except for `Abd al-Qahir ibn al-Sarri. Ibn Ma`in was asked about him and said: He is trustworthy. Another hadith Al-Tabarani narrated from the hadith of Qatada on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Umair, on the authority of his father that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God promised me that three hundred thousand of my nation would enter Paradise. Umair said: O Messenger of God, give us more. He said: This way, with his hand. Umair said: O Messenger of God, give us more. Umar said: It is enough for you. If God wills, He will admit people to Paradise with a handful or a single handful. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Umar spoke the truth.” Another hadith Al-Tabarani said: Ahmad bin Khalid told us, Abu Tobah told us, Muawiyah bin Salam told us on the authority of Zaid bin Salam that he heard Abu Salam say: Abdullah bin Aamer told me that Qais Al-Kindi told him that Abu Saeed Al-Anmari told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My Lord promised me that He will admit seventy thousand of my nation to Paradise without account, and every thousand will intercede for seventy thousand, then my Lord will take three handfuls with His two hands.” That is what Qais said, so I said to Abu Saeed: Did you hear this from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: Yes, with my ears, and my heart has retained it. Abu Saeed said: He said, meaning the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: And that, God Almighty willing, will include the emigrants of my nation and God will fulfill the remainder of our Arabs. Muhammad bin Sahl bin Askar narrated this hadith on the authority of Abu Tawbah al-Rabi’ bin Nafi’ with his chain of transmission similarly, and he added: Abu Saeed said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, calculated that, and it amounted to four hundred thousand thousand and ninety thousand thousand. Another hadith Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hashim ibn Murthad al-Tabarani told us, Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Ayyash told us, my father told me, Damdam ibn Zur’ah told me, on the authority of Shuraih ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, a group of you will be sent to Paradise on the Day of Resurrection, all of them striking the earth. The angels will say: Why did more people come with Muhammad than came with the prophets?” This is a good chain of transmission. Another type - From the hadiths that indicate the virtue, honor, and dignity of this nation before God the Almighty, and that it is the best nation in this world and the hereafter. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, Abu al-Zubayr told me on the authority of Jabir that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: I hope that those of my nation who follow me on the Day of Resurrection will be a quarter of Paradise. He said: “So we said ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then he said: “I hope that they will be a third of the people.” He said: “So we said ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then he said: “I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise.” And this is how he narrated it on the authority of Ruh on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, and it meets the conditions of Muslim. It is proven in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Ishaq al-Subai’i on the authority of Amr bin Maymun, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: Are you not pleased to be a quarter of the people of Paradise? So we said ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then he said: Are you not pleased to be a third of the people of Paradise? So we said ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then he said: I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise. Another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud. Al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Musawar told us, `Affan ibn Muslim told us, `Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, al-Harith ibn Hasira told me, al-Qasim ibn `Abd al-Rahman told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How will you be when a quarter of Paradise is for you and three quarters of it are for the rest of the people? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: How will you be when a third of it is for you? They said: That is more. He said: How will you be when half of it is for you? They said: That is more. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, eighty of which are for you. Al-Tabarani said: Al-Harith ibn Hasira is the only one to narrate it. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim told us, Dhirar ibn Murrah Abu Sinan al-Shaibani told us, on the authority of Muharib ibn Dithar, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, and this nation is eighty rows from that. And he narrated it likewise on the authority of Affan on the authority of Abd al-Aziz on his authority, and al-Tirmidhi included it on the authority of Abu Sinan on his authority, and he said: This is a good hadith, and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri on the authority of Alqamah ibn Marthad, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father on his authority. Another hadith - Al-Tabarani narrated from the hadith of Sulayman bin Abd al-Rahman al-Dimashqi: Khalid bin Yazid al-Bajali told us, Sulayman bin Ali bin Abdullah bin Abbas told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, eighty of which are from my nation. Khalid bin Yazid al-Bajali was the only one to narrate it, and Ibn Adi spoke about it. Another hadith Al-Tabarani said: Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal told us, Musa bin Ghailan told us, Hashim bin Mukhallad told us, Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Amr, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: When A group of the first and a group of the last was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You are a quarter of the people of Paradise, you are a third of the people of Paradise, you are half of the people of Paradise, you are two-thirds of the people of Paradise. Abdul Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection. We are the first people to enter Paradise, but they were given the Book before us and we were given it after them. So God guided us to the truth in what they differed about. So this is the day in which they differed, people will follow us. Tomorrow will be for the Jews and the day after tomorrow will be for the Christians.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim on the authority of Abdullah bin Tawus on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Al-A'mash on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection, and we are the first to enter Paradise. And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. Another hadith - Al-Daraqutni narrated in Al-Afrad from the hadith of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqil on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Paradise was forbidden to all the prophets until I enter it, and it was forbidden to the nations until my nation enters it. Then he said: Ibn Aqil was the only one to narrate it on the authority of Al-Zuhri, and no one else narrated it on his authority. Zuhair bin Muhammad was the only one to narrate it on the authority of Ibn Aqil, and Amr bin Abi Salamah was the only one to narrate it on the authority of Zuhair. Abu Ahmad bin Adi Al-Hafiz narrated it, and he said: Ahmad bin Al-Hussein bin Ishaq told us, Abu Bakr Al-A’in Muhammad bin Abi Atab told us, Abu Hafs Al-Tanisi told us - meaning Amr bin Abi Salamah - Sadaqa Al-Dimashqi told us on the authority of Zuhair bin Muhammad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqil on the authority of Al-Zuhri. Al-Tha’labi narrated it: Abu al-Abbas al-Mukhalladi told us, Abu Na’im Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad told us, Ahmad ibn Isa al-Tanisi told us, Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us, Sadaqah ibn Abdullah told us, on the authority of Zuhair ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Ibn Aqil, on his authority. These hadiths are in the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: “You are the best nation produced for mankind. You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in God.” So whoever from this nation is characterized by these qualities is included with them in this praise and commendation of them, as Qatada said: It has reached us that Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, during his Hajj, saw the people rushing, so he recited this verse: You are the best nation produced for mankind. Then he said: Whoever is pleased to be from that nation, let him fulfill God’s condition regarding it. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. And whoever is not characterized by this is more like the People of the Book whom God condemned in His saying: They used not to forbid one another from the wrong they did Al-Baqarah 2:17. For this reason, when God praised this nation for these qualities, He began to condemn and rebuke the People of the Book, so God said: And if the People of the Scripture had believed, meaning in what was revealed to Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, “it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are wicked,” meaning few of them believe in God and what was revealed to you and what was revealed to them, and most of them are misguided, disbelieving, and wicked. And disobedience. Then the Almighty said, informing His believing servants and giving them good report that victory and triumph will be theirs over the disbelieving atheist People of the Book. The Almighty said: “They will not harm you except with an injury. And if they fight you, they will turn their backs to you; then they will not be helped.” And so it happened. On the day of Khaybar, God humiliated them and made their noses ache. Likewise, those before them from the Jews of Medina, Banu Qaynuqa, Banu Nadir, and Banu Qurayzah, all of them were humiliated by God. Likewise, the Christians in the Levant, the Companions defeated them in more than one place, and they were deprived of the kingdom of the Levant forever and ever. The band of Islam will continue to exist in the Levant until Jesus, son of Mary, descends while they are still like that. He will rule by the religion of Islam and the law of Muhammad, may the best prayers and peace be upon him. He will break the cross, kill the pigs, and abolish the jizya, and will accept nothing but Islam. Then God the Almighty said: And humiliation has been imposed upon them wherever they are found, except by a covenant from God and a covenant from the people. That is, God has imposed humiliation and degradation upon them wherever they are, so they are not safe. Except by a covenant from God, that is, by a protection from God, which is the covenant of protection for them, imposing the jizyah on them, and imposing the rulings of the religion on them. And a covenant from the people, that is, security from them for them, as in the case of a truce, a covenanted one, and a prisoner if one of the Muslims grants him security, even if it is a woman, and likewise a slave according to one of the two opinions of the scholars. Ibn Abbas said: Except by a covenant from God and a covenant from the people, that is, by a covenant from God and a covenant from the people. This is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ata, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said. And His statement: And they incurred the wrath of God, that is, they were obligated, so they committed themselves to the wrath of God, and they deserved it. And poverty has been imposed upon them, that is, they were obligated to it by fate and by law. That is why He said, That is because they disbelieved in the signs of God and killed the prophets unjustly. That is, what drove them to do that was arrogance, oppression, and envy, and that was followed by humiliation, lowliness, and poverty forever, connected to the humiliation of the Hereafter. Then God the Almighty said, That is because they disobeyed and were transgressing. That is, what drove them to disbelieve in the signs of God and kill the messengers of God, and they were destined for that - that they were frequently disobeying the commands of God the Almighty and committing sins against God, and transgressing against the law of God. So we seek refuge in God from that, and God the Almighty is the One sought for help. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Habib told us, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Mu’ammar al-Azdi, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Children of Israel used to kill three hundred prophets a day, and then a market would be held to kill them at the end of the day.
3:111: The Almighty tells us about this Muhammadan nation that they are the best of nations, so He the Almighty said: You are the best nation produced for mankind. Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Maysarah, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, You are the best nation produced for mankind. He said: The best of people for mankind, you bring them in chains around their necks until they enter Islam. And this is what Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Atiyah Al-Awfi, Ikrimah, Ata, and Al-Rabi bin Anas said: You are the best nation produced for mankind, meaning the best of people for mankind, and the meaning is that they are the best of nations and the most beneficial people to people, and for this reason He said: You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in God. Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad bin Abdul Malik told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umaira, on the authority of the husband of Durrah bint Abi Lahab, on the authority of Durrah bint Abi Lahab, who said: "A man stood up to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was on the pulpit, and said: O Messenger of God, which of the people is the best? He said: The best of people are those who recite the Qur’an the most, are those who fear God the most, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and maintain ties of kinship. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, and al-Nasa’i in his Sunan, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God the Almighty: You are the best nation produced for mankind. He said: They are those who migrated with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca to Medina. The correct view is that this verse is general for the entire nation, each generation according to its own circumstances, and the best of their generations are those among whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, then those who came after them, then those who came after them, as He said in the other verse: And thus We have made you a just community, meaning the best, that you will be witnesses over the people. In Musnad of Imam Ahmad, Jami` al-Tirmidhi, Sunan Ibn Majah and Mustadrak al-Hakim, on the authority of Hakim ibn Mu`awiyah ibn Haidah, on the authority of his father, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘You are the best of seventy nations, and you are the most honorable to God, the Almighty. ’” This is a well-known hadith, and al-Tirmidhi classified it as hasan. It is also narrated on the authority of Mu`adh ibn Jabal and Abu Sa`id, similar to it. This nation has achieved the lead in good deeds through its Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for he is the most honorable of God’s creation and the most honorable of the Messengers to God. God sent him with a complete and great law that no Prophet or Messenger before him was given. So, working according to his method and path is enough to replace a little of what a lot of work from others cannot replace, as Imam Ahmad said: ‘Abd al-Rahman told us, Ibn Zuhair told us, on the authority of Abdullah, meaning Ibn Muhammad ibn `Aqil, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Ali, who is Ibn al-Hanafiyyah, that he heard `Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, say: “The Messenger of God said: I have been given what none of the Prophets have been given.” We said, O Messenger of God, what is it? He said, I have been aided by terror, I have been given the keys to the earth, I have been named Ahmad, the earth has been made a means of purification for me, and my nation has been made the best of nations. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this source, and its chain of transmission is good. Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Al-Ala Al-Hasan bin Suwar told us, Laith told us, on the authority of Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Halbas Yazid bin Maysarah, who said: I heard Umm Al-Darda’, may God be pleased with her, say: I heard Abu Al-Darda’, may God be pleased with him, say: “I heard Abu Al-Qasim, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and I had never heard him use his kunya before or after that, saying: God Almighty says: O Jesus, I will send after you a nation who, if what they like befalls them, will praise and thank them, and if what they dislike befalls them, they will seek reward and be patient, but they have no patience or knowledge.” He said: O Lord, how can this be for them, and they have no patience or knowledge? He said: I will give them from My patience and knowledge. There are hadiths that are appropriate to mention here. Imam Ahmad said: Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, Al-Masoudi told us, Bakir bin Al-Akhns told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have been given seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being brought to account, their faces like the moon on the night of the full moon, their hearts like the heart of one man, so I asked my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, for more, and He increased me with each one by seventy thousand.” Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: I saw that this would come upon the people of the villages and would befall those on the edges of the deserts. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Bakr Al-Sahmi told us, Hisham bin Hassan told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Mihran, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaid, on the authority of Maimun bin Mihran, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Bakr: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: My Lord has given me seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being brought to account. Umar said: O Messenger of God, why didn’t you ask Him for more? He said: I asked Him for more, and He gave me seventy thousand with each man. Umar said: Why didn’t you ask Him for more? He said: I asked Him for more, and He gave me this much.” And Abdullah bin Bakr spread his hands apart, and Abdullah said: And he stretched out his arms, and Abdullah urged, and Hisham said: This is from God, and he does not know how many. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abu Al-Yaman told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Damdam bin Zur’ah, who said: Shureih bin Ubaid said: Thawban fell ill in Homs, and Abdullah bin Qurt Al-Azdi was in charge of it, so he did not visit him. Then a man from the Kalaa’in came to visit Thawban, and Thawban said to him: Will you write? He said: Yes. He said: Write. So he wrote to the emir Abdullah bin Qurt from Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: As for what follows, if Moses and Jesus, peace be upon them, had a servant in your presence, you would have visited him. Then he folded the letter and said to him: Will you deliver it to him? He said: Yes. So the man went with his letter and gave it to Ibn Qurt, and when he saw him, he stood up in a panic, and the people said: What is the matter with him? Has something happened? Then Thawban came until he entered upon him, visited him and sat with him for a while, then he stood up and Thawban took his cloak and said: Sit down until I tell you a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in which he said: Seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account or punished, and with every thousand there will be seventy thousand. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this source and its chain of transmission is all trustworthy men from Syria and Homs, so it is a sound hadith, praise and thanks be to God. Another path: Al-Tabarani said: Amr bin Ishaq bin Zubayriq Al-Himsi told us, Muhammad bin Ismail, meaning Ibn Ayyash, told us, my father told me, on the authority of Damdam bin Zar’ah, on the authority of Shureih bin Ubaid, on the authority of Abu Asma Al-Rahbi, on the authority of Thawban, may God be pleased with him, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘My Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, promised me seventy thousand of my nation who will not be held accountable, with every thousand seventy thousand.’” Perhaps this is what is preserved with the addition of Abu Asma Al-Rahbi between Shureih and Thawban, and God knows best. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: We talked most of the time with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, one night, then we went to him and he said: “The prophets were shown to me tonight with their nations. A prophet would pass by with three people, a prophet with a group, a prophet with a few people, and a prophet with no one with him, until Moses, peace be upon him, passed by with a large group of the Children of Israel. I was amazed and said: Who are these? It was said: This is your brother Moses with the Children of Israel. He said: I said: Where are my nation? It was said: Look to your right. I looked and saw that the curtains had been closed with the faces of men. Then it was said to me: Look to your left. I looked and saw that the horizon had been closed with the faces of men. It was said to me: Are you satisfied? I said: I am satisfied, O Lord. He said: It was said to me: There are seventy thousand with these who will enter Paradise without being brought to account. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And he said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, if you are able to be among the seventy thousand, then do so. If you fall short, then be among the people of the valley. If you fall short, then be among the people of the horizon, for I have seen people quarreling with one another. So Ukasha bin Muhsin stood up and said: O Messenger of God, pray to God to make me one of them, meaning one of the seventy. So he prayed for him, and another man stood up and said: Pray to God, O Messenger of God, to make me one of them. So he said: Ukasha has preceded you in that. He said: Then we talked and said: Who do you think these seventy thousand are? They are people who were born in Islam and did not associate anything with God until they died. So that reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “They are those who do not seek ruqyah, nor cauterize, nor take omens, and they put their trust in their Lord.” This is how Ahmad narrated it with this chain of transmission and this context. He also narrated it on the authority of Abd al-Samad on the authority of Hisham on the authority of Qatadah with his chain of transmission similarly, and he added after his saying: I am satisfied, O Lord, I am satisfied, O Lord. He said: I am satisfied. I said: Yes. He said: Look to your left. He said: So I looked and saw that the horizon was blocked by the faces of men. He said: Are you satisfied? I said: I am satisfied. This is a sound chain of transmission from this source, transmitted only by Ahmad, and they did not include it. Another hadith Ahmad ibn Mani’ said: Abd al-Malik ibn Abd al-Aziz told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The nations were presented to me with seasons, and my nation was pleased with me. Then I saw them and I was amazed by their large numbers and their appearance. They filled the plains and the mountains. He said: Are you satisfied, O Muhammad? I said: Yes. He said: With these are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being brought to account. They are those who do not seek incantations or cauterize, and they put their trust in their Lord. Then ‘Ukasha ibn Muhsin stood up and said: O Messenger of God, ask God to make me one of them. He said: You are one of them. Then another man stood up and said: Ask God to make me one of them. He said: ‘Ukasha beat you to it.” Narrated by al-Hafiz al-Dhiya’ al-Maqdisi, who said: This, in my opinion, meets the conditions of Muslim. Another hadith Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Al-Judhu’i Al-Qadi told us, Uqbah ibn Mukram told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hassan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account or punished. It was said: Who are they? He said: They are those who do not cauterize, nor seek omens, nor believe in omens, and they put their trust in their Lord. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Hisham ibn Hassan, and he mentioned Ukasha. Another hadith It was established in the two Sahihs on the authority of Az-Zuhri on the authority of Sa`id ibn Al-Musayyab that Abu Hurairah told him: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘A group of my nation will enter Paradise, and they will be seventy thousand, and their faces will shine like the moon on a full moon night.’ Abu Hurairah said: ‘Ukasha ibn Muhsin Al-Asadi stood up, raising his blanket and said: ‘O Messenger of God, pray to God to make me one of them.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O God, make him one of them.’ Then a man from the Ansar stood up and said the same thing, and he said: ‘Ukasha beat you to it.’” Another hadith Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Yahya ibn Uthman told us, Saeed ibn Abi Maryam told us, Abu Ghassan told us, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa`d, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Seventy thousand - or seven hundred thousand - of my nation will enter Paradise, some of them taking others, until the first of them and the last of them enter Paradise, and their faces will be like the moon on the night of the full moon.” Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of `Abd al-`Aziz ibn Abi Hazim on the authority of his father on the authority of Sahl on his authority. Another Hadith Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj said in his Sahih: Saeed bin Mansour told us, Hisham told us, Hiseen bin Abdul Rahman told us, he said: I was with Saeed bin Jubair and he said, Which of you saw the star that fell last night? I said: I did. Then I said: I was not praying, but I was stung. He said: So what did you do? I said: I sought ruqyah. He said: What made you do that? I said: A Hadith narrated to us by Al-Sha’bi. He said: And what did Al-Sha’bi tell you? I said: He told us on the authority of Buraydah ibn al-Husaib al-Aslami that he said: There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye or a fever. He said: He who has concluded what he heard has done well. However, Ibn Abbas told us on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “The nations were presented to me and I saw the Prophet with a group of people, the Prophet with one or two men, and the Prophet with no one with him. Then a great multitude was raised to me and I thought that they were my nation. Then it was said to me: This is Moses and his people, but look to the horizon. So I looked and saw a great multitude. Then it was said to me: Look to the other horizon and see a great multitude. Then it was said to me: This is your nation and with them are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being held accountable or punished. Then he got up and entered his house.” So the people began to argue about those who will enter Paradise without being held accountable or punished. Some of them said: Perhaps they are those who accompanied the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some of them said: Perhaps they are those who were born in Islam and did not associate anything with God. They mentioned things, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to them and said: What are you arguing about? So they told him. He said: They are those who do not perform ruqyah, nor seek ruqyah from others, nor take omens, and they put their trust in their Lord. Then Ukasha bin Muhsin stood up and said: Ask God to make me one of them. He said: You are one of them. Then another man stood up and said: Ask God to make me one of them. He said: Ukasha beat you to it. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Asid bin Zaid on the authority of Hisham, but he does not have: they do not perform ruqyah. Another hadith Ahmad said: Ruh ibn Ubadah told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, Abu al-Zubayr told me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mention a hadith, in which it says: The first group will be saved, their faces like the moon on the night of the full moon, seventy thousand who will not be held accountable, then those who follow them will be like the brightest star in the sky.” Then likewise, and he mentioned the rest of it. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Ruh, except that he did not mention the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Another hadith Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Abi Asim said in his book Al-Sunan: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad, I heard Abu Umamah Al-Bahili say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “My Lord promised me that seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise, with each thousand seventy thousand who will not be held accountable or punished, and three handfuls from the handfuls of my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic.” And this is how Al-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Hisham bin Ammar on the authority of Ismail bin Ayyash, and this is a good chain of transmission. Another way On the authority of Abu Umamah. Ibn Abi Asim said, Dahim told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us on the authority of Safwan bin Amr, on the authority of Salim bin Amir, on the authority of Abu Al-Yaman Al-Hawzani, whose name is Amir bin Abdullah bin Luhay, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, who said: “God promised me that seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account. Yazid bin Al-Akhns said: By God, those among your nation, O Messenger of God, are like a reddish fly among flies. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God promised me seventy thousand, with each thousand seventy thousand and He gave me three handfuls more.” This is also a good chain of transmission. Another hadith Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Khalid told us, Abu Tobah told us, Muawiyah ibn Salam told us on the authority of Zayd ibn Salam that he heard Abu Salam say: Aamer ibn Zayd al-Bakali told me that he heard Utbah ibn Abd al-Salami, may God be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My Lord, the Almighty, promised me that seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account, then every thousand will intercede for seventy thousand, then my Lord, the Almighty, will scoop up three handfuls of dust in His hands.” So Umar said: God will intercede for the first seventy for their fathers, sons, and clans, and I hope that God will make me one of the last handfuls of dust. Al-Hafiz al-Dhiya Abu Abdullah al-Maqdisi said in his book Sifat al-Jannah: I do not know of any defect in this chain of transmission, and God knows best. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told me, Hisham, meaning Al-Dastawai, told us, Yahya bin Abi Katheer told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Abi Maimouna, Ata bin Yasar told us that Rafa’ah Al-Juhani told him, he said: We set out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until we were at Al-Kadeed, or he said: at Qudayd, and he mentioned a hadith in which he said: “My Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, promised me that seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account, and I hope that they will not enter it until you and your righteous spouses and offspring have settled in dwellings in Paradise.” Al-Dhiya’ said: This, in my opinion, is in accordance with the conditions of Muslim. Another hadith Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma’mar informed us on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Nadr ibn Anas, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God promised me that He would admit four hundred thousand of my nation into Paradise. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: Give us more, O Messenger of God. He said: By God, this is it. Umar said: That is enough, O Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr said: Leave me alone, and what does it matter to you if God admits us all into Paradise? Umar said: God willing, He will admit His creation into Paradise with one hand. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Umar has spoken the truth. This hadith with this chain of transmission is unique to Abd al-Razzaq. Al-Dhiya’ said it and Al-Hafiz Abu Na’im Al-Isfahani narrated it. He said: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Mukhallad told us, Ibrahim bin Al-Haitham Al-Baldi told us, Sulayman bin Harb told us, Abu Hilal told us on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: My Lord promised me that He would admit one hundred thousand of my nation into Paradise. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, give us more. He said: And so it was, and Sulayman bin Harb pointed with his hand in the same manner. I said: O Messenger of God, give us more. Umar said: God is able to admit people into Paradise with a single handful. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Umar has spoken the truth. This is a strange hadith from this source. Abu Hilal’s name is Muhammad bin Salim Al-Rasibi, from Basra. Another chain of transmission on the authority of Anas. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr told us, `Abd al-Qahir ibn al-Sarri al-Sulami told us, Hamid told us on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise. They said: ‘Give us more, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘For every man there are seventy thousand.’ They said: ‘Give us more,’ and he was on a sand dune. He said like this and threw some with his hand. They said: ‘O Messenger of God, may God distance those who enter Hell after this.’” This is a good chain of transmission, and all of its men are trustworthy, except for `Abd al-Qahir ibn al-Sarri. Ibn Ma`in was asked about him and said: He is trustworthy. Another hadith Al-Tabarani narrated from the hadith of Qatada on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Umair, on the authority of his father that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God promised me that three hundred thousand of my nation would enter Paradise. Umair said: O Messenger of God, give us more. He said: This way, with his hand. Umair said: O Messenger of God, give us more. Umar said: It is enough for you. If God wills, He will admit people to Paradise with a handful or a single handful. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Umar spoke the truth.” Another hadith Al-Tabarani said: Ahmad bin Khalid told us, Abu Tobah told us, Muawiyah bin Salam told us on the authority of Zaid bin Salam that he heard Abu Salam say: Abdullah bin Aamer told me that Qais Al-Kindi told him that Abu Saeed Al-Anmari told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My Lord promised me that He will admit seventy thousand of my nation to Paradise without account, and every thousand will intercede for seventy thousand, then my Lord will take three handfuls with His two hands.” That is what Qais said, so I said to Abu Saeed: Did you hear this from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: Yes, with my ears, and my heart has retained it. Abu Saeed said: He said, meaning the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: And that, God Almighty willing, will include the emigrants of my nation and God will fulfill the remainder of our Arabs. Muhammad bin Sahl bin Askar narrated this hadith on the authority of Abu Tawbah al-Rabi’ bin Nafi’ with his chain of transmission similarly, and he added: Abu Saeed said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, calculated that, and it amounted to four hundred thousand thousand and ninety thousand thousand. Another hadith Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hashim ibn Murthad al-Tabarani told us, Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Ayyash told us, my father told me, Damdam ibn Zur’ah told me, on the authority of Shuraih ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, a group of you will be sent to Paradise on the Day of Resurrection, all of them striking the earth. The angels will say: Why did more people come with Muhammad than came with the prophets?” This is a good chain of transmission. Another type - From the hadiths that indicate the virtue, honor, and dignity of this nation before God the Almighty, and that it is the best nation in this world and the hereafter. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, Abu al-Zubayr told me on the authority of Jabir that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: I hope that those of my nation who follow me on the Day of Resurrection will be a quarter of Paradise. He said: “So we said ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then he said: “I hope that they will be a third of the people.” He said: “So we said ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then he said: “I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise.” And this is how he narrated it on the authority of Ruh on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, and it meets the conditions of Muslim. It is proven in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Ishaq al-Subai’i on the authority of Amr bin Maymun, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: Are you not pleased to be a quarter of the people of Paradise? So we said ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then he said: Are you not pleased to be a third of the people of Paradise? So we said ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then he said: I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise. Another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud. Al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Musawar told us, `Affan ibn Muslim told us, `Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, al-Harith ibn Hasira told me, al-Qasim ibn `Abd al-Rahman told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How will you be when a quarter of Paradise is for you and three quarters of it are for the rest of the people? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: How will you be when a third of it is for you? They said: That is more. He said: How will you be when half of it is for you? They said: That is more. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, eighty of which are for you. Al-Tabarani said: Al-Harith ibn Hasira is the only one to narrate it. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim told us, Dhirar ibn Murrah Abu Sinan al-Shaibani told us, on the authority of Muharib ibn Dithar, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, and this nation is eighty rows from that. And he narrated it likewise on the authority of Affan on the authority of Abd al-Aziz on his authority, and al-Tirmidhi included it on the authority of Abu Sinan on his authority, and he said: This is a good hadith, and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri on the authority of Alqamah ibn Marthad, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father on his authority. Another hadith - Al-Tabarani narrated from the hadith of Sulayman bin Abd al-Rahman al-Dimashqi: Khalid bin Yazid al-Bajali told us, Sulayman bin Ali bin Abdullah bin Abbas told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, eighty of which are from my nation. Khalid bin Yazid al-Bajali was the only one to narrate it, and Ibn Adi spoke about it. Another hadith Al-Tabarani said: Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal told us, Musa bin Ghailan told us, Hashim bin Mukhallad told us, Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Amr, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: When A group of the first and a group of the last was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You are a quarter of the people of Paradise, you are a third of the people of Paradise, you are half of the people of Paradise, you are two-thirds of the people of Paradise. Abdul Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection. We are the first people to enter Paradise, but they were given the Book before us and we were given it after them. So God guided us to the truth in what they differed about. So this is the day in which they differed, people will follow us. Tomorrow will be for the Jews and the day after tomorrow will be for the Christians.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim on the authority of Abdullah bin Tawus on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Al-A'mash on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection, and we are the first to enter Paradise. And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. Another hadith - Al-Daraqutni narrated in Al-Afrad from the hadith of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqil on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Paradise was forbidden to all the prophets until I enter it, and it was forbidden to the nations until my nation enters it. Then he said: Ibn Aqil was the only one to narrate it on the authority of Al-Zuhri, and no one else narrated it on his authority. Zuhair bin Muhammad was the only one to narrate it on the authority of Ibn Aqil, and Amr bin Abi Salamah was the only one to narrate it on the authority of Zuhair. Abu Ahmad bin Adi Al-Hafiz narrated it, and he said: Ahmad bin Al-Hussein bin Ishaq told us, Abu Bakr Al-A’in Muhammad bin Abi Atab told us, Abu Hafs Al-Tanisi told us - meaning Amr bin Abi Salamah - Sadaqa Al-Dimashqi told us on the authority of Zuhair bin Muhammad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqil on the authority of Al-Zuhri. Al-Tha’labi narrated it: Abu al-Abbas al-Mukhalladi told us, Abu Na’im Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad told us, Ahmad ibn Isa al-Tanisi told us, Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us, Sadaqah ibn Abdullah told us, on the authority of Zuhair ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Ibn Aqil, on his authority. These hadiths are in the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: “You are the best nation produced for mankind. You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in God.” So whoever from this nation is characterized by these qualities is included with them in this praise and commendation of them, as Qatada said: It has reached us that Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, during his Hajj, saw the people rushing, so he recited this verse: You are the best nation produced for mankind. Then he said: Whoever is pleased to be from that nation, let him fulfill God’s condition regarding it. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. And whoever is not characterized by this is more like the People of the Book whom God condemned in His saying: They used not to forbid one another from the wrong they did Al-Baqarah 2:17. For this reason, when God praised this nation for these qualities, He began to condemn and rebuke the People of the Book, so God said: And if the People of the Scripture had believed, meaning in what was revealed to Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, “it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are wicked,” meaning few of them believe in God and what was revealed to you and what was revealed to them, and most of them are misguided, disbelieving, and wicked. And disobedience. Then the Almighty said, informing His believing servants and giving them good report that victory and triumph will be theirs over the disbelieving atheist People of the Book. The Almighty said: “They will not harm you except with an injury. And if they fight you, they will turn their backs to you; then they will not be helped.” And so it happened. On the day of Khaybar, God humiliated them and made their noses ache. Likewise, those before them from the Jews of Medina, Banu Qaynuqa, Banu Nadir, and Banu Qurayzah, all of them were humiliated by God. Likewise, the Christians in the Levant, the Companions defeated them in more than one place, and they were deprived of the kingdom of the Levant forever and ever. The band of Islam will continue to exist in the Levant until Jesus, son of Mary, descends while they are still like that. He will rule by the religion of Islam and the law of Muhammad, may the best prayers and peace be upon him. He will break the cross, kill the pigs, and abolish the jizya, and will accept nothing but Islam. Then God the Almighty said: And humiliation has been imposed upon them wherever they are found, except by a covenant from God and a covenant from the people. That is, God has imposed humiliation and degradation upon them wherever they are, so they are not safe. Except by a covenant from God, that is, by a protection from God, which is the covenant of protection for them, imposing the jizyah on them, and imposing the rulings of the religion on them. And a covenant from the people, that is, security from them for them, as in the case of a truce, a covenanted one, and a prisoner if one of the Muslims grants him security, even if it is a woman, and likewise a slave according to one of the two opinions of the scholars. Ibn Abbas said: Except by a covenant from God and a covenant from the people, that is, by a covenant from God and a covenant from the people. This is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ata, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said. And His statement: And they incurred the wrath of God, that is, they were obligated, so they committed themselves to the wrath of God, and they deserved it. And poverty has been imposed upon them, that is, they were obligated to it by fate and by law. That is why He said, That is because they disbelieved in the signs of God and killed the prophets unjustly. That is, what drove them to do that was arrogance, oppression, and envy, and that was followed by humiliation, lowliness, and poverty forever, connected to the humiliation of the Hereafter. Then God the Almighty said, That is because they disobeyed and were transgressing. That is, what drove them to disbelieve in the signs of God and kill the messengers of God, and they were destined for that - that they were frequently disobeying the commands of God the Almighty and committing sins against God, and transgressing against the law of God. So we seek refuge in God from that, and God the Almighty is the One sought for help. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Habib told us, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Mu’ammar al-Azdi, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Children of Israel used to kill three hundred prophets a day, and then a market would be held to kill them at the end of the day.
3:112: The Almighty tells us about this Muhammadan nation that they are the best of nations, so He the Almighty said: You are the best nation produced for mankind. Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Maysarah, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, You are the best nation produced for mankind. He said: The best of people for mankind, you bring them in chains around their necks until they enter Islam. And this is what Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Atiyah Al-Awfi, Ikrimah, Ata, and Al-Rabi bin Anas said: You are the best nation produced for mankind, meaning the best of people for mankind, and the meaning is that they are the best of nations and the most beneficial people to people, and for this reason He said: You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in God. Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad bin Abdul Malik told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umaira, on the authority of the husband of Durrah bint Abi Lahab, on the authority of Durrah bint Abi Lahab, who said: "A man stood up to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was on the pulpit, and said: O Messenger of God, which of the people is the best? He said: The best of people are those who recite the Qur’an the most, are those who fear God the most, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and maintain ties of kinship. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, and al-Nasa’i in his Sunan, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God the Almighty: You are the best nation produced for mankind. He said: They are those who migrated with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca to Medina. The correct view is that this verse is general for the entire nation, each generation according to its own circumstances, and the best of their generations are those among whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, then those who came after them, then those who came after them, as He said in the other verse: And thus We have made you a just community, meaning the best, that you will be witnesses over the people. In Musnad of Imam Ahmad, Jami` al-Tirmidhi, Sunan Ibn Majah and Mustadrak al-Hakim, on the authority of Hakim ibn Mu`awiyah ibn Haidah, on the authority of his father, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘You are the best of seventy nations, and you are the most honorable to God, the Almighty. ’” This is a well-known hadith, and al-Tirmidhi classified it as hasan. It is also narrated on the authority of Mu`adh ibn Jabal and Abu Sa`id, similar to it. This nation has achieved the lead in good deeds through its Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for he is the most honorable of God’s creation and the most honorable of the Messengers to God. God sent him with a complete and great law that no Prophet or Messenger before him was given. So, working according to his method and path is enough to replace a little of what a lot of work from others cannot replace, as Imam Ahmad said: ‘Abd al-Rahman told us, Ibn Zuhair told us, on the authority of Abdullah, meaning Ibn Muhammad ibn `Aqil, on the authority of Muhammad ibn `Ali, who is Ibn al-Hanafiyyah, that he heard `Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, say: “The Messenger of God said: I have been given what none of the Prophets have been given.” We said, O Messenger of God, what is it? He said, I have been aided by terror, I have been given the keys to the earth, I have been named Ahmad, the earth has been made a means of purification for me, and my nation has been made the best of nations. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this source, and its chain of transmission is good. Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Al-Ala Al-Hasan bin Suwar told us, Laith told us, on the authority of Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Halbas Yazid bin Maysarah, who said: I heard Umm Al-Darda’, may God be pleased with her, say: I heard Abu Al-Darda’, may God be pleased with him, say: “I heard Abu Al-Qasim, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and I had never heard him use his kunya before or after that, saying: God Almighty says: O Jesus, I will send after you a nation who, if what they like befalls them, will praise and thank them, and if what they dislike befalls them, they will seek reward and be patient, but they have no patience or knowledge.” He said: O Lord, how can this be for them, and they have no patience or knowledge? He said: I will give them from My patience and knowledge. There are hadiths that are appropriate to mention here. Imam Ahmad said: Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, Al-Masoudi told us, Bakir bin Al-Akhns told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have been given seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being brought to account, their faces like the moon on the night of the full moon, their hearts like the heart of one man, so I asked my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, for more, and He increased me with each one by seventy thousand.” Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: I saw that this would come upon the people of the villages and would befall those on the edges of the deserts. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Bakr Al-Sahmi told us, Hisham bin Hassan told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Mihran, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaid, on the authority of Maimun bin Mihran, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Bakr: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: My Lord has given me seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being brought to account. Umar said: O Messenger of God, why didn’t you ask Him for more? He said: I asked Him for more, and He gave me seventy thousand with each man. Umar said: Why didn’t you ask Him for more? He said: I asked Him for more, and He gave me this much.” And Abdullah bin Bakr spread his hands apart, and Abdullah said: And he stretched out his arms, and Abdullah urged, and Hisham said: This is from God, and he does not know how many. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abu Al-Yaman told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Damdam bin Zur’ah, who said: Shureih bin Ubaid said: Thawban fell ill in Homs, and Abdullah bin Qurt Al-Azdi was in charge of it, so he did not visit him. Then a man from the Kalaa’in came to visit Thawban, and Thawban said to him: Will you write? He said: Yes. He said: Write. So he wrote to the emir Abdullah bin Qurt from Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: As for what follows, if Moses and Jesus, peace be upon them, had a servant in your presence, you would have visited him. Then he folded the letter and said to him: Will you deliver it to him? He said: Yes. So the man went with his letter and gave it to Ibn Qurt, and when he saw him, he stood up in a panic, and the people said: What is the matter with him? Has something happened? Then Thawban came until he entered upon him, visited him and sat with him for a while, then he stood up and Thawban took his cloak and said: Sit down until I tell you a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in which he said: Seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account or punished, and with every thousand there will be seventy thousand. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this source and its chain of transmission is all trustworthy men from Syria and Homs, so it is a sound hadith, praise and thanks be to God. Another path: Al-Tabarani said: Amr bin Ishaq bin Zubayriq Al-Himsi told us, Muhammad bin Ismail, meaning Ibn Ayyash, told us, my father told me, on the authority of Damdam bin Zar’ah, on the authority of Shureih bin Ubaid, on the authority of Abu Asma Al-Rahbi, on the authority of Thawban, may God be pleased with him, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘My Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, promised me seventy thousand of my nation who will not be held accountable, with every thousand seventy thousand.’” Perhaps this is what is preserved with the addition of Abu Asma Al-Rahbi between Shureih and Thawban, and God knows best. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: We talked most of the time with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, one night, then we went to him and he said: “The prophets were shown to me tonight with their nations. A prophet would pass by with three people, a prophet with a group, a prophet with a few people, and a prophet with no one with him, until Moses, peace be upon him, passed by with a large group of the Children of Israel. I was amazed and said: Who are these? It was said: This is your brother Moses with the Children of Israel. He said: I said: Where are my nation? It was said: Look to your right.
