I looked and saw that the curtains had been closed with the faces of men. Then it was said to me: Look to your left. I looked and saw that the horizon had been closed with the faces of men. It was said to me: Are you satisfied? I said: I am satisfied, O Lord. He said: It was said to me: There are seventy thousand with these who will enter Paradise without being brought to account. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And he said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, if you are able to be among the seventy thousand, then do so. If you fall short, then be among the people of the valley. If you fall short, then be among the people of the horizon, for I have seen people quarreling with one another. So Ukasha bin Muhsin stood up and said: O Messenger of God, pray to God to make me one of them, meaning one of the seventy. So he prayed for him, and another man stood up and said: Pray to God, O Messenger of God, to make me one of them. So he said: Ukasha has preceded you in that. He said: Then we talked and said: Who do you think these seventy thousand are? They are people who were born in Islam and did not associate anything with God until they died. So that reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “They are those who do not seek ruqyah, nor cauterize, nor take omens, and they put their trust in their Lord.” This is how Ahmad narrated it with this chain of transmission and this context. He also narrated it on the authority of Abd al-Samad on the authority of Hisham on the authority of Qatadah with his chain of transmission similarly, and he added after his saying: I am satisfied, O Lord, I am satisfied, O Lord. He said: I am satisfied. I said: Yes. He said: Look to your left. He said: So I looked and saw that the horizon was blocked by the faces of men. He said: Are you satisfied? I said: I am satisfied. This is a sound chain of transmission from this source, transmitted only by Ahmad, and they did not include it. Another hadith Ahmad ibn Mani’ said: Abd al-Malik ibn Abd al-Aziz told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The nations were presented to me with seasons, and my nation was pleased with me. Then I saw them and I was amazed by their large numbers and their appearance. They filled the plains and the mountains. He said: Are you satisfied, O Muhammad? I said: Yes. He said: With these are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being brought to account. They are those who do not seek incantations or cauterize, and they put their trust in their Lord. Then ‘Ukasha ibn Muhsin stood up and said: O Messenger of God, ask God to make me one of them. He said: You are one of them. Then another man stood up and said: Ask God to make me one of them. He said: ‘Ukasha beat you to it.” Narrated by al-Hafiz al-Dhiya’ al-Maqdisi, who said: This, in my opinion, meets the conditions of Muslim. Another hadith Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Al-Judhu’i Al-Qadi told us, Uqbah ibn Mukram told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hassan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account or punished. It was said: Who are they? He said: They are those who do not cauterize, nor seek omens, nor believe in omens, and they put their trust in their Lord. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Hisham ibn Hassan, and he mentioned Ukasha. Another hadith It was established in the two Sahihs on the authority of Az-Zuhri on the authority of Sa`id ibn Al-Musayyab that Abu Hurairah told him: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘A group of my nation will enter Paradise, and they will be seventy thousand, and their faces will shine like the moon on a full moon night.’ Abu Hurairah said: ‘Ukasha ibn Muhsin Al-Asadi stood up, raising his blanket and said: ‘O Messenger of God, pray to God to make me one of them.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O God, make him one of them.’ Then a man from the Ansar stood up and said the same thing, and he said: ‘Ukasha beat you to it.’” Another hadith Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Yahya ibn Uthman told us, Saeed ibn Abi Maryam told us, Abu Ghassan told us, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa`d, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Seventy thousand - or seven hundred thousand - of my nation will enter Paradise, some of them taking others, until the first of them and the last of them enter Paradise, and their faces will be like the moon on the night of the full moon.” Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of `Abd al-`Aziz ibn Abi Hazim on the authority of his father on the authority of Sahl on his authority. Another Hadith Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj said in his Sahih: Saeed bin Mansour told us, Hisham told us, Hiseen bin Abdul Rahman told us, he said: I was with Saeed bin Jubair and he said, Which of you saw the star that fell last night? I said: I did. Then I said: I was not praying, but I was stung. He said: So what did you do? I said: I sought ruqyah. He said: What made you do that? I said: A Hadith narrated to us by Al-Sha’bi. He said: And what did Al-Sha’bi tell you? I said: He told us on the authority of Buraydah ibn al-Husaib al-Aslami that he said: There is no ruqyah except for the evil eye or a fever. He said: He who has concluded what he heard has done well. However, Ibn Abbas told us on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “The nations were presented to me and I saw the Prophet with a group of people, the Prophet with one or two men, and the Prophet with no one with him. Then a great multitude was raised to me and I thought that they were my nation. Then it was said to me: This is Moses and his people, but look to the horizon. So I looked and saw a great multitude. Then it was said to me: Look to the other horizon and see a great multitude. Then it was said to me: This is your nation and with them are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without being held accountable or punished. Then he got up and entered his house.” So the people began to argue about those who will enter Paradise without being held accountable or punished. Some of them said: Perhaps they are those who accompanied the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some of them said: Perhaps they are those who were born in Islam and did not associate anything with God. They mentioned things, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to them and said: What are you arguing about? So they told him. He said: They are those who do not perform ruqyah, nor seek ruqyah from others, nor take omens, and they put their trust in their Lord. Then Ukasha bin Muhsin stood up and said: Ask God to make me one of them. He said: You are one of them. Then another man stood up and said: Ask God to make me one of them. He said: Ukasha beat you to it. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Asid bin Zaid on the authority of Hisham, but he does not have: they do not perform ruqyah. Another hadith Ahmad said: Ruh ibn Ubadah told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, Abu al-Zubayr told me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mention a hadith, in which it says: The first group will be saved, their faces like the moon on the night of the full moon, seventy thousand who will not be held accountable, then those who follow them will be like the brightest star in the sky.” Then likewise, and he mentioned the rest of it. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Ruh, except that he did not mention the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Another hadith Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Abi Asim said in his book Al-Sunan: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us on the authority of Muhammad bin Ziyad, I heard Abu Umamah Al-Bahili say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “My Lord promised me that seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise, with each thousand seventy thousand who will not be held accountable or punished, and three handfuls from the handfuls of my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic.” And this is how Al-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Hisham bin Ammar on the authority of Ismail bin Ayyash, and this is a good chain of transmission. Another way On the authority of Abu Umamah. Ibn Abi Asim said, Dahim told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us on the authority of Safwan bin Amr, on the authority of Salim bin Amir, on the authority of Abu Al-Yaman Al-Hawzani, whose name is Amir bin Abdullah bin Luhay, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, who said: “God promised me that seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account. Yazid bin Al-Akhns said: By God, those among your nation, O Messenger of God, are like a reddish fly among flies. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God promised me seventy thousand, with each thousand seventy thousand and He gave me three handfuls more.” This is also a good chain of transmission. Another hadith Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Khalid told us, Abu Tobah told us, Muawiyah ibn Salam told us on the authority of Zayd ibn Salam that he heard Abu Salam say: Aamer ibn Zayd al-Bakali told me that he heard Utbah ibn Abd al-Salami, may God be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My Lord, the Almighty, promised me that seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account, then every thousand will intercede for seventy thousand, then my Lord, the Almighty, will scoop up three handfuls of dust in His hands.” So Umar said: God will intercede for the first seventy for their fathers, sons, and clans, and I hope that God will make me one of the last handfuls of dust. Al-Hafiz al-Dhiya Abu Abdullah al-Maqdisi said in his book Sifat al-Jannah: I do not know of any defect in this chain of transmission, and God knows best. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told me, Hisham, meaning Al-Dastawai, told us, Yahya bin Abi Katheer told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Abi Maimouna, Ata bin Yasar told us that Rafa’ah Al-Juhani told him, he said: We set out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until we were at Al-Kadeed, or he said: at Qudayd, and he mentioned a hadith in which he said: “My Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, promised me that seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without being brought to account, and I hope that they will not enter it until you and your righteous spouses and offspring have settled in dwellings in Paradise.” Al-Dhiya’ said: This, in my opinion, is in accordance with the conditions of Muslim. Another hadith Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma’mar informed us on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Nadr ibn Anas, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God promised me that He would admit four hundred thousand of my nation into Paradise. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: Give us more, O Messenger of God. He said: By God, this is it. Umar said: That is enough, O Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr said: Leave me alone, and what does it matter to you if God admits us all into Paradise? Umar said: God willing, He will admit His creation into Paradise with one hand. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Umar has spoken the truth. This hadith with this chain of transmission is unique to Abd al-Razzaq. Al-Dhiya’ said it and Al-Hafiz Abu Na’im Al-Isfahani narrated it. He said: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Mukhallad told us, Ibrahim bin Al-Haitham Al-Baldi told us, Sulayman bin Harb told us, Abu Hilal told us on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: My Lord promised me that He would admit one hundred thousand of my nation into Paradise. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, give us more. He said: And so it was, and Sulayman bin Harb pointed with his hand in the same manner. I said: O Messenger of God, give us more. Umar said: God is able to admit people into Paradise with a single handful. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Umar has spoken the truth. This is a strange hadith from this source. Abu Hilal’s name is Muhammad bin Salim Al-Rasibi, from Basra. Another chain of transmission on the authority of Anas. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr told us, `Abd al-Qahir ibn al-Sarri al-Sulami told us, Hamid told us on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise. They said: ‘Give us more, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘For every man there are seventy thousand.’ They said: ‘Give us more,’ and he was on a sand dune. He said like this and threw some with his hand. They said: ‘O Messenger of God, may God distance those who enter Hell after this.’” This is a good chain of transmission, and all of its men are trustworthy, except for `Abd al-Qahir ibn al-Sarri. Ibn Ma`in was asked about him and said: He is trustworthy. Another hadith Al-Tabarani narrated from the hadith of Qatada on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Anas, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Umair, on the authority of his father that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God promised me that three hundred thousand of my nation would enter Paradise. Umair said: O Messenger of God, give us more. He said: This way, with his hand. Umair said: O Messenger of God, give us more. Umar said: It is enough for you. If God wills, He will admit people to Paradise with a handful or a single handful. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Umar spoke the truth.” Another hadith Al-Tabarani said: Ahmad bin Khalid told us, Abu Tobah told us, Muawiyah bin Salam told us on the authority of Zaid bin Salam that he heard Abu Salam say: Abdullah bin Aamer told me that Qais Al-Kindi told him that Abu Saeed Al-Anmari told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My Lord promised me that He will admit seventy thousand of my nation to Paradise without account, and every thousand will intercede for seventy thousand, then my Lord will take three handfuls with His two hands.” That is what Qais said, so I said to Abu Saeed: Did you hear this from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: Yes, with my ears, and my heart has retained it. Abu Saeed said: He said, meaning the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: And that, God Almighty willing, will include the emigrants of my nation and God will fulfill the remainder of our Arabs. Muhammad bin Sahl bin Askar narrated this hadith on the authority of Abu Tawbah al-Rabi’ bin Nafi’ with his chain of transmission similarly, and he added: Abu Saeed said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, calculated that, and it amounted to four hundred thousand thousand and ninety thousand thousand. Another hadith Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hashim ibn Murthad al-Tabarani told us, Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Ayyash told us, my father told me, Damdam ibn Zur’ah told me, on the authority of Shuraih ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, a group of you will be sent to Paradise on the Day of Resurrection, all of them striking the earth. The angels will say: Why did more people come with Muhammad than came with the prophets?” This is a good chain of transmission. Another type - From the hadiths that indicate the virtue, honor, and dignity of this nation before God the Almighty, and that it is the best nation in this world and the hereafter. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, Abu al-Zubayr told me on the authority of Jabir that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: I hope that those of my nation who follow me on the Day of Resurrection will be a quarter of Paradise. He said: “So we said ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then he said: “I hope that they will be a third of the people.” He said: “So we said ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then he said: “I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise.” And this is how he narrated it on the authority of Ruh on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, and it meets the conditions of Muslim. It is proven in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Ishaq al-Subai’i on the authority of Amr bin Maymun, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: Are you not pleased to be a quarter of the people of Paradise? So we said ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then he said: Are you not pleased to be a third of the people of Paradise? So we said ‘Allahu Akbar,’ then he said: I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise. Another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud. Al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Musawar told us, `Affan ibn Muslim told us, `Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, al-Harith ibn Hasira told me, al-Qasim ibn `Abd al-Rahman told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How will you be when a quarter of Paradise is for you and three quarters of it are for the rest of the people? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: How will you be when a third of it is for you? They said: That is more. He said: How will you be when half of it is for you? They said: That is more. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, eighty of which are for you. Al-Tabarani said: Al-Harith ibn Hasira is the only one to narrate it. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim told us, Dhirar ibn Murrah Abu Sinan al-Shaibani told us, on the authority of Muharib ibn Dithar, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, and this nation is eighty rows from that. And he narrated it likewise on the authority of Affan on the authority of Abd al-Aziz on his authority, and al-Tirmidhi included it on the authority of Abu Sinan on his authority, and he said: This is a good hadith, and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri on the authority of Alqamah ibn Marthad, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father on his authority. Another hadith - Al-Tabarani narrated from the hadith of Sulayman bin Abd al-Rahman al-Dimashqi: Khalid bin Yazid al-Bajali told us, Sulayman bin Ali bin Abdullah bin Abbas told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows, eighty of which are from my nation. Khalid bin Yazid al-Bajali was the only one to narrate it, and Ibn Adi spoke about it. Another hadith Al-Tabarani said: Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal told us, Musa bin Ghailan told us, Hashim bin Mukhallad told us, Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Amr, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: When A group of the first and a group of the last was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You are a quarter of the people of Paradise, you are a third of the people of Paradise, you are half of the people of Paradise, you are two-thirds of the people of Paradise. Abdul Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection. We are the first people to enter Paradise, but they were given the Book before us and we were given it after them. So God guided us to the truth in what they differed about. So this is the day in which they differed, people will follow us. Tomorrow will be for the Jews and the day after tomorrow will be for the Christians.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim on the authority of Abdullah bin Tawus on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Al-A'mash on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection, and we are the first to enter Paradise. And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. Another hadith - Al-Daraqutni narrated in Al-Afrad from the hadith of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqil on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Paradise was forbidden to all the prophets until I enter it, and it was forbidden to the nations until my nation enters it. Then he said: Ibn Aqil was the only one to narrate it on the authority of Al-Zuhri, and no one else narrated it on his authority. Zuhair bin Muhammad was the only one to narrate it on the authority of Ibn Aqil, and Amr bin Abi Salamah was the only one to narrate it on the authority of Zuhair. Abu Ahmad bin Adi Al-Hafiz narrated it, and he said: Ahmad bin Al-Hussein bin Ishaq told us, Abu Bakr Al-A’in Muhammad bin Abi Atab told us, Abu Hafs Al-Tanisi told us - meaning Amr bin Abi Salamah - Sadaqa Al-Dimashqi told us on the authority of Zuhair bin Muhammad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqil on the authority of Al-Zuhri. Al-Tha’labi narrated it: Abu al-Abbas al-Mukhalladi told us, Abu Na’im Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad told us, Ahmad ibn Isa al-Tanisi told us, Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us, Sadaqah ibn Abdullah told us, on the authority of Zuhair ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Ibn Aqil, on his authority. These hadiths are in the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: “You are the best nation produced for mankind. You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in God.” So whoever from this nation is characterized by these qualities is included with them in this praise and commendation of them, as Qatada said: It has reached us that Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, during his Hajj, saw the people rushing, so he recited this verse: You are the best nation produced for mankind. Then he said: Whoever is pleased to be from that nation, let him fulfill God’s condition regarding it. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. And whoever is not characterized by this is more like the People of the Book whom God condemned in His saying: They used not to forbid one another from the wrong they did Al-Baqarah 2:17. For this reason, when God praised this nation for these qualities, He began to condemn and rebuke the People of the Book, so God said: And if the People of the Scripture had believed, meaning in what was revealed to Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, “it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are wicked,” meaning few of them believe in God and what was revealed to you and what was revealed to them, and most of them are misguided, disbelieving, and wicked. And disobedience. Then the Almighty said, informing His believing servants and giving them good report that victory and triumph will be theirs over the disbelieving atheist People of the Book. The Almighty said: “They will not harm you except with an injury. And if they fight you, they will turn their backs to you; then they will not be helped.” And so it happened. On the day of Khaybar, God humiliated them and made their noses ache. Likewise, those before them from the Jews of Medina, Banu Qaynuqa, Banu Nadir, and Banu Qurayzah, all of them were humiliated by God. Likewise, the Christians in the Levant, the Companions defeated them in more than one place, and they were deprived of the kingdom of the Levant forever and ever. The band of Islam will continue to exist in the Levant until Jesus, son of Mary, descends while they are still like that. He will rule by the religion of Islam and the law of Muhammad, may the best prayers and peace be upon him. He will break the cross, kill the pigs, and abolish the jizya, and will accept nothing but Islam. Then God the Almighty said: And humiliation has been imposed upon them wherever they are found, except by a covenant from God and a covenant from the people. That is, God has imposed humiliation and degradation upon them wherever they are, so they are not safe. Except by a covenant from God, that is, by a protection from God, which is the covenant of protection for them, imposing the jizyah on them, and imposing the rulings of the religion on them. And a covenant from the people, that is, security from them for them, as in the case of a truce, a covenanted one, and a prisoner if one of the Muslims grants him security, even if it is a woman, and likewise a slave according to one of the two opinions of the scholars. Ibn Abbas said: Except by a covenant from God and a covenant from the people, that is, by a covenant from God and a covenant from the people. This is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ata, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said. And His statement: And they incurred the wrath of God, that is, they were obligated, so they committed themselves to the wrath of God, and they deserved it. And poverty has been imposed upon them, that is, they were obligated to it by fate and by law. That is why He said, That is because they disbelieved in the signs of God and killed the prophets unjustly. That is, what drove them to do that was arrogance, oppression, and envy, and that was followed by humiliation, lowliness, and poverty forever, connected to the humiliation of the Hereafter. Then God the Almighty said, That is because they disobeyed and were transgressing. That is, what drove them to disbelieve in the signs of God and kill the messengers of God, and they were destined for that - that they were frequently disobeying the commands of God the Almighty and committing sins against God, and transgressing against the law of God. So we seek refuge in God from that, and God the Almighty is the One sought for help. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn Habib told us, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Mu’ammar al-Azdi, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Children of Israel used to kill three hundred prophets a day, and then a market would be held to kill them at the end of the day.
3:113: Ibn Abi Nujayh said: Al-Hasan bin Yazid Al-Ajli claimed, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, regarding the Almighty’s statement: They are not equal among the People of the Scripture - there is a community standing. He said: The People of the Scripture and the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, are not equal. And this is what Al-Suddi said. This statement is supported by the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal in his Musnad: Abu al-Nadr and Hasan ibn Musa told us: Shaiban told us on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delayed the Isha prayer, then went out to the mosque, and found the people waiting for the prayer. He said: ‘As for the people of these religions, there is no one who remembers God at this hour except you.’” He said: “These verses were revealed: ‘They are not all alike. Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing, reciting the verses of God during the hours of the night and prostrating. They believe in God and the Last Day, and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and hasten to good deeds. Those are among the righteous. And whatever good they do - never will it be denied them. And God is Knowing of the righteous.’” What is well-known among many commentators, as mentioned by Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others, and narrated by al-`Awfi on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, is that these verses were revealed about those who believed from the rabbis of the People of the Scripture, such as `Abdullah ibn Salam, Asad ibn `Ubayd, Tha`labah ibn Sa`yah, Asid ibn Sa`yah, and others, meaning that those mentioned above are not all alike. By blaming the People of the Book, and those who converted to Islam, and for this reason the Almighty said: They are not equal, meaning not all of them are equal, rather some of them are believers and some of them are criminals, and for this reason the Almighty said: Among the People of the Book is a community standing, meaning standing by the command of God, obeying His law, following the Prophet of God, so they are standing, meaning upright, reciting the verses of God during the hours of the night and prostrating, meaning they stand at night and increase their night prayers, and recite the Qur’an in their prayers, “They believe in God and the Last Day, and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and hasten to good deeds. And those are among the righteous,” and these are the ones mentioned at the end of the Surah, And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in God and what was revealed to you and what was revealed to them, humbly submissive to God, the verse, and for this reason the Almighty said here, And whatever good they do - never will it be denied, meaning it will not be lost with God, rather He will reward them for it with the greatest reward, and God is Knowing of the righteous, meaning no work of a worker is hidden from Him, and the reward of one who does good work is not lost with Him. Then the Almighty said, informing about the disbelieving polytheists, Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them at all against God, meaning that they will not be repelled from God’s wrath or punishment if He intends it for them. And those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally. Then He gave an example of what the disbelievers spend in this worldly life, as stated by Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and Al-Suddi. The Almighty said, The likeness of what they spend in this worldly life is like a wind within which is a cold chill, meaning intense cold, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, and others. Ata' said: Cold and ice. Also on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid, In it is a cold meaning fire. This goes back to the first, because severe cold, especially ice, burns crops and fruits, just as something is burned by fire. It struck the crops of a people who wronged themselves and destroyed them meaning it burned them. By that, he means the scorching wind when it descends on a crop that is about to be mowed or harvested, so it destroys it and takes away the fruit or crops in it, so it takes them away and spoils them, so its owner loses them when he is most in need of them. Likewise, the disbelievers, God wipes out the reward of their deeds in this world and its fruits, just as He takes away the fruits of this crop because of the sins of its owner. Likewise, these people built their work on something other than a foundation and without a basis. And God did not wrong them, but they wrong themselves.

3:115: Ibn Abi Nujayh said: Al-Hasan bin Yazid Al-Ajli claimed, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, regarding the Almighty’s statement: They are not equal among the People of the Scripture - there is a community standing. He said: The People of the Scripture and the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, are not equal. And this is what Al-Suddi said. This statement is supported by the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal in his Musnad: Abu al-Nadr and Hasan ibn Musa told us: Shaiban told us on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delayed the Isha prayer, then went out to the mosque, and found the people waiting for the prayer. He said: ‘As for the people of these religions, there is no one who remembers God at this hour except you.’” He said: “These verses were revealed: ‘They are not all alike. Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing, reciting the verses of God during the hours of the night and prostrating. They believe in God and the Last Day, and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and hasten to good deeds. Those are among the righteous. And whatever good they do - never will it be denied them. And God is Knowing of the righteous.’” What is well-known among many commentators, as mentioned by Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others, and narrated by al-`Awfi on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, is that these verses were revealed about those who believed from the rabbis of the People of the Scripture, such as `Abdullah ibn Salam, Asad ibn `Ubayd, Tha`labah ibn Sa`yah, Asid ibn Sa`yah, and others, meaning that those mentioned above are not all alike. By blaming the People of the Book, and those who converted to Islam, and for this reason the Almighty said: They are not equal, meaning not all of them are equal, rather some of them are believers and some of them are criminals, and for this reason the Almighty said: Among the People of the Book is a community standing, meaning standing by the command of God, obeying His law, following the Prophet of God, so they are standing, meaning upright, reciting the verses of God during the hours of the night and prostrating, meaning they stand at night and increase their night prayers, and recite the Qur’an in their prayers, “They believe in God and the Last Day, and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and hasten to good deeds. And those are among the righteous,” and these are the ones mentioned at the end of the Surah, And indeed, among the People of the Book are those who believe in God and what was revealed to you and what was revealed to them, humbly submissive to God, the verse, and for this reason the Almighty said here, And whatever good they do - never will it be denied, meaning it will not be lost with God, rather He will reward them for it with the greatest reward, and God is Knowing of the righteous, meaning no work of a worker is hidden from Him, and the reward of one who does good work is not lost with Him. Then the Almighty said, informing about the disbelieving polytheists, Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them at all against God, meaning that they will not be repelled from God’s wrath or punishment if He intends it for them. And those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally. Then He gave an example of what the disbelievers spend in this worldly life, as stated by Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and Al-Suddi. The Almighty said, The likeness of what they spend in this worldly life is like a wind within which is a cold chill, meaning intense cold, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, and others. Ata' said: Cold and ice. Also on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid, In it is a cold meaning fire. This goes back to the first, because severe cold, especially ice, burns crops and fruits, just as something is burned by fire. It struck the crops of a people who wronged themselves and destroyed them meaning it burned them. By that, he means the scorching wind when it descends on a crop that is about to be mowed or harvested, so it destroys it and takes away the fruit or crops in it, so it takes them away and spoils them, so its owner loses them when he is most in need of them. Likewise, the disbelievers, God wipes out the reward of their deeds in this world and its fruits, just as He takes away the fruits of this crop because of the sins of its owner. Likewise, these people built their work on something other than a foundation and without a basis. And God did not wrong them, but they wrong themselves.

3:118: The Blessed and Most High says, forbidding His believing servants from taking the hypocrites as intimates, meaning that they reveal to them their secrets and what they conceal for their enemies. The hypocrites, with all their effort and energy, spare no effort in ruining the believers, meaning that they strive to oppose them and harm them with everything possible, and with whatever deceit and trickery they can, and they desire what will distress the believers and embarrass them and make it difficult for them. The Almighty says: Do not take intimates from other than yourselves meaning from other than you from the people of religions, and the intimates of a man are his family who are aware of his inner affairs. Al-Bukhari, Al-Nasa’i and others narrated from a group of people, including Yunus, Yahya bin Sa’id, Musa bin Uqbah and Ibn Abi Atiq, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God did not send a prophet or appoint a successor except that he had two entourages: an entourage that commanded him to do good and urged him to do it, and an entourage that commanded him to do evil and urged him to do it. The one who is protected is the one whom God protects.” Al-Awza’i and Mu’awiyah bin Salam narrated it on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a similar chain of transmission to the Prophet. It is possible that it is with Al-Zuhri on the authority of Abu Salamah on their authority. Al-Nasa’i also included it on the authority of Al-Zuhri. Al-Bukhari included it in his Sahih and said: Ubaydullah bin Abi Ja’far said on the authority of Safwan bin Salim on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of Abu Ayyub Al-Ansari, and he mentioned it. It is possible that it is with Abu Salamah on the authority of three of the Companions, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Ayoub Muhammad ibn al-Wazzan told us, Isa ibn Yunus told us, on the authority of Abu Hayyan al-Taimi, on the authority of Abu al-Zinba’, on the authority of Ibn Abi al-Dahqana, who said: It was said to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him: There is a young man from the people of al-Hirah who is a memorizer and a scribe, so why don’t you make him a scribe? He said: Then you have made an entourage from among the non-believers. In this trace and this verse there is evidence that the People of the Covenant are not permitted to be employed in writing that involves oppression against the Muslims and knowledge of the inner workings of their affairs that it is feared they will divulge to the enemies of the people of war. For this reason, the Almighty said: They spare no effort to cause you harm and wish you would suffer. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Ishaq bin Israel told us, Hisham told us, Al-A’wam told us on the authority of Al-Azhar bin Rashid, who said: They used to come to Anas, and if he told them a hadith and they did not know what it was, they would come to Al-Hasan, meaning Al-Basri, and he would explain it to them. He said: One day, it was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Do not seek light from the fire of the polytheists, and do not engrave Arabic on your rings. They did not know what it was, so they came to Al-Hasan and said to him: Anas told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not seek light from the fire of the polytheists, and do not engrave Arabic on your rings. Al-Hasan said: As for his saying: Do not engrave Arabic on your rings: Muhammad The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Do not seek light from the fire of the polytheists. He said: Do not consult the polytheists in your affairs. Then Al-Hasan said: “The confirmation of that is in the Book of God: ‘O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those other than yourselves. ’” This is how Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la may God have mercy on him narrated it. Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Mujahid bin Musa, on the authority of Hisham, and Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Hisham with a similar chain of transmission without mentioning the interpretation of Al-Hasan Al-Basri. This interpretation is questionable, but its meaning is clear: Do not engrave on your rings anything in Arabic, meaning in Arabic script, lest it resemble the engraving of the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ring, for its engraving was Muhammad, the Messenger of God. This is why it came in the authentic hadith that he forbade anyone from engraving on his engraving. As for seeking light from the fire of the polytheists, its meaning is that you do not approach them in dwellings such that you are with them in their country, but rather keep your distance from them and emigrate from their country. For this reason, Abu Dawud narrated: Their two fires will not be seen. And in the other hadith: Whoever gathers with a polytheist or lives with him is like him. So the hadith was interpreted according to what Al-Hasan, may God have mercy on him, said, and citing the verse as evidence for it is questionable, and God knows best. Then the Almighty said: Hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their hearts conceal is greater. That is, the enmity has appeared on the pages of their faces and the slips of their tongues, along with what they contain in their hearts of hatred for Islam and its people, something that is not hidden from a wise and intelligent person. For this reason, the Almighty said: We have made clear to you the signs, if you would understand. And the Almighty said: Here you are, loving them, but they do not love you. That is, you, O believers, love the hypocrites because of the faith they show you, so you love them for that, and they do not love you, neither inwardly nor outwardly. And you believe in the entire Book. That is, you do not have any doubt or suspicion about any of it, while they have doubt, suspicion, and confusion. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And you believe in the entire Book, meaning in your Book and their Book and in the books that came before that, and they disbelieve in your Book, so you are more deserving of hatred for them than they are for you. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. And when they meet you, they say, ‘We believe,’ but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage, and the fingertips are the tips of the fingers, as Qatada said. And the poet said: I wish my saliva wetted my throat and my fingers could hold ten Ibn Masoud, As-Suddi and Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas said: “The fingers are the toes. This is the way of the hypocrites. They show faith and love to the believers, but inwardly they are the opposite of that in every way, as God the Almighty said: “And when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you out of rage.” This is the most intense rage and resentment. God the Almighty said: “Say, ‘Die in your rage. Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts.’” That is, no matter how much you envy the believers and that angers you from them, know that God will perfect His favor upon His believing servants and perfect His religion, uphold His word and manifest His religion. So die in your rage. Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts. That is, He is Knowing of what your consciences conceal and what your innermost thoughts hold of hatred, envy and rancor towards the believers. He will reward you for it in this world by showing you the opposite of what you hope for, and in the Hereafter with severe torment in the Fire in which you will abide eternally, with no escape from it and no exit from which you will have. Then God the Almighty said: If good befalls you, it distresses them, but if evil befalls you, they rejoice at it. This state indicates the intensity of their enmity towards the believers, which is that if the believers are granted fertility, victory, support, and they increase in number and their supporters are strengthened, this distresses the hypocrites. And if a drought befalls the Muslims or the enemies defeat them, because of God’s wisdom in that - as happened on the Day of Uhud - the hypocrites rejoice at that. God the Almighty said, addressing the believers: But if you are patient and fear God, not at all will their plot harm you Al-An’am 2:17. God the Almighty guides them to safety from the evil of the wicked and the plot of the immoral by using patience, fear of God, and putting their trust in God, who encompasses their enemies, for they have no power or strength except through Him. He is the One Whose wills is, and what He does not will is not, and nothing occurs in existence except by His decree and will, and whoever puts his trust in Him, He will suffice him. Then the Almighty proceeded to mention the story of Uhud and the test it contained for His believing servants, and the distinction between the believers and the hypocrites and the explanation of the patience of the patient. The Almighty said:

He is the One Whose wills is, and what He does not will is not, and nothing occurs in existence except by His decree and will, and whoever puts his trust in Him, He will suffice him. Then the Almighty proceeded to mention the story of Uhud and the test it contained for His believing servants, and the distinction between the believers and the hypocrites and the explanation of the patience of the patient. The Almighty said:
3:120: The Blessed and Most High says, forbidding His believing servants from taking the hypocrites as intimates, meaning that they reveal to them their secrets and what they conceal for their enemies. The hypocrites, with all their effort and energy, spare no effort in ruining the believers, meaning that they strive to oppose them and harm them with everything possible, and with whatever deceit and trickery they can, and they desire what will distress the believers and embarrass them and make it difficult for them. The Almighty says: “Do not take intimates from other than yourselves” meaning from other than you from the people of religions, and the intimates of a man are his family who are aware of his inner affairs. Al-Bukhari, Al-Nasa’i and others narrated from a group of people, including Yunus, Yahya bin Sa’id, Musa bin Uqbah and Ibn Abi Atiq, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God did not send a prophet or appoint a successor except that he had two entourages: an entourage that commanded him to do good and urged him to do it, and an entourage that commanded him to do evil and urged him to do it. The one who is protected is the one whom God protects.” Al-Awza’i and Mu’awiyah bin Salam narrated it on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a similar chain of transmission to the Prophet. It is possible that it is with Al-Zuhri on the authority of Abu Salamah on their authority. Al-Nasa’i also included it on the authority of Al-Zuhri. Al-Bukhari included it in his Sahih and said: Ubaydullah bin Abi Ja’far said on the authority of Safwan bin Salim on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of Abu Ayyub Al-Ansari, and he mentioned it. It is possible that it is with Abu Salamah on the authority of three of the Companions, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Ayoub Muhammad ibn al-Wazzan told us, Isa ibn Yunus told us, on the authority of Abu Hayyan al-Taimi, on the authority of Abu al-Zinba’, on the authority of Ibn Abi al-Dahqana, who said: It was said to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him: There is a young man from the people of al-Hirah who is a memorizer and a scribe, so why don’t you make him a scribe? He said: Then you have made an entourage from among the non-believers. In this trace and this verse there is evidence that the People of the Covenant are not permitted to be employed in writing that involves oppression against the Muslims and knowledge of the inner workings of their affairs that it is feared they will divulge to the enemies of the people of war. For this reason, the Almighty said: They spare no effort to cause you harm and wish you would suffer. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Ishaq bin Israel told us, Hisham told us, Al-A’wam told us on the authority of Al-Azhar bin Rashid, who said: They used to come to Anas, and if he told them a hadith and they did not know what it was, they would come to Al-Hasan, meaning Al-Basri, and he would explain it to them. He said: One day, it was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Do not seek light from the fire of the polytheists, and do not engrave Arabic on your rings. They did not know what it was, so they came to Al-Hasan and said to him: Anas told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not seek light from the fire of the polytheists, and do not engrave Arabic on your rings. Al-Hasan said: As for his saying: Do not engrave Arabic on your rings: Muhammad The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Do not seek light from the fire of the polytheists. He said: Do not consult the polytheists in your affairs. Then Al-Hasan said: “The confirmation of that is in the Book of God: ‘O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those other than yourselves. ’” This is how Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la may God have mercy on him narrated it. Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Mujahid bin Musa, on the authority of Hisham, and Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Hisham with a similar chain of transmission without mentioning the interpretation of Al-Hasan Al-Basri. This interpretation is questionable, but its meaning is clear: Do not engrave on your rings anything in Arabic, meaning in Arabic script, lest it resemble the engraving of the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ring, for its engraving was Muhammad, the Messenger of God. This is why it came in the authentic hadith that he forbade anyone from engraving on his engraving. As for seeking light from the fire of the polytheists, its meaning is that you do not approach them in dwellings such that you are with them in their country, but rather keep your distance from them and emigrate from their country. For this reason, Abu Dawud narrated: Their two fires will not be seen. And in the other hadith: Whoever gathers with a polytheist or lives with him is like him. So the hadith was interpreted according to what Al-Hasan, may God have mercy on him, said, and citing the verse as evidence for it is questionable, and God knows best. Then the Almighty said: Hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their hearts conceal is greater. That is, the enmity has appeared on the pages of their faces and the slips of their tongues, along with what they contain in their hearts of hatred for Islam and its people, something that is not hidden from a wise and intelligent person. For this reason, the Almighty said: We have made clear to you the signs, if you would understand. And the Almighty said: Here you are, loving them, but they do not love you. That is, you, O believers, love the hypocrites because of the faith they show you, so you love them for that, and they do not love you, neither inwardly nor outwardly. And you believe in the entire Book. That is, you do not have any doubt or suspicion about any of it, while they have doubt, suspicion, and confusion. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And you believe in the entire Book, meaning in your Book and their Book and in the books that came before that, and they disbelieve in your Book, so you are more deserving of hatred for them than they are for you. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. And when they meet you, they say, ‘We believe,’ but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage, and the fingertips are the tips of the fingers, as Qatada said. And the poet said: I wish my saliva wetted my throat and my fingers could hold ten Ibn Masoud, As-Suddi and Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas said: “The fingers are the toes. This is the way of the hypocrites. They show faith and love to the believers, but inwardly they are the opposite of that in every way, as God the Almighty said: “And when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you out of rage.” This is the most intense rage and resentment. God the Almighty said: “Say, ‘Die in your rage. Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts.’” That is, no matter how much you envy the believers and that angers you from them, know that God will perfect His favor upon His believing servants and perfect His religion, uphold His word and manifest His religion. So die in your rage. Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts. That is, He is Knowing of what your consciences conceal and what your innermost thoughts hold of hatred, envy and rancor towards the believers. He will reward you for it in this world by showing you the opposite of what you hope for, and in the Hereafter with severe torment in the Fire in which you will abide eternally, with no escape from it and no exit from which you will have. Then God the Almighty said: If good befalls you, it distresses them, but if evil befalls you, they rejoice at it. This state indicates the intensity of their enmity towards the believers, which is that if the believers are granted fertility, victory, support, and they increase in number and their supporters are strengthened, this distresses the hypocrites. And if a drought befalls the Muslims or the enemies defeat them, because of God’s wisdom in that - as happened on the Day of Uhud - the hypocrites rejoice at that. God the Almighty said, addressing the believers: But if you are patient and fear God, not at all will their plot harm you Al-An’am 2:17. God the Almighty guides them to safety from the evil of the wicked and the plot of the immoral by using patience, fear of God, and putting their trust in God, who encompasses their enemies, for they have no power or strength except through Him. He is the One Whose wills is, and what He does not will is not, and nothing occurs in existence except by His decree and will, and whoever puts his trust in Him, He will suffice him. Then the Almighty proceeded to mention the story of Uhud and the test it contained for His believing servants, and the distinction between the believers and the hypocrites and the explanation of the patience of the patient. The Almighty said:
3:121: According to the majority of scholars, this incident refers to the Day of Uhud. This was stated by Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi, and others. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: It refers to the Day of the Confederates. Narrated by Ibn Jarir, but it is strange and cannot be relied upon. The Battle of Uhud took place on Saturday, Shawwal, in the year 3 AH. Qatadah said: It was eleven nights before the end of Shawwal. And Ikrimah said: On Saturday, the middle of Shawwal, and God knows best, and the reason for it was that when the polytheists killed those of their nobles on the day of Badr and the caravan was safe with what was in it of the trade that was with Abu Sufyan, and when they returned to Mecca, the sons of those who were killed, and the leaders of those who remained said to Abu Sufyan: I am setting aside this money to fight Muhammad, so spend it on that, so they gathered the crowds and the Abyssinians, and they came with about three thousand until they camped near Uhud facing Madinah, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed on Friday, and when he finished, he prayed over a man from Banu al-Najjar called Malik ibn Amr, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, consulted the people, Should he go out to them or stay in Madinah? Abdullah ibn Ubayy suggested staying in Madinah, and if they stayed, they would stay in Bishr, and if they entered it, the men would fight them in their faces, and the women and children would throw stones at them from above them, and if they returned, they would return disappointed. Others from the Companions who had not witnessed Badr suggested going out to them, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered and put on his clothes. To his nation and went out against them, and some of them regretted and said: Perhaps we forced the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they said: O Messenger of God, if you want us to stay, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is not appropriate for a prophet, when he wears a dress for his nation, to return until God rules in his favor. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out with a thousand of his companions, and when they were at the junction, Abdullah bin Ubayy returned with a third of the army, angry because he did not return to his statement, and he and his companions said: If we knew of fighting today, we would have followed you, but we do not see you fighting today. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued walking until he reached the ravine of Uhud in the valley’s side. He turned his back and his army to Uhud, and said: No one should fight until we order him to fight. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prepared for the fight with seven hundred of his companions. He appointed Abdullah bin Jubair, the brother of Banu Amr bin Awf, as commander of the archers. The archers that day were fifty men, so he said to them, “Shoot the horses away from us, and do not let us attack from your side. Stay where you are, whether it is our turn or our turn. If you see the birds snatching us away, do not move from your place.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appeared between two shields, and gave the banner to Mus`ab ibn `Umair, the brother of Banu `Abd al-Dar. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, allowed some of the young men to go on that day and postponed others until he had them go on the day of the Trench about two years after that day. The Quraysh mobilized, and they were three thousand, with two hundred horses that they had set aside. They put Khalid ibn al-Walid on the right flank of the cavalry, and Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl on the left flank, and they gave the banner to Banu Abd al-Dar. Then there was between the two groups what will be detailed in its place in these verses, God willing. For this reason, God Almighty said: And when you went forth from your family, you assigned the believers to their stations for battle, meaning you assigned them to the right and left flanks and wherever you commanded them. And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, meaning He hears what you say, and He knows your innermost thoughts. Ibn Jarir mentioned here a question, the gist of which is: How do you say that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, marched to Uhud on Friday after the prayer, while God Almighty said: And when you went forth from your family to appoint the believers to their stations for battle (al-Baqarah 2:170)? Then his answer to it was: His going forth to appoint them to their stations was on Saturday, at the beginning of the day. And God Almighty said: When two parties among you were about to lose heart (al-Baqarah 2:170), al-Bukhari said: Ali ibn Abdullah told us, Sufyan told us, he said: Amr said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: When two parties among you were about to lose heart (al-Baqarah 2:170) was revealed about us. He said: We are the two parties, Banu Haritha and Banu Salamah. And we do not like - and Sufyan said once - and it does not please me that it was not revealed because God Almighty said: And God is their protector (al-Baqarah 2:170). Muslim also narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah. And more than one of the Salaf said the same: They are Banu Haritha and Banu Salamah. And the Almighty’s saying: And God certainly gave you victory at Badr meaning the day of Badr, which was on Friday, corresponding to the seventeenth of the month of Ramadan in the year two of the Hijra, and it is the day of the Criterion on which God honored Islam and its people, and stamped out polytheism, and destroyed its place and its party. This is despite the small number of Muslims on that day, for they were three hundred and thirteen men, among them horsemen and seventy camels, and the rest were infantry who did not have all the numbers they needed. The enemy on that day was between nine hundred and a thousand in iron and white armor, complete equipment, branded horses, and extra jewelry. So God honored His Messenger and revealed His revelation and sending down, and made the face of the Prophet and his tribe white, and disgraced Satan and his generation. For this reason, the Almighty said, thanking His believing servants and his pious party, And God had already given you victory at Badr when you were weak, meaning, your number was few, so that they would know that victory is from God, not from great numbers and numbers. For this reason, the Almighty said in another verse, “And on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, and the earth, vast as it is, became strait for you; then you turned back, fleeing. Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down soldiers you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved. That is the recompense of the disbelievers. Then God will turn in mercy after that to whom He wills. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.” Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us on the authority of Samak, who said: I heard `Ayyadh al-Ash`ari say: I witnessed Yarmouk and we had five commanders: Abu `Ubaydah, Yazid ibn Abi Sufyan, Ibn Hasana, Khalid ibn al-Walid, and `Ayyadh, not the `Ayyadh who told Samak, who said: And `Umar said: If there is fighting, Abu `Ubaydah is your commander. So we wrote to him saying: Death has come to us, and we have sought his help. So he wrote to us saying: Your letter has come to me asking for my help, and I will guide you to the One who is more powerful in victory and more fortified in army: God the Almighty, so seek His help. For Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was victorious on the day of Badr with fewer men than you. So when this letter of mine comes to you, fight them and do not turn back to me. So we fought them and defeated them by four farsakhs. He said: We seized wealth, so we consulted each other, and `Ayyadh advised us to give ten for every head. Abu `Ubaydah said: Who will bet on me? A young man said: I will, if you do not get angry. He said: So he outran him, and I saw the two heels of Abu Ubaidah jumping while he was behind him on a bare horse. This is a sound chain of transmission. Ibn Hibban included it in his Sahih from the hadith of Bandar on the authority of Ghundar in a similar manner. Al-Hafiz Al-Dhiya Al-Maqdisi chose it in his book. Badr is a neighborhood between Mecca and Medina known for its well, attributed to a man who dug it, called Badr ibn Al-Narain. Al-Sha’bi said: Badr is a well belonging to a man called Badr. His statement, So fear God that you may be grateful, means that you will perform His obedience.
