For this reason, God Almighty said: And when you went forth from your family, you assigned the believers to their stations for battle, meaning you assigned them to the right and left flanks and wherever you commanded them. And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, meaning He hears what you say, and He knows your innermost thoughts. Ibn Jarir mentioned here a question, the gist of which is: How do you say that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, marched to Uhud on Friday after the prayer, while God Almighty said: And when you went forth from your family to appoint the believers to their stations for battle (al-Baqarah 2:170)? Then his answer to it was: His going forth to appoint them to their stations was on Saturday, at the beginning of the day. And God Almighty said: When two parties among you were about to lose heart (al-Baqarah 2:170), al-Bukhari said: Ali ibn Abdullah told us, Sufyan told us, he said: Amr said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: When two parties among you were about to lose heart (al-Baqarah 2:170) was revealed about us. He said: We are the two parties, Banu Haritha and Banu Salamah. And we do not like - and Sufyan said once - and it does not please me that it was not revealed because God Almighty said: And God is their protector (al-Baqarah 2:170). Muslim also narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah. And more than one of the Salaf said the same: They are Banu Haritha and Banu Salamah. And the Almighty’s saying: And God certainly gave you victory at Badr meaning the day of Badr, which was on Friday, corresponding to the seventeenth of the month of Ramadan in the year two of the Hijra, and it is the day of the Criterion on which God honored Islam and its people, and stamped out polytheism, and destroyed its place and its party. This is despite the small number of Muslims on that day, for they were three hundred and thirteen men, among them horsemen and seventy camels, and the rest were infantry who did not have all the numbers they needed. The enemy on that day was between nine hundred and a thousand in iron and white armor, complete equipment, branded horses, and extra jewelry. So God honored His Messenger and revealed His revelation and sending down, and made the face of the Prophet and his tribe white, and disgraced Satan and his generation. For this reason, the Almighty said, thanking His believing servants and his pious party, And God had already given you victory at Badr when you were weak, meaning, your number was few, so that they would know that victory is from God, not from great numbers and numbers. For this reason, the Almighty said in another verse, “And on the day of Hunayn, when your great number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, and the earth, vast as it is, became strait for you; then you turned back, fleeing. Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down soldiers you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved. That is the recompense of the disbelievers. Then God will turn in mercy after that to whom He wills. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.” Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us on the authority of Samak, who said: I heard `Ayyadh al-Ash`ari say: I witnessed Yarmouk and we had five commanders: Abu `Ubaydah, Yazid ibn Abi Sufyan, Ibn Hasana, Khalid ibn al-Walid, and `Ayyadh, not the `Ayyadh who told Samak, who said: And `Umar said: If there is fighting, Abu `Ubaydah is your commander. So we wrote to him saying: Death has come to us, and we have sought his help. So he wrote to us saying: Your letter has come to me asking for my help, and I will guide you to the One who is more powerful in victory and more fortified in army: God the Almighty, so seek His help. For Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was victorious on the day of Badr with fewer men than you. So when this letter of mine comes to you, fight them and do not turn back to me. So we fought them and defeated them by four farsakhs. He said: We seized wealth, so we consulted each other, and `Ayyadh advised us to give ten for every head. Abu `Ubaydah said: Who will bet on me? A young man said: I will, if you do not get angry. He said: So he outran him, and I saw the two heels of Abu Ubaidah jumping while he was behind him on a bare horse. This is a sound chain of transmission. Ibn Hibban included it in his Sahih from the hadith of Bandar on the authority of Ghundar in a similar manner. Al-Hafiz Al-Dhiya Al-Maqdisi chose it in his book. Badr is a neighborhood between Mecca and Medina known for its well, attributed to a man who dug it, called Badr ibn Al-Narain. Al-Sha’bi said: Badr is a well belonging to a man called Badr. His statement, So fear God that you may be grateful, means that you will perform His obedience.
3:124: The commentators differed about this promise, was it on the day of Badr or the day of Uhud? There are two opinions one of them that his saying: When you said to the believers is related to his saying: And God had already helped you at Badr and this was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Aamer Al-Shaabi, Al-Rabi' bin Anas and others, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Abbad bin Mansour said on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his saying: When you said to the believers, 'Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels?' He said: This is on the day of Badr, narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Then he said: My father told us, Musa bin Ismail told us, Wahib told us, Dawud told us on the authority of Amer, meaning Al-Shaabi: The Muslims heard on the day of Badr that Kurz bin Jabir was supporting the polytheists, and that was difficult for them, so God Almighty revealed: “Will it not suffice for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down? Yes, if you are patient and fear God and they come upon you at once, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels marked.” He said: So Kurz was defeated, but he did not reinforce the polytheists, and God did not reinforce the Muslims with the five. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: God reinforced the Muslims with a thousand, then they became three thousand, then they became five thousand. If it is said: What is the connection between this verse according to this statement, and God Almighty’s statement in the story of Badr: “When you called upon your Lord, and He answered you, ‘I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another.’ And God did not make it except as good tidings and that your hearts might be reassured thereby. And victory is not but from God. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise.” The answer is that the mention of the thousand here does not contradict the three thousand and above, because He said: in succession meaning that others will follow them and thousands like them will follow them. This context is similar to the context in Surat Al Imran. It appears that this was on the day of Badr, as is well known that the fighting of the angels was on the day of Badr, and God knows best. Saeed bin Abi Arubah said, on the authority of Qatada: God supported the Muslims on the day of Badr with five thousand. The second statement - This promise is related to His statement: And when you left your family, you assigned the believers positions for battle, and that was on the day of Uhud, and this is the statement of Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak, Az-Zuhri, Musa bin Uqbah and others. But they said: The five thousand reinforcements were not provided because the Muslims fled that day. Ikrimah added: Nor the three thousand, because God Almighty said: Yes, if you are patient and fear God. So they were not patient, but fled, so they were not reinforced by a single king. And His statement: Yes, if you are patient and fear God means: Be patient with your enemy, fear Me, and obey My command. And God Almighty said: And they will come upon you in this haste of theirs. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Rabi’, and Al-Suddi said: That is, from this direction of theirs. Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Abu Salih said: That is, from this anger of theirs. Ad-Dahhak said: From their anger and their face. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: From this journey of theirs, and it is said: From this anger of theirs. God the Almighty says: Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels with marks, meaning marked with a mark. Abu Ishaq al-Sabi’i said on the authority of Haritha ibn Mudrib, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: The mark of the angels on the day of Badr was white wool, and their mark was also on the forelocks of their horses. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Then he said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Hudbah ibn Khalid told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Alqamah, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, regarding this verse marked, he said: with red wool. Mujahid said: marked means their manes are omitted, their forelocks are marked with white wool on the tails of the horses. Al-Awfi said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The angels came to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, marked with wool, so Muhammad and his companions marked themselves and their horses with their mark with wool. Qatada and Ikrimah said: Marked means with the mark of battle. Makhul said: Marked with turbans. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Abdul Quddus bin Habib from Ata bin Abi Rabah from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his statement: Marked: Marked. The mark of the angels on the day of Badr was black turbans, and on the day of Hunayn they were red turbans. It was narrated from the hadith of Husain bin Mukhariq from Saeed from Al-Hakam from Muqsim from Ibn Abbas, who said: The angels did not fight except on the day of Badr. Ibn Ishaq said: I was told by someone I do not accuse, from Muqsim from Ibn Abbas, who said: The mark of the angels on the day of Badr was white turbans that they let down on their backs, and on the day of Hunayn they were red turbans. The angels did not strike on any day except the day of Badr, and on other days they were in number and support and did not strike. Then he narrated it on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Ammarah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned something similar. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Ahmasi told us, Waki’ told us, Hisham bin Urwah told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Abbad, that Al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with him, was wearing a yellow turban on the day of Badr, wrapping himself in it, so the angels descended upon them wearing yellow turbans. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr, and he mentioned it. And the Almighty said: And God did not make it except as good tidings for you and that your hearts might be reassured thereby meaning that God did not send down the angels and inform you of their sending down except as good tidings for you and to comfort your hearts and reassure them. Otherwise, victory is from God, who, if He willed, would have taken revenge on His enemies without you, and without need for you to fight them, as God the Almighty said after commanding the believers to fight: “That is so. And if God had willed, He could have taken revenge on them, but that He may test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the way of God - never will He let their deeds perish. He will guide them and amend their condition. And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them.” That is why He said here: “And God did not make it except as good tidings for you and that your hearts might be reassured thereby. And victory is only from God, the Almighty, the Wise.” That is, He is the Possessor of the might that cannot be reached, and wisdom in His decree and rulings. Then God the Almighty said: That He may cut off a portion of those who disbelieve. That is, He commanded you to fight and struggle because of the wisdom He has in that in every decree. That is why He mentioned all possible categories of the disbelieving fighters, and He said: That He may cut off a portion meaning to destroy a nation of those who disbelieve. Those who disbelieved, or He will subdue them, meaning He will humiliate them and turn them back in anger because they did not get what they wanted from you. That is why He said: or He will subdue them so they turn back disappointed, meaning they did not get what they hoped for. Then he objected with a sentence that indicated that the judgment in this world and the hereafter is His alone, with no partner for Him. So the Most High said: You have no part in the matter, meaning, rather, the matter is entirely up to Me, as the Most High said: You are only responsible for conveying [the message], and upon Us is the reckoning, and He said: You are not responsible for their guidance, but God guides whom He wills, and He said: Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but God guides whom He wills. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said regarding His statement: You have no part in the matter, meaning, you have no part in the judgment over My servants except what I have commanded you to do regarding them. Then the Most High mentioned the rest of the categories, saying: Or He turns to them, meaning, from what they are in of disbelief, so He guides them after misguidance, or He punishes them, meaning, in this world and the hereafter, for their disbelief and sins. For this reason, He said: For indeed, they are wrongdoers, meaning, they deserve that. Al-Bukhari said: Habban bin Musa told us, Abdullah told us, Muammar told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Salim told me on the authority of his father, “That he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say when he raised his head from bowing in the second rak’ah of Fajr: ‘O God, curse so-and-so and so-and-so,’ after he had said: ‘God hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, to You is praise.’ Then God Almighty revealed: ‘You have no part in the matter,’” the verse. And thus it was narrated by Al-Nasa’i on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak and Abd Al-Razzaq, both of them on the authority of Muammar. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Al-Nadr told us, Abu Aqil told us - Ahmad said: He is Abdullah bin Aqil, a trustworthy hadith master - Omar bin Hamza told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: O God, curse so-and-so, O God, curse Al-Harith bin Hisham, O God, curse Suhayl bin Amr, O God, curse Safwan bin Umayya. Then this verse was revealed: You have no part in the matter, whether He forgives them or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers. So He forgave them all. Ahmad said: Abu Mu’awiyah Al-Ghalabi told us, Khalid bin Al-Harith told us, Muhammad bin Ajlan told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Abdullah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate against four people. He said: Then God revealed: You have no part in the matter, to the end of the verse. He said: And God guided them to Islam. Muhammad bin Ajlan said on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate against some of the polytheists, naming them by name, until God revealed: You have no part in the matter al-Baqarah 2:17. Al-Bukhari also said: Musa bin Ismail told us, Ibrahim bin Sa’d told us, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Sa’id bin al-Musayyab, and Abu Salamah bin Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to supplicate against someone, or for someone, he would recite the Qunut after bowing, and he would sometimes say: When he said: “God hears those who praise Him, our Lord, to You is praise: O God, save al-Walid bin al-Walid, Salamah bin Hisham, Ayyash bin Abi Rabi’ah, and the oppressed among the believers, O God, intensify Your punishment on Mudar, and make them years like the years of Joseph,” he would say that out loud. And he used to say in some of his prayers in the Fajr prayer: O God, curse so-and-so and so-and-so, for some of the tribes of the Arabs, until God revealed: You have no part in the matter al-Baqarah 2:17. Al-Bukhari said: Humayd and Thabit said, on the authority of Anas bin Malik: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was wounded on the Day of Uhud, so he said: How can a people succeed who have wounded their Prophet?” Then, You have no part in the matter was revealed. This hadith, which Al-Bukhari included in his Sahih, was attributed to him. Al-Bukhari said in the Battle of UHud 11:Yahya bin Abdullah Al-Sulami told us, Abdullah told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Salim bin Abdullah bin Abihi told me that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, “When he raised his head from bowing in the last rak’ah of Fajr, ‘O God, curse so-and-so and so-and-so and so-and-so,’ after he had said, ‘God hears those who praise Him. Our Lord, to You is praise.’ Then, God revealed, “You have no part in the matter” and the verse. On the authority of Hanzala bin Abi Sufyan, he said: I heard Salim bin Abdullah say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate against Safwan bin Umayya, Suhayl bin Amr, and Al-Harith bin Hisham, so the verse was revealed: ‘You have no part in the matter, whether He forgives them or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers.’” This is how Al-Bukhari mentioned this addition, suspended and disconnected, and it was mentioned previously as a connected chain of transmission in Musnad Ahmad. Imam Ahmad said: Hisham told us, Hamid told us, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had his front tooth broken on the day of Uhud, and he was wounded in the forehead until blood ran down his face. He said: How can a people succeed who did this to their Prophet, while he was calling them to their Lord, the Almighty and Majestic?” So God revealed: You have no part in the matter, whether He forgives them or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers. Muslim is the only one to transmit it, and he narrated it on the authority of Al-Qa’nabi, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, and he mentioned it. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Husayn bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Matar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was injured on the day of Uhud, and his front tooth was broken and his eyebrow was parted. He fell down wearing two coats of mail and blood was flowing. Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, passed by him, sat him up, and wiped his face. He regained consciousness and said: ‘How can a people do this to their Prophet, while he was calling them to God Almighty?’ Then God revealed: ‘You have no part in the matter’ verse. Abd al-Razzaq narrated it similarly on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada, but he did not say: ‘Then he regained consciousness.’” Then the Almighty said: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, meaning that everything belongs to Him, and its people are slaves before Him. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, meaning that He is the One who controls, so there is no questioning of His judgment, and He is not questioned about what He does, while they are questioned. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.

Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: God reinforced the Muslims with a thousand, then they became three thousand, then they became five thousand. Abbad bin Mansour said on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his saying: When you said to the believers, 'Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels?' He said: This is on the day of Badr, narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Then he said: My father told us, Musa bin Ismail told us, Wahib told us, Dawud told us on the authority of Amer, meaning Al-Shaabi: The Muslims heard on the day of Badr that Kurz bin Jabir was supporting the polytheists, and that was difficult for them, so God Almighty revealed: “Will it not suffice for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down? Yes, if you are patient and fear God and they come upon you at once, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels marked.” He said: So Kurz was defeated, but he did not reinforce the polytheists, and God did not reinforce the Muslims with the five. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: God reinforced the Muslims with a thousand, then they became three thousand, then they became five thousand. And victory is not but from God. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise.” The answer is that the mention of the thousand here does not contradict the three thousand and above, because He said: in succession meaning that others will follow them and thousands like them will follow them. This context is similar to the context in Surat Al Imran. It appears that this was on the day of Badr, as is well known that the fighting of the angels was on the day of Badr, and God knows best. Saeed bin Abi Arubah said, on the authority of Qatada: God supported the Muslims on the day of Badr with five thousand. But they said: The five thousand reinforcements were not provided because the Muslims fled that day. Ikrimah added: Nor the three thousand, because God Almighty said: Yes, if you are patient and fear God. So they were not patient, but fled, so they were not reinforced by a single king. Ad-Dahhak said: From their anger and their face. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: From this journey of theirs, and it is said: From this anger of theirs. God the Almighty says: Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels with marks, meaning marked with a mark. Abu Ishaq al-Sabi’i said on the authority of Haritha ibn Mudrib, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: The mark of the angels on the day of Badr was white wool, and their mark was also on the forelocks of their horses. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Then he said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Hudbah ibn Khalid told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Alqamah, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, regarding this verse marked, he said: with red wool. Mujahid said: marked means their manes are omitted, their forelocks are marked with white wool on the tails of the horses. Al-Awfi said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The angels came to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, marked with wool, so Muhammad and his companions marked themselves and their horses with their mark with wool. Qatada and Ikrimah said: Marked means with the mark of battle. Makhul said: Marked with turbans. Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the hadith of Abdul Quddus bin Habib from Ata bin Abi Rabah from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his statement: Marked: Marked. The mark of the angels on the day of Badr was black turbans, and on the day of Hunayn they were red turbans. The angels did not strike on any day except the day of Badr, and on other days they were in number and support and did not strike. Then he narrated it on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Ammarah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned something similar. For this reason, He said: For indeed, they are wrongdoers, meaning, they deserve that. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Al-Nadr told us, Abu Aqil told us - Ahmad said: He is Abdullah bin Aqil, a trustworthy hadith master - Omar bin Hamza told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: O God, curse so-and-so, O God, curse Al-Harith bin Hisham, O God, curse Suhayl bin Amr, O God, curse Safwan bin Umayya. Then this verse was revealed: You have no part in the matter, whether He forgives them or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers. So He forgave them all. Ahmad said: Abu Mu’awiyah Al-Ghalabi told us, Khalid bin Al-Harith told us, Muhammad bin Ajlan told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Abdullah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate against four people. He said: Then God revealed: You have no part in the matter, to the end of the verse. He said: And God guided them to Islam. Muhammad bin Ajlan said on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate against some of the polytheists, naming them by name, until God revealed: You have no part in the matter al-Baqarah 2:17. Al-Bukhari also said: Musa bin Ismail told us, Ibrahim bin Sa’d told us, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Sa’id bin al-Musayyab, and Abu Salamah bin Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to supplicate against someone, or for someone, he would recite the Qunut after bowing, and he would sometimes say: When he said: “God hears those who praise Him, our Lord, to You is praise: O God, save al-Walid bin al-Walid, Salamah bin Hisham, Ayyash bin Abi Rabi’ah, and the oppressed among the believers, O God, intensify Your punishment on Mudar, and make them years like the years of Joseph,” he would say that out loud. And he used to say in some of his prayers in the Fajr prayer: O God, curse so-and-so and so-and-so, for some of the tribes of the Arabs, until God revealed: You have no part in the matter al-Baqarah 2:17. Al-Bukhari said: Humayd and Thabit said, on the authority of Anas bin Malik: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was wounded on the Day of Uhud, so he said: How can a people succeed who have wounded their Prophet?” Then, You have no part in the matter was revealed. This hadith, which Al-Bukhari included in his Sahih, was attributed to him. Al-Bukhari said in the Battle of UHud 11:Yahya bin Abdullah Al-Sulami told us, Abdullah told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Salim bin Abdullah bin Abihi told me that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, “When he raised his head from bowing in the last rak’ah of Fajr, ‘O God, curse so-and-so and so-and-so and so-and-so,’ after he had said, ‘God hears those who praise Him. Our Lord, to You is praise.’ Then, God revealed, “You have no part in the matter” and the verse. On the authority of Hanzala bin Abi Sufyan, he said: I heard Salim bin Abdullah say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate against Safwan bin Umayya, Suhayl bin Amr, and Al-Harith bin Hisham, so the verse was revealed: ‘You have no part in the matter, whether He forgives them or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers.’” This is how Al-Bukhari mentioned this addition, suspended and disconnected, and it was mentioned previously as a connected chain of transmission in Musnad Ahmad. Imam Ahmad said: Hisham told us, Hamid told us, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had his front tooth broken on the day of Uhud, and he was wounded in the forehead until blood ran down his face. He said: How can a people succeed who did this to their Prophet, while he was calling them to their Lord, the Almighty and Majestic?” So God revealed: You have no part in the matter, whether He forgives them or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers. Muslim is the only one to transmit it, and he narrated it on the authority of Al-Qa’nabi, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, and he mentioned it. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Husayn bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Matar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was injured on the day of Uhud, and his front tooth was broken and his eyebrow was parted. He fell down wearing two coats of mail and blood was flowing. Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, passed by him, sat him up, and wiped his face. He regained consciousness and said: ‘How can a people do this to their Prophet, while he was calling them to God Almighty?’ Then God revealed: ‘You have no part in the matter’ verse. Abd al-Razzaq narrated it similarly on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada, but he did not say: ‘Then he regained consciousness.’” Then the Almighty said: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, meaning that everything belongs to Him, and its people are slaves before Him. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, meaning that He is the One who controls, so there is no questioning of His judgment, and He is not questioned about what He does, while they are questioned. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.
3:130: The Almighty says, forbidding His believing servants from engaging in usury and consuming it in multiples, as they used to say in the days of ignorance: When the due date of a debt comes, either pay it or increase it. If he pays it, otherwise, he increases it in the period, and the other increases it in the amount, and so on every year, perhaps the little will be doubled until it becomes a lot multiplied. The Almighty commanded His servants to be pious, so that they may succeed in the first and the last, then He threatened them with the Fire and warned them against it, so the Almighty said: “And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers. And obey God and the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.” Then He urged them to hasten to do good deeds and hasten to attain the acts of worship, so the Almighty said: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous. That is, just as the Fire was prepared for the disbelievers. It has been said that the meaning of His saying its width is the heavens and the earth is an indication of the vastness of its length, as He said in describing the furnishings of Paradise: its linings are of brocade. That is, what do you think? By the backs? It was said: Rather, its width is like its length because it is a dome under the throne, and the domed and round thing is as wide as its length. This is indicated by what was established in the Sahih: “If you ask God for Paradise, then ask Him for Al-Firdaws, for it is the highest part of Paradise and the middle of Paradise, and from it the rivers of Paradise flow, and its roof is the Throne of the Most Merciful.” This verse is like the Almighty’s saying in Surat al-Hadid 57:Race one another to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth, the verse. We narrated in Musnad Al-Imam Ahmad that Heraclius wrote to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: You have invited me to a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God, so where is the night when the day comes? Ibn Jarir narrated it and said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Muslim bin Khalid told me on the authority of Abu Khathim, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Rashid, on the authority of Ya’la bin Murrah, who said: “I met Al-Tanukhi, the messenger of Heraclius to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Homs, an old man who had become corrupt. He said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the letter of Heraclius, so he handed the paper to a man on his left. He said: I said: Who is your companion who reads? They said: Mu’awiyah. Then it was the letter of my companion: You have written inviting me to a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous. So where is the Fire?” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God! Where is the night when the day comes? Al-A’mash, Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu’bah said on the authority of Qays ibn Muslim on the authority of Tariq ibn Shihab: Some Jews asked Umar ibn al-Khattab about a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? Umar said to them: Have you seen when the day comes, where is the night? And when the night comes, where is the day? They said: Something similar has been taken from the Torah. Ibn Jarir narrated it through three chains of transmission. Then he said: Ahmad ibn Hazim told us, Abu Nu’aym told us, Ja’far ibn Burqan told us, Yazid ibn al-A’sam told us: A man from the People of the Book said: They say, A Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Where is the night when the day comes, and where is the day when the night comes? This has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Mu’ammar told us, Al-Mughirah ibn Salamah Abu Hisham told us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn al-A’sam, on the authority of His uncle Yazid ibn al-Asamm, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, said: “A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘Have you seen the words of God the Almighty: “A Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth,” then where is the Fire? He said: ‘Have you seen that when the night comes it covers everything, so where is the day?’ He said: ‘Wherever God wills.’ He said: ‘And so the Fire will be wherever God the Almighty wills.’” This has two possible meanings one of them that the meaning in that is that it does not necessarily follow from our not seeing the night when the day comes that it is not in a place, even if we do not know it, and so the Fire will be wherever God the Almighty wills, and this is more apparent as mentioned previously in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of al-Bazzar. Second That the meaning is that if the day covers the face of the world from this side, then the night is from the other side, so likewise Paradise is in the highest of the high above the heavens under the Throne and its width, as God Almighty said like the width of the heaven and the earth and Hell is in the lowest of the low, so there is no contradiction between it being like the width of the heavens and the earth and the existence of Hell, and God knows best. Then God the Almighty mentioned the description of the people of Paradise, saying, Those who spend in ease and hardship, meaning in hardship and ease, in comfort and distress, in health and sickness, and in all circumstances, just as He said, Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, meaning that nothing distracts them from obeying God the Almighty and spending in what pleases Him, and doing good to His creation from their relatives and others with various types of righteousness. And God the Almighty said, And those who restrain anger and pardon the people, meaning that if anger arises in them, they restrain it, meaning they conceal it and do not act on it, and they pardon those who wrong them. It was mentioned in some of the narrations: “God the Most High says: O son of Adam, remember Me when you become angry, and I will remember you when you become angry, so that I will not destroy you among those whom I destroy.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Abu Ya’la said in his Musnad: Abu Musa al-Zaman told us, Isa bin Shu’aib al-Dareer Abu al-Fadl told us, al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman al-Jizi told me on the authority of Abu Amr bin Anas bin Malik, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever restrains his anger, God will restrain his punishment from him. Whoever guards his tongue, God will cover his faults. Whoever apologizes to God, God will accept his apology.” This is a strange hadith, and its chain of transmission is questionable. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, Malik told us on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa’id bin al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The strong man is not the one who wrestles, but the strong man is the one who controls himself when he is angry. The two sheikhs narrated it on the authority of Malik. Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taymi, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Suwaid, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Which of you would rather have the wealth of his heir than his own wealth? They said: O Messenger of God, there is none among us who does not love his wealth more than the wealth of his heir. He said: “Know that there is none among you who does not love the wealth of his heir more than his own wealth. Your wealth from your wealth is only what you have sent forward, and the wealth of your heir is what you have delayed.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you consider to be a wrestler among you? We said: The one who is not wrestled by men. He said: No, but the one who controls himself when he is angry. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you consider to be a slave among you? We said: The one who has no children. He said: No, but the slave is the one who has not sent forward any of his children. Al-Bukhari included the first chapter of it, and Muslim included the original of this hadith, on the authority of Al-A’mash. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, I heard Urwah ibn `Abdullah al-Ju`fi narrating on the authority of Hasbah or Ibn Abi Hasin, on the authority of a man who witnessed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, giving a sermon, and he said, Do you know what ruqūb is? We said, The one who has no children. He said, Ruqūb is all the ones who have children and then died without having given anything from them. He said, Do you know what sāluq is? They said, The one who has no wealth. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The sāluq is all the one who has wealth and then died without giving anything from it. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, What is sarā`? They said, The one who is struck down. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Sarā` is all the sarā`, the one who becomes angry and his anger becomes intense, his face turns red, and his hair stands up, so he is struck down by his anger. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr told us, Hisham ibn Urwah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, on the authority of his uncle called Jariyah ibn Qudamah Al-Sa’di, “that he asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, say to me something that will benefit me and make it short for me so that I may understand it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not get angry. So he repeated it to him until he repeated it to him many times, each time saying: Do not get angry.” And this is how he narrated it on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah on the authority of Hisham on his authority, and he also narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id Al-Qattan on the authority of Hisham on his authority, “that a man said: O Messenger of God, say to me something and make it short for me so that I may understand it. He said: Do not get angry.” The hadith is narrated only by Ahmad. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman, “On the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A man said: O Messenger of God, advise me. He said: Do not get angry. The man said: So I thought about it when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said what he said, and I saw that anger brings together all evil.” Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Abu Ibn Harb ibn Abi Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: He was watering from his cistern when some people came and said: Who among you will bring water to Abu Dharr and count the hairs from his head? A man said: I will. So the man came and brought water to him from the cistern and pounded it. Abu Dharr was standing, so he sat down and then lay down. It was said to him: O Abu Dharr, why did you sit down and then lie down? He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: If one of you becomes angry while standing, let him sit down. If the anger goes away from him, then all well and good, otherwise let him lie down.” Abu Dawood narrated it from Ahmad ibn Hanbal with his chain of transmission, except that it was included in his narration on the authority of Abu Harb on the authority of Abu Dharr. The correct version is Ibn Abi Harb on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Dharr, as Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated it on the authority of his father. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim bin Khalid told us, Abu Wa’il al-San’ani told us: We were sitting with Urwah bin Muhammad when a man entered and said to him words that angered him. When he angered him, he stood up and came back to us after having performed ablution. He said: My father told me on the authority of my grandfather Atiyah - he is Ibn Sa’d al-Sa’di - and he was a companion - he said: “The Messenger of God said: Anger is from the devil, and the devil was created from fire, and fire is extinguished only with water. So when one of you becomes angry, let him perform ablution.” And this is how Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Ibrahim bin Khalid al-San’ani on the authority of Abu Wa’il al-Qass al-Muradi al-San’ani. Abu Dawud said: I think he was Abdullah bin Buhair. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Noah bin Ja’una al-Salami told us, on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever gives respite to someone in difficulty or forgives him, God will protect him from the heat of Hell. Indeed, the work of Paradise is made difficult by a hill - three times - Indeed, the work of Hell is made easy by a slip. And the happy one is the one who is protected from trials, and there is no sip more beloved to God than a sip of anger that a servant swallows. No servant of God swallows it except that it fills his stomach with faith.’” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it, and its chain of transmission is good, with no one who is wounded in it, and its text is good. Another hadith with the same meaning - Abu Dawud said: Uqbah bin Makram told us, Abd al-Rahman, meaning Ibn Mahdi, told us, on the authority of Bishr, meaning Ibn Mansur, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ajlan, on the authority of Suwaid bin Wahb, on the authority of a man from the sons of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever suppresses anger when he is able to vent it, God will fill him with security and faith. Whoever refrains from wearing a beautiful garment when he is able to do so - Bishr said: I think he said: out of humility - God will clothe him with the garment of honor. Whoever marries for God, God will clothe him with the crown of kingship.” Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Yazid told us: Saeed told us, Abu Marhum told me on the authority of Sahl bin Muadh bin Anas, on the authority of his father, “The Messenger of God said: Whoever suppresses his anger when he is able to vent it, God will call him in front of all creation and let him choose from any of the houris he wants.” Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Ayoub, and Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Gharib. Another hadith - Abd al-Razzaq said: Dawud ibn Qays informed us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of a man from the people of Ash-Sham called Abd al-Jalil, on the authority of his uncle, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, regarding the words of God Almighty: And those who restrain anger, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever restrains anger when he is able to give vent to it, God will fill him with security and faith. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Another hadith - Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad told us, Yahya ibn Abi Talib told us, Ali ibn Asim told us, Yunus ibn Ubayd told me on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘A servant has not taken a sip of food that is better in reward than a sip of anger that he swallows seeking the face of God.’” And Ibn Majah narrated it likewise on the authority of Bishr ibn Umar, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd, with the same chain of transmission. So God Almighty’s statement: And those who restrain anger means that they do not act out their anger on people, but rather they restrain their evil from them, and they seek reward for that from God Almighty. Then God the Almighty said: And those who pardon people meaning, while refraining from evil, they pardon those who wronged them in their souls, so that no grudge remains in their souls against anyone, and this is the most perfect state, and for this reason He said: And God loves the doers of good so this is from the stations of goodness, and in the hadith: “There are three things that I swear by: no wealth is diminished by charity, and God does not increase a servant through forgiveness except in honor, and whoever humbles himself before God, God will raise him up.” Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Musa bin Uqbah from Ishaq bin Yahya bin Talhah Al-Qurashi, from Ubadah bin As-Samit, from Ubayy bin Ka’b that the Messenger of God, “said: Whoever is pleased to have a lofty building and be raised in status, let him pardon those who wronged him, give to those who deprived him, and connect with those who severed ties with him.” Then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it. Ibn Mardawayh included it from the hadith of Ali, Ka’b bin Ujrah, Abu Hurayrah, and Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with them, in a similar manner. It was narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, a crier will call out, saying: Where are those who pardoned people? Come to your Lord and take your rewards. It is the right of every Muslim man, if he pardons, to enter Paradise.” And God Almighty said: And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins. That is, if they commit a sin, they follow it up with repentance and seeking forgiveness. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Hammam bin Yahya told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Abdullah bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He said: A man committed a sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant committed a sin and knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant. Then he committed another sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant. Then he committed another sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant.” With it, I bear witness that I have forgiven my servant, so let him do whatever he wants.” It was included in Sahih from the hadith of Ishaq bin Abi Talha, in a similar manner. Another Hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr and Abu Amir told us: Zuhair told us: Saad al-Ta’i told us: Abu al-Mudallah, the freed slave of the Mother of the Believers, heard Abu Hurairah, we said: O Messenger of God, when we see you, our hearts soften, and we are from the people of the Hereafter, and when we leave you, the world pleases us, and we smell women and children. He said: “If you were to be in every state in the state you are in with me, the angels would shake your hands with their palms, and visit you in your homes. And if you did not sin, God would bring people who would sin so that He would forgive them.” We said: O Messenger of God, tell us about Paradise, what is its structure? He said: A brick of gold and a brick of silver, its mortar is the most fragrant musk, its pebbles are pearls and rubies, and its soil is saffron. Whoever enters it will be blessed and will not be miserable, and will live forever and will not die. His clothes will not wear out, and his youth will not fade. There are three whose supplications will not be rejected: the just ruler, the fasting person until he breaks his fast, and the supplication of the one who is not fasting until he breaks his fast.” The oppressed person is carried on the clouds and the gates of heaven are opened for him, and the Lord says: By My glory, I will surely aid you, even if after a while. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from another chain of transmission on the authority of Sa`d. Ablution and two rak`ahs of prayer are confirmed upon repentance, as narrated by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal: Waki` told us, Mis`ar and Sufyan Al-Thawri told us on the authority of Uthman ibn Al-Maghbarah Al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Ali ibn Rabi`ah, on the authority of Asma` ibn Al-Hakam Al-Fazari, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: Whenever I heard a hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God would benefit me with whatever He willed from it. And if someone else tells me about it, I make him swear, and if he swears to me, I believe him. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, told me - and Abu Bakr spoke the truth - that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There is no man who commits a sin, then performs ablution and does it well - Misa’ar said - then prays - Sufyan said - then prays two rak’ahs, and seeks forgiveness from God Almighty, except that He forgives him.” And thus it was narrated by Ali ibn al-Madini, al-Humaidi, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, the people of the Sunan, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, al-Bazzar, and al-Daraqutni through various chains of transmission on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Mughira with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is a good hadith, and we have mentioned its chains of transmission, and the discussion of it is complete in Musnad Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him. In short, it is a good hadith, and it is narrated by the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, on the authority of the Prophet’s successor, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with them both. What bears witness to the authenticity of this hadith is what Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is none among you who performs ablution and completes it, then says: I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, except that the eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and he may enter through whichever one he wishes.” And in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, that he performed ablution for them as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, then said: “I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then prays two rak’ahs in which he does not think, his previous sins will be forgiven.” This hadith has been proven from the narration of the four Imams, the Rightly-Guided Caliphs, on the authority of the Master of the First and the Last, and the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds, as indicated by the clear Book, that seeking forgiveness for sins benefits sinners. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Ja’far ibn Sulayman informed us on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: It has been reported to me that when this verse was revealed, And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins, the verse, Satan wept. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Mahraz bin Awn told us, Uthman bin Matar told us, Abdul Ghafoor told us, on the authority of Abu Nasirah, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He said, ‘Upon you is saying ‘There is no god but God’ and seeking forgiveness, so do a lot of them, for Satan said, ‘I have destroyed people with sins and they have destroyed me with ‘There is no god but God’ and seeking forgiveness. So when I saw that, I have destroyed them with desires, and they think that they are guided.’” Uthman bin Matar and his sheikh are weak. Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Amr and Abu Al-Haitham Al-Atwari on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Satan said: O Lord, by Your glory, I will continue to mislead Your servants as long as their souls are in their bodies. God Almighty said: By My glory and majesty, I will continue to forgive them as long as they seek My forgiveness.” Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Umar ibn Abi Khalifa told us, I heard Abu Badr narrating on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: “A man came and said: O Messenger of God, I have committed a sin. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you sin, seek forgiveness from your Lord. He said: I seek forgiveness, then I sin again. He said: If you sin again, seek forgiveness from your Lord. He said it the fourth time, seek forgiveness from your Lord, until Satan is the one who regrets.” This is a strange hadith from this source. And the Almighty’s saying: And who forgives sins except God? means that no one forgives them except Him, as Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Mus’ab told us, Salam ibn Maskeen and al-Mubarak told us on the authority of al-Hasan on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Sari’ that a prisoner was brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: O God, I repent to You and I do not repent to Muhammad. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The truth has been made known to its people. And His saying: And they did not persist in what they did while they knew means that they repented from their sins and returned to God soon, and they did not continue in the sin and persist in it without giving it up. And if the sin was repeated from them, they would repent from it, as al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Ishaq ibn Abi Isra’il and others told us, they said: Abu Yahya Abd al-Hamid al-Hammani told us on the authority of Uthman ibn Waqid, on the authority of Abu Nasirah, on the authority of a freed slave of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He who seeks forgiveness will not persist, even if he returns seventy times a day.” And Abu Dawud narrated it. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Bazzar in his Musnad from the hadith of Uthman bin Waqid - and Yahya bin Ma'een authenticated him with it - and his Sheikh Abu Nasirah Al-Wasiti, whose name is Muslim bin Ubaid, who was authenticated by Imam Ahmad and Ibn Hibban. Ali bin Al-Madini and Al-Tirmidhi said: The chain of transmission of this hadith is not that good. It appears that it is due to the ignorance of the client of Abu Bakr, but the ignorance of someone like him does not harm because he is a great follower, and it is sufficient for him to attribute it to Abu Bakr, so it is a good hadith, and God knows best. And his statement, and they know, Mujahid and Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair said, and they know, that whoever repents, God will accept his repentance. This is like the statement of God, the Most High, Do they not know that God accepts repentance from His servants? and His statement, And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful. And there are many similar examples to this. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Jarir told us, Habban - he is Ibn Zaid Al-Sharabi - told us, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “that he said while he was on the pulpit: ‘Be merciful and you will be shown mercy, and forgive and you will be forgiven. Woe to those who defy speech, woe to those who persist in what they have done while they know.’” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. Then God the Almighty said after describing them with what He described them with: Their reward is forgiveness from their Lord meaning their reward for these attributes is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow meaning of various types of drinks abiding therein meaning abiding therein and excellent is the reward of the workers God the Almighty praises Paradise.
3:132: The Almighty says, forbidding His believing servants from engaging in usury and consuming it in multiples, as they used to say in the days of ignorance: When the due date of a debt comes, either pay it or increase it. If he pays it, otherwise, he increases it in the period, and the other increases it in the amount, and so on every year, perhaps the little will be doubled until it becomes a lot multiplied. The Almighty commanded His servants to be pious, so that they may succeed in the first and the last, then He threatened them with the Fire and warned them against it, so the Almighty said: “And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers. And obey God and the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.” Then He urged them to hasten to do good deeds and hasten to attain the acts of worship, so the Almighty said: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous. That is, just as the Fire was prepared for the disbelievers. It has been said that the meaning of His saying its width is the heavens and the earth is an indication of the vastness of its length, as He said in describing the furnishings of Paradise: its linings are of brocade. That is, what do you think? By the backs? It was said: Rather, its width is like its length because it is a dome under the throne, and the domed and round thing is as wide as its length. This is indicated by what was established in the Sahih: “If you ask God for Paradise, then ask Him for Al-Firdaws, for it is the highest part of Paradise and the middle of Paradise, and from it the rivers of Paradise flow, and its roof is the Throne of the Most Merciful.” This verse is like the Almighty’s saying in Surat al-Hadid 57:Race one another to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth, the verse. We narrated in Musnad Al-Imam Ahmad that Heraclius wrote to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: You have invited me to a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God, so where is the night when the day comes? Ibn Jarir narrated it and said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Muslim bin Khalid told me on the authority of Abu Khathim, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Rashid, on the authority of Ya’la bin Murrah, who said: “I met Al-Tanukhi, the messenger of Heraclius to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Homs, an old man who had become corrupt. He said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the letter of Heraclius, so he handed the paper to a man on his left. He said: I said: Who is your companion who reads? They said: Mu’awiyah. Then it was the letter of my companion: You have written inviting me to a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous. So where is the Fire?” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God! Where is the night when the day comes? Al-A’mash, Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu’bah said on the authority of Qays ibn Muslim on the authority of Tariq ibn Shihab: Some Jews asked Umar ibn al-Khattab about a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? Umar said to them: Have you seen when the day comes, where is the night? And when the night comes, where is the day? They said: Something similar has been taken from the Torah. Ibn Jarir narrated it through three chains of transmission. Then he said: Ahmad ibn Hazim told us, Abu Nu’aym told us, Ja’far ibn Burqan told us, Yazid ibn al-A’sam told us: A man from the People of the Book said: They say, A Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Where is the night when the day comes, and where is the day when the night comes? This has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Mu’ammar told us, Al-Mughirah ibn Salamah Abu Hisham told us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn al-A’sam, on the authority of His uncle Yazid ibn al-Asamm, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, said: “A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘Have you seen the words of God the Almighty: “A Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth,” then where is the Fire? He said: ‘Have you seen that when the night comes it covers everything, so where is the day?’ He said: ‘Wherever God wills.’ He said: ‘And so the Fire will be wherever God the Almighty wills.’” This has two possible meanings one of them that the meaning in that is that it does not necessarily follow from our not seeing the night when the day comes that it is not in a place, even if we do not know it, and so the Fire will be wherever God the Almighty wills, and this is more apparent as mentioned previously in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of al-Bazzar. Second That the meaning is that if the day covers the face of the world from this side, then the night is from the other side, so likewise Paradise is in the highest of the high above the heavens under the Throne and its width, as God Almighty said like the width of the heaven and the earth and Hell is in the lowest of the low, so there is no contradiction between it being like the width of the heavens and the earth and the existence of Hell, and God knows best. Then God the Almighty mentioned the description of the people of Paradise, saying, Those who spend in ease and hardship, meaning in hardship and ease, in comfort and distress, in health and sickness, and in all circumstances, just as He said, Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, meaning that nothing distracts them from obeying God the Almighty and spending in what pleases Him, and doing good to His creation from their relatives and others with various types of righteousness. And God the Almighty said, And those who restrain anger and pardon the people, meaning that if anger arises in them, they restrain it, meaning they conceal it and do not act on it, and they pardon those who wrong them. It was mentioned in some of the narrations: “God the Most High says: O son of Adam, remember Me when you become angry, and I will remember you when you become angry, so that I will not destroy you among those whom I destroy.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Abu Ya’la said in his Musnad: Abu Musa al-Zaman told us, Isa bin Shu’aib al-Dareer Abu al-Fadl told us, al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman al-Jizi told me on the authority of Abu Amr bin Anas bin Malik, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever restrains his anger, God will restrain his punishment from him. Whoever guards his tongue, God will cover his faults. Whoever apologizes to God, God will accept his apology.” This is a strange hadith, and its chain of transmission is questionable. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, Malik told us on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa’id bin al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The strong man is not the one who wrestles, but the strong man is the one who controls himself when he is angry. The two sheikhs narrated it on the authority of Malik. Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taymi, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Suwaid, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Which of you would rather have the wealth of his heir than his own wealth? They said: O Messenger of God, there is none among us who does not love his wealth more than the wealth of his heir. He said: “Know that there is none among you who does not love the wealth of his heir more than his own wealth. Your wealth from your wealth is only what you have sent forward, and the wealth of your heir is what you have delayed.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you consider to be a wrestler among you? We said: The one who is not wrestled by men. He said: No, but the one who controls himself when he is angry. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you consider to be a slave among you? We said: The one who has no children. He said: No, but the slave is the one who has not sent forward any of his children. Al-Bukhari included the first chapter of it, and Muslim included the original of this hadith, on the authority of Al-A’mash. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, I heard Urwah ibn `Abdullah al-Ju`fi narrating on the authority of Hasbah or Ibn Abi Hasin, on the authority of a man who witnessed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, giving a sermon, and he said, Do you know what ruqūb is? We said, The one who has no children. He said, Ruqūb is all the ones who have children and then died without having given anything from them. He said, Do you know what sāluq is? They said, The one who has no wealth. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The sāluq is all the one who has wealth and then died without giving anything from it. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, What is sarā`? They said, The one who is struck down. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Sarā` is all the sarā`, the one who becomes angry and his anger becomes intense, his face turns red, and his hair stands up, so he is struck down by his anger. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr told us, Hisham ibn Urwah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, on the authority of his uncle called Jariyah ibn Qudamah Al-Sa’di, “that he asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, say to me something that will benefit me and make it short for me so that I may understand it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not get angry. So he repeated it to him until he repeated it to him many times, each time saying: Do not get angry.” And this is how he narrated it on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah on the authority of Hisham on his authority, and he also narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id Al-Qattan on the authority of Hisham on his authority, “that a man said: O Messenger of God, say to me something and make it short for me so that I may understand it. He said: Do not get angry.” The hadith is narrated only by Ahmad. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman, “On the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A man said: O Messenger of God, advise me. He said: Do not get angry. The man said: So I thought about it when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said what he said, and I saw that anger brings together all evil.” Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Abu Ibn Harb ibn Abi Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: He was watering from his cistern when some people came and said: Who among you will bring water to Abu Dharr and count the hairs from his head? A man said: I will. So the man came and brought water to him from the cistern and pounded it. Abu Dharr was standing, so he sat down and then lay down. It was said to him: O Abu Dharr, why did you sit down and then lie down? He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: If one of you becomes angry while standing, let him sit down. If the anger goes away from him, then all well and good, otherwise let him lie down.” Abu Dawood narrated it from Ahmad ibn Hanbal with his chain of transmission, except that it was included in his narration on the authority of Abu Harb on the authority of Abu Dharr. The correct version is Ibn Abi Harb on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Dharr, as Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated it on the authority of his father. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim bin Khalid told us, Abu Wa’il al-San’ani told us: We were sitting with Urwah bin Muhammad when a man entered and said to him words that angered him. When he angered him, he stood up and came back to us after having performed ablution. He said: My father told me on the authority of my grandfather Atiyah - he is Ibn Sa’d al-Sa’di - and he was a companion - he said: “The Messenger of God said: Anger is from the devil, and the devil was created from fire, and fire is extinguished only with water. So when one of you becomes angry, let him perform ablution.” And this is how Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Ibrahim bin Khalid al-San’ani on the authority of Abu Wa’il al-Qass al-Muradi al-San’ani. Abu Dawud said: I think he was Abdullah bin Buhair. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Noah bin Ja’una al-Salami told us, on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever gives respite to someone in difficulty or forgives him, God will protect him from the heat of Hell. Indeed, the work of Paradise is made difficult by a hill - three times - Indeed, the work of Hell is made easy by a slip. And the happy one is the one who is protected from trials, and there is no sip more beloved to God than a sip of anger that a servant swallows. No servant of God swallows it except that it fills his stomach with faith.’” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it, and its chain of transmission is good, with no one who is wounded in it, and its text is good. Another hadith with the same meaning - Abu Dawud said: Uqbah bin Makram told us, Abd al-Rahman, meaning Ibn Mahdi, told us, on the authority of Bishr, meaning Ibn Mansur, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ajlan, on the authority of Suwaid bin Wahb, on the authority of a man from the sons of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever suppresses anger when he is able to vent it, God will fill him with security and faith. Whoever refrains from wearing a beautiful garment when he is able to do so - Bishr said: I think he said: out of humility - God will clothe him with the garment of honor. Whoever marries for God, God will clothe him with the crown of kingship.” Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Yazid told us: Saeed told us, Abu Marhum told me on the authority of Sahl bin Muadh bin Anas, on the authority of his father, “The Messenger of God said: Whoever suppresses his anger when he is able to vent it, God will call him in front of all creation and let him choose from any of the houris he wants.” Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Ayoub, and Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Gharib. Another hadith - Abd al-Razzaq said: Dawud ibn Qays informed us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of a man from the people of Ash-Sham called Abd al-Jalil, on the authority of his uncle, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, regarding the words of God Almighty: And those who restrain anger, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever restrains anger when he is able to give vent to it, God will fill him with security and faith. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Another hadith - Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad told us, Yahya ibn Abi Talib told us, Ali ibn Asim told us, Yunus ibn Ubayd told me on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘A servant has not taken a sip of food that is better in reward than a sip of anger that he swallows seeking the face of God.’” And Ibn Majah narrated it likewise on the authority of Bishr ibn Umar, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd, with the same chain of transmission. So God Almighty’s statement: And those who restrain anger means that they do not act out their anger on people, but rather they restrain their evil from them, and they seek reward for that from God Almighty. Then God the Almighty said: And those who pardon people meaning, while refraining from evil, they pardon those who wronged them in their souls, so that no grudge remains in their souls against anyone, and this is the most perfect state, and for this reason He said: And God loves the doers of good so this is from the stations of goodness, and in the hadith: “There are three things that I swear by: no wealth is diminished by charity, and God does not increase a servant through forgiveness except in honor, and whoever humbles himself before God, God will raise him up.” Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Musa bin Uqbah from Ishaq bin Yahya bin Talhah Al-Qurashi, from Ubadah bin As-Samit, from Ubayy bin Ka’b that the Messenger of God, “said: Whoever is pleased to have a lofty building and be raised in status, let him pardon those who wronged him, give to those who deprived him, and connect with those who severed ties with him.” Then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it. Ibn Mardawayh included it from the hadith of Ali, Ka’b bin Ujrah, Abu Hurayrah, and Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with them, in a similar manner. It was narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, a crier will call out, saying: Where are those who pardoned people? Come to your Lord and take your rewards. It is the right of every Muslim man, if he pardons, to enter Paradise.” And God Almighty said: And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins. That is, if they commit a sin, they follow it up with repentance and seeking forgiveness. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Hammam bin Yahya told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Abdullah bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He said: A man committed a sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant committed a sin and knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant. Then he committed another sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant. Then he committed another sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant.” With it, I bear witness that I have forgiven my servant, so let him do whatever he wants.” It was included in Sahih from the hadith of Ishaq bin Abi Talha, in a similar manner. Another Hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr and Abu Amir told us: Zuhair told us: Saad al-Ta’i told us: Abu al-Mudallah, the freed slave of the Mother of the Believers, heard Abu Hurairah, we said: O Messenger of God, when we see you, our hearts soften, and we are from the people of the Hereafter, and when we leave you, the world pleases us, and we smell women and children. He said: “If you were to be in every state in the state you are in with me, the angels would shake your hands with their palms, and visit you in your homes.
