And if you did not sin, God would bring people who would sin so that He would forgive them.” We said: O Messenger of God, tell us about Paradise, what is its structure? He said: A brick of gold and a brick of silver, its mortar is the most fragrant musk, its pebbles are pearls and rubies, and its soil is saffron. Whoever enters it will be blessed and will not be miserable, and will live forever and will not die. His clothes will not wear out, and his youth will not fade. There are three whose supplications will not be rejected: the just ruler, the fasting person until he breaks his fast, and the supplication of the one who is not fasting until he breaks his fast.” The oppressed person is carried on the clouds and the gates of heaven are opened for him, and the Lord says: By My glory, I will surely aid you, even if after a while. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from another chain of transmission on the authority of Sa`d. Ablution and two rak`ahs of prayer are confirmed upon repentance, as narrated by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal: Waki` told us, Mis`ar and Sufyan Al-Thawri told us on the authority of Uthman ibn Al-Maghbarah Al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Ali ibn Rabi`ah, on the authority of Asma` ibn Al-Hakam Al-Fazari, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: Whenever I heard a hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God would benefit me with whatever He willed from it. And if someone else tells me about it, I make him swear, and if he swears to me, I believe him. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, told me - and Abu Bakr spoke the truth - that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There is no man who commits a sin, then performs ablution and does it well - Misa’ar said - then prays - Sufyan said - then prays two rak’ahs, and seeks forgiveness from God Almighty, except that He forgives him.” And thus it was narrated by Ali ibn al-Madini, al-Humaidi, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, the people of the Sunan, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, al-Bazzar, and al-Daraqutni through various chains of transmission on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Mughira with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is a good hadith, and we have mentioned its chains of transmission, and the discussion of it is complete in Musnad Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him. In short, it is a good hadith, and it is narrated by the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, on the authority of the Prophet’s successor, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with them both. What bears witness to the authenticity of this hadith is what Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is none among you who performs ablution and completes it, then says: I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, except that the eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and he may enter through whichever one he wishes.” And in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, that he performed ablution for them as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, then said: “I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then prays two rak’ahs in which he does not think, his previous sins will be forgiven.” This hadith has been proven from the narration of the four Imams, the Rightly-Guided Caliphs, on the authority of the Master of the First and the Last, and the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds, as indicated by the clear Book, that seeking forgiveness for sins benefits sinners. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Ja’far ibn Sulayman informed us on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: It has been reported to me that when this verse was revealed, And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins, the verse, Satan wept. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Mahraz bin Awn told us, Uthman bin Matar told us, Abdul Ghafoor told us, on the authority of Abu Nasirah, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He said, ‘Upon you is saying ‘There is no god but God’ and seeking forgiveness, so do a lot of them, for Satan said, ‘I have destroyed people with sins and they have destroyed me with ‘There is no god but God’ and seeking forgiveness. So when I saw that, I have destroyed them with desires, and they think that they are guided.’” Uthman bin Matar and his sheikh are weak. Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Amr and Abu Al-Haitham Al-Atwari on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Satan said: O Lord, by Your glory, I will continue to mislead Your servants as long as their souls are in their bodies. God Almighty said: By My glory and majesty, I will continue to forgive them as long as they seek My forgiveness.” Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Umar ibn Abi Khalifa told us, I heard Abu Badr narrating on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: “A man came and said: O Messenger of God, I have committed a sin. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you sin, seek forgiveness from your Lord. He said: I seek forgiveness, then I sin again. He said: If you sin again, seek forgiveness from your Lord. He said it the fourth time, seek forgiveness from your Lord, until Satan is the one who regrets.” This is a strange hadith from this source. And the Almighty’s saying: And who forgives sins except God? means that no one forgives them except Him, as Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Mus’ab told us, Salam ibn Maskeen and al-Mubarak told us on the authority of al-Hasan on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Sari’ that a prisoner was brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: O God, I repent to You and I do not repent to Muhammad. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The truth has been made known to its people. And His saying: And they did not persist in what they did while they knew means that they repented from their sins and returned to God soon, and they did not continue in the sin and persist in it without giving it up. And if the sin was repeated from them, they would repent from it, as al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Ishaq ibn Abi Isra’il and others told us, they said: Abu Yahya Abd al-Hamid al-Hammani told us on the authority of Uthman ibn Waqid, on the authority of Abu Nasirah, on the authority of a freed slave of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He who seeks forgiveness will not persist, even if he returns seventy times a day.” And Abu Dawud narrated it. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Bazzar in his Musnad from the hadith of Uthman bin Waqid - and Yahya bin Ma'een authenticated him with it - and his Sheikh Abu Nasirah Al-Wasiti, whose name is Muslim bin Ubaid, who was authenticated by Imam Ahmad and Ibn Hibban. Ali bin Al-Madini and Al-Tirmidhi said: The chain of transmission of this hadith is not that good. It appears that it is due to the ignorance of the client of Abu Bakr, but the ignorance of someone like him does not harm because he is a great follower, and it is sufficient for him to attribute it to Abu Bakr, so it is a good hadith, and God knows best. And his statement, and they know, Mujahid and Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair said, and they know, that whoever repents, God will accept his repentance. This is like the statement of God, the Most High, Do they not know that God accepts repentance from His servants? and His statement, And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful. And there are many similar examples to this. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Jarir told us, Habban - he is Ibn Zaid Al-Sharabi - told us, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “that he said while he was on the pulpit: ‘Be merciful and you will be shown mercy, and forgive and you will be forgiven. Woe to those who defy speech, woe to those who persist in what they have done while they know.’” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. Then God the Almighty said after describing them with what He described them with: Their reward is forgiveness from their Lord meaning their reward for these attributes is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow meaning of various types of drinks abiding therein meaning abiding therein and excellent is the reward of the workers God the Almighty praises Paradise.
3:133: The Almighty says, forbidding His believing servants from engaging in usury and consuming it in multiples, as they used to say in the days of ignorance: When the due date of a debt comes, either pay it or increase it. If he pays it, otherwise, he increases it in the period, and the other increases it in the amount, and so on every year, perhaps the little will be doubled until it becomes a lot multiplied. The Almighty commanded His servants to be pious, so that they may succeed in the first and the last, then He threatened them with the Fire and warned them against it, so the Almighty said: “And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers. And obey God and the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.” Then He urged them to hasten to do good deeds and hasten to attain the acts of worship, so the Almighty said: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous. That is, just as the Fire was prepared for the disbelievers. It has been said that the meaning of His saying its width is the heavens and the earth is an indication of the vastness of its length, as He said in describing the furnishings of Paradise: its linings are of brocade. That is, what do you think? By the backs? It was said: Rather, its width is like its length because it is a dome under the throne, and the domed and round thing is as wide as its length. This is indicated by what was established in the Sahih: “If you ask God for Paradise, then ask Him for Al-Firdaws, for it is the highest part of Paradise and the middle of Paradise, and from it the rivers of Paradise flow, and its roof is the Throne of the Most Merciful.” This verse is like the Almighty’s saying in Surat al-Hadid 57:Race one another to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth, the verse. We narrated in Musnad Al-Imam Ahmad that Heraclius wrote to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: You have invited me to a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God, so where is the night when the day comes? Ibn Jarir narrated it and said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Muslim bin Khalid told me on the authority of Abu Khathim, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Rashid, on the authority of Ya’la bin Murrah, who said: “I met Al-Tanukhi, the messenger of Heraclius to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Homs, an old man who had become corrupt. He said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the letter of Heraclius, so he handed the paper to a man on his left. He said: I said: Who is your companion who reads? They said: Mu’awiyah. Then it was the letter of my companion: You have written inviting me to a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous. So where is the Fire?” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God! Where is the night when the day comes? Al-A’mash, Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu’bah said on the authority of Qays ibn Muslim on the authority of Tariq ibn Shihab: Some Jews asked Umar ibn al-Khattab about a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? Umar said to them: Have you seen when the day comes, where is the night? And when the night comes, where is the day? They said: Something similar has been taken from the Torah. Ibn Jarir narrated it through three chains of transmission. Then he said: Ahmad ibn Hazim told us, Abu Nu’aym told us, Ja’far ibn Burqan told us, Yazid ibn al-A’sam told us: A man from the People of the Book said: They say, A Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Where is the night when the day comes, and where is the day when the night comes? This has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Mu’ammar told us, Al-Mughirah ibn Salamah Abu Hisham told us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn al-A’sam, on the authority of His uncle Yazid ibn al-Asamm, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, said: “A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘Have you seen the words of God the Almighty: “A Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth,” then where is the Fire? He said: ‘Have you seen that when the night comes it covers everything, so where is the day?’ He said: ‘Wherever God wills.’ He said: ‘And so the Fire will be wherever God the Almighty wills.’” This has two possible meanings one of them that the meaning in that is that it does not necessarily follow from our not seeing the night when the day comes that it is not in a place, even if we do not know it, and so the Fire will be wherever God the Almighty wills, and this is more apparent as mentioned previously in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of al-Bazzar. Second That the meaning is that if the day covers the face of the world from this side, then the night is from the other side, so likewise Paradise is in the highest of the high above the heavens under the Throne and its width, as God Almighty said like the width of the heaven and the earth and Hell is in the lowest of the low, so there is no contradiction between it being like the width of the heavens and the earth and the existence of Hell, and God knows best. Then God the Almighty mentioned the description of the people of Paradise, saying, Those who spend in ease and hardship, meaning in hardship and ease, in comfort and distress, in health and sickness, and in all circumstances, just as He said, Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, meaning that nothing distracts them from obeying God the Almighty and spending in what pleases Him, and doing good to His creation from their relatives and others with various types of righteousness. And God the Almighty said, And those who restrain anger and pardon the people, meaning that if anger arises in them, they restrain it, meaning they conceal it and do not act on it, and they pardon those who wrong them. It was mentioned in some of the narrations: “God the Most High says: O son of Adam, remember Me when you become angry, and I will remember you when you become angry, so that I will not destroy you among those whom I destroy.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Abu Ya’la said in his Musnad: Abu Musa al-Zaman told us, Isa bin Shu’aib al-Dareer Abu al-Fadl told us, al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman al-Jizi told me on the authority of Abu Amr bin Anas bin Malik, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever restrains his anger, God will restrain his punishment from him. Whoever guards his tongue, God will cover his faults. Whoever apologizes to God, God will accept his apology.” This is a strange hadith, and its chain of transmission is questionable. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, Malik told us on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa’id bin al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The strong man is not the one who wrestles, but the strong man is the one who controls himself when he is angry. The two sheikhs narrated it on the authority of Malik. Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taymi, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Suwaid, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Which of you would rather have the wealth of his heir than his own wealth? They said: O Messenger of God, there is none among us who does not love his wealth more than the wealth of his heir. He said: “Know that there is none among you who does not love the wealth of his heir more than his own wealth. Your wealth from your wealth is only what you have sent forward, and the wealth of your heir is what you have delayed.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you consider to be a wrestler among you? We said: The one who is not wrestled by men. He said: No, but the one who controls himself when he is angry. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you consider to be a slave among you? We said: The one who has no children. He said: No, but the slave is the one who has not sent forward any of his children. Al-Bukhari included the first chapter of it, and Muslim included the original of this hadith, on the authority of Al-A’mash. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, I heard Urwah ibn `Abdullah al-Ju`fi narrating on the authority of Hasbah or Ibn Abi Hasin, on the authority of a man who witnessed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, giving a sermon, and he said, Do you know what ruqūb is? We said, The one who has no children. He said, Ruqūb is all the ones who have children and then died without having given anything from them. He said, Do you know what sāluq is? They said, The one who has no wealth. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The sāluq is all the one who has wealth and then died without giving anything from it. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, What is sarā`? They said, The one who is struck down. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Sarā` is all the sarā`, the one who becomes angry and his anger becomes intense, his face turns red, and his hair stands up, so he is struck down by his anger. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr told us, Hisham ibn Urwah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, on the authority of his uncle called Jariyah ibn Qudamah Al-Sa’di, “that he asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, say to me something that will benefit me and make it short for me so that I may understand it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not get angry. So he repeated it to him until he repeated it to him many times, each time saying: Do not get angry.” And this is how he narrated it on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah on the authority of Hisham on his authority, and he also narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id Al-Qattan on the authority of Hisham on his authority, “that a man said: O Messenger of God, say to me something and make it short for me so that I may understand it. He said: Do not get angry.” The hadith is narrated only by Ahmad. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman, “On the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A man said: O Messenger of God, advise me. He said: Do not get angry. The man said: So I thought about it when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said what he said, and I saw that anger brings together all evil.” Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Abu Ibn Harb ibn Abi Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: He was watering from his cistern when some people came and said: Who among you will bring water to Abu Dharr and count the hairs from his head? A man said: I will. So the man came and brought water to him from the cistern and pounded it. Abu Dharr was standing, so he sat down and then lay down. It was said to him: O Abu Dharr, why did you sit down and then lie down? He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: If one of you becomes angry while standing, let him sit down. If the anger goes away from him, then all well and good, otherwise let him lie down.” Abu Dawood narrated it from Ahmad ibn Hanbal with his chain of transmission, except that it was included in his narration on the authority of Abu Harb on the authority of Abu Dharr. The correct version is Ibn Abi Harb on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Dharr, as Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated it on the authority of his father. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim bin Khalid told us, Abu Wa’il al-San’ani told us: We were sitting with Urwah bin Muhammad when a man entered and said to him words that angered him. When he angered him, he stood up and came back to us after having performed ablution. He said: My father told me on the authority of my grandfather Atiyah - he is Ibn Sa’d al-Sa’di - and he was a companion - he said: “The Messenger of God said: Anger is from the devil, and the devil was created from fire, and fire is extinguished only with water. So when one of you becomes angry, let him perform ablution.” And this is how Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Ibrahim bin Khalid al-San’ani on the authority of Abu Wa’il al-Qass al-Muradi al-San’ani. Abu Dawud said: I think he was Abdullah bin Buhair. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Noah bin Ja’una al-Salami told us, on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever gives respite to someone in difficulty or forgives him, God will protect him from the heat of Hell. Indeed, the work of Paradise is made difficult by a hill - three times - Indeed, the work of Hell is made easy by a slip. And the happy one is the one who is protected from trials, and there is no sip more beloved to God than a sip of anger that a servant swallows. No servant of God swallows it except that it fills his stomach with faith.’” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it, and its chain of transmission is good, with no one who is wounded in it, and its text is good. Another hadith with the same meaning - Abu Dawud said: Uqbah bin Makram told us, Abd al-Rahman, meaning Ibn Mahdi, told us, on the authority of Bishr, meaning Ibn Mansur, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ajlan, on the authority of Suwaid bin Wahb, on the authority of a man from the sons of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever suppresses anger when he is able to vent it, God will fill him with security and faith. Whoever refrains from wearing a beautiful garment when he is able to do so - Bishr said: I think he said: out of humility - God will clothe him with the garment of honor. Whoever marries for God, God will clothe him with the crown of kingship.” Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Yazid told us: Saeed told us, Abu Marhum told me on the authority of Sahl bin Muadh bin Anas, on the authority of his father, “The Messenger of God said: Whoever suppresses his anger when he is able to vent it, God will call him in front of all creation and let him choose from any of the houris he wants.” Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Ayoub, and Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Gharib. Another hadith - Abd al-Razzaq said: Dawud ibn Qays informed us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of a man from the people of Ash-Sham called Abd al-Jalil, on the authority of his uncle, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, regarding the words of God Almighty: And those who restrain anger, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever restrains anger when he is able to give vent to it, God will fill him with security and faith. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Another hadith - Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad told us, Yahya ibn Abi Talib told us, Ali ibn Asim told us, Yunus ibn Ubayd told me on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘A servant has not taken a sip of food that is better in reward than a sip of anger that he swallows seeking the face of God.’” And Ibn Majah narrated it likewise on the authority of Bishr ibn Umar, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd, with the same chain of transmission. So God Almighty’s statement: And those who restrain anger means that they do not act out their anger on people, but rather they restrain their evil from them, and they seek reward for that from God Almighty. Then God the Almighty said: And those who pardon people meaning, while refraining from evil, they pardon those who wronged them in their souls, so that no grudge remains in their souls against anyone, and this is the most perfect state, and for this reason He said: And God loves the doers of good so this is from the stations of goodness, and in the hadith: “There are three things that I swear by: no wealth is diminished by charity, and God does not increase a servant through forgiveness except in honor, and whoever humbles himself before God, God will raise him up.” Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Musa bin Uqbah from Ishaq bin Yahya bin Talhah Al-Qurashi, from Ubadah bin As-Samit, from Ubayy bin Ka’b that the Messenger of God, “said: Whoever is pleased to have a lofty building and be raised in status, let him pardon those who wronged him, give to those who deprived him, and connect with those who severed ties with him.” Then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it. Ibn Mardawayh included it from the hadith of Ali, Ka’b bin Ujrah, Abu Hurayrah, and Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with them, in a similar manner. It was narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, a crier will call out, saying: Where are those who pardoned people? Come to your Lord and take your rewards. It is the right of every Muslim man, if he pardons, to enter Paradise.” And God Almighty said: And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins. That is, if they commit a sin, they follow it up with repentance and seeking forgiveness. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Hammam bin Yahya told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Abdullah bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He said: A man committed a sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant committed a sin and knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant. Then he committed another sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant. Then he committed another sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant.” With it, I bear witness that I have forgiven my servant, so let him do whatever he wants.” It was included in Sahih from the hadith of Ishaq bin Abi Talha, in a similar manner. Another Hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr and Abu Amir told us: Zuhair told us: Saad al-Ta’i told us: Abu al-Mudallah, the freed slave of the Mother of the Believers, heard Abu Hurairah, we said: O Messenger of God, when we see you, our hearts soften, and we are from the people of the Hereafter, and when we leave you, the world pleases us, and we smell women and children. He said: “If you were to be in every state in the state you are in with me, the angels would shake your hands with their palms, and visit you in your homes. And if you did not sin, God would bring people who would sin so that He would forgive them.” We said: O Messenger of God, tell us about Paradise, what is its structure? He said: A brick of gold and a brick of silver, its mortar is the most fragrant musk, its pebbles are pearls and rubies, and its soil is saffron. Whoever enters it will be blessed and will not be miserable, and will live forever and will not die. His clothes will not wear out, and his youth will not fade. There are three whose supplications will not be rejected: the just ruler, the fasting person until he breaks his fast, and the supplication of the one who is not fasting until he breaks his fast.” The oppressed person is carried on the clouds and the gates of heaven are opened for him, and the Lord says: By My glory, I will surely aid you, even if after a while. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from another chain of transmission on the authority of Sa`d. Ablution and two rak`ahs of prayer are confirmed upon repentance, as narrated by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal: Waki` told us, Mis`ar and Sufyan Al-Thawri told us on the authority of Uthman ibn Al-Maghbarah Al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Ali ibn Rabi`ah, on the authority of Asma` ibn Al-Hakam Al-Fazari, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: Whenever I heard a hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God would benefit me with whatever He willed from it. And if someone else tells me about it, I make him swear, and if he swears to me, I believe him. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, told me - and Abu Bakr spoke the truth - that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There is no man who commits a sin, then performs ablution and does it well - Misa’ar said - then prays - Sufyan said - then prays two rak’ahs, and seeks forgiveness from God Almighty, except that He forgives him.” And thus it was narrated by Ali ibn al-Madini, al-Humaidi, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, the people of the Sunan, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, al-Bazzar, and al-Daraqutni through various chains of transmission on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Mughira with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is a good hadith, and we have mentioned its chains of transmission, and the discussion of it is complete in Musnad Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him. In short, it is a good hadith, and it is narrated by the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, on the authority of the Prophet’s successor, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with them both. What bears witness to the authenticity of this hadith is what Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is none among you who performs ablution and completes it, then says: I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, except that the eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and he may enter through whichever one he wishes.” And in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, that he performed ablution for them as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, then said: “I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then prays two rak’ahs in which he does not think, his previous sins will be forgiven.” This hadith has been proven from the narration of the four Imams, the Rightly-Guided Caliphs, on the authority of the Master of the First and the Last, and the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds, as indicated by the clear Book, that seeking forgiveness for sins benefits sinners. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Ja’far ibn Sulayman informed us on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: It has been reported to me that when this verse was revealed, And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins, the verse, Satan wept. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Mahraz bin Awn told us, Uthman bin Matar told us, Abdul Ghafoor told us, on the authority of Abu Nasirah, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He said, ‘Upon you is saying ‘There is no god but God’ and seeking forgiveness, so do a lot of them, for Satan said, ‘I have destroyed people with sins and they have destroyed me with ‘There is no god but God’ and seeking forgiveness. So when I saw that, I have destroyed them with desires, and they think that they are guided.’” Uthman bin Matar and his sheikh are weak. Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Amr and Abu Al-Haitham Al-Atwari on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Satan said: O Lord, by Your glory, I will continue to mislead Your servants as long as their souls are in their bodies. God Almighty said: By My glory and majesty, I will continue to forgive them as long as they seek My forgiveness.” Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Umar ibn Abi Khalifa told us, I heard Abu Badr narrating on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: “A man came and said: O Messenger of God, I have committed a sin. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you sin, seek forgiveness from your Lord. He said: I seek forgiveness, then I sin again. He said: If you sin again, seek forgiveness from your Lord. He said it the fourth time, seek forgiveness from your Lord, until Satan is the one who regrets.” This is a strange hadith from this source. And the Almighty’s saying: And who forgives sins except God? means that no one forgives them except Him, as Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Mus’ab told us, Salam ibn Maskeen and al-Mubarak told us on the authority of al-Hasan on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Sari’ that a prisoner was brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: O God, I repent to You and I do not repent to Muhammad. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The truth has been made known to its people. And His saying: And they did not persist in what they did while they knew means that they repented from their sins and returned to God soon, and they did not continue in the sin and persist in it without giving it up. And if the sin was repeated from them, they would repent from it, as al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Ishaq ibn Abi Isra’il and others told us, they said: Abu Yahya Abd al-Hamid al-Hammani told us on the authority of Uthman ibn Waqid, on the authority of Abu Nasirah, on the authority of a freed slave of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He who seeks forgiveness will not persist, even if he returns seventy times a day.” And Abu Dawud narrated it. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Bazzar in his Musnad from the hadith of Uthman bin Waqid - and Yahya bin Ma'een authenticated him with it - and his Sheikh Abu Nasirah Al-Wasiti, whose name is Muslim bin Ubaid, who was authenticated by Imam Ahmad and Ibn Hibban. Ali bin Al-Madini and Al-Tirmidhi said: The chain of transmission of this hadith is not that good. It appears that it is due to the ignorance of the client of Abu Bakr, but the ignorance of someone like him does not harm because he is a great follower, and it is sufficient for him to attribute it to Abu Bakr, so it is a good hadith, and God knows best. And his statement, and they know, Mujahid and Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair said, and they know, that whoever repents, God will accept his repentance. This is like the statement of God, the Most High, Do they not know that God accepts repentance from His servants? and His statement, And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful. And there are many similar examples to this. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Jarir told us, Habban - he is Ibn Zaid Al-Sharabi - told us, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “that he said while he was on the pulpit: ‘Be merciful and you will be shown mercy, and forgive and you will be forgiven. Woe to those who defy speech, woe to those who persist in what they have done while they know.’” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. Then God the Almighty said after describing them with what He described them with: Their reward is forgiveness from their Lord meaning their reward for these attributes is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow meaning of various types of drinks abiding therein meaning abiding therein and excellent is the reward of the workers God the Almighty praises Paradise.
3:134: The Almighty says, forbidding His believing servants from engaging in usury and consuming it in multiples, as they used to say in the days of ignorance: When the due date of a debt comes, either pay it or increase it. If he pays it, otherwise, he increases it in the period, and the other increases it in the amount, and so on every year, perhaps the little will be doubled until it becomes a lot multiplied. The Almighty commanded His servants to be pious, so that they may succeed in the first and the last, then He threatened them with the Fire and warned them against it, so the Almighty said: “And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers. And obey God and the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.” Then He urged them to hasten to do good deeds and hasten to attain the acts of worship, so the Almighty said: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous. That is, just as the Fire was prepared for the disbelievers. It has been said that the meaning of His saying its width is the heavens and the earth is an indication of the vastness of its length, as He said in describing the furnishings of Paradise: its linings are of brocade. That is, what do you think? By the backs? It was said: Rather, its width is like its length because it is a dome under the throne, and the domed and round thing is as wide as its length. This is indicated by what was established in the Sahih: “If you ask God for Paradise, then ask Him for Al-Firdaws, for it is the highest part of Paradise and the middle of Paradise, and from it the rivers of Paradise flow, and its roof is the Throne of the Most Merciful.” This verse is like the Almighty’s saying in Surat al-Hadid 57:Race one another to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth, the verse. We narrated in Musnad Al-Imam Ahmad that Heraclius wrote to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: You have invited me to a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God, so where is the night when the day comes? Ibn Jarir narrated it and said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Muslim bin Khalid told me on the authority of Abu Khathim, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Rashid, on the authority of Ya’la bin Murrah, who said: “I met Al-Tanukhi, the messenger of Heraclius to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Homs, an old man who had become corrupt. He said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the letter of Heraclius, so he handed the paper to a man on his left. He said: I said: Who is your companion who reads? They said: Mu’awiyah. Then it was the letter of my companion: You have written inviting me to a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous. So where is the Fire?” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God! Where is the night when the day comes? Al-A’mash, Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu’bah said on the authority of Qays ibn Muslim on the authority of Tariq ibn Shihab: Some Jews asked Umar ibn al-Khattab about a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? Umar said to them: Have you seen when the day comes, where is the night? And when the night comes, where is the day? They said: Something similar has been taken from the Torah. Ibn Jarir narrated it through three chains of transmission. Then he said: Ahmad ibn Hazim told us, Abu Nu’aym told us, Ja’far ibn Burqan told us, Yazid ibn al-A’sam told us: A man from the People of the Book said: They say, A Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Where is the night when the day comes, and where is the day when the night comes? This has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Mu’ammar told us, Al-Mughirah ibn Salamah Abu Hisham told us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn al-A’sam, on the authority of His uncle Yazid ibn al-Asamm, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, said: “A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘Have you seen the words of God the Almighty: “A Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth,” then where is the Fire? He said: ‘Have you seen that when the night comes it covers everything, so where is the day?’ He said: ‘Wherever God wills.’ He said: ‘And so the Fire will be wherever God the Almighty wills.’” This has two possible meanings one of them that the meaning in that is that it does not necessarily follow from our not seeing the night when the day comes that it is not in a place, even if we do not know it, and so the Fire will be wherever God the Almighty wills, and this is more apparent as mentioned previously in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of al-Bazzar. Second That the meaning is that if the day covers the face of the world from this side, then the night is from the other side, so likewise Paradise is in the highest of the high above the heavens under the Throne and its width, as God Almighty said like the width of the heaven and the earth and Hell is in the lowest of the low, so there is no contradiction between it being like the width of the heavens and the earth and the existence of Hell, and God knows best. Then God the Almighty mentioned the description of the people of Paradise, saying, Those who spend in ease and hardship, meaning in hardship and ease, in comfort and distress, in health and sickness, and in all circumstances, just as He said, Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, meaning that nothing distracts them from obeying God the Almighty and spending in what pleases Him, and doing good to His creation from their relatives and others with various types of righteousness. And God the Almighty said, And those who restrain anger and pardon the people, meaning that if anger arises in them, they restrain it, meaning they conceal it and do not act on it, and they pardon those who wrong them. It was mentioned in some of the narrations: “God the Most High says: O son of Adam, remember Me when you become angry, and I will remember you when you become angry, so that I will not destroy you among those whom I destroy.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Abu Ya’la said in his Musnad: Abu Musa al-Zaman told us, Isa bin Shu’aib al-Dareer Abu al-Fadl told us, al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman al-Jizi told me on the authority of Abu Amr bin Anas bin Malik, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever restrains his anger, God will restrain his punishment from him. Whoever guards his tongue, God will cover his faults. Whoever apologizes to God, God will accept his apology.” This is a strange hadith, and its chain of transmission is questionable. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, Malik told us on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa’id bin al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The strong man is not the one who wrestles, but the strong man is the one who controls himself when he is angry. The two sheikhs narrated it on the authority of Malik. Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taymi, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Suwaid, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Which of you would rather have the wealth of his heir than his own wealth? They said: O Messenger of God, there is none among us who does not love his wealth more than the wealth of his heir. He said: “Know that there is none among you who does not love the wealth of his heir more than his own wealth. Your wealth from your wealth is only what you have sent forward, and the wealth of your heir is what you have delayed.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you consider to be a wrestler among you? We said: The one who is not wrestled by men. He said: No, but the one who controls himself when he is angry. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you consider to be a slave among you? We said: The one who has no children. He said: No, but the slave is the one who has not sent forward any of his children. Al-Bukhari included the first chapter of it, and Muslim included the original of this hadith, on the authority of Al-A’mash. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, I heard Urwah ibn `Abdullah al-Ju`fi narrating on the authority of Hasbah or Ibn Abi Hasin, on the authority of a man who witnessed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, giving a sermon, and he said, Do you know what ruqūb is? We said, The one who has no children. He said, Ruqūb is all the ones who have children and then died without having given anything from them. He said, Do you know what sāluq is? They said, The one who has no wealth. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The sāluq is all the one who has wealth and then died without giving anything from it. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, What is sarā`? They said, The one who is struck down. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Sarā` is all the sarā`, the one who becomes angry and his anger becomes intense, his face turns red, and his hair stands up, so he is struck down by his anger. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr told us, Hisham ibn Urwah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, on the authority of his uncle called Jariyah ibn Qudamah Al-Sa’di, “that he asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, say to me something that will benefit me and make it short for me so that I may understand it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not get angry. So he repeated it to him until he repeated it to him many times, each time saying: Do not get angry.” And this is how he narrated it on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah on the authority of Hisham on his authority, and he also narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id Al-Qattan on the authority of Hisham on his authority, “that a man said: O Messenger of God, say to me something and make it short for me so that I may understand it. He said: Do not get angry.” The hadith is narrated only by Ahmad. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman, “On the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A man said: O Messenger of God, advise me. He said: Do not get angry. The man said: So I thought about it when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said what he said, and I saw that anger brings together all evil.” Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Abu Ibn Harb ibn Abi Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: He was watering from his cistern when some people came and said: Who among you will bring water to Abu Dharr and count the hairs from his head? A man said: I will. So the man came and brought water to him from the cistern and pounded it. Abu Dharr was standing, so he sat down and then lay down. It was said to him: O Abu Dharr, why did you sit down and then lie down? He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: If one of you becomes angry while standing, let him sit down. If the anger goes away from him, then all well and good, otherwise let him lie down.” Abu Dawood narrated it from Ahmad ibn Hanbal with his chain of transmission, except that it was included in his narration on the authority of Abu Harb on the authority of Abu Dharr. The correct version is Ibn Abi Harb on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Dharr, as Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated it on the authority of his father. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim bin Khalid told us, Abu Wa’il al-San’ani told us: We were sitting with Urwah bin Muhammad when a man entered and said to him words that angered him. When he angered him, he stood up and came back to us after having performed ablution. He said: My father told me on the authority of my grandfather Atiyah - he is Ibn Sa’d al-Sa’di - and he was a companion - he said: “The Messenger of God said: Anger is from the devil, and the devil was created from fire, and fire is extinguished only with water. So when one of you becomes angry, let him perform ablution.” And this is how Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Ibrahim bin Khalid al-San’ani on the authority of Abu Wa’il al-Qass al-Muradi al-San’ani. Abu Dawud said: I think he was Abdullah bin Buhair. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Noah bin Ja’una al-Salami told us, on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever gives respite to someone in difficulty or forgives him, God will protect him from the heat of Hell. Indeed, the work of Paradise is made difficult by a hill - three times - Indeed, the work of Hell is made easy by a slip. And the happy one is the one who is protected from trials, and there is no sip more beloved to God than a sip of anger that a servant swallows. No servant of God swallows it except that it fills his stomach with faith.’” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it, and its chain of transmission is good, with no one who is wounded in it, and its text is good. Another hadith with the same meaning - Abu Dawud said: Uqbah bin Makram told us, Abd al-Rahman, meaning Ibn Mahdi, told us, on the authority of Bishr, meaning Ibn Mansur, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ajlan, on the authority of Suwaid bin Wahb, on the authority of a man from the sons of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever suppresses anger when he is able to vent it, God will fill him with security and faith. Whoever refrains from wearing a beautiful garment when he is able to do so - Bishr said: I think he said: out of humility - God will clothe him with the garment of honor. Whoever marries for God, God will clothe him with the crown of kingship.” Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Yazid told us: Saeed told us, Abu Marhum told me on the authority of Sahl bin Muadh bin Anas, on the authority of his father, “The Messenger of God said: Whoever suppresses his anger when he is able to vent it, God will call him in front of all creation and let him choose from any of the houris he wants.” Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Ayoub, and Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Gharib. Another hadith - Abd al-Razzaq said: Dawud ibn Qays informed us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of a man from the people of Ash-Sham called Abd al-Jalil, on the authority of his uncle, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, regarding the words of God Almighty: And those who restrain anger, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever restrains anger when he is able to give vent to it, God will fill him with security and faith. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Another hadith - Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad told us, Yahya ibn Abi Talib told us, Ali ibn Asim told us, Yunus ibn Ubayd told me on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘A servant has not taken a sip of food that is better in reward than a sip of anger that he swallows seeking the face of God.’” And Ibn Majah narrated it likewise on the authority of Bishr ibn Umar, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd, with the same chain of transmission. So God Almighty’s statement: And those who restrain anger means that they do not act out their anger on people, but rather they restrain their evil from them, and they seek reward for that from God Almighty. Then God the Almighty said: And those who pardon people meaning, while refraining from evil, they pardon those who wronged them in their souls, so that no grudge remains in their souls against anyone, and this is the most perfect state, and for this reason He said: And God loves the doers of good so this is from the stations of goodness, and in the hadith: “There are three things that I swear by: no wealth is diminished by charity, and God does not increase a servant through forgiveness except in honor, and whoever humbles himself before God, God will raise him up.” Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Musa bin Uqbah from Ishaq bin Yahya bin Talhah Al-Qurashi, from Ubadah bin As-Samit, from Ubayy bin Ka’b that the Messenger of God, “said: Whoever is pleased to have a lofty building and be raised in status, let him pardon those who wronged him, give to those who deprived him, and connect with those who severed ties with him.” Then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it. Ibn Mardawayh included it from the hadith of Ali, Ka’b bin Ujrah, Abu Hurayrah, and Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with them, in a similar manner. It was narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, a crier will call out, saying: Where are those who pardoned people? Come to your Lord and take your rewards. It is the right of every Muslim man, if he pardons, to enter Paradise.” And God Almighty said: And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins. That is, if they commit a sin, they follow it up with repentance and seeking forgiveness. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Hammam bin Yahya told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Abdullah bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He said: A man committed a sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant committed a sin and knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant. Then he committed another sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant. Then he committed another sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant.” With it, I bear witness that I have forgiven my servant, so let him do whatever he wants.” It was included in Sahih from the hadith of Ishaq bin Abi Talha, in a similar manner. Another Hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr and Abu Amir told us: Zuhair told us: Saad al-Ta’i told us: Abu al-Mudallah, the freed slave of the Mother of the Believers, heard Abu Hurairah, we said: O Messenger of God, when we see you, our hearts soften, and we are from the people of the Hereafter, and when we leave you, the world pleases us, and we smell women and children. He said: “If you were to be in every state in the state you are in with me, the angels would shake your hands with their palms, and visit you in your homes. And if you did not sin, God would bring people who would sin so that He would forgive them.” We said: O Messenger of God, tell us about Paradise, what is its structure? He said: A brick of gold and a brick of silver, its mortar is the most fragrant musk, its pebbles are pearls and rubies, and its soil is saffron. Whoever enters it will be blessed and will not be miserable, and will live forever and will not die. His clothes will not wear out, and his youth will not fade. There are three whose supplications will not be rejected: the just ruler, the fasting person until he breaks his fast, and the supplication of the one who is not fasting until he breaks his fast.” The oppressed person is carried on the clouds and the gates of heaven are opened for him, and the Lord says: By My glory, I will surely aid you, even if after a while. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from another chain of transmission on the authority of Sa`d. Ablution and two rak`ahs of prayer are confirmed upon repentance, as narrated by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal: Waki` told us, Mis`ar and Sufyan Al-Thawri told us on the authority of Uthman ibn Al-Maghbarah Al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Ali ibn Rabi`ah, on the authority of Asma` ibn Al-Hakam Al-Fazari, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: Whenever I heard a hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God would benefit me with whatever He willed from it. And if someone else tells me about it, I make him swear, and if he swears to me, I believe him. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, told me - and Abu Bakr spoke the truth - that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There is no man who commits a sin, then performs ablution and does it well - Misa’ar said - then prays - Sufyan said - then prays two rak’ahs, and seeks forgiveness from God Almighty, except that He forgives him.” And thus it was narrated by Ali ibn al-Madini, al-Humaidi, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, the people of the Sunan, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, al-Bazzar, and al-Daraqutni through various chains of transmission on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Mughira with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is a good hadith, and we have mentioned its chains of transmission, and the discussion of it is complete in Musnad Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him. In short, it is a good hadith, and it is narrated by the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, on the authority of the Prophet’s successor, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with them both. What bears witness to the authenticity of this hadith is what Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is none among you who performs ablution and completes it, then says: I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, except that the eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and he may enter through whichever one he wishes.” And in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, that he performed ablution for them as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, then said: “I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then prays two rak’ahs in which he does not think, his previous sins will be forgiven.” This hadith has been proven from the narration of the four Imams, the Rightly-Guided Caliphs, on the authority of the Master of the First and the Last, and the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds, as indicated by the clear Book, that seeking forgiveness for sins benefits sinners. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Ja’far ibn Sulayman informed us on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: It has been reported to me that when this verse was revealed, And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins, the verse, Satan wept. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Mahraz bin Awn told us, Uthman bin Matar told us, Abdul Ghafoor told us, on the authority of Abu Nasirah, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He said, ‘Upon you is saying ‘There is no god but God’ and seeking forgiveness, so do a lot of them, for Satan said, ‘I have destroyed people with sins and they have destroyed me with ‘There is no god but God’ and seeking forgiveness. So when I saw that, I have destroyed them with desires, and they think that they are guided.’” Uthman bin Matar and his sheikh are weak. Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Amr and Abu Al-Haitham Al-Atwari on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Satan said: O Lord, by Your glory, I will continue to mislead Your servants as long as their souls are in their bodies. God Almighty said: By My glory and majesty, I will continue to forgive them as long as they seek My forgiveness.” Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Umar ibn Abi Khalifa told us, I heard Abu Badr narrating on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: “A man came and said: O Messenger of God, I have committed a sin. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you sin, seek forgiveness from your Lord. He said: I seek forgiveness, then I sin again. He said: If you sin again, seek forgiveness from your Lord. He said it the fourth time, seek forgiveness from your Lord, until Satan is the one who regrets.” This is a strange hadith from this source. And the Almighty’s saying: And who forgives sins except God? means that no one forgives them except Him, as Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Mus’ab told us, Salam ibn Maskeen and al-Mubarak told us on the authority of al-Hasan on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Sari’ that a prisoner was brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: O God, I repent to You and I do not repent to Muhammad. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The truth has been made known to its people. And His saying: And they did not persist in what they did while they knew means that they repented from their sins and returned to God soon, and they did not continue in the sin and persist in it without giving it up. And if the sin was repeated from them, they would repent from it, as al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Ishaq ibn Abi Isra’il and others told us, they said: Abu Yahya Abd al-Hamid al-Hammani told us on the authority of Uthman ibn Waqid, on the authority of Abu Nasirah, on the authority of a freed slave of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He who seeks forgiveness will not persist, even if he returns seventy times a day.” And Abu Dawud narrated it. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Bazzar in his Musnad from the hadith of Uthman bin Waqid - and Yahya bin Ma'een authenticated him with it - and his Sheikh Abu Nasirah Al-Wasiti, whose name is Muslim bin Ubaid, who was authenticated by Imam Ahmad and Ibn Hibban. Ali bin Al-Madini and Al-Tirmidhi said: The chain of transmission of this hadith is not that good. It appears that it is due to the ignorance of the client of Abu Bakr, but the ignorance of someone like him does not harm because he is a great follower, and it is sufficient for him to attribute it to Abu Bakr, so it is a good hadith, and God knows best. And his statement, "and they know, Mujahid and Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair said, and they know," that whoever repents, God will accept his repentance. This is like the statement of God, the Most High, "Do they not know that God accepts repentance from His servants? and His statement, And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful." And there are many similar examples to this. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Jarir told us, Habban - he is Ibn Zaid Al-Sharabi - told us, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “that he said while he was on the pulpit: ‘Be merciful and you will be shown mercy, and forgive and you will be forgiven. Woe to those who defy speech, woe to those who persist in what they have done while they know.’” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. Then God the Almighty said after describing them with what He described them with: Their reward is forgiveness from their Lord meaning their reward for these attributes is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow meaning of various types of drinks abiding therein meaning abiding therein and excellent is the reward of the workers God the Almighty praises Paradise.
3:135: The Almighty says, forbidding His believing servants from engaging in usury and consuming it in multiples, as they used to say in the days of ignorance: When the due date of a debt comes, either pay it or increase it. If he pays it, otherwise, he increases it in the period, and the other increases it in the amount, and so on every year, perhaps the little will be doubled until it becomes a lot multiplied. The Almighty commanded His servants to be pious, so that they may succeed in the first and the last, then He threatened them with the Fire and warned them against it, so the Almighty said: “And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers. And obey God and the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.” Then He urged them to hasten to do good deeds and hasten to attain the acts of worship, so the Almighty said: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous. That is, just as the Fire was prepared for the disbelievers. It has been said that the meaning of His saying its width is the heavens and the earth is an indication of the vastness of its length, as He said in describing the furnishings of Paradise: its linings are of brocade. That is, what do you think? By the backs? It was said: Rather, its width is like its length because it is a dome under the throne, and the domed and round thing is as wide as its length. This is indicated by what was established in the Sahih: “If you ask God for Paradise, then ask Him for Al-Firdaws, for it is the highest part of Paradise and the middle of Paradise, and from it the rivers of Paradise flow, and its roof is the Throne of the Most Merciful.” This verse is like the Almighty’s saying in Surat al-Hadid 57:Race one another to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth, the verse. We narrated in Musnad Al-Imam Ahmad that Heraclius wrote to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: You have invited me to a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God, so where is the night when the day comes? Ibn Jarir narrated it and said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Muslim bin Khalid told me on the authority of Abu Khathim, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Rashid, on the authority of Ya’la bin Murrah, who said: “I met Al-Tanukhi, the messenger of Heraclius to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Homs, an old man who had become corrupt. He said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the letter of Heraclius, so he handed the paper to a man on his left. He said: I said: Who is your companion who reads? They said: Mu’awiyah. Then it was the letter of my companion: You have written inviting me to a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous. So where is the Fire?” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God! Where is the night when the day comes? Al-A’mash, Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu’bah said on the authority of Qays ibn Muslim on the authority of Tariq ibn Shihab: Some Jews asked Umar ibn al-Khattab about a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? Umar said to them: Have you seen when the day comes, where is the night? And when the night comes, where is the day? They said: Something similar has been taken from the Torah. Ibn Jarir narrated it through three chains of transmission. Then he said: Ahmad ibn Hazim told us, Abu Nu’aym told us, Ja’far ibn Burqan told us, Yazid ibn al-A’sam told us: A man from the People of the Book said: They say, A Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Where is the night when the day comes, and where is the day when the night comes? This has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Mu’ammar told us, Al-Mughirah ibn Salamah Abu Hisham told us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn al-A’sam, on the authority of His uncle Yazid ibn al-Asamm, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, said: “A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘Have you seen the words of God the Almighty: “A Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth,” then where is the Fire? He said: ‘Have you seen that when the night comes it covers everything, so where is the day?’ He said: ‘Wherever God wills.’ He said: ‘And so the Fire will be wherever God the Almighty wills.’” This has two possible meanings one of them that the meaning in that is that it does not necessarily follow from our not seeing the night when the day comes that it is not in a place, even if we do not know it, and so the Fire will be wherever God the Almighty wills, and this is more apparent as mentioned previously in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of al-Bazzar. Second That the meaning is that if the day covers the face of the world from this side, then the night is from the other side, so likewise Paradise is in the highest of the high above the heavens under the Throne and its width, as God Almighty said like the width of the heaven and the earth and Hell is in the lowest of the low, so there is no contradiction between it being like the width of the heavens and the earth and the existence of Hell, and God knows best. Then God the Almighty mentioned the description of the people of Paradise, saying, Those who spend in ease and hardship, meaning in hardship and ease, in comfort and distress, in health and sickness, and in all circumstances, just as He said, Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, meaning that nothing distracts them from obeying God the Almighty and spending in what pleases Him, and doing good to His creation from their relatives and others with various types of righteousness. And God the Almighty said, And those who restrain anger and pardon the people, meaning that if anger arises in them, they restrain it, meaning they conceal it and do not act on it, and they pardon those who wrong them. It was mentioned in some of the narrations: “God the Most High says: O son of Adam, remember Me when you become angry, and I will remember you when you become angry, so that I will not destroy you among those whom I destroy.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Abu Ya’la said in his Musnad: Abu Musa al-Zaman told us, Isa bin Shu’aib al-Dareer Abu al-Fadl told us, al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman al-Jizi told me on the authority of Abu Amr bin Anas bin Malik, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever restrains his anger, God will restrain his punishment from him. Whoever guards his tongue, God will cover his faults. Whoever apologizes to God, God will accept his apology.” This is a strange hadith, and its chain of transmission is questionable. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, Malik told us on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa’id bin al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The strong man is not the one who wrestles, but the strong man is the one who controls himself when he is angry. The two sheikhs narrated it on the authority of Malik. Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taymi, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Suwaid, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Which of you would rather have the wealth of his heir than his own wealth? They said: O Messenger of God, there is none among us who does not love his wealth more than the wealth of his heir. He said: “Know that there is none among you who does not love the wealth of his heir more than his own wealth. Your wealth from your wealth is only what you have sent forward, and the wealth of your heir is what you have delayed.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you consider to be a wrestler among you? We said: The one who is not wrestled by men. He said: No, but the one who controls himself when he is angry. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you consider to be a slave among you? We said: The one who has no children. He said: No, but the slave is the one who has not sent forward any of his children. Al-Bukhari included the first chapter of it, and Muslim included the original of this hadith, on the authority of Al-A’mash. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, I heard Urwah ibn `Abdullah al-Ju`fi narrating on the authority of Hasbah or Ibn Abi Hasin, on the authority of a man who witnessed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, giving a sermon, and he said, Do you know what ruqūb is? We said, The one who has no children. He said, Ruqūb is all the ones who have children and then died without having given anything from them. He said, Do you know what sāluq is? They said, The one who has no wealth. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The sāluq is all the one who has wealth and then died without giving anything from it. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, What is sarā`? They said, The one who is struck down. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Sarā` is all the sarā`, the one who becomes angry and his anger becomes intense, his face turns red, and his hair stands up, so he is struck down by his anger. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr told us, Hisham ibn Urwah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, on the authority of his uncle called Jariyah ibn Qudamah Al-Sa’di, “that he asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, say to me something that will benefit me and make it short for me so that I may understand it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not get angry. So he repeated it to him until he repeated it to him many times, each time saying: Do not get angry.” And this is how he narrated it on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah on the authority of Hisham on his authority, and he also narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id Al-Qattan on the authority of Hisham on his authority, “that a man said: O Messenger of God, say to me something and make it short for me so that I may understand it. He said: Do not get angry.” The hadith is narrated only by Ahmad. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman, “On the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A man said: O Messenger of God, advise me. He said: Do not get angry.
