The man said: So I thought about it when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said what he said, and I saw that anger brings together all evil.” Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Abu Ibn Harb ibn Abi Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: He was watering from his cistern when some people came and said: Who among you will bring water to Abu Dharr and count the hairs from his head? A man said: I will. So the man came and brought water to him from the cistern and pounded it. Abu Dharr was standing, so he sat down and then lay down. It was said to him: O Abu Dharr, why did you sit down and then lie down? He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: If one of you becomes angry while standing, let him sit down. If the anger goes away from him, then all well and good, otherwise let him lie down.” Abu Dawood narrated it from Ahmad ibn Hanbal with his chain of transmission, except that it was included in his narration on the authority of Abu Harb on the authority of Abu Dharr. The correct version is Ibn Abi Harb on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Dharr, as Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated it on the authority of his father. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim bin Khalid told us, Abu Wa’il al-San’ani told us: We were sitting with Urwah bin Muhammad when a man entered and said to him words that angered him. When he angered him, he stood up and came back to us after having performed ablution. He said: My father told me on the authority of my grandfather Atiyah - he is Ibn Sa’d al-Sa’di - and he was a companion - he said: “The Messenger of God said: Anger is from the devil, and the devil was created from fire, and fire is extinguished only with water. So when one of you becomes angry, let him perform ablution.” And this is how Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Ibrahim bin Khalid al-San’ani on the authority of Abu Wa’il al-Qass al-Muradi al-San’ani. Abu Dawud said: I think he was Abdullah bin Buhair. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Noah bin Ja’una al-Salami told us, on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever gives respite to someone in difficulty or forgives him, God will protect him from the heat of Hell. Indeed, the work of Paradise is made difficult by a hill - three times - Indeed, the work of Hell is made easy by a slip. And the happy one is the one who is protected from trials, and there is no sip more beloved to God than a sip of anger that a servant swallows. No servant of God swallows it except that it fills his stomach with faith.’” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it, and its chain of transmission is good, with no one who is wounded in it, and its text is good. Another hadith with the same meaning - Abu Dawud said: Uqbah bin Makram told us, Abd al-Rahman, meaning Ibn Mahdi, told us, on the authority of Bishr, meaning Ibn Mansur, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ajlan, on the authority of Suwaid bin Wahb, on the authority of a man from the sons of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever suppresses anger when he is able to vent it, God will fill him with security and faith. Whoever refrains from wearing a beautiful garment when he is able to do so - Bishr said: I think he said: out of humility - God will clothe him with the garment of honor. Whoever marries for God, God will clothe him with the crown of kingship.” Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Yazid told us: Saeed told us, Abu Marhum told me on the authority of Sahl bin Muadh bin Anas, on the authority of his father, “The Messenger of God said: Whoever suppresses his anger when he is able to vent it, God will call him in front of all creation and let him choose from any of the houris he wants.” Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Ayoub, and Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Gharib. Another hadith - Abd al-Razzaq said: Dawud ibn Qays informed us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of a man from the people of Ash-Sham called Abd al-Jalil, on the authority of his uncle, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, regarding the words of God Almighty: And those who restrain anger, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever restrains anger when he is able to give vent to it, God will fill him with security and faith. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Another hadith - Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad told us, Yahya ibn Abi Talib told us, Ali ibn Asim told us, Yunus ibn Ubayd told me on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘A servant has not taken a sip of food that is better in reward than a sip of anger that he swallows seeking the face of God.’” And Ibn Majah narrated it likewise on the authority of Bishr ibn Umar, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd, with the same chain of transmission. So God Almighty’s statement: And those who restrain anger means that they do not act out their anger on people, but rather they restrain their evil from them, and they seek reward for that from God Almighty. Then God the Almighty said: And those who pardon people meaning, while refraining from evil, they pardon those who wronged them in their souls, so that no grudge remains in their souls against anyone, and this is the most perfect state, and for this reason He said: And God loves the doers of good so this is from the stations of goodness, and in the hadith: “There are three things that I swear by: no wealth is diminished by charity, and God does not increase a servant through forgiveness except in honor, and whoever humbles himself before God, God will raise him up.” Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Musa bin Uqbah from Ishaq bin Yahya bin Talhah Al-Qurashi, from Ubadah bin As-Samit, from Ubayy bin Ka’b that the Messenger of God, “said: Whoever is pleased to have a lofty building and be raised in status, let him pardon those who wronged him, give to those who deprived him, and connect with those who severed ties with him.” Then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it. Ibn Mardawayh included it from the hadith of Ali, Ka’b bin Ujrah, Abu Hurayrah, and Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with them, in a similar manner. It was narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, a crier will call out, saying: Where are those who pardoned people? Come to your Lord and take your rewards. It is the right of every Muslim man, if he pardons, to enter Paradise.” And God Almighty said: And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins. That is, if they commit a sin, they follow it up with repentance and seeking forgiveness. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Hammam bin Yahya told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Abdullah bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He said: A man committed a sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant committed a sin and knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant. Then he committed another sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant. Then he committed another sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant.” With it, I bear witness that I have forgiven my servant, so let him do whatever he wants.” It was included in Sahih from the hadith of Ishaq bin Abi Talha, in a similar manner. Another Hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr and Abu Amir told us: Zuhair told us: Saad al-Ta’i told us: Abu al-Mudallah, the freed slave of the Mother of the Believers, heard Abu Hurairah, we said: O Messenger of God, when we see you, our hearts soften, and we are from the people of the Hereafter, and when we leave you, the world pleases us, and we smell women and children. He said: “If you were to be in every state in the state you are in with me, the angels would shake your hands with their palms, and visit you in your homes. And if you did not sin, God would bring people who would sin so that He would forgive them.” We said: O Messenger of God, tell us about Paradise, what is its structure? He said: A brick of gold and a brick of silver, its mortar is the most fragrant musk, its pebbles are pearls and rubies, and its soil is saffron. Whoever enters it will be blessed and will not be miserable, and will live forever and will not die. His clothes will not wear out, and his youth will not fade. There are three whose supplications will not be rejected: the just ruler, the fasting person until he breaks his fast, and the supplication of the one who is not fasting until he breaks his fast.” The oppressed person is carried on the clouds and the gates of heaven are opened for him, and the Lord says: By My glory, I will surely aid you, even if after a while. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from another chain of transmission on the authority of Sa`d. Ablution and two rak`ahs of prayer are confirmed upon repentance, as narrated by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal: Waki` told us, Mis`ar and Sufyan Al-Thawri told us on the authority of Uthman ibn Al-Maghbarah Al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Ali ibn Rabi`ah, on the authority of Asma` ibn Al-Hakam Al-Fazari, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: Whenever I heard a hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God would benefit me with whatever He willed from it. And if someone else tells me about it, I make him swear, and if he swears to me, I believe him. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, told me - and Abu Bakr spoke the truth - that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There is no man who commits a sin, then performs ablution and does it well - Misa’ar said - then prays - Sufyan said - then prays two rak’ahs, and seeks forgiveness from God Almighty, except that He forgives him.” And thus it was narrated by Ali ibn al-Madini, al-Humaidi, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, the people of the Sunan, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, al-Bazzar, and al-Daraqutni through various chains of transmission on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Mughira with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is a good hadith, and we have mentioned its chains of transmission, and the discussion of it is complete in Musnad Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him. In short, it is a good hadith, and it is narrated by the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, on the authority of the Prophet’s successor, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with them both. What bears witness to the authenticity of this hadith is what Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is none among you who performs ablution and completes it, then says: I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, except that the eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and he may enter through whichever one he wishes.” And in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, that he performed ablution for them as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, then said: “I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then prays two rak’ahs in which he does not think, his previous sins will be forgiven.” This hadith has been proven from the narration of the four Imams, the Rightly-Guided Caliphs, on the authority of the Master of the First and the Last, and the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds, as indicated by the clear Book, that seeking forgiveness for sins benefits sinners. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Ja’far ibn Sulayman informed us on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: It has been reported to me that when this verse was revealed, And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins, the verse, Satan wept. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Mahraz bin Awn told us, Uthman bin Matar told us, Abdul Ghafoor told us, on the authority of Abu Nasirah, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He said, ‘Upon you is saying ‘There is no god but God’ and seeking forgiveness, so do a lot of them, for Satan said, ‘I have destroyed people with sins and they have destroyed me with ‘There is no god but God’ and seeking forgiveness. So when I saw that, I have destroyed them with desires, and they think that they are guided.’” Uthman bin Matar and his sheikh are weak. Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Amr and Abu Al-Haitham Al-Atwari on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Satan said: O Lord, by Your glory, I will continue to mislead Your servants as long as their souls are in their bodies. God Almighty said: By My glory and majesty, I will continue to forgive them as long as they seek My forgiveness.” Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Umar ibn Abi Khalifa told us, I heard Abu Badr narrating on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: “A man came and said: O Messenger of God, I have committed a sin. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you sin, seek forgiveness from your Lord. He said: I seek forgiveness, then I sin again. He said: If you sin again, seek forgiveness from your Lord. He said it the fourth time, seek forgiveness from your Lord, until Satan is the one who regrets.” This is a strange hadith from this source. And the Almighty’s saying: And who forgives sins except God? means that no one forgives them except Him, as Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Mus’ab told us, Salam ibn Maskeen and al-Mubarak told us on the authority of al-Hasan on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Sari’ that a prisoner was brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: O God, I repent to You and I do not repent to Muhammad. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The truth has been made known to its people. And His saying: And they did not persist in what they did while they knew means that they repented from their sins and returned to God soon, and they did not continue in the sin and persist in it without giving it up. And if the sin was repeated from them, they would repent from it, as al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Ishaq ibn Abi Isra’il and others told us, they said: Abu Yahya Abd al-Hamid al-Hammani told us on the authority of Uthman ibn Waqid, on the authority of Abu Nasirah, on the authority of a freed slave of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He who seeks forgiveness will not persist, even if he returns seventy times a day.” And Abu Dawud narrated it. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Bazzar in his Musnad from the hadith of Uthman bin Waqid - and Yahya bin Ma'een authenticated him with it - and his Sheikh Abu Nasirah Al-Wasiti, whose name is Muslim bin Ubaid, who was authenticated by Imam Ahmad and Ibn Hibban. Ali bin Al-Madini and Al-Tirmidhi said: The chain of transmission of this hadith is not that good. It appears that it is due to the ignorance of the client of Abu Bakr, but the ignorance of someone like him does not harm because he is a great follower, and it is sufficient for him to attribute it to Abu Bakr, so it is a good hadith, and God knows best. And his statement, and they know, Mujahid and Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair said, and they know, that whoever repents, God will accept his repentance. This is like the statement of God, the Most High, Do they not know that God accepts repentance from His servants? and His statement, And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful. And there are many similar examples to this. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Jarir told us, Habban - he is Ibn Zaid Al-Sharabi - told us, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “that he said while he was on the pulpit: ‘Be merciful and you will be shown mercy, and forgive and you will be forgiven. Woe to those who defy speech, woe to those who persist in what they have done while they know.’” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. Then God the Almighty said after describing them with what He described them with: Their reward is forgiveness from their Lord meaning their reward for these attributes is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow meaning of various types of drinks abiding therein meaning abiding therein and excellent is the reward of the workers God the Almighty praises Paradise.
3:136: The Almighty says, forbidding His believing servants from engaging in usury and consuming it in multiples, as they used to say in the days of ignorance: When the due date of a debt comes, either pay it or increase it. If he pays it, otherwise, he increases it in the period, and the other increases it in the amount, and so on every year, perhaps the little will be doubled until it becomes a lot multiplied. The Almighty commanded His servants to be pious, so that they may succeed in the first and the last, then He threatened them with the Fire and warned them against it, so the Almighty said: “And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers. And obey God and the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.” Then He urged them to hasten to do good deeds and hasten to attain the acts of worship, so the Almighty said: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous. That is, just as the Fire was prepared for the disbelievers. It has been said that the meaning of His saying its width is the heavens and the earth is an indication of the vastness of its length, as He said in describing the furnishings of Paradise: its linings are of brocade. That is, what do you think? By the backs? It was said: Rather, its width is like its length because it is a dome under the throne, and the domed and round thing is as wide as its length. This is indicated by what was established in the Sahih: “If you ask God for Paradise, then ask Him for Al-Firdaws, for it is the highest part of Paradise and the middle of Paradise, and from it the rivers of Paradise flow, and its roof is the Throne of the Most Merciful.” This verse is like the Almighty’s saying in Surat al-Hadid 57:Race one another to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth, the verse. We narrated in Musnad Al-Imam Ahmad that Heraclius wrote to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: You have invited me to a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God, so where is the night when the day comes? Ibn Jarir narrated it and said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Muslim bin Khalid told me on the authority of Abu Khathim, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Rashid, on the authority of Ya’la bin Murrah, who said: “I met Al-Tanukhi, the messenger of Heraclius to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Homs, an old man who had become corrupt. He said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the letter of Heraclius, so he handed the paper to a man on his left. He said: I said: Who is your companion who reads? They said: Mu’awiyah. Then it was the letter of my companion: You have written inviting me to a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous. So where is the Fire?” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God! Where is the night when the day comes? Al-A’mash, Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu’bah said on the authority of Qays ibn Muslim on the authority of Tariq ibn Shihab: Some Jews asked Umar ibn al-Khattab about a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? Umar said to them: Have you seen when the day comes, where is the night? And when the night comes, where is the day? They said: Something similar has been taken from the Torah. Ibn Jarir narrated it through three chains of transmission. Then he said: Ahmad ibn Hazim told us, Abu Nu’aym told us, Ja’far ibn Burqan told us, Yazid ibn al-A’sam told us: A man from the People of the Book said: They say, A Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell? Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Where is the night when the day comes, and where is the day when the night comes? This has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Mu’ammar told us, Al-Mughirah ibn Salamah Abu Hisham told us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn al-A’sam, on the authority of His uncle Yazid ibn al-Asamm, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, said: “A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘Have you seen the words of God the Almighty: “A Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth,” then where is the Fire? He said: ‘Have you seen that when the night comes it covers everything, so where is the day?’ He said: ‘Wherever God wills.’ He said: ‘And so the Fire will be wherever God the Almighty wills.’” This has two possible meanings one of them that the meaning in that is that it does not necessarily follow from our not seeing the night when the day comes that it is not in a place, even if we do not know it, and so the Fire will be wherever God the Almighty wills, and this is more apparent as mentioned previously in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of al-Bazzar. Second That the meaning is that if the day covers the face of the world from this side, then the night is from the other side, so likewise Paradise is in the highest of the high above the heavens under the Throne and its width, as God Almighty said like the width of the heaven and the earth and Hell is in the lowest of the low, so there is no contradiction between it being like the width of the heavens and the earth and the existence of Hell, and God knows best. Then God the Almighty mentioned the description of the people of Paradise, saying, Those who spend in ease and hardship, meaning in hardship and ease, in comfort and distress, in health and sickness, and in all circumstances, just as He said, Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly, meaning that nothing distracts them from obeying God the Almighty and spending in what pleases Him, and doing good to His creation from their relatives and others with various types of righteousness. And God the Almighty said, And those who restrain anger and pardon the people, meaning that if anger arises in them, they restrain it, meaning they conceal it and do not act on it, and they pardon those who wrong them. It was mentioned in some of the narrations: “God the Most High says: O son of Adam, remember Me when you become angry, and I will remember you when you become angry, so that I will not destroy you among those whom I destroy.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Abu Ya’la said in his Musnad: Abu Musa al-Zaman told us, Isa bin Shu’aib al-Dareer Abu al-Fadl told us, al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman al-Jizi told me on the authority of Abu Amr bin Anas bin Malik, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever restrains his anger, God will restrain his punishment from him. Whoever guards his tongue, God will cover his faults. Whoever apologizes to God, God will accept his apology.” This is a strange hadith, and its chain of transmission is questionable. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, Malik told us on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa’id bin al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The strong man is not the one who wrestles, but the strong man is the one who controls himself when he is angry. The two sheikhs narrated it on the authority of Malik. Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taymi, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Suwaid, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Which of you would rather have the wealth of his heir than his own wealth? They said: O Messenger of God, there is none among us who does not love his wealth more than the wealth of his heir. He said: “Know that there is none among you who does not love the wealth of his heir more than his own wealth. Your wealth from your wealth is only what you have sent forward, and the wealth of your heir is what you have delayed.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you consider to be a wrestler among you? We said: The one who is not wrestled by men. He said: No, but the one who controls himself when he is angry. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you consider to be a slave among you? We said: The one who has no children. He said: No, but the slave is the one who has not sent forward any of his children. Al-Bukhari included the first chapter of it, and Muslim included the original of this hadith, on the authority of Al-A’mash. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, I heard Urwah ibn `Abdullah al-Ju`fi narrating on the authority of Hasbah or Ibn Abi Hasin, on the authority of a man who witnessed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, giving a sermon, and he said, Do you know what ruqūb is? We said, The one who has no children. He said, Ruqūb is all the ones who have children and then died without having given anything from them. He said, Do you know what sāluq is? They said, The one who has no wealth. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The sāluq is all the one who has wealth and then died without giving anything from it. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, What is sarā`? They said, The one who is struck down. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Sarā` is all the sarā`, the one who becomes angry and his anger becomes intense, his face turns red, and his hair stands up, so he is struck down by his anger. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr told us, Hisham ibn Urwah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, on the authority of his uncle called Jariyah ibn Qudamah Al-Sa’di, “that he asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, say to me something that will benefit me and make it short for me so that I may understand it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not get angry. So he repeated it to him until he repeated it to him many times, each time saying: Do not get angry.” And this is how he narrated it on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah on the authority of Hisham on his authority, and he also narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id Al-Qattan on the authority of Hisham on his authority, “that a man said: O Messenger of God, say to me something and make it short for me so that I may understand it. He said: Do not get angry.” The hadith is narrated only by Ahmad. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman, “On the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A man said: O Messenger of God, advise me. He said: Do not get angry. The man said: So I thought about it when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said what he said, and I saw that anger brings together all evil.” Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Abu Ibn Harb ibn Abi Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: He was watering from his cistern when some people came and said: Who among you will bring water to Abu Dharr and count the hairs from his head? A man said: I will. So the man came and brought water to him from the cistern and pounded it. Abu Dharr was standing, so he sat down and then lay down. It was said to him: O Abu Dharr, why did you sit down and then lie down? He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: If one of you becomes angry while standing, let him sit down. If the anger goes away from him, then all well and good, otherwise let him lie down.” Abu Dawood narrated it from Ahmad ibn Hanbal with his chain of transmission, except that it was included in his narration on the authority of Abu Harb on the authority of Abu Dharr. The correct version is Ibn Abi Harb on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Dharr, as Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated it on the authority of his father. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim bin Khalid told us, Abu Wa’il al-San’ani told us: We were sitting with Urwah bin Muhammad when a man entered and said to him words that angered him. When he angered him, he stood up and came back to us after having performed ablution. He said: My father told me on the authority of my grandfather Atiyah - he is Ibn Sa’d al-Sa’di - and he was a companion - he said: “The Messenger of God said: Anger is from the devil, and the devil was created from fire, and fire is extinguished only with water. So when one of you becomes angry, let him perform ablution.” And this is how Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Ibrahim bin Khalid al-San’ani on the authority of Abu Wa’il al-Qass al-Muradi al-San’ani. Abu Dawud said: I think he was Abdullah bin Buhair. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Yazid told us, Noah bin Ja’una al-Salami told us, on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever gives respite to someone in difficulty or forgives him, God will protect him from the heat of Hell. Indeed, the work of Paradise is made difficult by a hill - three times - Indeed, the work of Hell is made easy by a slip. And the happy one is the one who is protected from trials, and there is no sip more beloved to God than a sip of anger that a servant swallows. No servant of God swallows it except that it fills his stomach with faith.’” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it, and its chain of transmission is good, with no one who is wounded in it, and its text is good. Another hadith with the same meaning - Abu Dawud said: Uqbah bin Makram told us, Abd al-Rahman, meaning Ibn Mahdi, told us, on the authority of Bishr, meaning Ibn Mansur, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ajlan, on the authority of Suwaid bin Wahb, on the authority of a man from the sons of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of his father, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever suppresses anger when he is able to vent it, God will fill him with security and faith. Whoever refrains from wearing a beautiful garment when he is able to do so - Bishr said: I think he said: out of humility - God will clothe him with the garment of honor. Whoever marries for God, God will clothe him with the crown of kingship.” Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Yazid told us: Saeed told us, Abu Marhum told me on the authority of Sahl bin Muadh bin Anas, on the authority of his father, “The Messenger of God said: Whoever suppresses his anger when he is able to vent it, God will call him in front of all creation and let him choose from any of the houris he wants.” Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Ayoub, and Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Gharib. Another hadith - Abd al-Razzaq said: Dawud ibn Qays informed us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of a man from the people of Ash-Sham called Abd al-Jalil, on the authority of his uncle, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, regarding the words of God Almighty: And those who restrain anger, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever restrains anger when he is able to give vent to it, God will fill him with security and faith. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Another hadith - Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad told us, Yahya ibn Abi Talib told us, Ali ibn Asim told us, Yunus ibn Ubayd told me on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘A servant has not taken a sip of food that is better in reward than a sip of anger that he swallows seeking the face of God.’” And Ibn Majah narrated it likewise on the authority of Bishr ibn Umar, on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd, with the same chain of transmission. So God Almighty’s statement: And those who restrain anger means that they do not act out their anger on people, but rather they restrain their evil from them, and they seek reward for that from God Almighty. Then God the Almighty said: And those who pardon people meaning, while refraining from evil, they pardon those who wronged them in their souls, so that no grudge remains in their souls against anyone, and this is the most perfect state, and for this reason He said: And God loves the doers of good so this is from the stations of goodness, and in the hadith: “There are three things that I swear by: no wealth is diminished by charity, and God does not increase a servant through forgiveness except in honor, and whoever humbles himself before God, God will raise him up.” Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Musa bin Uqbah from Ishaq bin Yahya bin Talhah Al-Qurashi, from Ubadah bin As-Samit, from Ubayy bin Ka’b that the Messenger of God, “said: Whoever is pleased to have a lofty building and be raised in status, let him pardon those who wronged him, give to those who deprived him, and connect with those who severed ties with him.” Then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it. Ibn Mardawayh included it from the hadith of Ali, Ka’b bin Ujrah, Abu Hurayrah, and Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with them, in a similar manner. It was narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, a crier will call out, saying: Where are those who pardoned people? Come to your Lord and take your rewards. It is the right of every Muslim man, if he pardons, to enter Paradise.” And God Almighty said: And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins. That is, if they commit a sin, they follow it up with repentance and seeking forgiveness. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Hammam bin Yahya told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Abdullah bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He said: A man committed a sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant committed a sin and knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant. Then he committed another sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant. Then he committed another sin and said: O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it. God, the Almighty, said: My servant knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes them to task. I have forgiven My servant.” With it, I bear witness that I have forgiven my servant, so let him do whatever he wants.” It was included in Sahih from the hadith of Ishaq bin Abi Talha, in a similar manner. Another Hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr and Abu Amir told us: Zuhair told us: Saad al-Ta’i told us: Abu al-Mudallah, the freed slave of the Mother of the Believers, heard Abu Hurairah, we said: O Messenger of God, when we see you, our hearts soften, and we are from the people of the Hereafter, and when we leave you, the world pleases us, and we smell women and children. He said: “If you were to be in every state in the state you are in with me, the angels would shake your hands with their palms, and visit you in your homes. And if you did not sin, God would bring people who would sin so that He would forgive them.” We said: O Messenger of God, tell us about Paradise, what is its structure? He said: A brick of gold and a brick of silver, its mortar is the most fragrant musk, its pebbles are pearls and rubies, and its soil is saffron. Whoever enters it will be blessed and will not be miserable, and will live forever and will not die. His clothes will not wear out, and his youth will not fade. There are three whose supplications will not be rejected: the just ruler, the fasting person until he breaks his fast, and the supplication of the one who is not fasting until he breaks his fast.” The oppressed person is carried on the clouds and the gates of heaven are opened for him, and the Lord says: By My glory, I will surely aid you, even if after a while. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from another chain of transmission on the authority of Sa`d. Ablution and two rak`ahs of prayer are confirmed upon repentance, as narrated by Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal: Waki` told us, Mis`ar and Sufyan Al-Thawri told us on the authority of Uthman ibn Al-Maghbarah Al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Ali ibn Rabi`ah, on the authority of Asma` ibn Al-Hakam Al-Fazari, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: Whenever I heard a hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God would benefit me with whatever He willed from it. And if someone else tells me about it, I make him swear, and if he swears to me, I believe him. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, told me - and Abu Bakr spoke the truth - that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There is no man who commits a sin, then performs ablution and does it well - Misa’ar said - then prays - Sufyan said - then prays two rak’ahs, and seeks forgiveness from God Almighty, except that He forgives him.” And thus it was narrated by Ali ibn al-Madini, al-Humaidi, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, the people of the Sunan, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, al-Bazzar, and al-Daraqutni through various chains of transmission on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Mughira with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is a good hadith, and we have mentioned its chains of transmission, and the discussion of it is complete in Musnad Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him. In short, it is a good hadith, and it is narrated by the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, on the authority of the Prophet’s successor, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with them both. What bears witness to the authenticity of this hadith is what Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is none among you who performs ablution and completes it, then says: I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, without partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, except that the eight gates of Paradise will be opened for him, and he may enter through whichever one he wishes.” And in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, that he performed ablution for them as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, then said: “I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then prays two rak’ahs in which he does not think, his previous sins will be forgiven.” This hadith has been proven from the narration of the four Imams, the Rightly-Guided Caliphs, on the authority of the Master of the First and the Last, and the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds, as indicated by the clear Book, that seeking forgiveness for sins benefits sinners. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Ja’far ibn Sulayman informed us on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: It has been reported to me that when this verse was revealed, And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins, the verse, Satan wept. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Mahraz bin Awn told us, Uthman bin Matar told us, Abdul Ghafoor told us, on the authority of Abu Nasirah, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He said, ‘Upon you is saying ‘There is no god but God’ and seeking forgiveness, so do a lot of them, for Satan said, ‘I have destroyed people with sins and they have destroyed me with ‘There is no god but God’ and seeking forgiveness. So when I saw that, I have destroyed them with desires, and they think that they are guided.’” Uthman bin Matar and his sheikh are weak. Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Amr and Abu Al-Haitham Al-Atwari on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Satan said: O Lord, by Your glory, I will continue to mislead Your servants as long as their souls are in their bodies. God Almighty said: By My glory and majesty, I will continue to forgive them as long as they seek My forgiveness.” Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Umar ibn Abi Khalifa told us, I heard Abu Badr narrating on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: “A man came and said: O Messenger of God, I have committed a sin. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you sin, seek forgiveness from your Lord. He said: I seek forgiveness, then I sin again. He said: If you sin again, seek forgiveness from your Lord. He said it the fourth time, seek forgiveness from your Lord, until Satan is the one who regrets.” This is a strange hadith from this source. And the Almighty’s saying: And who forgives sins except God? means that no one forgives them except Him, as Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Mus’ab told us, Salam ibn Maskeen and al-Mubarak told us on the authority of al-Hasan on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Sari’ that a prisoner was brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: O God, I repent to You and I do not repent to Muhammad. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The truth has been made known to its people. And His saying: And they did not persist in what they did while they knew means that they repented from their sins and returned to God soon, and they did not continue in the sin and persist in it without giving it up. And if the sin was repeated from them, they would repent from it, as al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Ishaq ibn Abi Isra’il and others told us, they said: Abu Yahya Abd al-Hamid al-Hammani told us on the authority of Uthman ibn Waqid, on the authority of Abu Nasirah, on the authority of a freed slave of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He who seeks forgiveness will not persist, even if he returns seventy times a day.” And Abu Dawud narrated it. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Bazzar in his Musnad from the hadith of Uthman bin Waqid - and Yahya bin Ma'een authenticated him with it - and his Sheikh Abu Nasirah Al-Wasiti, whose name is Muslim bin Ubaid, who was authenticated by Imam Ahmad and Ibn Hibban. Ali bin Al-Madini and Al-Tirmidhi said: The chain of transmission of this hadith is not that good. It appears that it is due to the ignorance of the client of Abu Bakr, but the ignorance of someone like him does not harm because he is a great follower, and it is sufficient for him to attribute it to Abu Bakr, so it is a good hadith, and God knows best. And his statement, and they know, Mujahid and Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair said, and they know, that whoever repents, God will accept his repentance. This is like the statement of God, the Most High, Do they not know that God accepts repentance from His servants? and His statement, And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful. And there are many similar examples to this. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Jarir told us, Habban - he is Ibn Zaid Al-Sharabi - told us, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “that he said while he was on the pulpit: ‘Be merciful and you will be shown mercy, and forgive and you will be forgiven. Woe to those who defy speech, woe to those who persist in what they have done while they know.’” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. Then God the Almighty said after describing them with what He described them with: Their reward is forgiveness from their Lord meaning their reward for these attributes is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow meaning of various types of drinks abiding therein meaning abiding therein and excellent is the reward of the workers God the Almighty praises Paradise.
3:137: The Almighty says, addressing His believing servants who were afflicted on the day of Uhud and seventy of them were killed, There have already been precedents before you, meaning something similar to this happened to the nations who were followers of the prophets before you, then the end was theirs, and the rest is upon the disbelievers. For this reason, the Almighty said, So travel through the land and see what was the end of those who denied. Then the Almighty said, This is an exposition for the people, meaning the Qur’an explains matters clearly and how the nations of old dealt with their enemies. And guidance and instruction, meaning the Qur’an contains report of what came before you. Guidance is for your hearts, and admonition for the righteous, meaning a deterrent from forbidden things and sins. Then the Almighty said, comforting the believers: And do not weaken meaning do not become weak because of what happened, and do not grieve, and you will be superior if you are believers meaning the outcome and victory are for you, O believers. If a wound has touched you, a wound similar to it has touched the [opposing] people meaning if you have been wounded and a group of you have been killed, your enemies have been afflicted with similar killing and wounds. And those days We alternate among the people meaning We give the enemies victory over you sometimes, and if the outcome is yours, because of the wisdom in that, and for this reason the Almighty said: And that God may test those who have believed Ibn Abbas said: In such a case, so that we may see who will be patient in confronting the enemies. And that He may take from among you martyrs meaning they will be killed in His cause and sacrifice their lives in His pleasure. “And God does not love the wrongdoers. And that God may purify those who have believed” meaning He may forgive them their sins if they have sins. Otherwise, He may raise them in their degrees according to what has befallen them. And His statement, And He will destroy the disbelievers, meaning that if they are victorious, they will transgress and act insolently, and that will be the cause of their destruction, ruin, annihilation, and annihilation. Then the Almighty said, Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while God has not yet made evident those among you who strive and made evident the steadfast? That is, do you think that you will enter Paradise without being tested by fighting and hardships, as the Almighty said in Surat Al-Baqarah, Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [trials] have not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you - they were afflicted with poverty and hardship and were shaken? The verse. And the Almighty said, “Alif, Lam, Meem. Do people think that they will be left to say, “We believe” and they will not be tested?” The verse, and for this reason He said here, Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while God has not yet made evident those among you who strive and made evident the steadfast? That is, you will not be granted entry into Paradise until you are tested and God sees among you those who strive in His cause and those who are steadfast in resisting the enemies. And His statement, And you were wishing for death before you met it, but you have seen it while you were looking on, meaning, you, O believers, before this day, were wishing to meet the enemy, burning with desire to confront them and desire to fight them and be patient with them. Now what you wished for and sought has come to you, so fight and be patient. It has been proven in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not wish to meet the enemy, and ask God for well-being. And when you meet them, be patient and know that Paradise is under the shade of swords.” For this reason, God the Almighty said, And you have seen it, meaning you witnessed death at the time of the flashing of swords, the sharpness of spears, the clashing of spears, and the rows of men fighting. Theologians express this by imagination, which is seeing something that is not tangible, like something tangible, just as a sheep imagines the friendship of a ram and the enmity of a wolf.

Then the Almighty said, Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while God has not yet made evident those among you who strive and made evident the steadfast? That is, do you think that you will enter Paradise without being tested by fighting and hardships, as the Almighty said in Surat Al-Baqarah, Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [trials] have not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you - they were afflicted with poverty and hardship and were shaken? The verse. And the Almighty said, “Alif, Lam, Meem. Do people think that they will be left to say, “We believe” and they will not be tested?” The verse, and for this reason He said here, Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while God has not yet made evident those among you who strive and made evident the steadfast? That is, you will not be granted entry into Paradise until you are tested and God sees among you those who strive in His cause and those who are steadfast in resisting the enemies. And His statement, And you were wishing for death before you met it, but you have seen it while you were looking on, meaning, you, O believers, before this day, were wishing to meet the enemy, burning with desire to confront them and desire to fight them and be patient with them. Now what you wished for and sought has come to you, so fight and be patient. It has been proven in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not wish to meet the enemy, and ask God for well-being. And when you meet them, be patient and know that Paradise is under the shade of swords.” For this reason, God the Almighty said, And you have seen it, meaning you witnessed death at the time of the flashing of swords, the sharpness of spears, the clashing of spears, and the rows of men fighting. Theologians express this by imagination, which is seeing something that is not tangible, like something tangible, just as a sheep imagines the friendship of a ram and the enmity of a wolf.
3:144: When the Muslims were defeated on the day of Uhud and those who were killed were killed, Satan called out: Behold, Muhammad has been killed. Ibn Qami'ah returned to the polytheists and said to them: You have killed Muhammad, but he had struck the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and wounded him in the head. This fell into the hearts of many people and they believed that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been killed, and they permitted that to happen to him, as God has told about many of the prophets, peace be upon them. So weakness and frailty occurred and he was delayed from fighting. In that regard, God Almighty revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace: And Muhammad is no more than a Messenger; before him have been Messengers. That is, he has an example in the message and in the permissibility of killing him. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of his father: A man from the Muhajireen passed by a man from the Ansar while he was wallowing in his blood and said to him: O so-and-so, do you know that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, has been killed? The Ansari said: If Muhammad has been killed, then he has conveyed his message, so fight for your religion. Then the verse was revealed: And Muhammad is no more than a Messenger; before him have been Messengers. The Messengers” narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi in Dalil Al-Nubuwwah. Then God the Almighty said, denouncing those who have become weak, Then if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? That is, will you go back in reverse. And whoever turns back on his heels will never harm God at all, and God will reward the grateful. That is, those who obeyed Him and fought for His religion, and followed His Messenger, alive and dead. Likewise, it is proven in the Sahihs, Musnads, Sunans, and other books of Islam through multiple chains of transmission that provide certainty. I mentioned that in the Musnads of the two Shaykhs Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them, that As-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, recited this verse when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died. Al-Bukhari said: Yahya bin Bakir told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Aqeel, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, Abu Salamah told me that Aisha, may God be pleased with her, told him that Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, came on a horse from his residence in As-Sunh until he dismounted and entered the mosque. He did not speak to the people until he entered upon Aisha. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed tayammum while he was covered with a garment of Habra. He uncovered his face, then leaned over him, kissed him and wept. Then he said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you. By God, God will not cause you to die twice. As for the death that was decreed for you, you have brought it forward. Al-Zuhri said: Abu Salamah told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that Abu Bakr went out and Umar was speaking to the people, so he said: Sit down, Umar. Umar refused to sit down, so the people turned to him and left Umar. Abu Bakr said: As for what comes after, whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died, and whoever worshipped God, God is alive and will not die. God the Almighty said: “Muhammad is no more than a messenger; many messengers have passed away before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will never harm God at all. And God will reward the grateful.” He said: By God, it was as if the people did not know that God had revealed this verse until Abu Bakr recited it to them, and all the people received it from him, and no human being heard it except that he recited it. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab informed me that Umar said: By God, it was only when I heard Abu Bakr reciting it that I became paralyzed until my legs could not support me, and I fell to the ground. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz told us, Amr ibn Hammad ibn Talhah al-Qannad told us, Asbat ibn Nasr told us, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that Ali used to say during the lifetime of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? By God, we will not turn back on our heels after God has guided us. By God, if he dies or is killed, I will fight for what he fought for until I die. By God, I am his brother, his guardian, his cousin, and his heir. So who is more deserving of him than me? And the Almighty said: And no soul can die except by God’s permission, at a predetermined time. That is, no one dies except by God’s decree and until he completes the period that God has set for him. That is why He said at a predetermined time, like His saying: And no one lives long, nor does his lifespan decrease except in a predetermined time. And like His saying: It is He who created you from clay, then decreed a term, and a specified term is with Him. This verse contains encouragement for cowards and an exhortation for them to fight, because advancing or retreating does not decrease lifespan or increase it, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Abbas bin Yazid Al-Abdi told us: I heard Abu Mu’awiyah from Al-A’mash from Habib bin Sahban, who said: A man from the Muslims, and he was Hajar bin Adi, said: What prevents you from crossing to these enemy, this drop of semen - meaning the Tigris - And no soul can die except by God’s permission, at a predetermined time. Then he charged his horse into the Tigris, and when he charged, he charged the people, and when the enemy saw them, they said: A register, so they fled. And His statement, And whoever desires the reward of this world, We give him thereof; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We give him thereof, meaning whoever does his work for this world only, will receive from it what God has decreed for him, and he will not have a share in the Hereafter. And whoever intends with his work the Hereafter, God will give him thereof along with what He has allotted for him in this world, as God Almighty said, “Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase for him his harvest. And whoever desires the harvest of this world, We give him thereof, and there is not for him in the Hereafter any share.” And God Almighty said, “Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him therein what We will for whomever We intend. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will burn, blamed and banished. But whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the necessary effort while he is a believer - it is those whose effort is ever appreciated.” That is why He said here, And We will reward the grateful, meaning We will give them from Our grace and mercy in this world and the Hereafter according to their gratitude and work. Then God Almighty said, comforting the believers for what had happened to their souls on the Day of Uhud, And how many a prophet fought with whom many pious men fought. It was said that its meaning is how many a prophet was killed and many were killed with him. Many of his companions are Rabbi. This statement is the choice of Ibn Jarir, who said: As for those who read many rabbis fought with him, they said: What is meant by killing is the Prophet and some of the rabbis with him, not all of them, and he only denied weakness and frailty from those who remained from the rabbis who were not killed. He said: And whoever read fought chose that, because he said: If they had been killed, there would have been no known meaning for God’s statement they did not weaken because it is impossible for them to be described as not weakening or becoming weak after they were killed. Then he chose the reading of whoever read many rabbis fought with him, because God rebuked in these verses and the ones before them those who fled on the day of Uhud and abandoned the fighting when they heard the caller shouting that Muhammad had been killed, so God rebuked them for fleeing and abandoning the fighting, and said to them, If he dies or is killed, O believers, will you turn back from your religion and turn back on your heels? It was said: How many prophets were killed before him from his companions, many rabbis? And the words of Ibn Ishaq in the biography require another statement, for he said: And how many prophets were killed while with him were Rabbiyun, meaning groups, so they did not weaken after their Prophet, nor did they weaken against their enemy, nor did they submit to what befell them in the struggle for the sake of God and their religion, and that is patience. And God loves the patient. So He made His statement, With him are many Rabbiyun a state. Al-Suhayli supported this statement and exaggerated it, and he has a direction for His statement, So they did not weaken when what befell them the verse, and this is what Al-Umawi narrated in his Maghazi from the book of Muhammad bin Ibrahim and no one else narrated it, and some of them read, Many Rabbiyun fought with him. Sufyan Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, Many Rabbiyun meaning thousands, and Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi, Al-Rabi’, and Ata Al-Khurasani said: Rabbiyun are large groups, and Abd Al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Al-Hasan, Many Rabbiyun meaning many scholars, and from him also: Scholars of patience, righteous and pious. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of some of the grammarians of Basra that the Rabbiyyin are those who worship the Almighty Lord. He said: Some of them responded to him and said: If that were the case, it would have been said: Rabbiyyin with the opening of the ra’. Ibn Zayd said: The Rabbiyyin are the followers and the subjects, and the Rabbanis are the governors. They did not lose heart for what befell them in the cause of God, nor did they weaken, nor did they humble themselves. Qatada and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said, They did not weaken by the killing of their Prophet, nor did they humble themselves meaning: they did not turn away from their insight or their religion and fight for what God’s Prophet fought for until they joined God. Ibn Abbas said, nor did they humble themselves they were humble. As-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: They were not humbled before their enemy. Muhammad ibn Ishaq, As-Suddi and Qatadah said: That is, that did not befall them when their Prophet was killed. “And God loves the patient. Their only saying was that they said, ‘Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our transgression in our conduct and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people.’” That is, they had no other choice but that. So God gave them the reward of this world, that is, victory, triumph and a good end, and the best reward of the Hereafter, that is, He combined that for them with this. And God loves the doers of good.

Then he chose the reading of whoever read many rabbis fought with him, because God rebuked in these verses and the ones before them those who fled on the day of Uhud and abandoned the fighting when they heard the caller shouting that Muhammad had been killed, so God rebuked them for fleeing and abandoning the fighting, and said to them, If he dies or is killed, O believers, will you turn back from your religion and turn back on your heels? It was said: How many prophets were killed before him from his companions, many rabbis? And the words of Ibn Ishaq in the biography require another statement, for he said: And how many prophets were killed while with him were Rabbiyun, meaning groups, so they did not weaken after their Prophet, nor did they weaken against their enemy, nor did they submit to what befell them in the struggle for the sake of God and their religion, and that is patience. And God loves the patient. So He made His statement, With him are many Rabbiyun a state. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of some of the grammarians of Basra that the Rabbiyyin are those who worship the Almighty Lord. He said: Some of them responded to him and said: If that were the case, it would have been said: Rabbiyyin with the opening of the ra’. Ibn Zayd said: The Rabbiyyin are the followers and the subjects, and the Rabbanis are the governors. They did not lose heart for what befell them in the cause of God, nor did they weaken, nor did they humble themselves. Qatada and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said, They did not weaken by the killing of their Prophet, nor did they humble themselves meaning: they did not turn away from their insight or their religion and fight for what God’s Prophet fought for until they joined God. Ibn Abbas said, nor did they humble themselves they were humble. As-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: They were not humbled before their enemy. Muhammad ibn Ishaq, As-Suddi and Qatadah said: That is, that did not befall them when their Prophet was killed. “And God loves the patient. Their only saying was that they said, ‘Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our transgression in our conduct and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people.’” That is, they had no other choice but that. So God gave them the reward of this world, that is, victory, triumph and a good end, and the best reward of the Hereafter, that is, He combined that for them with this. And God loves the doers of good.
3:147: When the Muslims were defeated on the day of Uhud and those who were killed were killed, Satan called out: Behold, Muhammad has been killed. Ibn Qami'ah returned to the polytheists and said to them: You have killed Muhammad, but he had struck the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and wounded him in the head. This fell into the hearts of many people and they believed that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been killed, and they permitted that to happen to him, as God has told about many of the prophets, peace be upon them. So weakness and frailty occurred and he was delayed from fighting. In that regard, God Almighty revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace: And Muhammad is no more than a Messenger; before him have been Messengers. That is, he has an example in the message and in the permissibility of killing him. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of his father: A man from the Muhajireen passed by a man from the Ansar while he was wallowing in his blood and said to him: O so-and-so, do you know that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, has been killed? The Ansari said: If Muhammad has been killed, then he has conveyed his message, so fight for your religion. Then the verse was revealed: And Muhammad is no more than a Messenger; before him have been Messengers. The Messengers” narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi in Dalil Al-Nubuwwah. Then God the Almighty said, denouncing those who have become weak, Then if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? That is, will you go back in reverse. And whoever turns back on his heels will never harm God at all, and God will reward the grateful. That is, those who obeyed Him and fought for His religion, and followed His Messenger, alive and dead. Likewise, it is proven in the Sahihs, Musnads, Sunans, and other books of Islam through multiple chains of transmission that provide certainty. I mentioned that in the Musnads of the two Shaykhs Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them, that As-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, recited this verse when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died. Al-Bukhari said: Yahya bin Bakir told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Aqeel, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, Abu Salamah told me that Aisha, may God be pleased with her, told him that Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, came on a horse from his residence in As-Sunh until he dismounted and entered the mosque. He did not speak to the people until he entered upon Aisha. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed tayammum while he was covered with a garment of Habra. He uncovered his face, then leaned over him, kissed him and wept. Then he said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you. By God, God will not cause you to die twice. As for the death that was decreed for you, you have brought it forward. Al-Zuhri said: Abu Salamah told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that Abu Bakr went out and Umar was speaking to the people, so he said: Sit down, Umar. Umar refused to sit down, so the people turned to him and left Umar. Abu Bakr said: As for what comes after, whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died, and whoever worshipped God, God is alive and will not die. God the Almighty said: “Muhammad is no more than a messenger; many messengers have passed away before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will never harm God at all. And God will reward the grateful.” He said: By God, it was as if the people did not know that God had revealed this verse until Abu Bakr recited it to them, and all the people received it from him, and no human being heard it except that he recited it. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab informed me that Umar said: By God, it was only when I heard Abu Bakr reciting it that I became paralyzed until my legs could not support me, and I fell to the ground. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz told us, Amr ibn Hammad ibn Talhah al-Qannad told us, Asbat ibn Nasr told us, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that Ali used to say during the lifetime of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? By God, we will not turn back on our heels after God has guided us. By God, if he dies or is killed, I will fight for what he fought for until I die. By God, I am his brother, his guardian, his cousin, and his heir. So who is more deserving of him than me? And the Almighty said: And no soul can die except by God’s permission, at a predetermined time. That is, no one dies except by God’s decree and until he completes the period that God has set for him. That is why He said at a predetermined time, like His saying: And no one lives long, nor does his lifespan decrease except in a predetermined time. And like His saying: It is He who created you from clay, then decreed a term, and a specified term is with Him. This verse contains encouragement for cowards and an exhortation for them to fight, because advancing or retreating does not decrease lifespan or increase it, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Abbas bin Yazid Al-Abdi told us: I heard Abu Mu’awiyah from Al-A’mash from Habib bin Sahban, who said: A man from the Muslims, and he was Hajar bin Adi, said: What prevents you from crossing to these enemy, this drop of semen - meaning the Tigris - And no soul can die except by God’s permission, at a predetermined time. Then he charged his horse into the Tigris, and when he charged, he charged the people, and when the enemy saw them, they said: A register, so they fled. And His statement, And whoever desires the reward of this world, We give him thereof; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We give him thereof, meaning whoever does his work for this world only, will receive from it what God has decreed for him, and he will not have a share in the Hereafter. And whoever intends with his work the Hereafter, God will give him thereof along with what He has allotted for him in this world, as God Almighty said, “Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase for him his harvest. And whoever desires the harvest of this world, We give him thereof, and there is not for him in the Hereafter any share.” And God Almighty said, “Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him therein what We will for whomever We intend. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will burn, blamed and banished. But whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the necessary effort while he is a believer - it is those whose effort is ever appreciated.” That is why He said here, And We will reward the grateful, meaning We will give them from Our grace and mercy in this world and the Hereafter according to their gratitude and work. 3:149: The Almighty warns His believing servants against obeying the disbelievers and hypocrites, for obeying them brings ruin in this world and the Hereafter. That is why the Almighty said: If you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will become losers. Then He commanded them to obey Him, befriend Him, seek His help, and put their trust in Him. The Almighty said: Rather, God is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers. Then He gave them good report that He will cast fear of them and humiliation into the hearts of their enemies because of their disbelief and polytheism, along with what He has stored up for them in the Hereafter of torment and punishment. He said: "We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve because they have associated with God that for which He has not sent down any authority. Their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers." It has been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah that the Messenger of God said: "I have been given five things that were not given to any of the prophets before me: I have been aided by terror for a distance of a month's journey, the earth has been made a place of prostration and purification for me, and spoils of war have been made lawful for me." And I was given intercession, and the Prophet was sent to his people in particular, and I was sent to all people.” Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Sayyar, on the authority of Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My Lord has favored me over the prophets - or he said over the nations - in four things: He said: I was sent to all people, and the entire earth was made for me and for my nation a place of prostration and purification, so wherever a man of my nation finds prayer, his place of prostration and purification is with him, and I was aided by terror for a month’s journey, which he casts into the hearts of my enemies, and spoils of war were made lawful for me.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Sayyar al-Qurashi al-Umawi, their client from Damascus, who lived in Basra, on the authority of Abu Umamah Sadi bin Ajlan, may God be pleased with him, with it, and he said: It is good and authentic. Saeed bin Mansour said: Ibn Wahb informed us, Amr bin al-Harith informed me that Abu Yunus told him, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was aided by terror against the enemy. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Wahb. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad told us, Isra’il told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Burdah, on the authority of his father Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was given five things: I was sent to the red and the black, the earth was made pure and a place of prostration for me, spoils were made lawful for me and were not made lawful for those before me, I was aided by terror for a month, and I was given intercession, and there is no prophet who did not ask for his intercession. I hid my intercession and then made it for whoever died not associating anything with God.” Ahmad alone narrated it. Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God the Almighty: We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, he said: God cast terror into the heart of Abu Sufyan, so he returned to Mecca. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Abu Sufyan has indeed taken a part of you, and he has returned and God cast terror into his heart. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. And the words of God the Almighty: And God had fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission, Ibn Abbas said: God promised them victory. This verse may be used as evidence for one of the two previous sayings in the Almighty’s statement: “When you said to the believers, ‘Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?’ Yes, if you are patient and fear God and they come upon you at once, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels with marks.’” That was on the day of Uhud, because their enemy was three thousand fighters, so when they confronted them, victory and triumph were achieved early in the day for Islam. When what happened of the disobedience of the archers and the failure of some of the fighters, the promise that was conditional on steadfastness and obedience was delayed. For this reason, He said, And God has fulfilled His promise to you, meaning early in the day, when you were killing them, meaning killing them, by His permission, meaning by His giving you power over them, until you failed. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: Failure is cowardice. And you disputed about the matter and disobeyed, as happened to the archers, after He had shown you that which you love, which was victory over them.
