Among you are those who desire this world, and they are those who desired the spoils when they saw Defeat And among you is he who desires the Hereafter, then He turned you away from them to test you then He made them prevail over you to test you and examine you And He has certainly pardoned you that is, He forgave you for that action, and that, and God knows best, is due to the large number of the enemy and their numbers and the small number of the Muslims and their numbers. Ibn Jurayj said: His statement And He has certainly pardoned you he said: He did not eradicate you, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said the same: Ibn Jarir narrated them both And God is full of bounty to the believers and Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ubaydullah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: God has not given victory in a place like He gave victory on the day of Uhud, he said: So we denied that, and Ibn Abbas said: Between me and those who denied that is the Book of God, that God says on the day of Uhud And God had fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them with His permission Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan say: killing “until you were weak and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love. Among you are those who desire this world and among you are those who desire the Hereafter” the verse, and what he meant was And with these archers, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stationed them in a place and then said: Protect our backs, for if you see us being killed, do not help us, and if you see us having taken spoils, do not share with us. So when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took spoils and allowed the camp of the polytheists to be conquered, the archers all rushed into the camp to plunder, and the ranks of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met like this - and he interlocked his hands - and they took refuge, and when the archers left that position they were in, the horses entered from that place upon the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they struck each other, and they became confused and many Muslims were killed, and victory was for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions at the beginning of the day until seven or nine of the standard-bearers of the polytheists were killed, and the Muslims moved around towards the mountain, and they did not reach where the people say the cave is, but they were under the mortar, and the devil cried out: Muhammad has been killed, and they did not doubt that it was true, and we did not stop like that, we did not doubt that it was true until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appeared between the two Sa’dains, and we knew him. He said: We were so happy that it was as if we had not been afflicted with what afflicted us. He said: He climbed towards us and he was saying: The wrath of God has intensified against a people who bloodied the face of the Messenger of God. He said again: O God, they cannot prevail over us. Until he reached us, he remained for an hour, and then Abu Sufyan shouted at the bottom of the mountain: Let Hubal be exalted - twice, meaning his god - Where is the son of Abu Kabsha? Where is the son of Abu Quhafa? Where is the son of Ibn al-Khattab? Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of God, should I not answer him? He said: Yes. When he said: Let Hubal be exalted, Umar said: God is Most High and Most Majestic. Abu Sufyan said: Her eye has been comforted. So he turned away from her or did something. He said: Where is the son of Abu Kabsha? Where is the son of Abu Quhafa? Where is the son of Ibn al-Khattab? Umar said: “This is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is Abu Bakr, and here I am, Umar.” Abu Sufyan said: “A day is like the day of Badr. The days are in cycles, and war is a contest.” He said: Umar said: Our dead are not equal in Paradise. And your dead are in the Fire. He said: You claim that, so we have failed and lost. Abu Sufyan said: You will find mutilation among your dead, and that was not according to the opinion of our leaders. He said: Then the fanaticism of the Age of Ignorance overtook him, so he said: If that is the case, we would not hate it. This is a strange hadith and a strange context. It is from the mursals of Ibn Abbas, for no one witnessed it, nor his father. Al-Hakim included it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Abu al-Nadr al-Faqih, on the authority of Uthman ibn Saeed, on the authority of Salman ibn Dawud ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, and this is how Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Dalil al-Nubuwwah from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Hashemi on his authority. And some of it has supporting evidence in the Sahihs and elsewhere. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ata ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The women were behind the Muslims on the day of Uhud, finishing off the wounded polytheists. If I had sworn that day, I would have hoped to be fulfilled that none of us wanted the world, until God revealed: “Some of you desire this world and some of you desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you.” When the companions of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) disobeyed what they were commanded to do, the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) singled out nine men: seven from the Ansar and two men from Quraysh, and he was the tenth of them (may God bless him and grant him peace). When they overwhelmed him, he said: May God have mercy on the man who turned them away from us. Then a man from the Ansar stood up and fought for an hour until he was killed. When they overwhelmed him again, he said: May God have mercy on the man who turned them away from us. He continued saying that until the seven were killed. Then the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said to his two companions: We have not been fair to our companions. Abu Sufyan came and said: Hubal is superior. The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: “Say: God is higher and more majestic.” They said: God is higher and more majestic. Abu Sufyan said: We have Al-Uzza and you have no Uzza. The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: “Say: God is our protector and the disbelievers have no protector.” Abu Sufyan said: “A day for the day of Badr. A day against us and a day for us, a day for women and a day for men.” The eagle, Hanzala for Hanzala, so-and-so for so-and-so, and so-and-so for so-and-so. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are not equal: As for our dead, they are alive and provided for, but as for your dead, they are being tortured in the Fire. Abu Sufyan said: There was indeed an example among the people, and if he was cursed, it was not from among us. I did not command or forbid, nor did I like or dislike, nor did it upset me or please me. He said: So they looked and saw that Hamza’s belly had been ripped open, and Hind took his liver and chewed it but was unable to eat it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Did you eat something? They said: No. He said: God would not put anything of Hamza in the Fire. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, placed Hamza and prayed over him, and a man from the Ansar was brought and placed beside him and prayed over him. The Ansar lifted him up and left Hamza until another was brought and placed beside Hamza and prayed over him, then lifted him up and left Hamza, until he prayed over him seventy times that day. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Also. Al-Bukhari said: Ubaydullah bin Musa narrated to us on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa, who said: We encountered the polytheists that day and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, seated an army of archers and put Abdullah bin Jubair in charge of them, and said: “Do not move. If you see us prevailing over them, do not move, and if you see them prevailing over us, do not help us.” So when we met them, they fled until I saw the women running hard on the mountain, raising their legs and showing their anklets, and they began to say: The spoils, the spoils. So Abdullah bin Jubair said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered me not to move, but they refused. When they refused, they turned their faces away and seventy were killed. Abu Sufyan looked out and said: “Is Muhammad among the people?” He said: Do not answer him. He said: Is Ibn Abi Quhafah among the people? He said: Do not answer him. He said: Is Ibn Al-Khattab among the people? He said: These people have been killed, and if they were alive, they would have answered. So Umar could not control himself. He said to him: You have lied, O enemy of God, God has left for you that which grieves you. Abu Sufyan said: Hubal is exalted. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Answer him. They said: What should we say? He said: Say: God is higher and more exalted. Abu Sufyan said: We have Al-Uzza, and you have no Uzza. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Answer him. They said: What should we say? He said: Say: God is our Master, and you have no Master. Abu Sufyan said: A day for the day of Badr, and war is a contest, and you will find a mutilation that I did not command and it did not upset me. Al-Bukhari was the only one to narrate it from this source, then he narrated it from Amr bin Khalid from Zuhair bin Muawiyah, from Abu Ishaq, from Al-Bara’ in a similar manner, and he will come with something simpler than this. Al-Bukhari also said: Ubaidullah bin Saeed told us, Abu Usamah told us from Hisham bin Urwah, from his father, from Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: When the day of Uhud came, the polytheists were defeated, and Satan cried out: O servants of God, I am the last of you, so the first of them returned. So she and the last of them fought, and Hudhayfah saw his father Al-Yaman and said: O servants of God, my father is my father. He said: She said: By God, they did not hold back until they killed him, so Hudhayfah said: May God forgive you. Urwah said: By God, there was still good in Hudhayfah until he met God Almighty. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yahya ibn Ibad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr told me on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather that al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam said: By God, I saw myself looking at Hind’s servants and companions, their faces rolled up and they were running away, neither much nor little was enough to take them. The archers turned towards the army when the people fled from it, wanting to loot, and our backs were left for the horses, so they came to us from behind us, and a voice cried out: Muhammad has been killed. So we retreated and the people retreated upon us after we had captured the standard-bearers, until no one from the people came near it. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The standard of the polytheists remained fallen until Umrah bint Alqamah al-Harithiya took it and gave it to the Quraysh, so they fought with it. Al-Suddi said, on the authority of Abd Khair, who said: Abdullah ibn Masoud said: I did not think that any of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted the worldly life until what was revealed about us on the day of Uhud was revealed: Some of you want the world, and some of you want the Hereafter. It has been narrated from other sources on the authority of Ibn Masoud. And it was also narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and Abu Talha, narrated by Ibn Mardawayh in his interpretation, and the Almighty’s saying: Then He turned you away from them to test you. Ibn Ishaq said: Al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Rafi’, one of the sons of Adi ibn al-Najjar, told me: Anas ibn al-Nadr, the uncle of Anas ibn Malik, went to Umar ibn al-Khattab and Talha ibn Ubaydullah with some men from the Muhajireen and Ansar who had thrown down what was in their hands, so he said: What is leaving you? They said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has been killed. He said: What will you do with life after him? Rise and die as he died. Then he faced the people and fought until he was killed, may God be pleased with him. Al-Bukhari said: Hassan ibn Hassan told us, Muhammad ibn Talha told us, Hamid told us on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that his uncle, meaning Anas ibn al-Nadr, was absent from Badr and said: I was absent from the first battle of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. If God makes me witness with the Messenger of God, God will see what I find. So he met the day of Uhud and defeated the people, so he said: O God, I apologize to you for what… These people - meaning the Muslims - made it and I declare to you that I am innocent of what the polytheists brought. So he advanced with his sword and met Sa`d ibn Mu`adh and said: Where, Sa`d? I smell the fragrance of Paradise without anyone. So he went and was killed, and he was not recognized until his sister recognized him by his fingertip with a mole. He had eighty-odd stab wounds, blows and arrow wounds. This is the wording of al-Bukhari. Muslim included it in a hadith narrated by Thabit from Anas in a similar manner. Al-Bukhari also said: Abdun narrated to us, Abu Hamza narrated to us from Uthman ibn Muhab, who said: A man came to the House of Hajj and saw some people sitting. He said: Who are these people sitting? They said: These are Quraysh. He said: Who is the old man? They said: Ibn `Umar. So he came to him and said: I am going to ask you about something, so tell me. He said: Ask. He said: I ask you by the sanctity of this House, do you know that Uthman ibn `Affan fled on the day of Uhud? He said: Yes. He said: Do you know that he was absent from Badr and did not witness it? He said: Yes. He said: Do you know that he did not attend the Pledge of Ridwan and did not… He said: Yes. So he said: Allahu Akbar. Ibn Umar said: Come, so I may tell you and explain to you what you asked me about. As for his escape on the day of Uhud, I bear witness that God has pardoned him. As for his absence from Badr, he was married to the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she was sick. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: You will have the reward and share of a man who witnessed Badr. As for his absence from the Pledge of Ridwan, if there had been anyone more honorable in the valley of Mecca than Uthman, he would have sent him in his place. So he sent Uthman, and the Pledge of Ridwan took place after Uthman had gone to Mecca. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said with his right hand: This is the hand of Uthman, and he struck his hand with it and said: “This is the hand of Uthman. Go with it now.” Then Al-Bukhari narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Awanah, on the authority of Uthman ibn Abdullah ibn Muhabb. God the Almighty said: When you were ascending and not looking back at anyone meaning He turned you away from them while you were ascending, that is, in the mountain, fleeing from your enemies. Al-Hasan and Qatadah read When you were ascending meaning in the mountain, and not looking back at anyone meaning you were not looking back at anyone out of astonishment, fear and terror, and the Messenger is calling you from behind you meaning you had left him behind you calling you to stop fleeing from the enemies, and to return, come back and attack. Al-Suddi said: When the polytheists attacked the Muslims at Uhud and defeated them, some of them entered the city, and some of them went to the mountain on the rock and stood on it. So the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, began calling the people to the servants of God, to the servants of God. God mentioned their ascension to the mountain, then He mentioned the Prophet’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, calling them, saying: When you were ascending and not looking back at anyone, and the Messenger is calling you from behind you. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, Al-Rabi’ and Ibn Zayd said the same. Abdullah bin Al-Zubayri said: He mentions the defeat of the Muslims on the day of Uhud in his poem while he was a polytheist and had not yet converted to Islam, in which he says at the beginning: O crow of separation, have you heard? Say, for you are only speaking of something that has already been done. Good and evil have a limit, and both have a face and a face. Until he said: I wish my elders at Badr had witnessed the Khazraj’s fear of the sound of the weapons. When Quba narrated its ponds and the killing spread to Abd al-Ashel Then they started dancing, like a camel dancing high up in the mountain. So we killed twice as many of their nobles and we adjusted the slope of Badr, so it was balanced. Al-Haffan: Small camels. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had singled out twelve men from among his companions, as Imam Ahmad said: Hasan bin Musa told us, Zuhair told us, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-Bara bin Azib, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed Abdullah bin Jubair over the archers on the day of Uhud - and they were fifty men. He said: And he put them in a position, and said: “If you see us being snatched by birds, do not move until I send for you. And if you see us prevail over the enemy and trample them, do not move until I send for you.” He said: So they defeated them. He said: By God, I saw the women rushing up the mountain, their anklets and their clothes lifted. He said: The companions of Abdullah, the spoils, O people of the spoils, your companions have appeared, so what are you waiting for? Abdullah bin Jubair said: Have you forgotten what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to you? They said: By God, we will go to the people and take a share of the spoils. So when they came to them, their faces were turned away and they came forward. Defeated, that is what the Messenger calls them in their last days, so there remained with the Messenger of God only twelve men, so they killed seventy of us, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions killed one hundred and forty of the polytheists on the day of Badr, seventy prisoners and seventy dead. Abu Sufyan said: Is Muhammad among the people, is Muhammad among the people? - three times - he said. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade them from answering him, then he said: Is Ibn Abi Quhafah among the people? Is Ibn Abi Quhafah among the people? Is Ibn Al-Khattab among the people? Is Ibn Al-Khattab among the people? Then he turned to his companions and said: As for these, they have been killed and you have been spared from them, so Umar could not control himself but said: You have lied, by God, O enemy of God, those whom you have counted are all alive, and there remains for you what will upset you, so he said: A day for a day Badr, and war is a contest. And you will find among the people a mutilation that I did not order, and it did not upset me. Then he began to recite a rajaz saying: Hubal, Hubal, exalt. Hubal, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Will you not answer him? They said: O Messenger of God, what should we say? He said: Say God is higher and more majestic. He said: We have Al-Uzza, and you have no Uzza. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Will you not answer him? They said: O Messenger of God, what should we say? He said: Say God is our Master, and you have no Master. Al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Zuhair bin Muawiyah in an abbreviated form, and he narrated it from the hadith of Israel from Abu Ishaq in a more detailed form than this as mentioned above, and God knows best. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dalil Al-Nubuwwah from the hadith of Ammarah bin Ghaziyah, from Abu Al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: “The people fled from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud, and eleven men from the Ansar remained with him, and Talhah bin Ubaidullah, while he was climbing the mountain. The polytheists met them, so he said: Is there no one for these? Talhah said: I will, O Messenger of God. He said: As you are, O Talhah. A man from the Ansar said: I will, O Messenger of God. So he fought on his behalf, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who remained with him climbed, then the Ansari was killed.” So they caught up with him, and he said: Is there no man for these people? Talhah said the same as he had said, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said the same as he had said, and a man from the Ansar said: So I am, O Messenger of God, so he fought on his behalf and his companions ascended, then he was killed and they caught up with him, and he kept saying the same as he had said before, and Talhah said: So I am, O Messenger of God, so he detained him and a man from the Ansar asked him for permission to fight, so he gave him permission, and he fought like those who had been before him, until no one remained with him except Talhah, so they attacked them, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Who is for these people? Talhah said: I am, so he fought like all those who had been before him, and his fingers were injured, so he said: Enough, and the Messenger of God said: If you had said the name of God and mentioned the name of God, the angels would have lifted you up with the people looking at you until you entered the atmosphere of the sky, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ascended to his companions while they were gathered. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Wakee’, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim, who said: I saw Talhah’s hand paralyzed, with which he protected the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he (peace be upon him) said: “And he (peace be upon him) said: ‘On the Day of Uhud,’ meaning the Day of Uhud, in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: ‘On some of the days in which the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) fought, there remained none with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) except Talhah ibn Ubayd God and Sa’d, from their hadith.’ And al-Hasan ibn Arfa said: ‘Marwan ibn Mu’awiyah told us, from Hashim ibn Hashim al-Zuhri, who said: ‘I heard Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab say: ‘I heard Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas say: “The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) handed me his quiver on the Day of Uhud and said: ‘Shoot, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you.’” And al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Marwan ibn Mu’awiyah, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ‘Saleh ibn Kaysan told me on the authority of some of the family of Sa’d, from Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, that he shot on the Day of Uhud without the Messenger of God (peace be upon him).’ Sa’d said: ‘I saw the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) handing me arrows and saying: ‘Shoot, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you.’ He even handed me an arrow that had no tip, so I shot with it.’” "It was established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Ibrahim bin Sa`d, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Sa`d bin Abi Waqqas, who said: “On the day of Uhud, I saw on the right of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and on his left, two men wearing white clothes fighting on his behalf with the fiercest fighting I had ever seen before or after that day, meaning Gabriel and Michael, peace be upon them.” Hammad bin Salamah said on the authority of Ali bin Zaid and Thabit on the authority of Anas bin Malik: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was singled out on the day of Uhud with seven of the Ansar and two of the Quraysh. When they overwhelmed him, he said: ‘Whoever repels them from us will have Paradise,’ or ‘and he is my companion in Paradise.’ So a man from the Ansar stepped forward and fought until he was killed. Then they overwhelmed him again, and he said: ‘Whoever repels them from us will have Paradise,’ so a man from the Ansar stepped forward and fought until he was killed. He continued like that until the seven were killed, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his two companions: ‘We have not been fair to our companions.’” Narrated by Muslim on the authority of Hudbah bin Khalid, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, with something similar. Abu al-Aswad said on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr said: Abi bin Khalaf, the brother of Banu Jumah, had sworn while he was in Mecca to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When his oath reached the Messenger of God, he said, Rather, I will kill him, God willing. Then, on the day of Uhud, Abi came wearing iron, masked, saying, I will not escape if Muhammad escapes. So he charged at the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, intending to kill him. But Mus`ab bin `Umair, the brother of Banu `Abd al-Dar, met him, protecting the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with his own life. So he killed Mus`ab bin `Umair. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw the collarbone of Abi bin Khalaf through a gap between the hem of his armor and the blade, and stabbed him in it with his spear. He fell to the ground from his horse, and no blood came out of his stab wound. His companions came to him and carried him while he was mooing like a bull. They said to him, ‘What makes you so upset? It is only a scratch. ’ So he mentioned to them the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Rather, I will kill Abi.” Then he said, By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if this had happened to me, the people of Dhu al-Majaz would have died. All together, he died in the Fire, So may the companions of the Blaze be destroyed. It was narrated by Musa bin Uqbah in his Maghazi, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, in a similar manner. Muhammad bin Ishaq mentioned that he said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, leaned on the ravine, Ubayy bin Khalaf caught up with him and he was saying: ‘I will not be saved if I am saved.’ The people said: ‘O Messenger of God, let one of us help him.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Leave him.’ When he approached, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took the spear from Al-Harith bin Al-Samma. Some of the people said, ‘What was mentioned to me?’ When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it from him, he shook it so hard that we scattered from him as hair flies from the back of a camel when it shakes. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, faced him and stabbed him in the neck with a stab that caused him to fall off his horse repeatedly.” Al-Waqidi mentioned on the authority of Yunus bin Bakir, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Asim bin Amr bin Qatada, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ka’b bin Malik. On the authority of his father, something like that. Al-Waqidi said: Ibn Umar used to say: Abi bin Khalaf died in Batn Rabigh. I was walking in Batn Rabigh after a nightfall when I saw a blazing fire. I woke up and saw a man coming out of it, pulling on a chain, provoking thirst in him. A man said: Do not give him a drink, for this is the one killed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is Abi bin Khalaf. It was confirmed in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘God’s wrath was intense against a people who did this to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace – and he was pointing to his front teeth – and God’s wrath was intense against a man killed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the way of God.’” Al-Bukhari also included it on the authority of Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “God’s wrath was intense against the one killed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with his own hand in the way of God, and God’s wrath was intense against a people who bloodied the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” “And upon him be peace” - Ibn Ishaq said: “The front tooth of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was broken, his cheek was wounded, and his lip was injured.” The one who injured him was Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas. Salih ibn Kaysan told me, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: “I have never been so keen on killing anyone as I was on killing Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas, if what I know is that he was of bad character and hated by his people. And the statement of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “God’s wrath is intense against whoever bleeds the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace” was sufficient for me. And `Abd al-Razzaq said: Mu`mar informed us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of `Uthman al-Jazari, on the authority of Muqsim, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “supplicated against Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas on the day of Uhud when his front tooth was broken and his face was bleeding, and he said: O God, do not let a year pass over him until he dies as a disbeliever.” So a year had not passed over him until he died as a disbeliever in the Fire. And al-Waqidi mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abi Sabra, on the authority of Ishaq ibn `Abdullah ibn Abi Farwah, on the authority of Abu al-Huwayrith, on the authority of Nafi` ibn Jubayr said: I heard a man from the Muhajireen say: I witnessed Uhud and I saw arrows coming from every direction and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the middle of them, all of that being diverted from him. I saw Abdullah ibn Shihab al-Zuhri saying on that day: Show me Muhammad, I will not be saved if he is saved, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was beside him with no one with him. Then he passed him and Sufyan rebuked him for that, and he said: By God, I did not see him. I swear by God that he is protected from us! We went out four of us and we pledged and agreed to kill him, but we did not succeed in that. Al-Waqidi said: What is established with us is that the one who shot the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the cheeks was Ibn Qami’ah, and the one who caused his lip to bleed and his front tooth to be damaged was Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Ibn al-Mubarak told us on the authority of Ishaq ibn Yahya ibn Talhah ibn Ubayd God, Isa ibn Talhah told me on the authority of the Mother of the Believers Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: Whenever Abu Bakr mentioned the Battle of Uhud, he would say: That day was all for Talhah. Then he began to narrate, he said: I was the first to return on the Battle of Uhud, and I saw a man fighting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, behind him, and I think he said it was out of zeal. He said: I said: Talhah was where I missed what I missed, so I said: There is a man from my people who is dearer to me, and between me and the polytheists is a man I do not know, and I am closer to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, than he, and he walks quickly, and I do not remember it, and it was Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah. We went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: His front tooth was broken and his face was wounded, and two rings from the helmet’s ring entered his cheek. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Your companion wants Talhah, and he was bleeding, but we did not pay attention to what he said. He said: I went to remove that from his face, but Abu Ubaidah said, I swear to you by my right that you left me, so I left him. He did not want to take it with his hand and hurt the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he leaned on him with his mouth and pulled out one of the rings, and his front tooth fell with the ring. I went to do what he did, but he said, I swear to you by my right that you left me. He said, “So he did the same as he did the first time, and his other front tooth fell with the ring. Abu Ubaidah was the best of people in his wounds. We fixed the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then we came to Talhah in one of those graves, and there were seventy-odd, or less, or more, from stab wounds, arrows, and blows, and his finger was cut off, so we fixed the matter of him. Al-Haytham bin Kulayb and Al-Tabarani narrated it from the hadith of Ishaq bin Yahya. And with Al-Haitham, Abu Ubaidah said: I ask you by God, O Abu Bakr, to leave me alone? So Abu Ubaidah took the arrow in his mouth, and began to shake it out of dislike of harming the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he pulled out the arrow in his mouth, and Abu Ubaidah’s front tooth fell out. He mentioned its full form, and Al-Hafiz Al-Dhiya Al-Maqdisi chose it in his book. Ali bin Al-Madini weakened this hadith from the side of this Ishaq bin Yahya, because Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan, Ahmad, Yahya bin Ma’in, Al-Bukhari, Abu Zur’ah, Abu Hatim, Muhammad bin Saad, Al-Nasa’i and others spoke about it. Ibn Wahb said: Amr bin Al-Harith informed me that Umar bin Al-Sa’ib told him that he had heard that when Malik, Abu Abi Saeed Al-Khudri, was wounded by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud, he sucked the wound until it became clean and white, so it was said to him: Suck it in. He said: No, by God, I will never suck it in. Then he turned back to fight. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever wants to look at a man from the people of Paradise, let him look at this man, and he was martyred.” It has been proven in The two Sahihs, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Abi Hazim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sahl bin Saad, that he was asked about the wound of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: The face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was wounded, his front tooth was broken, and the egg was smashed on his head, may God bless him and grant him peace. Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was washing the blood, and Ali was pouring water on him with a shield. When Fatima saw that the water only increased the blood, she took a piece of matting and burned it until it became ashes. She stuck it to the wound and the blood stopped. The Almighty’s statement: So He rewarded you with grief for grief means He rewarded you with grief upon grief, as the Arabs say: It descended upon the Banu so-and-so, and it descended upon the Banu so-and-so. Ibn Jarir said: And similarly His statement: And I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees means on the trunks of palm trees. Ibn Abbas said: The first grief was due to the defeat, and when it was said that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was killed, and the second was when the polytheists overtook them on the mountain, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, they will not have the right to… And on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: The first grief was due to the defeat, and the second was when it was said that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was killed, which was more severe and greater for them than the defeat. Both were narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, and something similar was narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned something similar on the authority of Qatada as well. Al-Suddi said: The first grief was due to what they missed of the spoils and conquest, and the second was the enemy’s oversight of them. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: So He rewarded you with grief after grief, meaning distress after distress of the killing of those who were killed from your brothers, and the superiority of your enemy over you, and what occurred in your souls from the saying of those who said: Your Prophet was killed, so that was one after another upon you, grief after grief. Mujahid and Qatada said: The first grief was hearing of the killing of Muhammad, and the second was what happened to them of killing and wounds. The opposite was narrated on the authority of Qatada and al-Rabi’ ibn Anas. And on the authority of al-Suddi: The first was what they missed of victory and spoils, and the second was the enemy’s oversight of them. This statement was previously mentioned on the authority of al-Suddi. Ibn Jarir said: The most correct of these statements is the statement of the one who said: So He rewarded you with grief for grief. So He rewarded you with your grief, O believers, by God’s deprivation of you of the spoils of the polytheists and victory over them and the triumph over them, and what befell you of killing and wounds, on that day after He had shown you in all of that what you loved by your disobedience to the command of your Lord, and your opposition to the command of your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The grief of your thinking that your Prophet had been killed and the enemy had turned against you after your remnants from them. And the Almighty’s saying: So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you, meaning over what has escaped you of the spoils and victory over your enemy, nor over what has befallen you, of wounds and killing, said Ibn Abbas, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Suddi. And God is Aware of what you do. Glory be to Him and praise be to Him. There is no god but Him, the Most High, the Most Great.
3:150: The Almighty warns His believing servants against obeying the disbelievers and hypocrites, for obeying them brings ruin in this world and the Hereafter. That is why the Almighty said: If you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will become losers. Then He commanded them to obey Him, befriend Him, seek His help, and put their trust in Him. The Almighty said: Rather, God is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers. Then He gave them good report that He will cast fear of them and humiliation into the hearts of their enemies because of their disbelief and polytheism, along with what He has stored up for them in the Hereafter of torment and punishment. He said: "We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve because they have associated with God that for which He has not sent down any authority. Their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers." It has been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah that the Messenger of God said: "I have been given five things that were not given to any of the prophets before me: I have been aided by terror for a distance of a month's journey, the earth has been made a place of prostration and purification for me, and spoils of war have been made lawful for me." And I was given intercession, and the Prophet was sent to his people in particular, and I was sent to all people.” Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Sayyar, on the authority of Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My Lord has favored me over the prophets - or he said over the nations - in four things: He said: I was sent to all people, and the entire earth was made for me and for my nation a place of prostration and purification, so wherever a man of my nation finds prayer, his place of prostration and purification is with him, and I was aided by terror for a month’s journey, which he casts into the hearts of my enemies, and spoils of war were made lawful for me.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Sayyar al-Qurashi al-Umawi, their client from Damascus, who lived in Basra, on the authority of Abu Umamah Sadi bin Ajlan, may God be pleased with him, with it, and he said: It is good and authentic. Saeed bin Mansour said: Ibn Wahb informed us, Amr bin al-Harith informed me that Abu Yunus told him, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was aided by terror against the enemy. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Wahb. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad told us, Isra’il told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Burdah, on the authority of his father Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was given five things: I was sent to the red and the black, the earth was made pure and a place of prostration for me, spoils were made lawful for me and were not made lawful for those before me, I was aided by terror for a month, and I was given intercession, and there is no prophet who did not ask for his intercession. I hid my intercession and then made it for whoever died not associating anything with God.” Ahmad alone narrated it. Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God the Almighty: We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, he said: God cast terror into the heart of Abu Sufyan, so he returned to Mecca. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Abu Sufyan has indeed taken a part of you, and he has returned and God cast terror into his heart. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. And the words of God the Almighty: And God had fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission, Ibn Abbas said: God promised them victory. This verse may be used as evidence for one of the two previous sayings in the Almighty’s statement: “When you said to the believers, ‘Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?’ Yes, if you are patient and fear God and they come upon you at once, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels with marks.’” That was on the day of Uhud, because their enemy was three thousand fighters, so when they confronted them, victory and triumph were achieved early in the day for Islam. When what happened of the disobedience of the archers and the failure of some of the fighters, the promise that was conditional on steadfastness and obedience was delayed. For this reason, He said, And God has fulfilled His promise to you, meaning early in the day, when you were killing them, meaning killing them, by His permission, meaning by His giving you power over them, until you failed. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: Failure is cowardice. And you disputed about the matter and disobeyed, as happened to the archers, after He had shown you that which you love, which was victory over them. Among you are those who desire this world, and they are those who desired the spoils when they saw Defeat And among you is he who desires the Hereafter, then He turned you away from them to test you then He made them prevail over you to test you and examine you And He has certainly pardoned you that is, He forgave you for that action, and that, and God knows best, is due to the large number of the enemy and their numbers and the small number of the Muslims and their numbers. Ibn Jurayj said: His statement And He has certainly pardoned you he said: He did not eradicate you, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said the same: Ibn Jarir narrated them both And God is full of bounty to the believers and Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ubaydullah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: God has not given victory in a place like He gave victory on the day of Uhud, he said: So we denied that, and Ibn Abbas said: Between me and those who denied that is the Book of God, that God says on the day of Uhud And God had fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them with His permission Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan say: killing “until you were weak and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love. Among you are those who desire this world and among you are those who desire the Hereafter” the verse, and what he meant was And with these archers, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stationed them in a place and then said: Protect our backs, for if you see us being killed, do not help us, and if you see us having taken spoils, do not share with us. So when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took spoils and allowed the camp of the polytheists to be conquered, the archers all rushed into the camp to plunder, and the ranks of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met like this - and he interlocked his hands - and they took refuge, and when the archers left that position they were in, the horses entered from that place upon the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they struck each other, and they became confused and many Muslims were killed, and victory was for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions at the beginning of the day until seven or nine of the standard-bearers of the polytheists were killed, and the Muslims moved around towards the mountain, and they did not reach where the people say the cave is, but they were under the mortar, and the devil cried out: Muhammad has been killed, and they did not doubt that it was true, and we did not stop like that, we did not doubt that it was true until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appeared between the two Sa’dains, and we knew him. He said: We were so happy that it was as if we had not been afflicted with what afflicted us. He said: He climbed towards us and he was saying: The wrath of God has intensified against a people who bloodied the face of the Messenger of God. He said again: O God, they cannot prevail over us. Until he reached us, he remained for an hour, and then Abu Sufyan shouted at the bottom of the mountain: Let Hubal be exalted - twice, meaning his god - Where is the son of Abu Kabsha? Where is the son of Abu Quhafa? Where is the son of Ibn al-Khattab? Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of God, should I not answer him? He said: Yes. When he said: Let Hubal be exalted, Umar said: God is Most High and Most Majestic. Abu Sufyan said: Her eye has been comforted. So he turned away from her or did something. He said: Where is the son of Abu Kabsha? Where is the son of Abu Quhafa? Where is the son of Ibn al-Khattab? Umar said: “This is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is Abu Bakr, and here I am, Umar.” Abu Sufyan said: “A day is like the day of Badr. The days are in cycles, and war is a contest.” He said: Umar said: Our dead are not equal in Paradise. And your dead are in the Fire. He said: You claim that, so we have failed and lost. Abu Sufyan said: You will find mutilation among your dead, and that was not according to the opinion of our leaders. He said: Then the fanaticism of the Age of Ignorance overtook him, so he said: If that is the case, we would not hate it. This is a strange hadith and a strange context. It is from the mursals of Ibn Abbas, for no one witnessed it, nor his father. Al-Hakim included it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Abu al-Nadr al-Faqih, on the authority of Uthman ibn Saeed, on the authority of Salman ibn Dawud ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, and this is how Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Dalil al-Nubuwwah from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Hashemi on his authority. And some of it has supporting evidence in the Sahihs and elsewhere. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ata ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The women were behind the Muslims on the day of Uhud, finishing off the wounded polytheists. If I had sworn that day, I would have hoped to be fulfilled that none of us wanted the world, until God revealed: “Some of you desire this world and some of you desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you.” When the companions of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) disobeyed what they were commanded to do, the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) singled out nine men: seven from the Ansar and two men from Quraysh, and he was the tenth of them (may God bless him and grant him peace). When they overwhelmed him, he said: May God have mercy on the man who turned them away from us. Then a man from the Ansar stood up and fought for an hour until he was killed. When they overwhelmed him again, he said: May God have mercy on the man who turned them away from us. He continued saying that until the seven were killed. Then the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said to his two companions: We have not been fair to our companions. Abu Sufyan came and said: Hubal is superior. The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: “Say: God is higher and more majestic.” They said: God is higher and more majestic. Abu Sufyan said: We have Al-Uzza and you have no Uzza. The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: “Say: God is our protector and the disbelievers have no protector.” Abu Sufyan said: “A day for the day of Badr. A day against us and a day for us, a day for women and a day for men.” The eagle, Hanzala for Hanzala, so-and-so for so-and-so, and so-and-so for so-and-so. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are not equal: As for our dead, they are alive and provided for, but as for your dead, they are being tortured in the Fire. Abu Sufyan said: There was indeed an example among the people, and if he was cursed, it was not from among us. I did not command or forbid, nor did I like or dislike, nor did it upset me or please me. He said: So they looked and saw that Hamza’s belly had been ripped open, and Hind took his liver and chewed it but was unable to eat it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Did you eat something? They said: No. He said: God would not put anything of Hamza in the Fire. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, placed Hamza and prayed over him, and a man from the Ansar was brought and placed beside him and prayed over him. The Ansar lifted him up and left Hamza until another was brought and placed beside Hamza and prayed over him, then lifted him up and left Hamza, until he prayed over him seventy times that day. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Also. Al-Bukhari said: Ubaydullah bin Musa narrated to us on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa, who said: We encountered the polytheists that day and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, seated an army of archers and put Abdullah bin Jubair in charge of them, and said: “Do not move. If you see us prevailing over them, do not move, and if you see them prevailing over us, do not help us.” So when we met them, they fled until I saw the women running hard on the mountain, raising their legs and showing their anklets, and they began to say: The spoils, the spoils. So Abdullah bin Jubair said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered me not to move, but they refused. When they refused, they turned their faces away and seventy were killed. Abu Sufyan looked out and said: “Is Muhammad among the people?” He said: Do not answer him. He said: Is Ibn Abi Quhafah among the people? He said: Do not answer him. He said: Is Ibn Al-Khattab among the people? He said: These people have been killed, and if they were alive, they would have answered. So Umar could not control himself. He said to him: You have lied, O enemy of God, God has left for you that which grieves you. Abu Sufyan said: Hubal is exalted. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Answer him. They said: What should we say? He said: Say: God is higher and more exalted. Abu Sufyan said: We have Al-Uzza, and you have no Uzza. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Answer him. They said: What should we say? He said: Say: God is our Master, and you have no Master. Abu Sufyan said: A day for the day of Badr, and war is a contest, and you will find a mutilation that I did not command and it did not upset me. Al-Bukhari was the only one to narrate it from this source, then he narrated it from Amr bin Khalid from Zuhair bin Muawiyah, from Abu Ishaq, from Al-Bara’ in a similar manner, and he will come with something simpler than this. Al-Bukhari also said: Ubaidullah bin Saeed told us, Abu Usamah told us from Hisham bin Urwah, from his father, from Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: When the day of Uhud came, the polytheists were defeated, and Satan cried out: O servants of God, I am the last of you, so the first of them returned. So she and the last of them fought, and Hudhayfah saw his father Al-Yaman and said: O servants of God, my father is my father. He said: She said: By God, they did not hold back until they killed him, so Hudhayfah said: May God forgive you. Urwah said: By God, there was still good in Hudhayfah until he met God Almighty. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yahya ibn Ibad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr told me on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather that al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam said: By God, I saw myself looking at Hind’s servants and companions, their faces rolled up and they were running away, neither much nor little was enough to take them. The archers turned towards the army when the people fled from it, wanting to loot, and our backs were left for the horses, so they came to us from behind us, and a voice cried out: Muhammad has been killed. So we retreated and the people retreated upon us after we had captured the standard-bearers, until no one from the people came near it. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The standard of the polytheists remained fallen until Umrah bint Alqamah al-Harithiya took it and gave it to the Quraysh, so they fought with it. Al-Suddi said, on the authority of Abd Khair, who said: Abdullah ibn Masoud said: I did not think that any of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted the worldly life until what was revealed about us on the day of Uhud was revealed: Some of you want the world, and some of you want the Hereafter. It has been narrated from other sources on the authority of Ibn Masoud. And it was also narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and Abu Talha, narrated by Ibn Mardawayh in his interpretation, and the Almighty’s saying: Then He turned you away from them to test you. Ibn Ishaq said: Al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Rafi’, one of the sons of Adi ibn al-Najjar, told me: Anas ibn al-Nadr, the uncle of Anas ibn Malik, went to Umar ibn al-Khattab and Talha ibn Ubaydullah with some men from the Muhajireen and Ansar who had thrown down what was in their hands, so he said: What is leaving you? They said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has been killed. He said: What will you do with life after him? Rise and die as he died. Then he faced the people and fought until he was killed, may God be pleased with him. Al-Bukhari said: Hassan ibn Hassan told us, Muhammad ibn Talha told us, Hamid told us on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that his uncle, meaning Anas ibn al-Nadr, was absent from Badr and said: I was absent from the first battle of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. If God makes me witness with the Messenger of God, God will see what I find. So he met the day of Uhud and defeated the people, so he said: O God, I apologize to you for what… These people - meaning the Muslims - made it and I declare to you that I am innocent of what the polytheists brought. So he advanced with his sword and met Sa`d ibn Mu`adh and said: Where, Sa`d? I smell the fragrance of Paradise without anyone. So he went and was killed, and he was not recognized until his sister recognized him by his fingertip with a mole. He had eighty-odd stab wounds, blows and arrow wounds. This is the wording of al-Bukhari. Muslim included it in a hadith narrated by Thabit from Anas in a similar manner. Al-Bukhari also said: Abdun narrated to us, Abu Hamza narrated to us from Uthman ibn Muhab, who said: A man came to the House of Hajj and saw some people sitting. He said: Who are these people sitting? They said: These are Quraysh. He said: Who is the old man? They said: Ibn `Umar. So he came to him and said: I am going to ask you about something, so tell me. He said: Ask. He said: I ask you by the sanctity of this House, do you know that Uthman ibn `Affan fled on the day of Uhud? He said: Yes. He said: Do you know that he was absent from Badr and did not witness it? He said: Yes. He said: Do you know that he did not attend the Pledge of Ridwan and did not… He said: Yes. So he said: Allahu Akbar. Ibn Umar said: Come, so I may tell you and explain to you what you asked me about. As for his escape on the day of Uhud, I bear witness that God has pardoned him. As for his absence from Badr, he was married to the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she was sick. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: You will have the reward and share of a man who witnessed Badr. As for his absence from the Pledge of Ridwan, if there had been anyone more honorable in the valley of Mecca than Uthman, he would have sent him in his place. So he sent Uthman, and the Pledge of Ridwan took place after Uthman had gone to Mecca. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said with his right hand: This is the hand of Uthman, and he struck his hand with it and said: “This is the hand of Uthman. Go with it now.” Then Al-Bukhari narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Awanah, on the authority of Uthman ibn Abdullah ibn Muhabb. God the Almighty said: When you were ascending and not looking back at anyone meaning He turned you away from them while you were ascending, that is, in the mountain, fleeing from your enemies. Al-Hasan and Qatadah read When you were ascending meaning in the mountain, and not looking back at anyone meaning you were not looking back at anyone out of astonishment, fear and terror, and the Messenger is calling you from behind you meaning you had left him behind you calling you to stop fleeing from the enemies, and to return, come back and attack. Al-Suddi said: When the polytheists attacked the Muslims at Uhud and defeated them, some of them entered the city, and some of them went to the mountain on the rock and stood on it. So the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, began calling the people to the servants of God, to the servants of God. God mentioned their ascension to the mountain, then He mentioned the Prophet’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, calling them, saying: When you were ascending and not looking back at anyone, and the Messenger is calling you from behind you. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, Al-Rabi’ and Ibn Zayd said the same. Abdullah bin Al-Zubayri said: He mentions the defeat of the Muslims on the day of Uhud in his poem while he was a polytheist and had not yet converted to Islam, in which he says at the beginning: O crow of separation, have you heard? Say, for you are only speaking of something that has already been done. Good and evil have a limit, and both have a face and a face. Until he said: I wish my elders at Badr had witnessed the Khazraj’s fear of the sound of the weapons. When Quba narrated its ponds and the killing spread to Abd al-Ashel Then they started dancing, like a camel dancing high up in the mountain. So we killed twice as many of their nobles and we adjusted the slope of Badr, so it was balanced. Al-Haffan: Small camels. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had singled out twelve men from among his companions, as Imam Ahmad said: Hasan bin Musa told us, Zuhair told us, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-Bara bin Azib, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed Abdullah bin Jubair over the archers on the day of Uhud - and they were fifty men. He said: And he put them in a position, and said: “If you see us being snatched by birds, do not move until I send for you. And if you see us prevail over the enemy and trample them, do not move until I send for you.” He said: So they defeated them. He said: By God, I saw the women rushing up the mountain, their anklets and their clothes lifted. He said: The companions of Abdullah, the spoils, O people of the spoils, your companions have appeared, so what are you waiting for? Abdullah bin Jubair said: Have you forgotten what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to you? They said: By God, we will go to the people and take a share of the spoils. So when they came to them, their faces were turned away and they came forward. Defeated, that is what the Messenger calls them in their last days, so there remained with the Messenger of God only twelve men, so they killed seventy of us, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions killed one hundred and forty of the polytheists on the day of Badr, seventy prisoners and seventy dead. Abu Sufyan said: Is Muhammad among the people, is Muhammad among the people? - three times - he said. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade them from answering him, then he said: Is Ibn Abi Quhafah among the people? Is Ibn Abi Quhafah among the people? Is Ibn Al-Khattab among the people? Is Ibn Al-Khattab among the people? Then he turned to his companions and said: As for these, they have been killed and you have been spared from them, so Umar could not control himself but said: You have lied, by God, O enemy of God, those whom you have counted are all alive, and there remains for you what will upset you, so he said: A day for a day Badr, and war is a contest. And you will find among the people a mutilation that I did not order, and it did not upset me. Then he began to recite a rajaz saying: Hubal, Hubal, exalt. Hubal, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Will you not answer him? They said: O Messenger of God, what should we say? He said: Say God is higher and more majestic. He said: We have Al-Uzza, and you have no Uzza. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Will you not answer him? They said: O Messenger of God, what should we say? He said: Say God is our Master, and you have no Master. Al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Zuhair bin Muawiyah in an abbreviated form, and he narrated it from the hadith of Israel from Abu Ishaq in a more detailed form than this as mentioned above, and God knows best. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dalil Al-Nubuwwah from the hadith of Ammarah bin Ghaziyah, from Abu Al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: “The people fled from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud, and eleven men from the Ansar remained with him, and Talhah bin Ubaidullah, while he was climbing the mountain. The polytheists met them, so he said: Is there no one for these? Talhah said: I will, O Messenger of God. He said: As you are, O Talhah. A man from the Ansar said: I will, O Messenger of God. So he fought on his behalf, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who remained with him climbed, then the Ansari was killed.” So they caught up with him, and he said: Is there no man for these people? Talhah said the same as he had said, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said the same as he had said, and a man from the Ansar said: So I am, O Messenger of God, so he fought on his behalf and his companions ascended, then he was killed and they caught up with him, and he kept saying the same as he had said before, and Talhah said: So I am, O Messenger of God, so he detained him and a man from the Ansar asked him for permission to fight, so he gave him permission, and he fought like those who had been before him, until no one remained with him except Talhah, so they attacked them, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Who is for these people? Talhah said: I am, so he fought like all those who had been before him, and his fingers were injured, so he said: Enough, and the Messenger of God said: If you had said the name of God and mentioned the name of God, the angels would have lifted you up with the people looking at you until you entered the atmosphere of the sky, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ascended to his companions while they were gathered. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Wakee’, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim, who said: I saw Talhah’s hand paralyzed, with which he protected the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he (peace be upon him) said: “And he (peace be upon him) said: ‘On the Day of Uhud,’ meaning the Day of Uhud, in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman, from his father, from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: ‘On some of the days in which the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) fought, there remained none with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) except Talhah ibn Ubayd God and Sa’d, from their hadith.’ And al-Hasan ibn Arfa said: ‘Marwan ibn Mu’awiyah told us, from Hashim ibn Hashim al-Zuhri, who said: ‘I heard Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab say: ‘I heard Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas say: “The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) handed me his quiver on the Day of Uhud and said: ‘Shoot, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you.’” And al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Marwan ibn Mu’awiyah, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ‘Saleh ibn Kaysan told me on the authority of some of the family of Sa’d, from Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, that he shot on the Day of Uhud without the Messenger of God (peace be upon him).’ Sa’d said: ‘I saw the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) handing me arrows and saying: ‘Shoot, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you.’ He even handed me an arrow that had no tip, so I shot with it.’” "It was established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Ibrahim bin Sa`d, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Sa`d bin Abi Waqqas, who said: “On the day of Uhud, I saw on the right of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and on his left, two men wearing white clothes fighting on his behalf with the fiercest fighting I had ever seen before or after that day, meaning Gabriel and Michael, peace be upon them.” Hammad bin Salamah said on the authority of Ali bin Zaid and Thabit on the authority of Anas bin Malik: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was singled out on the day of Uhud with seven of the Ansar and two of the Quraysh. When they overwhelmed him, he said: ‘Whoever repels them from us will have Paradise,’ or ‘and he is my companion in Paradise.’ So a man from the Ansar stepped forward and fought until he was killed. Then they overwhelmed him again, and he said: ‘Whoever repels them from us will have Paradise,’ so a man from the Ansar stepped forward and fought until he was killed. He continued like that until the seven were killed, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his two companions: ‘We have not been fair to our companions.’” Narrated by Muslim on the authority of Hudbah bin Khalid, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, with something similar. Abu al-Aswad said on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr said: Abi bin Khalaf, the brother of Banu Jumah, had sworn while he was in Mecca to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When his oath reached the Messenger of God, he said, Rather, I will kill him, God willing. Then, on the day of Uhud, Abi came wearing iron, masked, saying, I will not escape if Muhammad escapes. So he charged at the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, intending to kill him. But Mus`ab bin `Umair, the brother of Banu `Abd al-Dar, met him, protecting the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with his own life. So he killed Mus`ab bin `Umair. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw the collarbone of Abi bin Khalaf through a gap between the hem of his armor and the blade, and stabbed him in it with his spear. He fell to the ground from his horse, and no blood came out of his stab wound. His companions came to him and carried him while he was mooing like a bull. They said to him, ‘What makes you so upset? It is only a scratch. ’ So he mentioned to them the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Rather, I will kill Abi.” Then he said, By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if this had happened to me, the people of Dhu al-Majaz would have died. All together, he died in the Fire, So may the companions of the Blaze be destroyed. It was narrated by Musa bin Uqbah in his Maghazi, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, in a similar manner. Muhammad bin Ishaq mentioned that he said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, leaned on the ravine, Ubayy bin Khalaf caught up with him and he was saying: ‘I will not be saved if I am saved.’ The people said: ‘O Messenger of God, let one of us help him.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Leave him.’ When he approached, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took the spear from Al-Harith bin Al-Samma. Some of the people said, ‘What was mentioned to me?’ When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it from him, he shook it so hard that we scattered from him as hair flies from the back of a camel when it shakes. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, faced him and stabbed him in the neck with a stab that caused him to fall off his horse repeatedly.” Al-Waqidi mentioned on the authority of Yunus bin Bakir, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Asim bin Amr bin Qatada, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ka’b bin Malik. On the authority of his father, something like that. Al-Waqidi said: Ibn Umar used to say: Abi bin Khalaf died in Batn Rabigh. I was walking in Batn Rabigh after a nightfall when I saw a blazing fire. I woke up and saw a man coming out of it, pulling on a chain, provoking thirst in him. A man said: Do not give him a drink, for this is the one killed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is Abi bin Khalaf. It was confirmed in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘God’s wrath was intense against a people who did this to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace – and he was pointing to his front teeth – and God’s wrath was intense against a man killed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the way of God.’” Al-Bukhari also included it on the authority of Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “God’s wrath was intense against the one killed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with his own hand in the way of God, and God’s wrath was intense against a people who bloodied the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” “And upon him be peace” - Ibn Ishaq said: “The front tooth of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was broken, his cheek was wounded, and his lip was injured.” The one who injured him was Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas. Salih ibn Kaysan told me, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: “I have never been so keen on killing anyone as I was on killing Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas, if what I know is that he was of bad character and hated by his people. And the statement of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “God’s wrath is intense against whoever bleeds the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace” was sufficient for me. And `Abd al-Razzaq said: Mu`mar informed us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of `Uthman al-Jazari, on the authority of Muqsim, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “supplicated against Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas on the day of Uhud when his front tooth was broken and his face was bleeding, and he said: O God, do not let a year pass over him until he dies as a disbeliever.” So a year had not passed over him until he died as a disbeliever in the Fire. And al-Waqidi mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abi Sabra, on the authority of Ishaq ibn `Abdullah ibn Abi Farwah, on the authority of Abu al-Huwayrith, on the authority of Nafi` ibn Jubayr said: I heard a man from the Muhajireen say: I witnessed Uhud and I saw arrows coming from every direction and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the middle of them, all of that being diverted from him. I saw Abdullah ibn Shihab al-Zuhri saying on that day: Show me Muhammad, I will not be saved if he is saved, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was beside him with no one with him. Then he passed him and Sufyan rebuked him for that, and he said: By God, I did not see him. I swear by God that he is protected from us! We went out four of us and we pledged and agreed to kill him, but we did not succeed in that. Al-Waqidi said: What is established with us is that the one who shot the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the cheeks was Ibn Qami’ah, and the one who caused his lip to bleed and his front tooth to be damaged was Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Ibn al-Mubarak told us on the authority of Ishaq ibn Yahya ibn Talhah ibn Ubayd God, Isa ibn Talhah told me on the authority of the Mother of the Believers Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: Whenever Abu Bakr mentioned the Battle of Uhud, he would say: That day was all for Talhah. Then he began to narrate, he said: I was the first to return on the Battle of Uhud, and I saw a man fighting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, behind him, and I think he said it was out of zeal. He said: I said: Talhah was where I missed what I missed, so I said: There is a man from my people who is dearer to me, and between me and the polytheists is a man I do not know, and I am closer to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, than he, and he walks quickly, and I do not remember it, and it was Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah. We went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: His front tooth was broken and his face was wounded, and two rings from the helmet’s ring entered his cheek. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Your companion wants Talhah, and he was bleeding, but we did not pay attention to what he said. He said: I went to remove that from his face, but Abu Ubaidah said, I swear to you by my right that you left me, so I left him. He did not want to take it with his hand and hurt the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he leaned on him with his mouth and pulled out one of the rings, and his front tooth fell with the ring. I went to do what he did, but he said, I swear to you by my right that you left me. He said, “So he did the same as he did the first time, and his other front tooth fell with the ring. Abu Ubaidah was the best of people in his wounds. We fixed the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then we came to Talhah in one of those graves, and there were seventy-odd, or less, or more, from stab wounds, arrows, and blows, and his finger was cut off, so we fixed the matter of him. Al-Haytham bin Kulayb and Al-Tabarani narrated it from the hadith of Ishaq bin Yahya. And with Al-Haitham, Abu Ubaidah said: I ask you by God, O Abu Bakr, to leave me alone? So Abu Ubaidah took the arrow in his mouth, and began to shake it out of dislike of harming the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he pulled out the arrow in his mouth, and Abu Ubaidah’s front tooth fell out. He mentioned its full form, and Al-Hafiz Al-Dhiya Al-Maqdisi chose it in his book. Ali bin Al-Madini weakened this hadith from the side of this Ishaq bin Yahya, because Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan, Ahmad, Yahya bin Ma’in, Al-Bukhari, Abu Zur’ah, Abu Hatim, Muhammad bin Saad, Al-Nasa’i and others spoke about it. Ibn Wahb said: Amr bin Al-Harith informed me that Umar bin Al-Sa’ib told him that he had heard that when Malik, Abu Abi Saeed Al-Khudri, was wounded by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud, he sucked the wound until it became clean and white, so it was said to him: Suck it in. He said: No, by God, I will never suck it in. Then he turned back to fight. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever wants to look at a man from the people of Paradise, let him look at this man, and he was martyred.” It has been proven in The two Sahihs, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Abi Hazim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sahl bin Saad, that he was asked about the wound of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: The face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was wounded, his front tooth was broken, and the egg was smashed on his head, may God bless him and grant him peace. Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was washing the blood, and Ali was pouring water on him with a shield. When Fatima saw that the water only increased the blood, she took a piece of matting and burned it until it became ashes. She stuck it to the wound and the blood stopped.
