Repeatedly - Al-Waqidi mentioned on the authority of Yunus bin Bakir on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Asim bin Amr bin Qatada, on the authority of Abdullah bin Kaab bin Malik, on the authority of his father, something similar to that. Al-Waqidi said: Ibn Omar used to say, “My father bin Khalaf died in Batn Rabigh. I was walking in Batn Rabigh after a part of the night, when I saw a blazing fire. I woke up and saw a man coming out of it with a chain, pulling it, arousing his thirst. A man said, “Do not give him a drink, for this is the one who was killed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” This is Abi bin Khalaf - and it was proven in the two Sahihs from the narration of Abd al-Razzaq from Muammar, from Hammam bin Munabbih from Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘God’s wrath was intense against a people who did something to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace’ - and he was pointing to his front teeth - and God’s wrath was intense against a man whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed in the way of God.” Al-Bukhari also included it from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj from Amr bin Dinar, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: “God’s wrath was intense against a person whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed with his own hand in the way of God, and God’s wrath was intense against a people who caused blood to flow from the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Ibn Ishaq said: “The front teeth of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were injured, his cheek was wounded, and his lip was wounded.” The one who injured him was Utbah bin Abi Waqqas, and Salih bin Kaysan told me, from someone who told him, from Saad bin Abi Waqqas, who said: I have never been so keen on killing anyone as I was keen on killing Utbah. Ibn Abi Waqqas, if what I know is of a man of bad character who is hated by his people, and the saying of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “God’s wrath is severe on whoever bleeds the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace,” is sufficient for me. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar informed us on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Uthman al-Jazari, on the authority of Muqsim, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “supplicated against Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas on the day of Uhud when his front tooth was broken and his face was bleed, and he said: O God, do not let a year pass over him until he dies as a disbeliever.” So a year had not passed over him until he died as a disbeliever in the Fire. Al-Waqidi mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abi Sabra, on the authority of Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Farwah, on the authority of Abu al-Huwayrith, on the authority of Nafi’ ibn Jubayr, who said: I heard a man from the Muhajireen say: I witnessed Uhud and I saw arrows coming from every direction and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the middle of them, all of that was being diverted from him. I saw Abdullah ibn Shihab al-Zuhri saying on that day: Show me Muhammad, I will not be saved if he is saved, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was beside him with no one with him, then… He passed by him, and Safwan rebuked him for that. He said, “By God, I have never seen him. I swear to God that he is forbidden from us!” We went out four of us and we pledged and agreed to kill him, but we did not succeed in that. Al-Waqidi said: What is established with us is that the one who shot the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the cheeks was Ibn Qami’ah, and the one who caused his lip to bleed and his front tooth to be damaged was Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Ibn al-Mubarak told us on the authority of Ishaq ibn Yahya ibn Talhah ibn Ubayd God, Isa ibn Talhah told me on the authority of the Mother of the Believers Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: Whenever Abu Bakr mentioned the Battle of Uhud, he would say: That day was all for Talhah. Then he began to narrate, he said: I was the first to return on the Battle of Uhud, and I saw a man fighting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, behind him, and I think he said it was out of zeal. He said: I said: Talhah was where I missed what I missed, so I said: There is a man from my people who is dearer to me, and between me and the polytheists is a man I do not know, and I am closer to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, than he, and he walks quickly, and I do not remember it, and it was Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah. We went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: His front tooth was broken and his face was wounded, and two rings from the helmet’s ring entered his cheek. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Your companion wants Talhah, and he was bleeding, but we did not pay attention to what he said. He said, “I went to remove that from his face, but Abu Ubaidah said, ‘I swear to you by my right that you left me,’ so I left him. He did not want to take it with his hand and hurt the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he leaned on him with his mouth and pulled out one of the rings, and his front tooth fell out with the ring. I went to do what he did, but he said, ‘I swear to you by my right that you left me.’ He said, ‘So he did the same as he did the first time, and his other front tooth fell out with the ring. Abu Ubaidah was the best of people in his wounds. We fixed the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then we came to Talhah in one of those graves, and there were seventy-odd, or less, or more, from stab wounds, arrows, and blows, and his finger had been cut off, so we fixed the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.’” And when Al-Haitham came, Abu Ubaidah said: I ask you by God, O Abu Bakr, to leave me alone? So Abu Ubaidah took the arrow in his mouth and began to shake it out of dislike of hurting the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he pulled out the arrow in his mouth and Abu Ubaidah’s front tooth fell out. He mentioned the rest of it, and Al-Hafiz Al-Dhiya Al-Maqdisi chose it in his book. Ali bin Al-Madini declared this hadith weak on the authority of Ishaq bin Yahya, because Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan, Ahmad, Yahya bin Ma’een, Al-Bukhari, Abu Zur’ah, Abu Hatim, Muhammad bin Sa’d, Al-Nasa’i and others spoke about him. Ibn Wahb said: Amr bin Al-Harith informed me that Umar bin Al-Sa’ib told him that he had heard that when Malik, Abu Abi Saeed Al-Khudri, was wounded by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud, he sucked the wound until it became clean and white, so it was said to him: Suck it in. He said: No, by God, I will never suck it in. Then he turned back to fight. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever wants to look at a man from the people of Paradise, let him look at this man, and he was martyred. It has been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Abi Hazim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sahl bin Sa`d, that he was asked about the wound of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: The face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was wounded, his front tooth was broken, and the egg was smashed on his head, may God bless him and grant him peace. Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was washing the blood, and Ali was pouring water on him with a shield. When Fatima saw that the water only increased the blood, she took a piece of matting and burned it until it became ashes, then she stuck it to the wound and the blood stopped. God Almighty said: So He rewarded you with grief for grief meaning He repaid you with grief for grief, as the Arabs say: It descended upon the Banu so-and-so, and it descended upon the Banu so-and-so. Ibn Jarir said: And likewise his saying, And I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, meaning on the trunks of palm trees. Ibn Abbas said: The first grief was due to the defeat, and when it was said that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was killed, and the second was when the polytheists overtook them on the mountain, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, they have no right to overtake us. And from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: The first grief was due to the defeat, and the second was when it was said that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was killed. That was more severe and greater for them than the defeat. Both were narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, and something similar was narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab, and Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned something similar from Qatadah as well. Al-Suddi said: The first grief was due to what they missed of the spoils and conquest, and the second was due to the enemy’s presence over them. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: So He rewarded you with grief after grief, meaning distress after distress from the killing of those of your brothers, and the superiority of your enemy over you, and what occurred in your souls from the saying of those who said: Your Prophet was killed, so that was one grief after another for you. Mujahid and Qatadah said: The grief The first is their hearing of the killing of Muhammad, and the second is what happened to them in terms of killing and wounds. Qatada and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said the opposite. Al-Suddi said: The first is what they missed out on in terms of victory and spoils, and the second is the enemy’s presence upon them. This statement from Al-Suddi has already been mentioned. Ibn Jarir said: The most correct of these sayings is the saying of the one who said, So He rewarded you with grief for grief. So He rewarded you with your grief, O believers, by God’s deprivation of you of the spoils of the polytheists and victory over them and the victory over them, and what befell you of killing and wounds, on that day after He had shown you in all of that what you love by your disobedience to the command of your Lord, and your opposition to the command of your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the grief of your thinking that your Prophet had been killed and the enemy had turned against you after your remnants from them. And the Almighty’s saying, So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you, meaning over what has escaped you of the spoils and victory over your enemy, nor over what has befallen you, of wounds and killing, said Ibn Abbas, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Suddi, And God is Aware of what you do. Glory be to Him and praise be to Him, there is no god but Him, the Most High.
3:153: The Almighty warns His believing servants against obeying the disbelievers and hypocrites, for obeying them brings ruin in this world and the Hereafter. That is why the Almighty said: If you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will become losers. Then He commanded them to obey Him, befriend Him, seek His help, and put their trust in Him. The Almighty said: Rather, God is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers. Then He gave them good report that He will cast fear of them and humiliation into the hearts of their enemies because of their disbelief and polytheism, along with what He has stored up for them in the Hereafter of torment and punishment. He said: "We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve because they have associated with God that for which He has not sent down any authority. Their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers." It has been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah that the Messenger of God said: "I have been given five things that were not given to any of the prophets before me: I have been aided by terror for a distance of a month's journey, the earth has been made a place of prostration and purification for me, and spoils of war have been made lawful for me." And I was given intercession, and the Prophet was sent to his people in particular, and I was sent to all people.” Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Sayyar, on the authority of Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My Lord has favored me over the prophets - or he said over the nations - in four things: He said: I was sent to all people, and the entire earth was made for me and for my nation a place of prostration and purification, so wherever a man of my nation finds prayer, his place of prostration and purification is with him, and I was aided by terror for a month’s journey, which he casts into the hearts of my enemies, and spoils of war were made lawful for me.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Sayyar al-Qurashi al-Umawi, their client from Damascus, who lived in Basra, on the authority of Abu Umamah Sadi bin Ajlan, may God be pleased with him, with it, and he said: It is good and authentic. Saeed bin Mansour said: Ibn Wahb informed us, Amr bin al-Harith informed me that Abu Yunus told him, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was aided by terror against the enemy. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Wahb. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad told us, Isra’il told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Burdah, on the authority of his father Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was given five things: I was sent to the red and the black, the earth was made pure for me and a place of prostration, spoils of war were made lawful for me but were not made lawful for those before me, I was aided by terror for a month, and I was given intercession, and there is no prophet who did not ask for his intercession. I kept my intercession hidden and then made it for whoever died not associating anything with God.” Ahmad alone narrated it. Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God, the Most High: We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, that God cast terror into the heart of Abu Sufyan, so he returned to Mecca. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Abu Sufyan has indeed taken a part of you, and he has returned and God has cast terror into his heart. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. And the Almighty said: And God has fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission. Ibn Abbas said: God promised them victory. This verse may be used as evidence for one of the two previous sayings in the Almighty’s saying: “When you said to the believers, ‘Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?’ Yes, if you are patient and fear God and they come to you at once, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels with marks.” That was on the day of Uhud, because their enemy was three thousand fighters. When they confronted them, victory and triumph were at the beginning of the day for Islam. When what happened of the disobedience of the archers and the failure of some of the fighters, the promise that was conditional on steadfastness and obedience was delayed. For this reason, He said: And God has fulfilled His promise to you, meaning at the beginning of the day, when you were killing them, meaning killing them, by His permission, meaning by His giving you power over them, until you failed. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: Failure is cowardice. And you disputed about the matter and disobeyed, as happened to the archers, after what happened. “I saw you as you love” which is the victory over them among you are those who desire this world and they are those who desired the spoils when they saw the defeat “and among you are those who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them to test you” then He made them prevail over you to test you and examine you and He has certainly pardoned you meaning He forgave you for that action, and that, and God knows best, is due to the large number of the enemy and their numbers and the small number of the Muslims and their numbers. Ibn Jurayj said: His statement and He has certainly pardoned you he said: He did not eradicate you, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said the same: Ibn Jarir narrated them both and God is full of bounty to the believers and Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ubaydullah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: God has not given victory in a place like He gave victory on the day of Uhud, he said: So we denied that, and Ibn Abbas said: Between me and those who denied that is the Book of God, that God says on the day of Uhud and God had fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them with His permission Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan say: killing until you failed and disputed In the matter and you disobeyed after He showed you what you love. Among you are those who desire this world and among you are those who desire the Hereafter. The verse, and what he meant by this were the archers, and that is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stationed them in a place and then said: “Protect our backs. If you see us being killed, do not help us, and if you see us having taken spoils, do not share with us.” So when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took spoils and allowed the camp of the polytheists to be invaded, the archers all rushed into the camp to plunder. The ranks of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met like this - and he interlaced his hands - and they took refuge. When the archers left that position they were in, the horses entered from that place upon the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they struck each other, and they became confused and many Muslims were killed. Victory was for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions at the beginning of the day until seven or nine of the standard-bearers of the polytheists were killed. The Muslims moved around towards the mountain, and they did not reach where people say the cave is, but they were under the hammer, and Satan cried out: Muhammad has been killed. They did not doubt that it was true, and we continued to do so, not doubting that it was true, until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appeared between the two Sa’dains. We recognized him by his glance when he walked. He said: We were so happy that it was as if what had happened to us had not happened to us. He said: He climbed towards us and he was saying: The wrath of God has intensified against a people who bloodied the face of the Messenger of God, and he said again: O God, they cannot surpass us, until he reached us. He remained for an hour, and then Abu Sufyan shouted at the bottom of the mountain: High is Hubal - twice, meaning his god - Where is the son of Abu Kabsha? Where is the son of Abu Quhafah? Where is the son of Ibn al-Khattab? Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of God, should I not answer him? He said: Yes. When he said: High is Hubal, Umar said: God is Most High and Most Majestic. Abu Sufyan said: Her eye has been comforted, so he turned away from it or something else. He said: Where is the son of Abu Kabsha? Where is the son of Abu Quhafah? Where is the son of Ibn al-Khattab? Umar said: “This is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is Abu Bakr, and here I am Umar.” He said: Abu Sufyan said, A day for the day of Badr, the days are cycles, and war is a game of chance. He said: Umar said: They are not the same, our dead are in Paradise, and your dead are in Hell. He said: You claim that, so we have failed and lost. Abu Sufyan said: You will find mutilation among your dead. And that was not according to the opinion of our leaders. He said: Then the zeal of the Age of Ignorance overtook him, so he said: If that was the case, we would not hate him. This is a strange hadith with a strange context, and it is from the mursals of Ibn Abbas, for no one witnessed it, nor his father. Al-Hakim included it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Abu al-Nadr al-Faqih, on the authority of Uthman ibn Sa`id, on the authority of Salman ibn Dawud ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, and Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated it in the same way in Dalā’il al-Nubuwwah from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Hashimi. And some of it has corroborating evidence in the Sahihs and elsewhere. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: On the day of Uhud, the women were behind the Muslims, finishing off the wounded polytheists. If I had sworn on that day, I would have hoped to be righteous, for none of us wanted the world, until God revealed: “Among you are those who desire the world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them that He might test you.” So when the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disobeyed and disobeyed what they were commanded to do, the Prophet singled them out. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was with nine men: seven from the Ansar, and two men from Quraysh, and he was the tenth of them, may God bless him and grant him peace. When they overwhelmed him, he said: May God have mercy on the man who repelled them from us. Then a man from the Ansar stood up and fought for an hour until he was killed. When they overwhelmed him again, he said: May God have mercy on the man who repelled them from us. He continued saying that until the seven were killed. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his two companions: We have not been fair to our companions. Then Abu Sufyan came and said: Hubal is superior. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Say: God is higher and more majestic.” They said: God is higher and more majestic. Abu Sufyan said: We have Al-Uzza, and you have no Uzza. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Say: God is our Master, and the disbelievers have no master.” Abu Sufyan said: “A day for the day of Badr. A day against us and a day for us, a day for women and a day for an eagle, Hanzala for Hanzala, so-and-so for so-and-so, and so-and-so for so-and-so.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are not equal. As for our dead, they are alive and provided for, but as for your dead, they are being tortured in Hell. Abu Sufyan said: There was indeed an example among the people, and if he cursed, it was not from among us. I did not command or forbid, I did not like or dislike, it did not upset me or please me. He said: So they looked and saw that Hamza’s stomach had been ripped open, and Hind had taken his liver and chewed it but was unable to eat it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Did you eat something? They said: No. He said: God would not let anything of Hamzah enter the Fire. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, placed Hamzah and prayed over him, and a man from the Ansar was brought and placed beside him and prayed over him. The Ansar lifted him up and left Hamzah until another was brought and placed beside Hamzah and prayed over him. Then he lifted him up and left Hamzah, until he prayed over him seventy prayers that day. Ahmad also transmitted it alone. Al-Bukhari said: Ubaydullah bin Musa told us on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa, who said: We encountered the polytheists on that day and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, seated an army of archers and put Abdullah bin Jubair in charge of them and said: Do not move. If you see us prevailing over them, do not move. If you see them prevailing over us, do not help us. So when we met them, they fled until I saw the women running hard on the mountain, raising their legs and their anklets showing, and they began to say: The spoils, the spoils. Abdullah bin Jubair said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entrusted me with He (peace be upon him) ordered them not to leave, but they refused. When they refused, they turned their faces away and seventy people were killed. Abu Sufyan looked out and said, Is Muhammad among the people? He said, Do not answer him. He said, Is Ibn Abi Quhafah among the people? He said, Do not answer him. He said, Is Ibn al-Khattab among the people? He said, “These people have been killed. If they were alive, they would have answered.” Umar could not control himself and said to him, “You lie, enemy of God. God has left for you that which grieves you.” Abu Sufyan said, Have Hubal prevailed. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, Answer him. They said, What should we say? He said, “Say: God is Most High and Most Majestic.” Abu Sufyan said, We have al-Uzza, and you have no Uzza. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, Answer him. They said, What should we say? He said, “Say: God is our Master, and you have no Master.” Abu Sufyan said: A day for the day of Badr, and war is a contest, and you will find a mutilation that I did not command and it did not upset me. Al-Bukhari is the only one to narrate it from this source, then he narrated it from Amr bin Khalid from Zuhair bin Muawiyah, from Abu Ishaq, from Al-Baraa in a similar manner, and he will come with something simpler than this. Al-Bukhari also said: Ubaidullah bin Saeed told us, Abu Usamah told us from Hisham bin Urwah, from his father, from Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: When the day of Uhud came, the polytheists were defeated, and Satan cried out: O servants of God, the last of you, so the first of them returned and fought with the last of them, and Hudhayfah saw his father Al-Yaman and said: O servants of God, my father, my father. He said: She said: By God, they did not hold back until they killed him, so Hudhayfah said: May God forgive you. Urwah said: By God, there was still good in Hudhayfah until he joined God Almighty. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yahya ibn Abbad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr told me on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather that al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam said: By God, I saw myself looking at Hind’s servants and companions with their sleeves rolled up and running away, neither much nor little was enough to take them. The archers turned towards the army when the people fled from it, wanting to plunder, and our backs were left to the horses, so they came at us from behind, and a crier cried out: Behold, Muhammad has been killed. So we retreated and the people retreated upon us after we had taken the standard-bearers, until no one from the people could come near it. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The standard of the polytheists remained fallen until Umrah bint Alqamah al-Harithiya took it and gave it to the Quraysh, so they fought with it. Al-Suddi said, on the authority of Abd al-Khair, who said: Abdullah ibn Mas`ud said: I did not think that any of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted this world until what was revealed about us on the Day of Uhud was revealed: Among you are those who desire this world and among you are those who desire the Hereafter. It has been narrated from other sources on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, and it was also narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and Abu Talhah, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated them in his interpretation. And the Almighty’s statement: Then He turned you away from them to test you. Ibn Ishaq said: Al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Rafi`, one of the sons of `Adi ibn al-Najjar, told me: Anas ibn al-Nadr, the uncle of Anas ibn Malik, went to `Umar ibn al-Khattab and Talhah ibn `Ubaydullah with some men from the Muhajireen and Ansar who had thrown down what was in their hands, and he said: What will leave you? They said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has been killed. He said: What will you do with life after him? Then he faced the people and fought until he was killed, may God be pleased with him. Al-Bukhari said: Hassan bin Hassan told us, Muhammad bin Talha told us, Hamid told us on the authority of Anas bin Malik that his uncle, meaning Anas bin Al-Nadr, was absent from Badr and said: I was absent from the first battle of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. If God makes me witness with the Messenger of God, God will see what I find. So he met the day of Uhud and defeated the people, so he said: O God, I apologize to You for what these people have done - meaning the Muslims - and I disavow before You what the polytheists have brought. So he advanced with his sword and met Saad bin Muadh, so he said: Where, Saad? I find the scent of Paradise before Uhud. So he went and was killed, and he was not recognized until his sister recognized him by a mole on his finger, and he had eighty-odd stab wounds, blows, and arrow wounds. This is the wording of Al-Bukhari. Muslim included it in a similar hadith from Thabit on the authority of Anas. Al-Bukhari also said: Abdun told us, Abu Hamza told us on the authority of Uthman bin Muhab, who said: A man came to perform Hajj to the House of God and saw some people sitting. He said: Who are these sitting? They said: These are Quraysh. He said: Who is the sheikh? They said: Ibn Umar. So he came to him and said: I am going to ask you about something, so tell me. He said: Ask. He said: I ask you by the sanctity of this House, do you know that Uthman ibn Affan fled on the day of Uhud? He said: Yes. He said: Do you know that he was absent from Badr and did not witness it? He said: Yes. He said: Do you know that he stayed away from the Pledge of Ridwan and did not witness it? He said: Yes. So he said: Allahu Akbar. Then Ibn Umar said: Come, so I may tell you and explain to you what you asked me about. As for his escape on the day of Uhud, I bear witness that God has forgiven him. As for his absence from Badr, he was married to the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she was sick. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: You will have the reward and share of a man who witnessed Badr. As for his absence from the Pledge of Ridwan, if there had been anyone more honorable in the valley of Mecca than Uthman, he would have sent him in his place. So he sent Uthman, and the Pledge of Ridwan took place after Uthman had gone to Mecca. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said with his right hand: This is the hand of Uthman, and he struck his hand with it and said: “This is the hand of Uthman. Go with it now.” Then Al-Bukhari narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Awanah, on the authority of Uthman ibn Abdullah ibn Muhabb. God the Almighty said: When you were ascending and not looking back at anyone meaning He turned you away from them while you were ascending, that is, in the mountain, fleeing from your enemies. Al-Hasan and Qatadah read When you were ascending meaning in the mountain, and not looking back at anyone meaning you were not looking back at anyone out of astonishment, fear and terror, and the Messenger is calling you from behind you meaning you had left him behind you calling you to stop fleeing from the enemies, and to return, come back and attack. Al-Suddi said: When the polytheists attacked the Muslims at Uhud and defeated them, some of them entered the city, and some of them went to the mountain on the rock and stood on it. So the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, began calling the people to the servants of God, to the servants of God. God mentioned their ascension to the mountain, then He mentioned the Prophet’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, calling them, saying: When you were ascending and not looking back at anyone, and the Messenger is calling you from behind you. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, Al-Rabi’ and Ibn Zayd said the same. Abdullah bin Al-Zubayri said: He mentions the defeat of the Muslims on the day of Uhud in his poem while he was a polytheist and had not yet converted to Islam, in which he says at the beginning: O crow of separation, have you heard? Say, for you are only speaking of something that has already been done. Good and evil have a limit, and both have a face and a face. Until he said: I wish my elders at Badr had witnessed the Khazraj’s fear of the sound of the weapons. When Quba narrated its ponds and the killing spread to Abd al-Ashel Then they started dancing, like a camel dancing high up in the mountain. So we killed twice as many of their nobles and we adjusted the slope of Badr, so it was balanced. Al-Haffan: small camels. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had singled out twelve of his companions, as Imam Ahmad said: Hasan ibn Musa told us, Zuhair told us, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-Bara’ ibn Azib, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed Abdullah ibn Jubayr over the archers on the day of Uhud - and they were fifty men - and he put them in a position, and said: If you see us being snatched by birds, do not move until I send for you, and if you see us prevail over the enemy and trample them, do not move until I send for you. He said: So they defeated them. He said: By God, I saw the women rushing up the mountain, their anklets and their clothes lifted, and he said: The companions of Abdullah, the spoils, O people of the spoils, your companions have appeared, so what are you waiting for? Abdullah ibn Jubayr said: Have you forgotten what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to you? They said: By God, we will go to the people, so we will take some of the spoils. So when they came to them, their faces were turned away and they came back defeated, and that is what the Messenger was calling them to in He left them, and there remained with the Messenger of God only twelve men, and they killed seventy of us. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions killed one hundred and forty of the polytheists on the day of Badr, seventy prisoners and seventy dead. Abu Sufyan said: Is Muhammad among the people? Is Muhammad among the people? - three times - he said. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade them from answering him, then he said: Is Ibn Abi Quhafah among the people? Is Ibn Abi Quhafah among the people? Is Ibn Al-Khattab among the people? Is Ibn Al-Khattab among the people? Then he turned to his companions and said: As for these, they have been killed and you have been spared from them. Umar could not control himself but said: You have lied, O enemy of God, those whom you have counted are all alive, and there remains for you that which will upset you. He said: A day for the day of Badr, and war is a contest. And you will find among the people mutilation which I did not order, and which did not upset me. Then he began to recite: Hubal is exalted, Hubal is exalted. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Will you not answer him? They said: O Messenger of God, what should we say? He said: Say: God is higher and more exalted. He said: We have Al-Uzza, and you have no Uzza. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Will you not answer him? They said: O Messenger of God, what should we say? He said: Say: God is our Master, and you have no Master. Al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Zuhair bin Muawiyah in an abbreviated form, and he narrated it from the hadith of Israel from Abu Ishaq in a more detailed form than this as mentioned above, and God knows best. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in Dalil al-Nubuwwah from the hadith of Ammarah bin Ghaziyah, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: “The people fled from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud, and eleven men from the Ansar remained with him, and Talhah bin Ubaydullah was climbing the mountain, and the polytheists met them, so he said: Is there no one for these? Talhah said: I am, O Messenger of God. He said: As you are, O Talhah. A man from the Ansar said: I am, O Messenger of God. So he fought on his behalf, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who remained with him climbed, then the Ansar was killed and they caught up with him, so he said: Is there no man for these? Talhah said the same as he said, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said the same as he said, so a man from the Ansar said: I am, O Messenger of God. So he fought on his behalf and his companions were climbing, then he was killed and they caught up with him, and he kept saying the same as he said before. Talha said: So I will, O Messenger of God. So he detained him and a man from the Ansar asked his permission to fight, so he gave him permission, so he fought like those who had been before him, until no one remained with him except Talha, so they attacked them, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Who is with these? Talha said: I will. So he fought like all those who had been before him fought, and his fingers were injured, so he said: Hush, so the Messenger of God said: If you had said the name of God and mentioned the name of God, the angels would have raised you up with the people looking at you until you entered the atmosphere of heaven. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ascended to his companions while they were gathered. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Wakee’, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim, who said: I saw Talhah’s hand paralyzed, with which he protected the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning the day of Uhud. And in the two Sahihs, on the authority of Mu’tamir bin Sulayman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: None remained with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on some of the days in which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought, except Talhah bin Ubayd God and Sa’d, according to their hadith. Al-Hasan bin Arafa said: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Hashim bin Hashim Al-Zuhri, who said: I heard Saeed bin Al-Musayyab say: I heard Saad bin Abi Waqqas say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, handed me his quiver on the day of Uhud and said: ‘Shoot, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you.’” Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad, on the authority of Marwan bin Muawiyah. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Salih bin Kaysan told me on the authority of some of the family of Saad, on the authority of Saad bin Abi Waqqas, that he shot on the day of Uhud without the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Saad said: “I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, handing me arrows and saying: ‘Shoot, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you.’ He even handed me an arrow that had no point, so I shot with it.” It was confirmed in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Ibrahim bin Saad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Saad bin Abi Waqqas, who said: “On the day of Uhud, I saw on the right of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and on his left two men wearing white clothes fighting on his behalf with the most intense fighting I had ever seen them before that day.” And after him, meaning Gabriel and Michael, peace be upon them.” And Hammad bin Salamah said on the authority of Ali bin Zaid and Thabit on the authority of Anas bin Malik: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was singled out on the day of Uhud with seven of the Ansar and two of the Quraysh. When they overwhelmed him, he said, ‘Who will repel them from us and he will have Paradise?’ or ‘He is my companion in Paradise.’ So a man from the Ansar came forward and fought until he was killed. Then they overwhelmed him again, and he said, ‘Who will repel them from us and he will have Paradise?’ So a man from the Ansar came forward and fought until he was killed. He continued like that until he killed the seven. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his two companions, ‘We have not been fair to our companions.’” Narrated by Muslim on the authority of Hudbah bin Khalid, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, with something similar. Abu al-Aswad said on the authority of Urwah bin al-Zubayr, who said: Ubayy bin Khalaf, the brother of Banu Jumah, had sworn while he was in Mecca to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When his oath reached the Messenger of God, he said, ‘Rather, I will kill him, God willing.’ So when the day of Uhud came, Ubayy came in iron, masked, and he was saying, ‘No.’” I was saved if Muhammad was saved. He attacked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, intending to kill him. Mus`ab ibn `Umair, the brother of Banu `Abd al-Dar, met him, protecting the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with himself. Mus`ab ibn `Umair was killed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw the collarbone of Abi ibn Khalaf through a gap between the hem of his armor and the blade, and stabbed him in it with his spear. He fell to the ground from his horse, and no blood came out of his stab wound. His companions came to him and carried him while he was mooing like a bull. They said to him: What has made you so upset? It is only a scratch. He mentioned to them the saying of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Rather, I will kill Ubayy. Then he said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if this had happened to me, to the people of Dhu’l-Majaz, they would all have died. So he died in the Fire, So, damnation to the companions of the Blaze. Musa ibn Uqbah narrated it in his Maghāzī, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, in a similar manner. Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, leaned against the ravine, Ubayy ibn Khalaf caught up with him and said: I will not be saved if I am saved. The people said: O Messenger of God, let one of us help him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Leave him. When he approached, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took the spear from al-Harith ibn al-Samma. Some of the people said: What was mentioned to me? When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it from him, he shook it so hard that we all flew away from him as hair flies from the back of a camel when it shakes. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, faced him and stabbed him in the neck with a stab that caused him to fall off his horse. Repeatedly - Al-Waqidi mentioned on the authority of Yunus bin Bakir on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Asim bin Amr bin Qatada, on the authority of Abdullah bin Kaab bin Malik, on the authority of his father, something similar to that. Al-Waqidi said: Ibn Omar used to say, “My father bin Khalaf died in Batn Rabigh. I was walking in Batn Rabigh after a part of the night, when I saw a blazing fire. I woke up and saw a man coming out of it with a chain, pulling it, arousing his thirst. A man said, “Do not give him a drink, for this is the one who was killed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” This is Abi bin Khalaf - and it was proven in the two Sahihs from the narration of Abd al-Razzaq from Muammar, from Hammam bin Munabbih from Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘God’s wrath was intense against a people who did something to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace’ - and he was pointing to his front teeth - and God’s wrath was intense against a man whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed in the way of God.” Al-Bukhari also included it from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj from Amr bin Dinar, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: “God’s wrath was intense against a person whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed with his own hand in the way of God, and God’s wrath was intense against a people who caused blood to flow from the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Ibn Ishaq said: “The front teeth of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were injured, his cheek was wounded, and his lip was wounded.” The one who injured him was Utbah bin Abi Waqqas, and Salih bin Kaysan told me, from someone who told him, from Saad bin Abi Waqqas, who said: I have never been so keen on killing anyone as I was keen on killing Utbah. Ibn Abi Waqqas, if what I know is of a man of bad character who is hated by his people, and the saying of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “God’s wrath is severe on whoever bleeds the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace,” is sufficient for me. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar informed us on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Uthman al-Jazari, on the authority of Muqsim, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “supplicated against Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas on the day of Uhud when his front tooth was broken and his face was bleed, and he said: O God, do not let a year pass over him until he dies as a disbeliever.” So a year had not passed over him until he died as a disbeliever in the Fire. Al-Waqidi mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abi Sabra, on the authority of Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Farwah, on the authority of Abu al-Huwayrith, on the authority of Nafi’ ibn Jubayr, who said: I heard a man from the Muhajireen say: I witnessed Uhud and I saw arrows coming from every direction and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the middle of them, all of that was being diverted from him. I saw Abdullah ibn Shihab al-Zuhri saying on that day: Show me Muhammad, I will not be saved if he is saved, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was beside him with no one with him, then… He passed by him, and Safwan rebuked him for that. He said, “By God, I have never seen him. I swear to God that he is forbidden from us!” We went out four of us and we pledged and agreed to kill him, but we did not succeed in that. Al-Waqidi said: What is established with us is that the one who shot the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the cheeks was Ibn Qami’ah, and the one who caused his lip to bleed and his front tooth to be damaged was Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Ibn al-Mubarak told us on the authority of Ishaq ibn Yahya ibn Talhah ibn Ubayd God, Isa ibn Talhah told me on the authority of the Mother of the Believers Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: Whenever Abu Bakr mentioned the Battle of Uhud, he would say: That day was all for Talhah. Then he began to narrate, he said: I was the first to return on the Battle of Uhud, and I saw a man fighting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, behind him, and I think he said it was out of zeal. He said: I said: Talhah was where I missed what I missed, so I said: There is a man from my people who is dearer to me, and between me and the polytheists is a man I do not know, and I am closer to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, than he, and he walks quickly, and I do not remember it, and it was Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah. We went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: His front tooth was broken and his face was wounded, and two rings from the helmet’s ring entered his cheek. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Your companion wants Talhah, and he was bleeding, but we did not pay attention to what he said. He said, “I went to remove that from his face, but Abu Ubaidah said, ‘I swear to you by my right that you left me,’ so I left him. He did not want to take it with his hand and hurt the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he leaned on him with his mouth and pulled out one of the rings, and his front tooth fell out with the ring. I went to do what he did, but he said, ‘I swear to you by my right that you left me.’ He said, ‘So he did the same as he did the first time, and his other front tooth fell out with the ring. Abu Ubaidah was the best of people in his wounds. We fixed the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then we came to Talhah in one of those graves, and there were seventy-odd, or less, or more, from stab wounds, arrows, and blows, and his finger had been cut off, so we fixed the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.’” And when Al-Haitham came, Abu Ubaidah said: I ask you by God, O Abu Bakr, to leave me alone? So Abu Ubaidah took the arrow in his mouth and began to shake it out of dislike of hurting the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he pulled out the arrow in his mouth and Abu Ubaidah’s front tooth fell out. He mentioned the rest of it, and Al-Hafiz Al-Dhiya Al-Maqdisi chose it in his book. Ali bin Al-Madini declared this hadith weak on the authority of Ishaq bin Yahya, because Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan, Ahmad, Yahya bin Ma’een, Al-Bukhari, Abu Zur’ah, Abu Hatim, Muhammad bin Sa’d, Al-Nasa’i and others spoke about him. Ibn Wahb said: Amr bin Al-Harith informed me that Umar bin Al-Sa’ib told him that he had heard that when Malik, Abu Abi Saeed Al-Khudri, was wounded by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud, he sucked the wound until it became clean and white, so it was said to him: Suck it in. He said: No, by God, I will never suck it in. Then he turned back to fight. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever wants to look at a man from the people of Paradise, let him look at this man, and he was martyred. It has been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Abi Hazim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sahl bin Sa`d, that he was asked about the wound of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: The face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was wounded, his front tooth was broken, and the egg was smashed on his head, may God bless him and grant him peace. Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was washing the blood, and Ali was pouring water on him with a shield. When Fatima saw that the water only increased the blood, she took a piece of matting and burned it until it became ashes, then she stuck it to the wound and the blood stopped. God Almighty said: So He rewarded you with grief for grief meaning He repaid you with grief for grief, as the Arabs say: It descended upon the Banu so-and-so, and it descended upon the Banu so-and-so. Ibn Jarir said: And likewise his saying, And I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, meaning on the trunks of palm trees. Ibn Abbas said: The first grief was due to the defeat, and when it was said that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was killed, and the second was when the polytheists overtook them on the mountain, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, they have no right to overtake us. And from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: The first grief was due to the defeat, and the second was when it was said that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was killed. That was more severe and greater for them than the defeat. Both were narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, and something similar was narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab, and Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned something similar from Qatadah as well. Al-Suddi said: The first grief was due to what they missed of the spoils and conquest, and the second was due to the enemy’s presence over them. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: So He rewarded you with grief after grief, meaning distress after distress from the killing of those of your brothers, and the superiority of your enemy over you, and what occurred in your souls from the saying of those who said: Your Prophet was killed, so that was one grief after another for you. Mujahid and Qatadah said: The grief The first is their hearing of the killing of Muhammad, and the second is what happened to them in terms of killing and wounds. Qatada and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said the opposite. Al-Suddi said: The first is what they missed out on in terms of victory and spoils, and the second is the enemy’s presence upon them. This statement from Al-Suddi has already been mentioned. Ibn Jarir said: The most correct of these sayings is the saying of the one who said, So He rewarded you with grief for grief. So He rewarded you with your grief, O believers, by God’s deprivation of you of the spoils of the polytheists and victory over them and the victory over them, and what befell you of killing and wounds, on that day after He had shown you in all of that what you love by your disobedience to the command of your Lord, and your opposition to the command of your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the grief of your thinking that your Prophet had been killed and the enemy had turned against you after your remnants from them. And the Almighty’s saying, So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you, meaning over what has escaped you of the spoils and victory over your enemy, nor over what has befallen you, of wounds and killing, said Ibn Abbas, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Suddi, And God is Aware of what you do. Glory be to Him and praise be to Him, there is no god but Him, the Most High.
3:154: The Almighty says, thanking His servants for what He sent down upon them of tranquility and security, which is the drowsiness that overcame them while they were ready to carry their weapons in a state of worry and grief, and drowsiness in such a state is evidence of safety, as the Almighty said in Surat Al-Anfal in the story of Badr, When drowsiness overcame you as a security from Him the verse, and Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Abu Naeem Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Razin, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: Drowsiness in battle is from God and in prayer is from Satan, and Al-Bukhari said and Khalifa told me: Yazid bin Zurai’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of Abu Talha, who said: I was among those who were overcome by drowsiness on the day of Uhud, until my sword fell from my hand repeatedly, it would fall and I would catch it, and it would fall and I would catch it, and thus he narrated it in Al-Maghazi with a chain of transmission, and he narrated it in the Book of Interpretation with a chain of transmission on the authority of Shaiban On the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of Abu Talha, he said: We were overcome by drowsiness while we were in our ranks on the day of Uhud. He said: My sword kept falling from my hand and I would grab it, and it would fall and I would grab it. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i and Al-Hakim from the hadith of Hammad bin Salamah, from Thabit, from Anas, from Abu Talhah, who said: I raised my head on the day of Uhud and looked, and there was not one of them that day except that he was leaning under his veil from drowsiness. The wording of Al-Tirmidhi, who said: Hasan Sahih. It was also narrated by Al-Nasa’i, from Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna, from Khalid bin Al-Harith, from Abu Qutaybah, from Ibn Abi Uday, both of them from Humayd, from Anas, who said: Abu Talhah said: I was among those upon whom drowsiness was cast. The hadith, and this is how it was narrated from Al-Zubayr and Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf. Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz told us, Abu Al-Husayn Muhammad bin Ya’qub told me, Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-Thaqafi told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak Al-Makhzumi told us, Yunus bin Muhammad told us, Shaiban told us from Qatada, Anas bin Malik told us that Abu Talhah said: Drowsiness overcame us while we were in our ranks on the day of Uhud, so my sword was placed on the ground. It falls from my hand and I pick it up and it falls and I pick it up. He said: The other group, the hypocrites, have no concern but themselves, the most cowardly, reckless and neglectful of the truth. They think about God other than the truth, the thought of the Age of Ignorance. That is, they are liars, people of doubt and suspicion about God Almighty. This is how he narrated it with this addition, as if it were the words of Qatada, may God have mercy on him, and it is as he said, for God Almighty says: Then He sent down upon you, after the distress, security, a drowsiness that overcame a party of you. That is, the people of faith, certainty, steadfastness and sincere trust, and they are those who are certain that God Almighty will support His Messenger and fulfill his hopes. For this reason, He said: And a party whose souls are concerned, that is, they are not overcome by drowsiness from anxiety, panic and fear. They think about God other than the truth, the thought of the Age of Ignorance. As He said in the other verse: Rather, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families. to the end of the verse. And thus these people believed that when the polytheists appeared at that moment, it was the decisive moment and that Islam and its people had perished. This is the way of the people of doubt and suspicion when something happens. The terrible thing is that these heinous suspicions happen to them, then the Almighty told about them that they say in that situation Do we have any part in the matter? So the Almighty said: “Say: The matter is entirely God’s. They conceal within themselves that which they do not reveal to you.” Then He explained what they concealed within themselves by saying: “They say: If we had any part in the matter, we would not have been killed here.” That is, they concealed this statement from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Ishaq said: Yahya bin Ibad bin Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr, who said: Az-Zubayr said: I saw myself with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when fear became intense for us, God sent sleep upon us, and there was not a man among us except that his chin was on his chest. He said: By God, I hear the words of Mu’tab bin Qushayr, and I hear them only as if they were in a dream, saying: If we had any part in the matter, we would not have been killed here. So I memorized it from him, and in that regard God revealed: “They say: If we had any part in the matter, we would not have been killed here,” based on the words of Mu’tab. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. God the Almighty said: “Say: ‘If you had been in your houses, those for whom death was decreed would have come forth to their deathbeds. ’” That is, this is a decree that God the Almighty has decreed and a definite judgment from which there is no escape or escape. God the Almighty said: And that God may test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts. That is, He tests you with what happened to you to distinguish the wicked from the good and to reveal to people the matter of the believer from the hypocrite in words and deeds. And God is Knowing of that within the breasts. That is, what is in the breasts of the secrets and consciences. Then God the Almighty said: Indeed, those of you who turned back on the day the two armies met, Satan caused them to slip only because of what they had earned. That is, because of some of their previous sins, as some of the predecessors said: The reward for a good deed is a good deed after it, and the punishment for a bad deed is a bad deed after it. Then God the Almighty said: And God has pardoned them. That is, what they had done of fleeing. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Forbearing. That is, He forgives sins and is patient with His creation and overlooks them. The hadith of Ibn Umar regarding Uthman and his turning back on the day of Uhud was presented, and that God pardoned him along with those who pardoned. On their authority when he said: And God has pardoned them. And it is appropriate to mention it here. Imam Ahmad said: Muawiyah bin Amr told us, Zaidah told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Shuqaiq, who said: Abd al-Rahman bin Awf met al-Walid bin Uqbah, and al-Walid said to him: Why do I see you being so estranged from the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman? Abd al-Rahman said to him: Tell him that I did not flee on the day of Hunayn. Asim said: He says on the day of UHud 11:And I did not stay behind from Badr, and I did not abandon the Sunnah of Umar. He said: So go and tell Uthman about that. He said: Uthman said: As for his saying that I did not flee on the day of Hunayn, how can he reproach me for a sin that God has pardoned? God the Almighty said: “Indeed, those of you who turned back on the day the two armies met, Satan only made them slip because of some of what they had earned. But God has pardoned them.” As for his saying that I stayed behind on the day of Badr, I was nursing Ruqayyah, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until she died, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, struck me with an arrow, and whoever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, struck an arrow for, then he has testified. As for his saying that I abandoned the Sunnah of Umar, then I do not… I can't stand her and neither can he, so go and tell him about it.

3:156: God Almighty forbids His believing servants from resembling the infidels in their corrupt belief, indicated by their statement about their brothers who died in travels and wars, if they had abandoned that what happened to them would not have happened to them, so God Almighty said: O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved and said about their brothers meaning about their brothers when they traveled throughout the land meaning they traveled for trade and the like or were fighting meaning they were in a war if they had been with us meaning in the country they would not have died nor been killed meaning they would not have died in the travels, nor were they killed in the war. And God Almighty said: that God may make that a regret in their hearts meaning He created this belief in their souls so that they would increase their regret over their death and killing. Then God Almighty said in response to them: And God gives life and causes death meaning in His hand is creation and to Him the matter returns, and no one lives or dies except by His will and decree, and no one’s life is increased or decreased except by His judgment and decree. And God is Knowing of what you do. “All-Seeing” means that His knowledge and insight are penetrating into all of His creation. Nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him. The Almighty’s statement: And if you are killed in the cause of God or die, forgiveness from God and mercy are better than what they accumulate. This includes that killing in the cause of God and death as well are a means to attaining God’s mercy, pardon and pleasure, and that is better than remaining in this world collecting its perishable debris. Then the Almighty informed us that everyone who dies or is killed, his fate and return is to God, the Almighty, the Majestic, and He will reward him for his deeds, if good then good, and if evil then evil, so the Almighty said: And if you die or are killed, to God you will be gathered.

3:159: The Almighty says, addressing His Messenger, thanking him and the believers for what He softened his heart with towards his nation who followed his command, abandoned his warning, and made his words pleasant to them: Then by the mercy of God, you were gentle with them. That is, what made you gentle with them, were it not for God’s mercy upon you and them? Qatada said: Then by the mercy of God, you were gentle with them. He says: Then by the mercy of God, you were gentle with them. What is the connection? The Arabs connect it with the definite article, as in His statement: Then by their breaking of their covenant. And with the indefinite article, as in His statement: In a little while. And thus here he said: Then by the mercy of God, you were gentle with them. That is, by the mercy of God. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: This is the character of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with which God sent him. And this noble verse is similar to the statement of the Almighty: “There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer; he is concerned over you and to the believers is kind and merciful.” And Imam Ahmad said: Haywah told us, Baqiyah told us, Muhammad bin Ziyad told us. Abu Rashid Al-Habrani told me: Abu Umamah Al-Bahili took my hand and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took my hand and said: O Abu Umamah, among the believers is he whose heart is soft towards me. Ahmad alone transmitted this. Then God, the Most High, said: And if you had been rude [in speech] and harsh [in heart], they would have disbanded from around you. The rude is the harsh, and what is meant by it here is harsh in speech, because He said after that harsh in heart, meaning if you had been bad in speech and hard-hearted towards them, they would have disbanded from you and left you, but God gathered them around you and made you gentle towards them to win their hearts over, as Abdullah bin Amr said: “I see the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the earlier books that he is not rude, nor harsh, nor loud in the markets, and he does not repay evil with evil, but he pardons and forgives.” Abu Ismail Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Tirmidhi said: Bishr bin Ubaid Al-Darimi informed us, Ammar bin Abd Al-Rahman informed us, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: God has commanded me to be lenient with people, just as He has commanded me to establish the obligatory duties. This is a strange hadith. That is why God the Almighty said: So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter. That is why the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to consult his companions about a matter whenever it happened, to please their hearts so that they would be more active in what they did, as he consulted them on the day of Badr about going to the caravan, and they said: “O Messenger of God, if you were to parade us across the sea, we would cross it with you, and if you were to take us to Barak al-Ghamad, we would go with you, and we will not say to you as the people of Moses said to Moses: Go, you and your Lord, and fight, for we are sitting here. Rather, we say: Go, for we are with you, in front of you, and on your right and on your left, fighting.” He also consulted them about where the camp would be, until Al-Mundhir bin Amr Al-Mu’naq indicated to die by advancing to the front of the people. He consulted them about whether he should stay in the city or go out to the enemy. Most of them suggested going out to them. So he went out to them and consulted them on the day of the Trench about reconciling with the confederates for a third of the fruits of the city that year. The two Saads, Saad bin Muadh and Saad bin Ubadah, refused him that, so he left that. He consulted them on the day of Hudaybiyyah about attacking the children of the polytheists. Abu Bakr said to him: We did not come to fight anyone, but we came to perform Umrah. So he agreed to what he said. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said in the story of the slander: “Advise me, O Muslims, about a people who destroyed my family and threw stones at them. By God, I do not know of any evil against my family, and who did they destroy them for? By God, I only know of good about him.” He consulted Ali and Usama about separating from Aisha may God be pleased with her. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to consult them in wars and the like. The jurists differed as to whether that was obligatory upon him or recommended to please their hearts. There are two opinions. Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Baghdadi informed us, Yahya ibn Ayyub al-`Alaf told us in Egypt, Sa`id ibn Abi Maryam told us, Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah told us, on the authority of `Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding the words of God the Almighty: And consult them in the matter. He said: Abu Bakr and `Umar, may God be pleased with them. Then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it. Al-Kalbi narrated it likewise on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: It was revealed about Abu Bakr and `Umar, and they were the disciples of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his ministers, and the fathers of the Muslims. Imam Ahmad narrated: Waki` told us, `Abd al-Hamid told us on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanim, “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Bakr and `Umar, ‘If we met in consultation, I would not oppose you.’” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of `Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about determination. He said: Consulting people of opinion, then following them.” Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Bakir narrated to us, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Abdul Malik ibn Umair, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The one who is consulted is trustworthy. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it, and al-Nasa’i authenticated it from the hadith of Abdul Malik ibn Umair with a more detailed chain of transmission than this. Then Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Aswad ibn Amir narrated to us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Amr al-Shaibani, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The one who is consulted is trustworthy.” He was the only one to narrate it. He also said: Abu Bakr narrated to us, Yahya ibn Zakariya ibn Abi Zaydah and Ali ibn Hashim narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If one of you consults his brother, let him advise him. He was also the only one to narrate it. And the Almighty’s saying: So when you have decided, then rely upon God meaning if you consult them about the matter and are determined to do it, then rely upon God in it Indeed, God loves those who rely [upon Him]. And the Almighty’s saying: If God helps you, none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? And in God let the believers rely. And this verse is as it was mentioned before from His saying: And victory comes only from God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Then He commanded them to rely upon Him, saying: And in God let the believers rely. And the Almighty’s saying: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan and more than one said: It is not befitting for a prophet to betray. And Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Al-Musayyab bin Wadheeh told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari told us on the authority of Sufyan bin Khasif on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They lost a quilt on the day of Badr, so they said: Perhaps the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it, so God revealed: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils, meaning betray. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib told us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, Khasif told us, Muqsim told us, Ibn Abbas told me that this verse, And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war, was revealed concerning a red cloak that was lost on the day of Badr. Some people said: Perhaps the Messenger of God had taken it, and they talked a lot about that, so God revealed, “And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war. And whoever takes spoils of war will come with what he has taken on the Day of Resurrection.” Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi both narrated it in the same way on the authority of Qutaybah, on the authority of Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and strange. Some of them narrated it on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Muqsim, meaning in a mursal form. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The hypocrites accused the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) of something he had lost, so God revealed: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas through other chains of transmission similar to what was mentioned above. This is to exonerate him (blessings and peace of God be upon him) from all forms of treachery in fulfilling the trust, dividing the spoils of war, and other things. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war meaning that he would divide some of the spoils for the sake of the army and leave others. Ad-Dahhak said the same. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war meaning that he would leave some of what was revealed to him and not convey it to his nation. Al-Hasan al-Basri, Tawus, Mujahid, and Ad-Dahhak recited: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war with a damma on the ya’, meaning that he would betray. Qatada and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: This verse was revealed on the day of Badr, and some of his companions had taken spoils of war. Ibn Jarir narrated it from them, then he narrated from some of them that he interpreted this reading to mean that he is accused of treason, then God Almighty said: “And whoever embezzles will come with what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.” This is a severe threat and a definite warning. The Sunnah also forbade this in multiple hadiths. Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Malik told us, Zuhair told us, meaning Ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah Ibn Muhammad Ibn Aqil, from Ata Ibn Yasar, from Abu Malik Al-Ashja’i, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The greatest embezzlement before God is an arm’s length of land. You will find two men running after each other on the land - or in the house - and one of them will cut off an arm’s length from the share of his companion, and if he cuts it off, he will be hung around his neck from seven earths until the Day of Resurrection.” Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Musa bin Dawud told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Ibn Hubayrah and Al-Harith bin Yazid, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Jubayr, who said: I heard Al-Mustawrid bin Shaddad say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever is given a job and does not have a house, let him get a house. Or he does not have a wife, let him get married. Or he does not have a servant, let him get a servant. Or he does not have a mount, let him get a mount. And whoever acquires something other than that, then he is a thief.” This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it. Abu Dawud narrated it with another chain of narration and context, saying: Musa bin Marwan al-Raqi narrated to us, al-Mu'afi narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, on the authority of al-Harith bin Yazid, on the authority of Jubayr bin Nufayr, on the authority of al-Mustawrid bin Shaddad, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: "Whoever works for us, let him acquire a wife. If he does not have a servant, let him acquire a servant. If he does not have a home, let him acquire a home." He said: Abu Bakr said: I was told that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever does anything other than that is a transgressor or a thief." Our Sheikh, al-Hafiz al-Mizzi, may God have mercy on him, said: It was narrated by Ja'far bin Muhammad al-Faryabi on the authority of Musa bin Marwan, and he said: On the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Jubayr instead of Jubayr bin Nufayr, and this is more likely to be correct. Another hadith - Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Hafs ibn Bishr told us, Yaqub al-Qummi told us, Hafs ibn Humayd told us on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a bleating sheep and calling out: O Muhammad, O Muhammad.’ I will say: ‘I have no power over anything from God for you, I have conveyed it to you.’ I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a braying camel and calling out: O Muhammad, O Muhammad.’ I will say: ‘I have no power over anything from God for you, I have conveyed it to you.’ I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a neighing horse and calling out: O Muhammad, O Muhammad.’ I will say: ‘I have no power over anything from God for you, I have conveyed it to you.’ I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a leather husk and calling out: O Muhammad, O Muhammad.’ I will say: ‘I have no power over anything from God for you, I have conveyed it to you.’” None of the people of the six books narrated it. Another hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, he heard Urwah say: Abu Hamid Al-Sa’idi narrated to us: He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed a man from Azd called Ibn Al-Lutbiyyah to collect the zakat.
