Then he said: I recited from the mouth of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, seventy surahs. Should I abandon what I took from the mouth of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? And Wakee’ narrated in his interpretation on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: When the copies of the Qur’an were ordered to be burned, Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: O people, steal the copies of the Qur’an, for whoever steals it will bring what he stole on the Day of Resurrection. And what a good stealing copy of the Qur’an one of you will bring on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Dawud said, on the authority of Samurah bin Jundub, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, captured a booty, he would command Bilal to call out to the people, and they would bring their spoils, and he would take a fifth of it and divide it. Then a man came one day after The call was made with a bridle of hair. He said: O Messenger of God, this was from what we obtained from the spoils. He said: Did you hear Bilal calling three times? He said: Yes. He said: What prevented you from coming? So he apologized to him. He said: No, you will come with it on the Day of Resurrection and I will not accept it from you. And the Almighty said: Is he who pursues the pleasure of God like he who incurs the wrath of God and whose refuge is Hell, and an evil destination? That is, he who pursues the pleasure of God in what He has prescribed and thus deserves the pleasure of God and His abundant reward, and is protected from His severe punishment, is not equal to he who deserves the wrath of God and is bound by it, and there is no escape for him from it, and his refuge on the Day of Resurrection is Hell, and an evil destination. This verse has many parallels in the Qur’an, such as the Almighty’s saying: Is he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like he who is blind? and His saying: Is he to whom We have promised a good promise and he will attain it like he to whom We have given enjoyment of the enjoyment of worldly life? Then God the Almighty said: They are of degrees with God. Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Muhammad bin Ishaq said: meaning the people of good and the people of evil have degrees. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Kisa’i said: Stations, meaning they differ in their stations and degrees in Paradise and their levels in Hell, like the Almighty’s saying: And for all are degrees according to what they have done verse. That is why the Almighty said: And God is Seeing of what they do verse, meaning He will give them what they deserve. He will not wrong them with good nor increase their evil, rather He will reward each worker according to his work. The Almighty said: God has certainly conferred a great favor upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves verse, meaning from their own kind so that they could address him, ask him, sit with him, and benefit from him, as the Almighty said: And among His signs is that He created for you from among yourselves mates that you may find tranquility in them verse, meaning from your own kind. The Almighty said: “Say, ‘I am only a man like you. It has been revealed to me that your God is one God’” verse. God the Almighty said: And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets. God the Almighty said: And We did not send before you any except men to whom We revealed from the people of the towns. God the Almighty said: O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you? This is more eloquent in gratitude that the messenger to them should be from among them, such that they can address him and consult him in understanding the speech on his behalf. For this reason God the Almighty said: He recites to them His verses meaning the Qur’an and purifies them meaning he commands them to do good and forbids them from evil so that their souls may be purified and cleansed from the filth and evil that they were immersed in during their state of polytheism and ignorance, and teaches them the Book and wisdom meaning the Qur’an and the Sunnah, although they were before meaning before this Messenger in manifest error meaning in clear error and ignorance that is evident to everyone.
3:162: The Almighty says, addressing His Messenger, thanking him and the believers for what He softened his heart with towards his nation who followed his command, abandoned his warning, and made his words pleasant to them: Then by the mercy of God, you were gentle with them. That is, what made you gentle with them, were it not for God’s mercy upon you and them? Qatada said: Then by the mercy of God, you were gentle with them. He says: Then by the mercy of God, you were gentle with them. What is the connection? The Arabs connect it with the definite article, as in His statement: Then by their breaking of their covenant. And with the indefinite article, as in His statement: In a little while. And thus here he said: Then by the mercy of God, you were gentle with them. That is, by the mercy of God. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: This is the character of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with which God sent him. And this noble verse is similar to the statement of the Almighty: “There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer; he is concerned over you and to the believers is kind and merciful.” And Imam Ahmad said: Haywah told us, Baqiyah told us, Muhammad bin Ziyad told us. Abu Rashid Al-Habrani told me: Abu Umamah Al-Bahili took my hand and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took my hand and said: O Abu Umamah, among the believers is he whose heart is soft towards me. Ahmad alone transmitted this. Then God, the Most High, said: And if you had been rude [in speech] and harsh [in heart], they would have disbanded from around you. The rude is the harsh, and what is meant by it here is harsh in speech, because He said after that harsh in heart, meaning if you had been bad in speech and hard-hearted towards them, they would have disbanded from you and left you, but God gathered them around you and made you gentle towards them to win their hearts over, as Abdullah bin Amr said: “I see the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the earlier books that he is not rude, nor harsh, nor loud in the markets, and he does not repay evil with evil, but he pardons and forgives.” Abu Ismail Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Tirmidhi said: Bishr bin Ubaid Al-Darimi informed us, Ammar bin Abd Al-Rahman informed us, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: God has commanded me to be lenient with people, just as He has commanded me to establish the obligatory duties. This is a strange hadith. That is why God the Almighty said: So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter. That is why the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to consult his companions about a matter whenever it happened, to please their hearts so that they would be more active in what they did, as he consulted them on the day of Badr about going to the caravan, and they said: “O Messenger of God, if you were to parade us across the sea, we would cross it with you, and if you were to take us to Barak al-Ghamad, we would go with you, and we will not say to you as the people of Moses said to Moses: Go, you and your Lord, and fight, for we are sitting here. Rather, we say: Go, for we are with you, in front of you, and on your right and on your left, fighting.” He also consulted them about where the camp would be, until Al-Mundhir bin Amr Al-Mu’naq indicated to die by advancing to the front of the people. He consulted them about whether he should stay in the city or go out to the enemy. Most of them suggested going out to them. So he went out to them and consulted them on the day of the Trench about reconciling with the confederates for a third of the fruits of the city that year. The two Saads, Saad bin Muadh and Saad bin Ubadah, refused him that, so he left that. He consulted them on the day of Hudaybiyyah about attacking the children of the polytheists. Abu Bakr said to him: We did not come to fight anyone, but we came to perform Umrah. So he agreed to what he said. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said in the story of the slander: “Advise me, O Muslims, about a people who destroyed my family and threw stones at them. By God, I do not know of any evil against my family, and who did they destroy them for? By God, I only know of good about him.” He consulted Ali and Usama about separating from Aisha may God be pleased with her. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to consult them in wars and the like. The jurists differed as to whether that was obligatory upon him or recommended to please their hearts. There are two opinions. Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Baghdadi informed us, Yahya ibn Ayyub al-`Alaf told us in Egypt, Sa`id ibn Abi Maryam told us, Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah told us, on the authority of `Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding the words of God the Almighty: And consult them in the matter. He said: Abu Bakr and `Umar, may God be pleased with them. Then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it. Al-Kalbi narrated it likewise on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: It was revealed about Abu Bakr and `Umar, and they were the disciples of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his ministers, and the fathers of the Muslims. Imam Ahmad narrated: Waki` told us, `Abd al-Hamid told us on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanim, “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Bakr and `Umar, ‘If we met in consultation, I would not oppose you.’” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of `Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about determination. He said: Consulting people of opinion, then following them.” Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Bakir narrated to us, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Abdul Malik ibn Umair, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The one who is consulted is trustworthy. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it, and al-Nasa’i authenticated it from the hadith of Abdul Malik ibn Umair with a more detailed chain of transmission than this. Then Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Aswad ibn Amir narrated to us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Amr al-Shaibani, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The one who is consulted is trustworthy.” He was the only one to narrate it. He also said: Abu Bakr narrated to us, Yahya ibn Zakariya ibn Abi Zaydah and Ali ibn Hashim narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If one of you consults his brother, let him advise him. He was also the only one to narrate it. And the Almighty’s saying: So when you have decided, then rely upon God meaning if you consult them about the matter and are determined to do it, then rely upon God in it Indeed, God loves those who rely [upon Him]. And the Almighty’s saying: If God helps you, none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? And in God let the believers rely. And this verse is as it was mentioned before from His saying: And victory comes only from God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Then He commanded them to rely upon Him, saying: And in God let the believers rely. And the Almighty’s saying: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan and more than one said: It is not befitting for a prophet to betray. And Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Al-Musayyab bin Wadheeh told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari told us on the authority of Sufyan bin Khasif on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They lost a quilt on the day of Badr, so they said: Perhaps the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it, so God revealed: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils, meaning betray. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib told us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, Khasif told us, Muqsim told us, Ibn Abbas told me that this verse, And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war, was revealed concerning a red cloak that was lost on the day of Badr. Some people said: Perhaps the Messenger of God had taken it, and they talked a lot about that, so God revealed, “And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war. And whoever takes spoils of war will come with what he has taken on the Day of Resurrection.” Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi both narrated it in the same way on the authority of Qutaybah, on the authority of Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and strange. Some of them narrated it on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Muqsim, meaning in a mursal form. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The hypocrites accused the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) of something he had lost, so God revealed: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas through other chains of transmission similar to what was mentioned above. This is to exonerate him (blessings and peace of God be upon him) from all forms of treachery in fulfilling the trust, dividing the spoils of war, and other things. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war meaning that he would divide some of the spoils for the sake of the army and leave others. Ad-Dahhak said the same. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war meaning that he would leave some of what was revealed to him and not convey it to his nation. Al-Hasan al-Basri, Tawus, Mujahid, and Ad-Dahhak recited: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war with a damma on the ya’, meaning that he would betray. Qatada and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: This verse was revealed on the day of Badr, and some of his companions had taken spoils of war. Ibn Jarir narrated it from them, then he narrated from some of them that he interpreted this reading to mean that he is accused of treason, then God Almighty said: “And whoever embezzles will come with what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.” This is a severe threat and a definite warning. The Sunnah also forbade this in multiple hadiths. Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Malik told us, Zuhair told us, meaning Ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah Ibn Muhammad Ibn Aqil, from Ata Ibn Yasar, from Abu Malik Al-Ashja’i, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The greatest embezzlement before God is an arm’s length of land. You will find two men running after each other on the land - or in the house - and one of them will cut off an arm’s length from the share of his companion, and if he cuts it off, he will be hung around his neck from seven earths until the Day of Resurrection.” Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Musa bin Dawud told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Ibn Hubayrah and Al-Harith bin Yazid, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Jubayr, who said: I heard Al-Mustawrid bin Shaddad say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever is given a job and does not have a house, let him get a house. Or he does not have a wife, let him get married. Or he does not have a servant, let him get a servant. Or he does not have a mount, let him get a mount. And whoever acquires something other than that, then he is a thief.” This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it. Abu Dawud narrated it with another chain of narration and context, saying: Musa bin Marwan al-Raqi narrated to us, al-Mu'afi narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, on the authority of al-Harith bin Yazid, on the authority of Jubayr bin Nufayr, on the authority of al-Mustawrid bin Shaddad, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: "Whoever works for us, let him acquire a wife. If he does not have a servant, let him acquire a servant. If he does not have a home, let him acquire a home." He said: Abu Bakr said: I was told that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever does anything other than that is a transgressor or a thief. Our Sheikh, al-Hafiz al-Mizzi, may God have mercy on him, said: It was narrated by Ja'far bin Muhammad al-Faryabi on the authority of Musa bin Marwan, and he said: On the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Jubayr instead of Jubayr bin Nufayr, and this is more likely to be correct. Another hadith - Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Hafs ibn Bishr told us, Yaqub al-Qummi told us, Hafs ibn Humayd told us on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a bleating sheep and calling out: O Muhammad, O Muhammad.’ I will say: ‘I have no power over anything from God for you, I have conveyed it to you.’ I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a braying camel and calling out: O Muhammad, O Muhammad.’ I will say: ‘I have no power over anything from God for you, I have conveyed it to you.’ I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a neighing horse and calling out: O Muhammad, O Muhammad.’ I will say: ‘I have no power over anything from God for you, I have conveyed it to you.’ I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a leather husk and calling out: O Muhammad, O Muhammad.’ I will say: ‘I have no power over anything from God for you, I have conveyed it to you.’” None of the people of the six books narrated it. Another hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, he heard Urwah say: Abu Hamid Al-Sa’idi narrated to us: He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed a man from Azd called Ibn Al-Lutbiyyah to collect the zakat. He came and said: This is for you and this was given to me. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood on the pulpit and said: What is the matter with the worker whom we send and he comes and says: This is for you and this was given to me. Why did he not sit in the house of his father and mother and see whether he was given a gift or not? By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, none of you will bring anything of it except that he will bring it on the Day of Resurrection on his neck, whether it is a camel that roars, or a cow that moos, or a sheep that bleats. Then he raised his hands until we saw the whiteness of his armpits. Then he said: O God, have I conveyed the message?” Hisham bin Urwah added: Abu Hamid said: I saw it with my eyes and heard it with my ears. Ask Zaid bin Thabit. They both narrated it on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah. Al-Bukhari has: Ask Zaid bin Thabit. And others. A face on the authority of Al-Zuhri, and through a path on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, both on the authority of Urwah, on his authority. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq bin Isa told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Abu Hamid, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The gifts of workers are misappropriation.” This hadith is one of the individual hadiths of Ahmad, and its chain of transmission is weak, and it seems to be an abbreviation of the one before it, and God knows best. Another hadith - Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi said in the Book of Rulings: Abu Kurayb told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Yazid Al-Awdi, on the authority of Al-Mughirah bin Shibl, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim, on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me to Yemen, and when I set out, he sent after me, but I returned. He said, ‘Do you know why I sent to you? Do not take anything without my permission, for it is embezzlement. ’ And whoever embezzles will come with what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection. ’ This is why I have called you, so go on with your work.” This is a good, strange hadith that we do not know except from this source. There are hadiths on this topic from Adi bin Umaira, Buraydah, Al-Mustawrid bin Shaddad, Abu Hamid, and Ibn Umar. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ismail bin Aliyah told us, Abu Hayyan Yahya bin Saeed Al-Taymi told us, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah bin Umar bin Jarir, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up among us one day and mentioned theft, and he magnified it and magnified its matter, then he said: ‘I will not find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel roaring on his neck, and he will say: O Messenger of God, help me,’ and I will say: ‘I have no power over God for you, I have conveyed the message to you.’ I will not find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a horse neighing on his neck, and he will say: O Messenger of God, help me,’ and I will say: ‘I have no power over God for you, I have conveyed the message to you.’ I will not find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a bandage on his neck that is strangling him, and he will say: O Messenger of God, help me,’ and I will say: ‘I have no power over God for you, I have conveyed the message to you.’ I will not find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a silent person on his neck, and he will say: O Messenger of God, help me,’ and I will say: ‘I have no power over God for you, I have conveyed the message to you.’ You have something from God that I have conveyed to you.” They narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hayyan. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told us on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, Qais told me on the authority of Adi bin Umaira Al-Kindi who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O people, whoever among you does work for us and conceals from us a needle or more of it, it is a stipulation that he will bring on the Day of Resurrection. He said: A black man from the Ansar stood up - Mujalid said: He is Saeed bin Ubadah, it is as if I am looking at him - and said: O Messenger of God, accept your work from me. He said: What is that? He said: I heard you say: such and such. He said: And I am saying that now. Whoever we appoint to a job, let him come with it, little or much, and whatever he is given from it, he takes, and whatever he is forbidden from, he ends.” And Muslim and Abu Dawud narrated it in the same way through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Manbuth, a man from the family of Abu Rafi’, told me on the authority of Al-Fadl bin Ubaidullah bin Abu Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, who said: “When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed the afternoon prayer, he would sometimes go to Banu Abd Al-Ashhal and talk to them until sunset. Abu Rafi’ said: “While the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was hurrying to the sunset prayer, he passed by Al-Baqi’ and said: ‘Uff to you, uf to you’ twice. He shouted at me and I held back and thought that he wanted me. He said: ‘What is the matter with you? Walk.’ I said: ‘I have done something new, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘What is that?’ I said: ‘Uff to me.’ He said: ‘No, but this is the grave of so-and-so. I sent him to seek out the family of so-and-so, and he stole a tiger and now his armor is like it, made of fire.’” Another hadith - Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Salem Al-Kufi, the paralytic, told us - and he was in Mecca - Ubaidah bin Al-Aswad told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Al-Waleed, on the authority of Abu Sadiq, on the authority of Rabia bin Najed, on the authority of Ubadah bin Al-Samit, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would take a hair from the side of the camel from the spoils of war and then say: I have nothing in it except what one of you has. Beware of embezzlement, for embezzlement is a disgrace for its perpetrator on the Day of Resurrection. Give back the thread and needle and what is above that, and strive in the cause of God near and far, at home and on the journey, for striving is one of the gates of Paradise, for God saves from worry and grief through it, and establish the limits of God in those near and far, and do not let the blame of a blamer deter you in God’s cause.” Ibn Majah narrated some of it on the authority of the paralytic. Another hadith - On the authority of Amr bin Shuaib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Return the tailor and the needle, for embezzlement is a disgrace, a fire, and a shame upon its people on the Day of Resurrection.” Another hadith - Abu Dawud said: Uthman bin Abi Shaybah told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Abu al-Jahm, on the authority of Abu Mas`ud al-Ansari, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me as a messenger, then he said: Go, Abu Mas`ud, lest I find you on the Day of Resurrection with a camel from the charity camels coming on your back, roaring, and you have tied it up.” He said: Then I will not go. He said: Then I will not hate you. Abu Dawud is the only one to report it. Another hadith - Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Ibrahim informed us, Muhammad bin Uthman bin Abi Shaybah informed us, Abdul Hamid bin Saleh informed us, Ahmad bin Aban informed us on the authority of Alqamah bin Murthad, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “A stone is thrown into Hell and it falls for seventy years without reaching its bottom, and the stolen goods are brought and thrown with them, then it is said to the one who stole them, ‘Bring them.’ This is what His statement means: ‘And whoever steals will bring what he stole on the Day of Resurrection.’” Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, Ikrimah bin Ammar told us, Samak Al-Hanafi Abu Zamil told me, Abdullah bin Abbas told me, Umar bin Al-Khattab told me: When the day of Khaybar came, a group of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and said: So-and-so is a martyr and so-and-so is a martyr, until they came to a man and said: So-and-so is a martyr. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, I saw him in the Fire in a cloak that he had stolen. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O son of Al-Khattab, go and announce to the al-Nas 114:‘None shall enter Paradise except the believers.’ So I went out and announced: ‘None shall enter Paradise except the believers.’” Muslim and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Ikrimah bin Ammar. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih. Another hadith - Ibn Jarir said: Saeed bin Yahya Al-Umawi told us, my father told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “sent Saad bin Ubadah as a tax collector, and he said: Beware, Saad, of coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel that you are carrying and it is bellowing. He said: I will not take it nor will I come with it, so he excused him.” Then he narrated it on the authority of Ubaidullah on the authority of Nafi’ in a similar manner. Another hadith - Ahmad said: Abu Saeed told us, Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad told us, Saleh bin Muhammad bin Zaida told us, on the authority of Salim bin Abdullah, that he was with Muslimah bin Abdul Malik in the land of the Romans, and he found stolen goods in a man’s belongings. He said: So he asked Salim bin Abdullah, and he said: My father Abdullah told me, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you find stolen goods in someone’s belongings, burn them - he said: And I think he said: And beat him. He said: So he took out his belongings in the market and found a Qur’an in them, so he asked Salim, and he said: Sell it and give its price in charity.” And this is how Ali bin Al-Madini, Abu Dawud, and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad Al-Atdarwardi. Abu Dawud and Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari added, both of them on the authority of Abu Waqid Al-Laithi Al-Sagheer, Saleh bin Muhammad bin Zaida with it. Ali ibn al-Madini, al-Bukhari and others said: This is a rejected hadith narrated by Abu Waqid. Al-Daraqutni said: The correct view is that it is only from the fatwa of Salim. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may God have mercy on him, and those of his companions who followed him held the view based on this hadith. Al-Umawi narrated it on the authority of Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: The punishment for the transgressor is that his saddlebags are taken out and burned with what is in them. Then he narrated on the authority of Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Uthman ibn Ata’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali, who said: The transgressor’s saddlebags are gathered together and burned and he is flogged without a prescribed punishment. Abu Hanifa, Malik, al-Shafi’i and the majority disagreed with him and said: The transgressor’s belongings are not to be burned, but he is to be punished with a punishment similar to his. Al-Bukhari said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, refrained from praying over the transgressor, but his belongings were not burned.” And God knows best. Another hadith on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with him - Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb told me, Abdullah ibn Wahb told me, Amr ibn al-Harith told me that Musa ibn Jubayr told him: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Habbab al-Ansari told him: Abdullah ibn Unais told him: He and Umar ibn al-Khattab were discussing charity one day, and he said: Didn’t you hear the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he mentioned the embezzlement of charity: Whoever embezzles a camel or a sheep from it, he will carry it on the Day of Resurrection? Abdullah ibn Unais said: Yes. Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Amr ibn Sawad on the authority of Abdullah ibn Wahb on his authority. Al-Umawi narrated it on the authority of Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: The punishment of the embezzler is that his saddle be taken out and burned with what is in it. Then he narrated on the authority of Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Uthman ibn Ata’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali, who said: The embezzler’s saddle is gathered up and burned and he is flogged without a prescribed punishment. Imam Ahmad said: Aswad bin Aamer told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Jubayr bin Malik, who said: The copies of the Qur’an were ordered to be changed. He said: Ibn Masoud said: Whoever among you can steal a copy of the Qur’an, let him steal it, for whoever steals something will bring it on the Day of Resurrection. Then he said: I recited from the mouth of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, seventy surahs. Should I abandon what I took from the mouth of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? And Wakee’ narrated in his interpretation on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: When the copies of the Qur’an were ordered to be burned, Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: O people, steal the copies of the Qur’an, for whoever steals it will bring what he stole on the Day of Resurrection. And what a good stealing copy of the Qur’an one of you will bring on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Dawud said, on the authority of Samurah bin Jundub, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, captured a booty, he would command Bilal to call out to the people, and they would bring their spoils, and he would take a fifth of it and divide it. Then a man came one day after The call was made with a bridle of hair. He said: O Messenger of God, this was from what we obtained from the spoils. He said: Did you hear Bilal calling three times? He said: Yes. He said: What prevented you from coming? So he apologized to him. He said: No, you will come with it on the Day of Resurrection and I will not accept it from you. And the Almighty said: Is he who pursues the pleasure of God like he who incurs the wrath of God and whose refuge is Hell, and an evil destination? That is, he who pursues the pleasure of God in what He has prescribed and thus deserves the pleasure of God and His abundant reward, and is protected from His severe punishment, is not equal to he who deserves the wrath of God and is bound by it, and there is no escape for him from it, and his refuge on the Day of Resurrection is Hell, and an evil destination. This verse has many parallels in the Qur’an, such as the Almighty’s saying: Is he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like he who is blind? and His saying: Is he to whom We have promised a good promise and he will attain it like he to whom We have given enjoyment of the enjoyment of worldly life? Then God the Almighty said: They are of degrees with God. Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Muhammad bin Ishaq said: meaning the people of good and the people of evil have degrees. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Kisa’i said: Stations, meaning they differ in their stations and degrees in Paradise and their levels in Hell, like the Almighty’s saying: And for all are degrees according to what they have done verse. That is why the Almighty said: And God is Seeing of what they do verse, meaning He will give them what they deserve. He will not wrong them with good nor increase their evil, rather He will reward each worker according to his work. The Almighty said: God has certainly conferred a great favor upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves verse, meaning from their own kind so that they could address him, ask him, sit with him, and benefit from him, as the Almighty said: And among His signs is that He created for you from among yourselves mates that you may find tranquility in them verse, meaning from your own kind. The Almighty said: “Say, ‘I am only a man like you. It has been revealed to me that your God is one God’” verse. God the Almighty said: And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets. God the Almighty said: And We did not send before you any except men to whom We revealed from the people of the towns. God the Almighty said: O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you? This is more eloquent in gratitude that the messenger to them should be from among them, such that they can address him and consult him in understanding the speech on his behalf. For this reason God the Almighty said: He recites to them His verses meaning the Qur’an and purifies them meaning he commands them to do good and forbids them from evil so that their souls may be purified and cleansed from the filth and evil that they were immersed in during their state of polytheism and ignorance, and teaches them the Book and wisdom meaning the Qur’an and the Sunnah, although they were before meaning before this Messenger in manifest error meaning in clear error and ignorance that is evident to everyone.
3:163: The Almighty says, addressing His Messenger, thanking him and the believers for what He softened his heart with towards his nation who followed his command, abandoned his warning, and made his words pleasant to them: Then by the mercy of God, you were gentle with them. That is, what made you gentle with them, were it not for God’s mercy upon you and them? Qatada said: Then by the mercy of God, you were gentle with them. He says: Then by the mercy of God, you were gentle with them. What is the connection? The Arabs connect it with the definite article, as in His statement: Then by their breaking of their covenant. And with the indefinite article, as in His statement: In a little while. And thus here he said: Then by the mercy of God, you were gentle with them. That is, by the mercy of God. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: This is the character of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with which God sent him. And this noble verse is similar to the statement of the Almighty: “There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer; he is concerned over you and to the believers is kind and merciful.” And Imam Ahmad said: Haywah told us, Baqiyah told us, Muhammad bin Ziyad told us. Abu Rashid Al-Habrani told me: Abu Umamah Al-Bahili took my hand and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took my hand and said: O Abu Umamah, among the believers is he whose heart is soft towards me. Ahmad alone transmitted this. Then God, the Most High, said: And if you had been rude [in speech] and harsh [in heart], they would have disbanded from around you. The rude is the harsh, and what is meant by it here is harsh in speech, because He said after that harsh in heart, meaning if you had been bad in speech and hard-hearted towards them, they would have disbanded from you and left you, but God gathered them around you and made you gentle towards them to win their hearts over, as Abdullah bin Amr said: “I see the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the earlier books that he is not rude, nor harsh, nor loud in the markets, and he does not repay evil with evil, but he pardons and forgives.” Abu Ismail Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Tirmidhi said: Bishr bin Ubaid Al-Darimi informed us, Ammar bin Abd Al-Rahman informed us, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: God has commanded me to be lenient with people, just as He has commanded me to establish the obligatory duties. This is a strange hadith. That is why God the Almighty said: So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter. That is why the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to consult his companions about a matter whenever it happened, to please their hearts so that they would be more active in what they did, as he consulted them on the day of Badr about going to the caravan, and they said: “O Messenger of God, if you were to parade us across the sea, we would cross it with you, and if you were to take us to Barak al-Ghamad, we would go with you, and we will not say to you as the people of Moses said to Moses: Go, you and your Lord, and fight, for we are sitting here. Rather, we say: Go, for we are with you, in front of you, and on your right and on your left, fighting.” He also consulted them about where the camp would be, until Al-Mundhir bin Amr Al-Mu’naq indicated to die by advancing to the front of the people. He consulted them about whether he should stay in the city or go out to the enemy. Most of them suggested going out to them. So he went out to them and consulted them on the day of the Trench about reconciling with the confederates for a third of the fruits of the city that year. The two Saads, Saad bin Muadh and Saad bin Ubadah, refused him that, so he left that. He consulted them on the day of Hudaybiyyah about attacking the children of the polytheists. Abu Bakr said to him: We did not come to fight anyone, but we came to perform Umrah. So he agreed to what he said. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said in the story of the slander: “Advise me, O Muslims, about a people who destroyed my family and threw stones at them. By God, I do not know of any evil against my family, and who did they destroy them for? By God, I only know of good about him.” He consulted Ali and Usama about separating from Aisha may God be pleased with her. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to consult them in wars and the like. The jurists differed as to whether that was obligatory upon him or recommended to please their hearts. There are two opinions. Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Baghdadi informed us, Yahya ibn Ayyub al-`Alaf told us in Egypt, Sa`id ibn Abi Maryam told us, Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah told us, on the authority of `Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding the words of God the Almighty: And consult them in the matter. He said: Abu Bakr and `Umar, may God be pleased with them. Then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it. Al-Kalbi narrated it likewise on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: It was revealed about Abu Bakr and `Umar, and they were the disciples of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his ministers, and the fathers of the Muslims. Imam Ahmad narrated: Waki` told us, `Abd al-Hamid told us on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanim, “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Bakr and `Umar, ‘If we met in consultation, I would not oppose you.’” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of `Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about determination. He said: Consulting people of opinion, then following them.” Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Bakir narrated to us, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Abdul Malik ibn Umair, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The one who is consulted is trustworthy. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it, and al-Nasa’i authenticated it from the hadith of Abdul Malik ibn Umair with a more detailed chain of transmission than this. Then Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Aswad ibn Amir narrated to us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Amr al-Shaibani, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The one who is consulted is trustworthy.” He was the only one to narrate it. He also said: Abu Bakr narrated to us, Yahya ibn Zakariya ibn Abi Zaydah and Ali ibn Hashim narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If one of you consults his brother, let him advise him. He was also the only one to narrate it. And the Almighty’s saying: So when you have decided, then rely upon God meaning if you consult them about the matter and are determined to do it, then rely upon God in it Indeed, God loves those who rely [upon Him]. And the Almighty’s saying: If God helps you, none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? And in God let the believers rely. And this verse is as it was mentioned before from His saying: And victory comes only from God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Then He commanded them to rely upon Him, saying: And in God let the believers rely. And the Almighty’s saying: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan and more than one said: It is not befitting for a prophet to betray. And Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Al-Musayyab bin Wadheeh told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari told us on the authority of Sufyan bin Khasif on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They lost a quilt on the day of Badr, so they said: Perhaps the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it, so God revealed: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils, meaning betray. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib told us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, Khasif told us, Muqsim told us, Ibn Abbas told me that this verse, And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war, was revealed concerning a red cloak that was lost on the day of Badr. Some people said: Perhaps the Messenger of God had taken it, and they talked a lot about that, so God revealed, “And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war. And whoever takes spoils of war will come with what he has taken on the Day of Resurrection.” Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi both narrated it in the same way on the authority of Qutaybah, on the authority of Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and strange. Some of them narrated it on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Muqsim, meaning in a mursal form. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The hypocrites accused the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) of something he had lost, so God revealed: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas through other chains of transmission similar to what was mentioned above. This is to exonerate him (blessings and peace of God be upon him) from all forms of treachery in fulfilling the trust, dividing the spoils of war, and other things. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war meaning that he would divide some of the spoils for the sake of the army and leave others. Ad-Dahhak said the same. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war meaning that he would leave some of what was revealed to him and not convey it to his nation. Al-Hasan al-Basri, Tawus, Mujahid, and Ad-Dahhak recited: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war with a damma on the ya’, meaning that he would betray. Qatada and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: This verse was revealed on the day of Badr, and some of his companions had taken spoils of war. Ibn Jarir narrated it from them, then he narrated from some of them that he interpreted this reading to mean that he is accused of treason, then God Almighty said: “And whoever embezzles will come with what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.” This is a severe threat and a definite warning. The Sunnah also forbade this in multiple hadiths. Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Malik told us, Zuhair told us, meaning Ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah Ibn Muhammad Ibn Aqil, from Ata Ibn Yasar, from Abu Malik Al-Ashja’i, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The greatest embezzlement before God is an arm’s length of land. You will find two men running after each other on the land - or in the house - and one of them will cut off an arm’s length from the share of his companion, and if he cuts it off, he will be hung around his neck from seven earths until the Day of Resurrection.” Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Musa bin Dawud told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Ibn Hubayrah and Al-Harith bin Yazid, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Jubayr, who said: I heard Al-Mustawrid bin Shaddad say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever is given a job and does not have a house, let him get a house. Or he does not have a wife, let him get married. Or he does not have a servant, let him get a servant. Or he does not have a mount, let him get a mount. And whoever acquires something other than that, then he is a thief.” This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it. Abu Dawud narrated it with another chain of narration and context, saying: Musa bin Marwan al-Raqi narrated to us, al-Mu'afi narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, on the authority of al-Harith bin Yazid, on the authority of Jubayr bin Nufayr, on the authority of al-Mustawrid bin Shaddad, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: "Whoever works for us, let him acquire a wife. If he does not have a servant, let him acquire a servant. If he does not have a home, let him acquire a home." He said: Abu Bakr said: I was told that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever does anything other than that is a transgressor or a thief. Our Sheikh, al-Hafiz al-Mizzi, may God have mercy on him, said: It was narrated by Ja'far bin Muhammad al-Faryabi on the authority of Musa bin Marwan, and he said: On the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Jubayr instead of Jubayr bin Nufayr, and this is more likely to be correct. Another hadith - Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Hafs ibn Bishr told us, Yaqub al-Qummi told us, Hafs ibn Humayd told us on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a bleating sheep and calling out: O Muhammad, O Muhammad.’ I will say: ‘I have no power over anything from God for you, I have conveyed it to you.’ I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a braying camel and calling out: O Muhammad, O Muhammad.’ I will say: ‘I have no power over anything from God for you, I have conveyed it to you.’ I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a neighing horse and calling out: O Muhammad, O Muhammad.’ I will say: ‘I have no power over anything from God for you, I have conveyed it to you.’ I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a leather husk and calling out: O Muhammad, O Muhammad.’ I will say: ‘I have no power over anything from God for you, I have conveyed it to you.’” None of the people of the six books narrated it. Another hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, he heard Urwah say: Abu Hamid Al-Sa’idi narrated to us: He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed a man from Azd called Ibn Al-Lutbiyyah to collect the zakat. He came and said: This is for you and this was given to me. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood on the pulpit and said: What is the matter with the worker whom we send and he comes and says: This is for you and this was given to me. Why did he not sit in the house of his father and mother and see whether he was given a gift or not? By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, none of you will bring anything of it except that he will bring it on the Day of Resurrection on his neck, whether it is a camel that roars, or a cow that moos, or a sheep that bleats. Then he raised his hands until we saw the whiteness of his armpits. Then he said: O God, have I conveyed the message?” Hisham bin Urwah added: Abu Hamid said: I saw it with my eyes and heard it with my ears. Ask Zaid bin Thabit. They both narrated it on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah. Al-Bukhari has: Ask Zaid bin Thabit. And others. A face on the authority of Al-Zuhri, and through a path on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, both on the authority of Urwah, on his authority. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq bin Isa told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Abu Hamid, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The gifts of workers are misappropriation.” This hadith is one of the individual hadiths of Ahmad, and its chain of transmission is weak, and it seems to be an abbreviation of the one before it, and God knows best. Another hadith - Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi said in the Book of Rulings: Abu Kurayb told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Yazid Al-Awdi, on the authority of Al-Mughirah bin Shibl, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim, on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me to Yemen, and when I set out, he sent after me, but I returned. He said, ‘Do you know why I sent to you? Do not take anything without my permission, for it is embezzlement. ’ And whoever embezzles will come with what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection. ’ This is why I have called you, so go on with your work.” This is a good, strange hadith that we do not know except from this source. There are hadiths on this topic from Adi bin Umaira, Buraydah, Al-Mustawrid bin Shaddad, Abu Hamid, and Ibn Umar. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ismail bin Aliyah told us, Abu Hayyan Yahya bin Saeed Al-Taymi told us, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah bin Umar bin Jarir, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up among us one day and mentioned theft, and he magnified it and magnified its matter, then he said: ‘I will not find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel roaring on his neck, and he will say: O Messenger of God, help me,’ and I will say: ‘I have no power over God for you, I have conveyed the message to you.’ I will not find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a horse neighing on his neck, and he will say: O Messenger of God, help me,’ and I will say: ‘I have no power over God for you, I have conveyed the message to you.’ I will not find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a bandage on his neck that is strangling him, and he will say: O Messenger of God, help me,’ and I will say: ‘I have no power over God for you, I have conveyed the message to you.’ I will not find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a silent person on his neck, and he will say: O Messenger of God, help me,’ and I will say: ‘I have no power over God for you, I have conveyed the message to you.’ You have something from God that I have conveyed to you.” They narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hayyan. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told us on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, Qais told me on the authority of Adi bin Umaira Al-Kindi who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O people, whoever among you does work for us and conceals from us a needle or more of it, it is a stipulation that he will bring on the Day of Resurrection. He said: A black man from the Ansar stood up - Mujalid said: He is Saeed bin Ubadah, it is as if I am looking at him - and said: O Messenger of God, accept your work from me. He said: What is that? He said: I heard you say: such and such. He said: And I am saying that now. Whoever we appoint to a job, let him come with it, little or much, and whatever he is given from it, he takes, and whatever he is forbidden from, he ends.” And Muslim and Abu Dawud narrated it in the same way through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Manbuth, a man from the family of Abu Rafi’, told me on the authority of Al-Fadl bin Ubaidullah bin Abu Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, who said: “When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed the afternoon prayer, he would sometimes go to Banu Abd Al-Ashhal and talk to them until sunset. Abu Rafi’ said: “While the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was hurrying to the sunset prayer, he passed by Al-Baqi’ and said: ‘Uff to you, uf to you’ twice. He shouted at me and I held back and thought that he wanted me. He said: ‘What is the matter with you? Walk.’ I said: ‘I have done something new, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘What is that?’ I said: ‘Uff to me.’ He said: ‘No, but this is the grave of so-and-so. I sent him to seek out the family of so-and-so, and he stole a tiger and now his armor is like it, made of fire.’” Another hadith - Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Salem Al-Kufi, the paralytic, told us - and he was in Mecca - Ubaidah bin Al-Aswad told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Al-Waleed, on the authority of Abu Sadiq, on the authority of Rabia bin Najed, on the authority of Ubadah bin Al-Samit, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would take a hair from the side of the camel from the spoils of war and then say: I have nothing in it except what one of you has. Beware of embezzlement, for embezzlement is a disgrace for its perpetrator on the Day of Resurrection. Give back the thread and needle and what is above that, and strive in the cause of God near and far, at home and on the journey, for striving is one of the gates of Paradise, for God saves from worry and grief through it, and establish the limits of God in those near and far, and do not let the blame of a blamer deter you in God’s cause.” Ibn Majah narrated some of it on the authority of the paralytic. Another hadith - On the authority of Amr bin Shuaib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Return the tailor and the needle, for embezzlement is a disgrace, a fire, and a shame upon its people on the Day of Resurrection.” Another hadith - Abu Dawud said: Uthman bin Abi Shaybah told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Abu al-Jahm, on the authority of Abu Mas`ud al-Ansari, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me as a messenger, then he said: Go, Abu Mas`ud, lest I find you on the Day of Resurrection with a camel from the charity camels coming on your back, roaring, and you have tied it up.” He said: Then I will not go. He said: Then I will not hate you. Abu Dawud is the only one to report it. Another hadith - Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Ibrahim informed us, Muhammad bin Uthman bin Abi Shaybah informed us, Abdul Hamid bin Saleh informed us, Ahmad bin Aban informed us on the authority of Alqamah bin Murthad, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “A stone is thrown into Hell and it falls for seventy years without reaching its bottom, and the stolen goods are brought and thrown with them, then it is said to the one who stole them, ‘Bring them.’ This is what His statement means: ‘And whoever steals will bring what he stole on the Day of Resurrection.’” Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, Ikrimah bin Ammar told us, Samak Al-Hanafi Abu Zamil told me, Abdullah bin Abbas told me, Umar bin Al-Khattab told me: When the day of Khaybar came, a group of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and said: So-and-so is a martyr and so-and-so is a martyr, until they came to a man and said: So-and-so is a martyr. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, I saw him in the Fire in a cloak that he had stolen. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O son of Al-Khattab, go and announce to the al-Nas 114:‘None shall enter Paradise except the believers.’ So I went out and announced: ‘None shall enter Paradise except the believers.’” Muslim and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Ikrimah bin Ammar. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih. Another hadith - Ibn Jarir said: Saeed bin Yahya Al-Umawi told us, my father told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “sent Saad bin Ubadah as a tax collector, and he said: Beware, Saad, of coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel that you are carrying and it is bellowing. He said: I will not take it nor will I come with it, so he excused him.” Then he narrated it on the authority of Ubaidullah on the authority of Nafi’ in a similar manner. Another hadith - Ahmad said: Abu Saeed told us, Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad told us, Saleh bin Muhammad bin Zaida told us, on the authority of Salim bin Abdullah, that he was with Muslimah bin Abdul Malik in the land of the Romans, and he found stolen goods in a man’s belongings. He said: So he asked Salim bin Abdullah, and he said: My father Abdullah told me, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you find stolen goods in someone’s belongings, burn them - he said: And I think he said: And beat him. He said: So he took out his belongings in the market and found a Qur’an in them, so he asked Salim, and he said: Sell it and give its price in charity.” And this is how Ali bin Al-Madini, Abu Dawud, and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad Al-Atdarwardi. Abu Dawud and Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari added, both of them on the authority of Abu Waqid Al-Laithi Al-Sagheer, Saleh bin Muhammad bin Zaida with it. Ali ibn al-Madini, al-Bukhari and others said: This is a rejected hadith narrated by Abu Waqid. Al-Daraqutni said: The correct view is that it is only from the fatwa of Salim. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may God have mercy on him, and those of his companions who followed him held the view based on this hadith. Al-Umawi narrated it on the authority of Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: The punishment for the transgressor is that his saddlebags are taken out and burned with what is in them. Then he narrated on the authority of Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Uthman ibn Ata’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali, who said: The transgressor’s saddlebags are gathered together and burned and he is flogged without a prescribed punishment. Abu Hanifa, Malik, al-Shafi’i and the majority disagreed with him and said: The transgressor’s belongings are not to be burned, but he is to be punished with a punishment similar to his. Al-Bukhari said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, refrained from praying over the transgressor, but his belongings were not burned.” And God knows best. Another hadith on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with him - Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb told me, Abdullah ibn Wahb told me, Amr ibn al-Harith told me that Musa ibn Jubayr told him: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Habbab al-Ansari told him: Abdullah ibn Unais told him: He and Umar ibn al-Khattab were discussing charity one day, and he said: Didn’t you hear the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he mentioned the embezzlement of charity: Whoever embezzles a camel or a sheep from it, he will carry it on the Day of Resurrection? Abdullah ibn Unais said: Yes. Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Amr ibn Sawad on the authority of Abdullah ibn Wahb on his authority. Al-Umawi narrated it on the authority of Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: The punishment of the embezzler is that his saddle be taken out and burned with what is in it. Then he narrated on the authority of Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Uthman ibn Ata’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali, who said: The embezzler’s saddle is gathered up and burned and he is flogged without a prescribed punishment. Imam Ahmad said: Aswad bin Aamer told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Jubayr bin Malik, who said: The copies of the Qur’an were ordered to be changed. He said: Ibn Masoud said: Whoever among you can steal a copy of the Qur’an, let him steal it, for whoever steals something will bring it on the Day of Resurrection. Then he said: I recited from the mouth of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, seventy surahs. Should I abandon what I took from the mouth of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? And Wakee’ narrated in his interpretation on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: When the copies of the Qur’an were ordered to be burned, Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: O people, steal the copies of the Qur’an, for whoever steals it will bring what he stole on the Day of Resurrection. And what a good stealing copy of the Qur’an one of you will bring on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Dawud said, on the authority of Samurah bin Jundub, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, captured a booty, he would command Bilal to call out to the people, and they would bring their spoils, and he would take a fifth of it and divide it. Then a man came one day after The call was made with a bridle of hair. He said: O Messenger of God, this was from what we obtained from the spoils. He said: Did you hear Bilal calling three times? He said: Yes. He said: What prevented you from coming? So he apologized to him. He said: No, you will come with it on the Day of Resurrection and I will not accept it from you. And the Almighty said: Is he who pursues the pleasure of God like he who incurs the wrath of God and whose refuge is Hell, and an evil destination? That is, he who pursues the pleasure of God in what He has prescribed and thus deserves the pleasure of God and His abundant reward, and is protected from His severe punishment, is not equal to he who deserves the wrath of God and is bound by it, and there is no escape for him from it, and his refuge on the Day of Resurrection is Hell, and an evil destination. This verse has many parallels in the Qur’an, such as the Almighty’s saying: Is he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like he who is blind? and His saying: Is he to whom We have promised a good promise and he will attain it like he to whom We have given enjoyment of the enjoyment of worldly life? Then God the Almighty said: They are of degrees with God. Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Muhammad bin Ishaq said: meaning the people of good and the people of evil have degrees. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Kisa’i said: Stations, meaning they differ in their stations and degrees in Paradise and their levels in Hell, like the Almighty’s saying: And for all are degrees according to what they have done verse. That is why the Almighty said: And God is Seeing of what they do verse, meaning He will give them what they deserve. He will not wrong them with good nor increase their evil, rather He will reward each worker according to his work. The Almighty said: God has certainly conferred a great favor upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves verse, meaning from their own kind so that they could address him, ask him, sit with him, and benefit from him, as the Almighty said: And among His signs is that He created for you from among yourselves mates that you may find tranquility in them verse, meaning from your own kind. The Almighty said: “Say, ‘I am only a man like you. It has been revealed to me that your God is one God’” verse. God the Almighty said: And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets. God the Almighty said: And We did not send before you any except men to whom We revealed from the people of the towns. God the Almighty said: O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you? This is more eloquent in gratitude that the messenger to them should be from among them, such that they can address him and consult him in understanding the speech on his behalf. For this reason God the Almighty said: He recites to them His verses meaning the Qur’an and purifies them meaning he commands them to do good and forbids them from evil so that their souls may be purified and cleansed from the filth and evil that they were immersed in during their state of polytheism and ignorance, and teaches them the Book and wisdom meaning the Qur’an and the Sunnah, although they were before meaning before this Messenger in manifest error meaning in clear error and ignorance that is evident to everyone.
3:164: The Almighty says, addressing His Messenger, thanking him and the believers for what He softened his heart with towards his nation who followed his command, abandoned his warning, and made his words pleasant to them: Then by the mercy of God, you were gentle with them. That is, what made you gentle with them, were it not for God’s mercy upon you and them? Qatada said: Then by the mercy of God, you were gentle with them. He says: Then by the mercy of God, you were gentle with them. What is the connection? The Arabs connect it with the definite article, as in His statement: Then by their breaking of their covenant. And with the indefinite article, as in His statement: In a little while. And thus here he said: Then by the mercy of God, you were gentle with them. That is, by the mercy of God. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: This is the character of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with which God sent him. And this noble verse is similar to the statement of the Almighty: “There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer; he is concerned over you and to the believers is kind and merciful.” And Imam Ahmad said: Haywah told us, Baqiyah told us, Muhammad bin Ziyad told us. Abu Rashid Al-Habrani told me: Abu Umamah Al-Bahili took my hand and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took my hand and said: O Abu Umamah, among the believers is he whose heart is soft towards me. Ahmad alone transmitted this. Then God, the Most High, said: And if you had been rude [in speech] and harsh [in heart], they would have disbanded from around you. The rude is the harsh, and what is meant by it here is harsh in speech, because He said after that harsh in heart, meaning if you had been bad in speech and hard-hearted towards them, they would have disbanded from you and left you, but God gathered them around you and made you gentle towards them to win their hearts over, as Abdullah bin Amr said: “I see the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the earlier books that he is not rude, nor harsh, nor loud in the markets, and he does not repay evil with evil, but he pardons and forgives.” Abu Ismail Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Tirmidhi said: Bishr bin Ubaid Al-Darimi informed us, Ammar bin Abd Al-Rahman informed us, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: God has commanded me to be lenient with people, just as He has commanded me to establish the obligatory duties. This is a strange hadith. That is why God the Almighty said: So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter. That is why the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to consult his companions about a matter whenever it happened, to please their hearts so that they would be more active in what they did, as he consulted them on the day of Badr about going to the caravan, and they said: “O Messenger of God, if you were to parade us across the sea, we would cross it with you, and if you were to take us to Barak al-Ghamad, we would go with you, and we will not say to you as the people of Moses said to Moses: Go, you and your Lord, and fight, for we are sitting here. Rather, we say: Go, for we are with you, in front of you, and on your right and on your left, fighting.” He also consulted them about where the camp would be, until Al-Mundhir bin Amr Al-Mu’naq indicated to die by advancing to the front of the people. He consulted them about whether he should stay in the city or go out to the enemy. Most of them suggested going out to them. So he went out to them and consulted them on the day of the Trench about reconciling with the confederates for a third of the fruits of the city that year. The two Saads, Saad bin Muadh and Saad bin Ubadah, refused him that, so he left that. He consulted them on the day of Hudaybiyyah about attacking the children of the polytheists. Abu Bakr said to him: We did not come to fight anyone, but we came to perform Umrah. So he agreed to what he said. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said in the story of the slander: “Advise me, O Muslims, about a people who destroyed my family and threw stones at them. By God, I do not know of any evil against my family, and who did they destroy them for? By God, I only know of good about him.” He consulted Ali and Usama about separating from Aisha may God be pleased with her. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to consult them in wars and the like. The jurists differed as to whether that was obligatory upon him or recommended to please their hearts. There are two opinions. Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Baghdadi informed us, Yahya ibn Ayyub al-`Alaf told us in Egypt, Sa`id ibn Abi Maryam told us, Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah told us, on the authority of `Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding the words of God the Almighty: And consult them in the matter. He said: Abu Bakr and `Umar, may God be pleased with them. Then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it. Al-Kalbi narrated it likewise on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: It was revealed about Abu Bakr and `Umar, and they were the disciples of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his ministers, and the fathers of the Muslims. Imam Ahmad narrated: Waki` told us, `Abd al-Hamid told us on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanim, “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Bakr and `Umar, ‘If we met in consultation, I would not oppose you.’” Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of `Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about determination. He said: Consulting people of opinion, then following them.” Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Bakir narrated to us, on the authority of Shaiban, on the authority of Abdul Malik ibn Umair, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The one who is consulted is trustworthy. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it, and al-Nasa’i authenticated it from the hadith of Abdul Malik ibn Umair with a more detailed chain of transmission than this. Then Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Aswad ibn Amir narrated to us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Amr al-Shaibani, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The one who is consulted is trustworthy.” He was the only one to narrate it. He also said: Abu Bakr narrated to us, Yahya ibn Zakariya ibn Abi Zaydah and Ali ibn Hashim narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If one of you consults his brother, let him advise him. He was also the only one to narrate it. And the Almighty’s saying: So when you have decided, then rely upon God meaning if you consult them about the matter and are determined to do it, then rely upon God in it Indeed, God loves those who rely [upon Him]. And the Almighty’s saying: If God helps you, none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? And in God let the believers rely. And this verse is as it was mentioned before from His saying: And victory comes only from God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Then He commanded them to rely upon Him, saying: And in God let the believers rely. And the Almighty’s saying: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan and more than one said: It is not befitting for a prophet to betray. And Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Al-Musayyab bin Wadheeh told us, Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari told us on the authority of Sufyan bin Khasif on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They lost a quilt on the day of Badr, so they said: Perhaps the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it, so God revealed: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils, meaning betray. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib told us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, Khasif told us, Muqsim told us, Ibn Abbas told me that this verse, And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war, was revealed concerning a red cloak that was lost on the day of Badr. Some people said: Perhaps the Messenger of God had taken it, and they talked a lot about that, so God revealed, “And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war. And whoever takes spoils of war will come with what he has taken on the Day of Resurrection.” Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi both narrated it in the same way on the authority of Qutaybah, on the authority of Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad.
