Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and strange. Some of them narrated it on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Muqsim, meaning in a mursal form. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The hypocrites accused the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) of something he had lost, so God revealed: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas through other chains of transmission similar to what was mentioned above. This is to exonerate him (blessings and peace of God be upon him) from all forms of treachery in fulfilling the trust, dividing the spoils of war, and other things. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war meaning that he would divide some of the spoils for the sake of the army and leave others. Ad-Dahhak said the same. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war meaning that he would leave some of what was revealed to him and not convey it to his nation. Al-Hasan al-Basri, Tawus, Mujahid, and Ad-Dahhak recited: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war with a damma on the ya’, meaning that he would betray. Qatada and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: This verse was revealed on the day of Badr, and some of his companions had taken spoils of war. Ibn Jarir narrated it from them, then he narrated from some of them that he interpreted this reading to mean that he is accused of treason, then God Almighty said: “And whoever embezzles will come with what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.” This is a severe threat and a definite warning. The Sunnah also forbade this in multiple hadiths. Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Malik told us, Zuhair told us, meaning Ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah Ibn Muhammad Ibn Aqil, from Ata Ibn Yasar, from Abu Malik Al-Ashja’i, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The greatest embezzlement before God is an arm’s length of land. You will find two men running after each other on the land - or in the house - and one of them will cut off an arm’s length from the share of his companion, and if he cuts it off, he will be hung around his neck from seven earths until the Day of Resurrection.” Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Musa bin Dawud told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Ibn Hubayrah and Al-Harith bin Yazid, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Jubayr, who said: I heard Al-Mustawrid bin Shaddad say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever is given a job and does not have a house, let him get a house. Or he does not have a wife, let him get married. Or he does not have a servant, let him get a servant. Or he does not have a mount, let him get a mount. And whoever acquires something other than that, then he is a thief.” This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it. Abu Dawud narrated it with another chain of narration and context, saying: Musa bin Marwan al-Raqi narrated to us, al-Mu'afi narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, on the authority of al-Harith bin Yazid, on the authority of Jubayr bin Nufayr, on the authority of al-Mustawrid bin Shaddad, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: "Whoever works for us, let him acquire a wife. If he does not have a servant, let him acquire a servant. If he does not have a home, let him acquire a home." He said: Abu Bakr said: I was told that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever does anything other than that is a transgressor or a thief. Our Sheikh, al-Hafiz al-Mizzi, may God have mercy on him, said: It was narrated by Ja'far bin Muhammad al-Faryabi on the authority of Musa bin Marwan, and he said: On the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Jubayr instead of Jubayr bin Nufayr, and this is more likely to be correct. Another hadith - Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Hafs ibn Bishr told us, Yaqub al-Qummi told us, Hafs ibn Humayd told us on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a bleating sheep and calling out: O Muhammad, O Muhammad.’ I will say: ‘I have no power over anything from God for you, I have conveyed it to you.’ I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a braying camel and calling out: O Muhammad, O Muhammad.’ I will say: ‘I have no power over anything from God for you, I have conveyed it to you.’ I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a neighing horse and calling out: O Muhammad, O Muhammad.’ I will say: ‘I have no power over anything from God for you, I have conveyed it to you.’ I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a leather husk and calling out: O Muhammad, O Muhammad.’ I will say: ‘I have no power over anything from God for you, I have conveyed it to you.’” None of the people of the six books narrated it. Another hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, he heard Urwah say: Abu Hamid Al-Sa’idi narrated to us: He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed a man from Azd called Ibn Al-Lutbiyyah to collect the zakat. He came and said: This is for you and this was given to me. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood on the pulpit and said: What is the matter with the worker whom we send and he comes and says: This is for you and this was given to me. Why did he not sit in the house of his father and mother and see whether he was given a gift or not? By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, none of you will bring anything of it except that he will bring it on the Day of Resurrection on his neck, whether it is a camel that roars, or a cow that moos, or a sheep that bleats. Then he raised his hands until we saw the whiteness of his armpits. Then he said: O God, have I conveyed the message?” Hisham bin Urwah added: Abu Hamid said: I saw it with my eyes and heard it with my ears. Ask Zaid bin Thabit. They both narrated it on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah. Al-Bukhari has: Ask Zaid bin Thabit. And others. A face on the authority of Al-Zuhri, and through a path on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, both on the authority of Urwah, on his authority. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq bin Isa told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Abu Hamid, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The gifts of workers are misappropriation.” This hadith is one of the individual hadiths of Ahmad, and its chain of transmission is weak, and it seems to be an abbreviation of the one before it, and God knows best. Another hadith - Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi said in the Book of Rulings: Abu Kurayb told us, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Yazid Al-Awdi, on the authority of Al-Mughirah bin Shibl, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim, on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me to Yemen, and when I set out, he sent after me, but I returned. He said, ‘Do you know why I sent to you? Do not take anything without my permission, for it is embezzlement. ’ And whoever embezzles will come with what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection. ’ This is why I have called you, so go on with your work.” This is a good, strange hadith that we do not know except from this source. There are hadiths on this topic from Adi bin Umaira, Buraydah, Al-Mustawrid bin Shaddad, Abu Hamid, and Ibn Umar. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Ismail bin Aliyah told us, Abu Hayyan Yahya bin Saeed Al-Taymi told us, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah bin Umar bin Jarir, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up among us one day and mentioned theft, and he magnified it and magnified its matter, then he said: ‘I will not find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel roaring on his neck, and he will say: O Messenger of God, help me,’ and I will say: ‘I have no power over God for you, I have conveyed the message to you.’ I will not find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a horse neighing on his neck, and he will say: O Messenger of God, help me,’ and I will say: ‘I have no power over God for you, I have conveyed the message to you.’ I will not find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a bandage on his neck that is strangling him, and he will say: O Messenger of God, help me,’ and I will say: ‘I have no power over God for you, I have conveyed the message to you.’ I will not find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a silent person on his neck, and he will say: O Messenger of God, help me,’ and I will say: ‘I have no power over God for you, I have conveyed the message to you.’ You have something from God that I have conveyed to you.” They narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hayyan. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told us on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, Qais told me on the authority of Adi bin Umaira Al-Kindi who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O people, whoever among you does work for us and conceals from us a needle or more of it, it is a stipulation that he will bring on the Day of Resurrection. He said: A black man from the Ansar stood up - Mujalid said: He is Saeed bin Ubadah, it is as if I am looking at him - and said: O Messenger of God, accept your work from me. He said: What is that? He said: I heard you say: such and such. He said: And I am saying that now. Whoever we appoint to a job, let him come with it, little or much, and whatever he is given from it, he takes, and whatever he is forbidden from, he ends.” And Muslim and Abu Dawud narrated it in the same way through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Manbuth, a man from the family of Abu Rafi’, told me on the authority of Al-Fadl bin Ubaidullah bin Abu Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, who said: “When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed the afternoon prayer, he would sometimes go to Banu Abd Al-Ashhal and talk to them until sunset. Abu Rafi’ said: “While the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was hurrying to the sunset prayer, he passed by Al-Baqi’ and said: ‘Uff to you, uf to you’ twice. He shouted at me and I held back and thought that he wanted me. He said: ‘What is the matter with you? Walk.’ I said: ‘I have done something new, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘What is that?’ I said: ‘Uff to me.’ He said: ‘No, but this is the grave of so-and-so. I sent him to seek out the family of so-and-so, and he stole a tiger and now his armor is like it, made of fire.’” Another hadith - Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Salem Al-Kufi, the paralytic, told us - and he was in Mecca - Ubaidah bin Al-Aswad told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Al-Waleed, on the authority of Abu Sadiq, on the authority of Rabia bin Najed, on the authority of Ubadah bin Al-Samit, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would take a hair from the side of the camel from the spoils of war and then say: I have nothing in it except what one of you has. Beware of embezzlement, for embezzlement is a disgrace for its perpetrator on the Day of Resurrection. Give back the thread and needle and what is above that, and strive in the cause of God near and far, at home and on the journey, for striving is one of the gates of Paradise, for God saves from worry and grief through it, and establish the limits of God in those near and far, and do not let the blame of a blamer deter you in God’s cause.” Ibn Majah narrated some of it on the authority of the paralytic. Another hadith - On the authority of Amr bin Shuaib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Return the tailor and the needle, for embezzlement is a disgrace, a fire, and a shame upon its people on the Day of Resurrection.” Another hadith - Abu Dawud said: Uthman bin Abi Shaybah told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Abu al-Jahm, on the authority of Abu Mas`ud al-Ansari, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me as a messenger, then he said: Go, Abu Mas`ud, lest I find you on the Day of Resurrection with a camel from the charity camels coming on your back, roaring, and you have tied it up.” He said: Then I will not go. He said: Then I will not hate you. Abu Dawud is the only one to report it. Another hadith - Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Ibrahim informed us, Muhammad bin Uthman bin Abi Shaybah informed us, Abdul Hamid bin Saleh informed us, Ahmad bin Aban informed us on the authority of Alqamah bin Murthad, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “A stone is thrown into Hell and it falls for seventy years without reaching its bottom, and the stolen goods are brought and thrown with them, then it is said to the one who stole them, ‘Bring them.’ This is what His statement means: ‘And whoever steals will bring what he stole on the Day of Resurrection.’” Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, Ikrimah bin Ammar told us, Samak Al-Hanafi Abu Zamil told me, Abdullah bin Abbas told me, Umar bin Al-Khattab told me: When the day of Khaybar came, a group of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and said: So-and-so is a martyr and so-and-so is a martyr, until they came to a man and said: So-and-so is a martyr. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, I saw him in the Fire in a cloak that he had stolen. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O son of Al-Khattab, go and announce to the al-Nas 114:‘None shall enter Paradise except the believers.’ So I went out and announced: ‘None shall enter Paradise except the believers.’” Muslim and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Ikrimah bin Ammar. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih. Another hadith - Ibn Jarir said: Saeed bin Yahya Al-Umawi told us, my father told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “sent Saad bin Ubadah as a tax collector, and he said: Beware, Saad, of coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel that you are carrying and it is bellowing. He said: I will not take it nor will I come with it, so he excused him.” Then he narrated it on the authority of Ubaidullah on the authority of Nafi’ in a similar manner. Another hadith - Ahmad said: Abu Saeed told us, Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad told us, Saleh bin Muhammad bin Zaida told us, on the authority of Salim bin Abdullah, that he was with Muslimah bin Abdul Malik in the land of the Romans, and he found stolen goods in a man’s belongings. He said: So he asked Salim bin Abdullah, and he said: My father Abdullah told me, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you find stolen goods in someone’s belongings, burn them - he said: And I think he said: And beat him. He said: So he took out his belongings in the market and found a Qur’an in them, so he asked Salim, and he said: Sell it and give its price in charity.” And this is how Ali bin Al-Madini, Abu Dawud, and Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad Al-Atdarwardi. Abu Dawud and Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari added, both of them on the authority of Abu Waqid Al-Laithi Al-Sagheer, Saleh bin Muhammad bin Zaida with it. Ali ibn al-Madini, al-Bukhari and others said: This is a rejected hadith narrated by Abu Waqid. Al-Daraqutni said: The correct view is that it is only from the fatwa of Salim. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may God have mercy on him, and those of his companions who followed him held the view based on this hadith. Al-Umawi narrated it on the authority of Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: The punishment for the transgressor is that his saddlebags are taken out and burned with what is in them. Then he narrated on the authority of Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Uthman ibn Ata’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali, who said: The transgressor’s saddlebags are gathered together and burned and he is flogged without a prescribed punishment. Abu Hanifa, Malik, al-Shafi’i and the majority disagreed with him and said: The transgressor’s belongings are not to be burned, but he is to be punished with a punishment similar to his. Al-Bukhari said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, refrained from praying over the transgressor, but his belongings were not burned.” And God knows best. Another hadith on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with him - Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb told me, Abdullah ibn Wahb told me, Amr ibn al-Harith told me that Musa ibn Jubayr told him: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Habbab al-Ansari told him: Abdullah ibn Unais told him: He and Umar ibn al-Khattab were discussing charity one day, and he said: Didn’t you hear the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he mentioned the embezzlement of charity: Whoever embezzles a camel or a sheep from it, he will carry it on the Day of Resurrection? Abdullah ibn Unais said: Yes. Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Amr ibn Sawad on the authority of Abdullah ibn Wahb on his authority. Al-Umawi narrated it on the authority of Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: The punishment of the embezzler is that his saddle be taken out and burned with what is in it. Then he narrated on the authority of Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Uthman ibn Ata’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali, who said: The embezzler’s saddle is gathered up and burned and he is flogged without a prescribed punishment. Imam Ahmad said: Aswad bin Aamer told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Jubayr bin Malik, who said: The copies of the Qur’an were ordered to be changed. He said: Ibn Masoud said: Whoever among you can steal a copy of the Qur’an, let him steal it, for whoever steals something will bring it on the Day of Resurrection. Then he said: I recited from the mouth of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, seventy surahs. Should I abandon what I took from the mouth of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? And Wakee’ narrated in his interpretation on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: When the copies of the Qur’an were ordered to be burned, Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: O people, steal the copies of the Qur’an, for whoever steals it will bring what he stole on the Day of Resurrection. And what a good stealing copy of the Qur’an one of you will bring on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Dawud said, on the authority of Samurah bin Jundub, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, captured a booty, he would command Bilal to call out to the people, and they would bring their spoils, and he would take a fifth of it and divide it. Then a man came one day after The call was made with a bridle of hair. He said: O Messenger of God, this was from what we obtained from the spoils. He said: Did you hear Bilal calling three times? He said: Yes. He said: What prevented you from coming? So he apologized to him. He said: No, you will come with it on the Day of Resurrection and I will not accept it from you. And the Almighty said: Is he who pursues the pleasure of God like he who incurs the wrath of God and whose refuge is Hell, and an evil destination? That is, he who pursues the pleasure of God in what He has prescribed and thus deserves the pleasure of God and His abundant reward, and is protected from His severe punishment, is not equal to he who deserves the wrath of God and is bound by it, and there is no escape for him from it, and his refuge on the Day of Resurrection is Hell, and an evil destination. This verse has many parallels in the Qur’an, such as the Almighty’s saying: Is he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like he who is blind? and His saying: Is he to whom We have promised a good promise and he will attain it like he to whom We have given enjoyment of the enjoyment of worldly life? Then God the Almighty said: They are of degrees with God. Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Muhammad bin Ishaq said: meaning the people of good and the people of evil have degrees. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Kisa’i said: Stations, meaning they differ in their stations and degrees in Paradise and their levels in Hell, like the Almighty’s saying: And for all are degrees according to what they have done verse. That is why the Almighty said: And God is Seeing of what they do verse, meaning He will give them what they deserve. He will not wrong them with good nor increase their evil, rather He will reward each worker according to his work. The Almighty said: God has certainly conferred a great favor upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves verse, meaning from their own kind so that they could address him, ask him, sit with him, and benefit from him, as the Almighty said: And among His signs is that He created for you from among yourselves mates that you may find tranquility in them verse, meaning from your own kind. The Almighty said: “Say, ‘I am only a man like you. It has been revealed to me that your God is one God’” verse. God the Almighty said: And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets. God the Almighty said: And We did not send before you any except men to whom We revealed from the people of the towns. God the Almighty said: O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you? This is more eloquent in gratitude that the messenger to them should be from among them, such that they can address him and consult him in understanding the speech on his behalf. For this reason God the Almighty said: He recites to them His verses meaning the Qur’an and purifies them meaning he commands them to do good and forbids them from evil so that their souls may be purified and cleansed from the filth and evil that they were immersed in during their state of polytheism and ignorance, and teaches them the Book and wisdom meaning the Qur’an and the Sunnah, although they were before meaning before this Messenger in manifest error meaning in clear error and ignorance that is evident to everyone.
3:165: God the Almighty says: Or when a disaster befell you which is what befell them on the day of Uhud, killing seventy of them, you inflicted twice as much meaning on the day of Badr, for they killed seventy of the polytheists and took seventy prisoners, you said, ‘From where did this come to us?’ Say, ‘It is from yourselves.’ Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Qurad Abu Nuh told us, Ikrimah ibn Ammar told us, Samak al-Hanafi Abu Zamil told us, Ibn Abbas told me, Umar ibn al-Khattab told me, he said: When the day of Uhud came the following year, they were punished for what they did on the day of Badr, taking ransom, so seventy of them were killed, and the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fled from him, and his front tooth was broken, and the shell was smashed on his head, and blood flowed down his face, so God revealed: Or when a disaster befell you, having inflicted twice as much, you said, ‘From where did this come to us?’ Say, ‘It is from yourselves.’ From yourselves, by taking the ransom. And thus Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghazwan, who is Qurad Abu Nuh, with his chain of transmission but with a longer one. And thus al-Hasan al-Basri said, and Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Ismail ibn Ulayyah told us on the authority of Ibn Awn on the authority of Muhammad on the authority of Ubayd, H, Sanid said, who is Husayn: And Hajjaj told me on the authority of Jarir, on the authority of Muhammad on the authority of Ubaydah, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: “O Muhammad, God has disliked what your people have done in taking prisoners, and He has commanded you to give them a choice between two things: either they come forward and their necks are struck, or they take ransom on the condition that a number of them are killed.” He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the people and mentioned that to them, and they said: O Messenger of God, our tribes and our brothers, should we not take their ransom so that we may be strengthened to fight our enemy, and a number of them are martyred from among us? There is nothing in that that we dislike? He said: So seventy men were killed from them on the day of Uhud, a number of The prisoners of Badr,” and thus it was narrated by al-Nasa’i and al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Hafri, on the authority of Yahya ibn Zakariya ibn Abi Zaydah, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hassan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, with it. Then al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Gharib, we do not know it except from the hadith of Ibn Abi Zaydah, and Abu Usamah narrated something similar from Hisham, and it was narrated from Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a mursal. Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jurayj, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas and As-Suddi said: “Say: It is from yourselves” meaning because of your disobedience to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he ordered you not to move from your place, but you disobeyed, meaning the archers. Indeed, God has power over all things meaning He does what He wills and rules as He wills, there is no one to question His rule. Then God the Almighty said: And whatever befell you on the day the two armies met was by God’s permission meaning your flight before your enemy and their killing of a group of you and their wounding of others, it was by God’s decree and destiny, and He has wisdom in that. And that He may make evident the believers meaning those who were patient and steadfast and did not falter. “And that He may make evident those who were hypocrites and were told, ‘Come, fight in the cause of God or defend yourselves.’ They said, ‘If we had known there would be fighting, we would have followed you.’” Meaning the companions of Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul who returned with him in the middle of the road, and some men from the believers followed them, urging them to return, fight and help. That is why He said, Or defend yourselves. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Ad-Dahhak said: Abu Salih, Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said: They meant to increase the number of Muslims. Al-Hasan bin Salih said: They defended with supplication. Another said: They stayed, and they made excuses saying: If we knew that there would be fighting, we would have followed you. Mujahid said: They meant if we knew that you would encounter war, we would have come to you, but you will not encounter fighting. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Muhammad bin Muslim bin Shihab Al-Zuhri, Muhammad bin Yahya bin Habban, Asim bin Omar bin Qatada, Al-Hussain bin Abdul Rahman bin Amr bin Saad bin Muadh, and others from our scholars told me, all of them have narrated, he said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to us, meaning when he went out to Uhud with a thousand men from his companions, until he was in the middle of the road between Uhud and Medina, Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul with a third of the people withdrew from him and said: He obeyed them, so he went out and disobeyed me. By God, we do not know why we are killing ourselves here, O people? So he returned with those who followed him from his people, the hypocrites and the doubters. Abdullah bin Amr bin Haram, the brother of Banu Salamah, followed them, saying: O people, I remind you by God not to abandon your Prophet and your people when your enemy comes. They said: If we knew that you would fight, we would not have surrendered to you, but we do not see that there should be fighting. So when they resisted him and refused to do anything but leave them, he said: May God distance you, enemies of God, for God will suffice you. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went on. God the Almighty said: They will be nearer to disbelief, that Day, than to faith. They used this as evidence that a person’s circumstances may change, so that he may be in a state closer to disbelief, and in a state closer to faith, because of His saying: They will be nearer to disbelief, that Day, than to faith. Then God the Almighty said: They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts meaning that they say the statement without believing it to be true, and from this is their saying: If we had known there would be fighting, we would have followed you because they realized that an army of polytheists had come from a distant country burning with desire for the Muslims because of what happened to their leaders on the day of Badr. And they are many times the number of Muslims, so fighting will inevitably occur between them. For this reason God the Almighty said: And God knows best what they conceal Then God the Almighty said: Those who said to their brothers and sat [at home], 'If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed' meaning if they had listened to our advice to sit [at home] and not go out, they would not have been killed with those who were killed. God the Almighty said: Say, 'Then avert death from yourselves, if you should be truthful' meaning if sitting saves a person from being killed and dying, then you should not die, and death will inevitably come to you even if you were in fortified towers, so avert death from yourselves if you are truthful. Mujahid said on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah: This verse was revealed about Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul.
3:166: God the Almighty says: Or when a disaster befell you which is what befell them on the day of Uhud, killing seventy of them, you inflicted twice as much meaning on the day of Badr, for they killed seventy of the polytheists and took seventy prisoners, you said, ‘From where did this come to us?’ Say, ‘It is from yourselves.’ Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Qurad Abu Nuh told us, Ikrimah ibn Ammar told us, Samak al-Hanafi Abu Zamil told us, Ibn Abbas told me, Umar ibn al-Khattab told me, he said: When the day of Uhud came the following year, they were punished for what they did on the day of Badr, taking ransom, so seventy of them were killed, and the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fled from him, and his front tooth was broken, and the shell was smashed on his head, and blood flowed down his face, so God revealed: Or when a disaster befell you, having inflicted twice as much, you said, ‘From where did this come to us?’ Say, ‘It is from yourselves.’ From yourselves, by taking the ransom. And thus Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghazwan, who is Qurad Abu Nuh, with his chain of transmission but with a longer one. And thus al-Hasan al-Basri said, and Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Ismail ibn Ulayyah told us on the authority of Ibn Awn on the authority of Muhammad on the authority of Ubayd, H, Sanid said, who is Husayn: And Hajjaj told me on the authority of Jarir, on the authority of Muhammad on the authority of Ubaydah, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: “O Muhammad, God has disliked what your people have done in taking prisoners, and He has commanded you to give them a choice between two things: either they come forward and their necks are struck, or they take ransom on the condition that a number of them are killed.” He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the people and mentioned that to them, and they said: O Messenger of God, our tribes and our brothers, should we not take their ransom so that we may be strengthened to fight our enemy, and a number of them are martyred from among us? There is nothing in that that we dislike? He said: So seventy men were killed from them on the day of Uhud, a number of The prisoners of Badr,” and thus it was narrated by al-Nasa’i and al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Hafri, on the authority of Yahya ibn Zakariya ibn Abi Zaydah, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hassan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, with it. Then al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Gharib, we do not know it except from the hadith of Ibn Abi Zaydah, and Abu Usamah narrated something similar from Hisham, and it was narrated from Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a mursal. Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jurayj, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas and As-Suddi said: “Say: It is from yourselves” meaning because of your disobedience to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he ordered you not to move from your place, but you disobeyed, meaning the archers. Indeed, God has power over all things meaning He does what He wills and rules as He wills, there is no one to question His rule. Then God the Almighty said: And whatever befell you on the day the two armies met was by God’s permission meaning your flight before your enemy and their killing of a group of you and their wounding of others, it was by God’s decree and destiny, and He has wisdom in that. And that He may make evident the believers meaning those who were patient and steadfast and did not falter. “And that He may make evident those who were hypocrites and were told, ‘Come, fight in the cause of God or defend yourselves.’ They said, ‘If we had known there would be fighting, we would have followed you.’” Meaning the companions of Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul who returned with him in the middle of the road, and some men from the believers followed them, urging them to return, fight and help. That is why He said, Or defend yourselves. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Ad-Dahhak said: Abu Salih, Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said: They meant to increase the number of Muslims. Al-Hasan bin Salih said: They defended with supplication. Another said: They stayed, and they made excuses saying: If we knew that there would be fighting, we would have followed you. Mujahid said: They meant if we knew that you would encounter war, we would have come to you, but you will not encounter fighting. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Muhammad bin Muslim bin Shihab Al-Zuhri, Muhammad bin Yahya bin Habban, Asim bin Omar bin Qatada, Al-Hussain bin Abdul Rahman bin Amr bin Saad bin Muadh, and others from our scholars told me, all of them have narrated, he said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, came out to us, meaning when he went out to Uhud with a thousand men from his companions, until he was in the middle of the road between Uhud and Medina, Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul with a third of the people withdrew from him and said: He obeyed them, so he went out and disobeyed me. By God, we do not know why we are killing ourselves here, O people? So he returned with those who followed him from his people, the hypocrites and the doubters. Abdullah bin Amr bin Haram, the brother of Banu Salamah, followed them, saying: O people, I remind you by God not to abandon your Prophet and your people when your enemy comes. They said: If we knew that you would fight, we would not have surrendered to you, but we do not see that there should be fighting. So when they resisted him and refused to do anything but leave them, he said: May God distance you, enemies of God, for God will suffice you. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went on. God the Almighty said: They will be nearer to disbelief, that Day, than to faith. They used this as evidence that a person’s circumstances may change, so that he may be in a state closer to disbelief, and in a state closer to faith, because of His saying: They will be nearer to disbelief, that Day, than to faith. Then God the Almighty said: They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts meaning that they say the statement without believing it to be true, and from this is their saying: If we had known there would be fighting, we would have followed you because they realized that an army of polytheists had come from a distant country burning with desire for the Muslims because of what happened to their leaders on the day of Badr. And they are many times the number of Muslims, so fighting will inevitably occur between them. For this reason God the Almighty said: And God knows best what they conceal Then God the Almighty said: Those who said to their brothers and sat [at home], 'If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed' meaning if they had listened to our advice to sit [at home] and not go out, they would not have been killed with those who were killed. God the Almighty said: Say, 'Then avert death from yourselves, if you should be truthful' meaning if sitting saves a person from being killed and dying, then you should not die, and death will inevitably come to you even if you were in fortified towers, so avert death from yourselves if you are truthful. Mujahid said on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah: This verse was revealed about Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul.

3:169: God the Almighty tells us about the martyrs that even if they are killed in this world, their souls are alive and provided for in the eternal home. Muhammad bin Jarir said: Muhammad bin Marzuq told us, Amr bin Yunus told us on the authority of Ikrimah, Ibn Ishaq bin Abi Talhah told us, Anas bin Malik told me about the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, whom the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to the people of Bir Ma'unah. He said: I do not know, forty or seventy, and at that water was Amir bin At-Tufayl Al-Ja'fari. So those people from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out until they came to a cave overlooking the water and sat in it. Then some of them said to one another: Who among you will deliver the message of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the people of this water? He said - I think he was Ibn Milhan Al-Ansari -: I am delivering the message of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he went out until he came to a group of them and hid in front of the houses. Then he said: “O people of Bir Ma’una, I am the Messenger of God to you. I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. So believe in God and His Messenger.” Then a man came out to him from the house with a spear and struck him in the side until he came out from the other side. He said: God is Great, I have won, by the Lord of the Kaaba. So they followed his tracks until they reached his companions in the cave. Amir bin At-Tufayl killed them all. Ishaq said: Anas bin Malik told me that God revealed a Qur’an about them: Convey from us to our people that we have met our Lord, and He is pleased with us and we are pleased with Him. Then it was abrogated and lifted after we had read it for a while. Then God Almighty revealed: “And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.” Muslim said in his Sahih:: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, Abu Muawiyah narrated to us, Al-A’mash narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Murrah, on the authority of Masruq, who said: We asked Abdullah about this verse: “And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, and they are provided for.” He said: We asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, and he said: “Their souls are in the bodies of green birds, which have lanterns hanging from the Throne. They roam in Paradise wherever they wish, then they return to those lanterns. Then their Lord looked at them and said: Do you desire anything? They said: What do we desire when we roam in Paradise wherever we wish? He did that to them three times. When they saw that they would not be left without being asked, they said: O Lord, we want you to return our souls to our bodies so that we may be killed in Your way once again. When He saw that they had no need, they were left.” Something similar to this was narrated from the hadith of Anas and Abu Saeed. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad told us, Hammad told us, Thabit told us on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no soul that dies and has goodness with God that would be pleased to return to the world except the martyr, for he would be pleased to return to the world and be killed again because of what he sees of the virtue of martyrdom.” Muslim transmitted it only on the authority of Hammad. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Abdullah al-Madini told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Rabi’ah al-Salami, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Do you know that God brought your father back to life? He said to him: Make a wish of me. He said to him: I will be returned to the world so that I may be killed once again. He said: I have decided that they will not return to it. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this source. It has been proven in the two Sahihs and others that Abu Jabir, who is Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram al-Ansari, may God be pleased with him, was killed as a martyr on the day of Uhud. Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Walid said on the authority of Shu`bah on the authority of Ibn al-Munkadir: I heard Jabir say: When my father was killed, I began to cry and uncover the cloth from his face. The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to forbid me, but the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not forbid me. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not cry for him - or do not cry for him - the angels continued to shade him with their wings until he was taken up. He, Muslim, and al-Nasa’i transmitted it through another chain of transmission on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir, who said: When my father was killed on the day of Uhud, I began to uncover the cloth from his face and cry. He mentioned the rest of it in a similar manner. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yaqub told us, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, Ismail bin Umayyah bin Amr bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr al-Makki, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When your brothers were afflicted at Uhud, God placed their souls in the bodies of green birds, which would go to the rivers of Paradise, eat from its fruits, and take refuge in golden lanterns in the shade of the Throne. When they found the goodness of their drink and food, and the beauty of their resting place, they said: ‘If only our brothers knew what God has done for us, so that they would not give up jihad and turn away from war.’ God, the Almighty, said: ‘I will convey it to them on your behalf.’ Then God, the Almighty, revealed these verses: ‘And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision. ’ and what follows.” This is how Ahmad narrated it, and likewise Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Ismail bin Ayyash, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq. It was narrated by Abu Dawud and Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Abdullah bin Idris from Muhammad bin Ishaq from Ismail bin Umayyah from Abu Al-Zubayr from Saeed bin Jubair from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and he mentioned it, and this is more authentic. Sufyan Al-Thawri narrated it likewise from Salim Al-Aftas from Saeed bin Jubair from Ibn Abbas - and Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari from Sufyan from Ismail bin Abi Khalid from Saeed bin Jubair from Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed about Hamzah and his companions: “And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.” Then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, but they did not include it. Qatada, Al-Rabi’ and Al-Dahhak also said: It was revealed about those killed at Uhud. Another Hadith Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Abdullah bin Jaafar told us, Harun bin Sulaiman told us, Ali bin Abdullah Al-Madini told us, Musa bin Ibrahim bin Katheer bin Bashir bin Al-Fakih Al-Ansari told us, I heard Talha bin Kharash bin Abdul Rahman bin Kharash bin Al-Sammah Al-Ansari, he said: I heard Jabir bin Abdullah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at me one day and said: O Jabir, why do I see you worried? I said: O Messenger of God, my father was martyred and left behind a debt and children. He said: Shall I not tell you that God has never spoken to anyone except from behind a veil, and He spoke to your father directly? Ali said: Direct confrontation. He said: Ask Me and I will give it to you. He said: I ask You to return to the world so that I may be killed in Your cause a second time. The Lord Almighty said: Indeed, the word has already gone before from Me: They will not return to it. He said: O Lord, then convey it to those who are behind me. Then God revealed: And do not think that those who are killed in the way of God are dead. Then he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Salit al-Ansari, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jabir, with a similar chain of transmission. And thus al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Dalā’il al-Nubuwwah on the authority of Ali ibn al-Madini with it. And al-Bayhaqi also narrated it from the hadith of Abu Ubadah al-Ansari, who is ‘Isa ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, God willing, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of ‘Urwah, on the authority of ‘A’ishah, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Jabir: ‘O Jabir, shall I not give you good report? ’ He said: ‘Yes, God has given you good report. ’ He said: ‘I felt that God had brought your father back to life, and said: ‘Ask of My servant whatever you wish, and I will give it to you. ’ He said: ‘O Lord, I have not worshipped You as You should be worshipped. I hope that You will return me to the world so that I may fight with Your Prophet and be killed for You once again. ’ He said: ‘It has already been said from me that it will not return to it. ’” Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yaqub told us, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, Al-Harith bin Fadil Al-Ansari told us, on the authority of Mahmud bin Labid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The martyrs are on a river at the gate of Paradise, in a green dome, and their provision comes out to them from Paradise morning and evening.” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb: Abd Al-Rahman bin Sulayman and Ubaydah told us on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq with it, and it is a good chain of transmission. And as if the martyrs are divided into groups: some of their souls will roam in Paradise, and some of them will be on this river at the gate of Paradise, and it may be possible that their journey will end at this river, and they will gather there, and their provisions will be brought to them there and they will rest, and God knows best. We have narrated in Musnad al-Imam Ahmad a hadith in which there is good report for every believer that his soul will be in Paradise, roaming there as well, and eating from its fruits, and seeing the freshness and joy in it, and witnessing what God has prepared for it of honor, and it is with a sound, noble and great chain of transmission, in which three of the four imams, the owners of the followed schools of thought, have come together, for Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, on the authority of Malik ibn Anas al-Asbahi, may God have mercy on him, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka’b ibn Malik, on the authority of his father, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The soul of the believer is a bird that hangs in the trees of Paradise until God returns it to its body on the Day of Resurrection.” His saying hangs means eats, and in this hadith: The soul of the believer will be in the form of a bird in… “Paradise” As for the souls of the martyrs, as mentioned previously in the crops of green birds, they are like planets in relation to the souls of all believers, for they fly by themselves, so we ask God, the Generous, the Beneficent, to cause us to die in faith. And His Most High’s saying: Rejoicing in what God has given them to the end of the verse, meaning the martyrs who were killed in the way of God are alive with their Lord, and they are happy with what they are in of grace and happiness, and they are glad for their brothers who are killed after them in the way of God, that they are advancing upon them, and that they do not fear what is ahead of them nor are they sad for what they left behind them. We ask God for Paradise. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, And they are glad meaning they are happy for those of their brothers who are behind them to catch up with what they have done of their jihad, so that they may share with them in what they are in of the reward of God that He has given them. Al-Suddi said: The martyr will be brought a book in which it says: So-and-so will come to you on such-and-such a day, and so-and-so will come to you on such-and-such a day, and he will be happy with that as the people of this world are happy with their absent ones when they come back. Saeed bin Jubair said: When they entered Paradise and saw the honor it has for the martyrs, they said: Oh, if only our brothers in this world knew what we know of honor, so that when they witness battle they would engage in it themselves so that they may be martyred and attain what we have attained of goodness. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed them of their situation and the honor they are in, and he informed them, that is, their Lord, that I have revealed to your Prophet and informed him of your situation and what you are in, so they were happy with that, and that is what He said: And they rejoice for those who have not yet joined them from behind them Al-Bukhari and Muslim. It has been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, in the story of the companions of the well of Ma’unah, the seventy of the Ansar who were killed in one morning, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed and cursed those who killed them. Anas said: And a Qur’an was revealed about them, which we recited until it was lifted. Convey to our people that we have met our Lord, and He was pleased with us and satisfied us. Then God Almighty said: They rejoice in favor from God and in bounty and that God does not allow the reward of the believers to be lost. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: They rejoiced and were pleased when they saw the fulfillment of the promise and the great reward. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: This verse includes all believers, whether martyrs or others. God rarely mentions a bounty with which He mentioned the prophets or a reward that He gave them, except that He mentioned what He gave to the believers after them. And the Almighty said: Those who responded to God and the Messenger after the wounds had befallen them. This was on the day of Hamra’ al-Asad, and that is because when the polytheists inflicted what they inflicted on the Muslims, they turned back to their country, and when they continued on their way, they regretted why they did not complete the battle with the people of Medina and make it the decisive battle. So when this reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he urged the Muslims to go after them to frighten them and show them that they had strength and endurance, and he did not give permission to anyone except those who were present at the battle on the day of Uhud, except Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, for what we will mention, so the Muslims volunteered despite their wounds and infliction, in obedience to God Almighty and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: When the polytheists returned from Uhud, they said: You did not kill Muhammad, nor did you take the young camels with you. What a bad thing you have done! Return. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of that, so he called upon the Muslims, and they volunteered until they reached Hamra’ al-Asad - or Bir Abi Uyaynah - the doubt is from Sufyan - and the polytheists said: We will return the next year. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned, and it was considered a raid, and God Almighty revealed: Those who responded to God and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them - for those among them who did good and feared God is a great reward. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Mansur, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned it. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The day of Uhud was Saturday, the middle of Shawwal, and when the next day was Sunday, I did not… Ten nights had passed in Shawwal, and the muezzin of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called out to the people to seek out the enemy. His muezzin called out that no one should go out with us except those who had been present the day before. Jabir ibn Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram spoke to him and said: O Messenger of God, my father left me behind with my seven sisters, and he said: O my son, it is not appropriate for me or for you to leave these women without a man among them. I am not the one who would prefer you to fight with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, over myself, so stay behind with your sisters. So I stayed behind with them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him permission, so he went out with him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, only went out to frighten the enemy and to inform them that he had gone out in pursuit of them so that they would think that he was strong, and that what had befallen them had not weakened them against their enemy. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Abdullah bin Kharijah bin Zaid bin Thabit told me on the authority of Abu al-Sa’ib, the freed slave of Aisha bint Uthman: That a man from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Banu Abd al-Ashhal, who had witnessed the Battle of Uhud, said: I witnessed Uhud with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, my brother and I, and we returned wounded. When the muezzin of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave the call to go out in pursuit of the enemy, I said to my brother - or he said to me -: Are we missing a raid with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? By God, we do not have a mount to ride, and none of us is seriously wounded. So we went out with the Messenger of God, and I was less wounded than he was. Whenever he was overcome, I would carry him up a hill and he would walk up a hill, until we reached the point where the Muslims had reached. Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad bin Salam told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, Those who responded to God and the Messenger the verse, I said to Urwah: O son of my sister, your parents were among them, Al-Zubayr and Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with them, when the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, suffered what he suffered on the day of Uhud, and the polytheists turned away from him, he feared that they would return, so he said, Who will return after them? So seventy men volunteered from among them, among them Abu Bakr and Al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with them, this is how Al-Bukhari narrated it alone with this chain of transmission, and this is how Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Al-Asamm, on the authority of Abbas Al-Duri, on the authority of Abu Al-Nadr, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Mu’addib, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, then he said: It is authentic, and they did not include it, this is what he said. Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Hisham bin Ammar, and Hadiyyah bin Abdul Wahhab on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah. On the authority of Hisham bin Urwa, on his authority, and thus it was narrated by Saeed bin Mansour and Abu Bakr Al-Hamidi in his Musnad on the authority of Sufyan, on his authority. Al-Hakim also narrated it from the hadith of Ismail bin Abi Khalid from Al-Bahi, from Urwah, who said: Aisha said to me: O my son, your father is among those who responded to God and the Messenger after the wound befell them, then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Abdullah bin Jaafar told us from the original book, Samuyah told us, Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, Sufyan told us, Hisham told us from his father, from Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Your parents are among those who responded to God and the Messenger after the wound befell them, Abu Bakr and Al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with them.” And the attribution of this hadith is a complete mistake in terms of its chain of transmission because it contradicts the narration of trustworthy people from stopping at Aisha, may God be pleased with her, as we have presented, and in terms of its meaning, Al-Zubayr is not among the fathers of Aisha, but rather Aisha said that to Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, because he is the son of her sister Asma bint Abi Bakr. Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with them, and Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Saad told me, my father told me, my uncle told me, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God cast terror into the heart of Abu Sufyan on the day of Uhud after what had happened to him, so he returned to Mecca, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Abu Sufyan has suffered a part of you, and he has returned and God has cast terror into his heart. The Battle of Uhud was in Shawwal, and the merchants used to come to Medina in Dhul-Qi’dah, and they would camp at Badr al-Sughra once every year, and they came after the Battle of Uhud, and the believers were afflicted with wounds, and they complained about that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what afflicted them was severe, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, urged the people to set out with him and follow what they had been following, and he said: They are only setting out now to come for Hajj, and they will not be able to do the same until the next year. Then Satan came and frightened his followers, and said: The people have gathered against you, but the people refused to follow him, so he said: I am going, even if no one follows me, to urge the people. So Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Umar, Uthman, Ali, al-Zubayr, Sa`d, Talhah, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, and Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah volunteered with him, with seventy men. They set out in pursuit of Abu Sufyan, and they pursued him until they reached al-Safra`. Then God, the Most High, revealed: Those who responded to God and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them. Then Ibn Ishaq said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out until he reached Hamra` al-Asad, which is eight miles from Medina. Ibn Hisham said: He appointed Ibn Umm Maktum over Medina, and he stayed there on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday, then he returned to Medina. Ma`bad ibn Abi Ma`bad al-Khuza`i passed by him, as Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr told me. The Khuza`ah, both Muslims and polytheists, were a group of sincere advisers to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Tihamah. They made a deal with him, and they did not hide anything that was there from him. Ma`bad was a polytheist at that time, so he said: O Muhammad, by God, what has afflicted you has been very hard on us. In your companions, and we wish that God had spared you from them. Then he and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) went out at Hamra' al-Asad until he met Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and those with him at al-Rawha', and they had decided to return to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and his companions, and they said: We have achieved the goal of his companions, their leaders and their nobles, then we return before we eradicate them? We will attack the rest of them and then we will finish with them. When Abu Sufyan saw Ma'bad, he said: What is behind you, Ma'bad? He said: Muhammad and his companions are pursuing you in a group the likes of which I have never seen, they are burning with desire for you. Those who had stayed behind from him on your day have gathered with him and regretted what they did. They have a resentment towards you that I have never seen before. He said: Woe to you, what are you saying? He said: By God, I do not think that you should set out until you see the forelocks of the horses. He said: By God, we have decided to attack them to eradicate the rest of them. He said: I forbid you from that, and by God, what I saw made me recite some verses of poetry about them. He said: What did you say? He said: I said: My camel was almost knocked down by the sounds as the ground was covered with the locusts. He was a noble lion, not a coward when meeting, nor a slender disposition when facing off. I remained an enemy, I think the earth is tilted because of what they called a leader who will not be let down I said, Woe to Ibn Harb from meeting you when the plain is covered with mud. I am a warner to the people of valor, a warning to every one of them who has a desire and a sense. From the army of Ahmed, do not be afraid of the Tanablah, and what you warned about cannot be described as mere talk. He said: This made Abu Sufyan and those with him think twice, and a group of Banu Abd al-Qais passed by him and he said: Where are you going? They said: We are going to Medina. He said: Why? They said: We are going to provide provisions. He said: Will you deliver a message from me to Muhammad that I will send you to him and that I will carry these raisins for you in Ukaz tomorrow if you meet us? They said: Yes. He said: When you meet him, tell him that we have decided to march to him and his companions to eradicate their remnants. The group passed by the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was at Hamra al-Asad, and they told him what Abu Sufyan and his companions had said. They said: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. Ibn Hisham narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, who said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of their return, he said: ‘By Him in Whose Hand is my soul, I have offered them stones, if they were to be brought to them in the morning, they would be as if they had gone yesterday.’” Al-Hasan al-Basri said regarding his statement: Those who responded to God and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them, that Abu Sufyan and his companions had afflicted the Muslims with what they had afflicted and had returned. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Abu Sufyan has returned and God has cast terror into his heart, so who will volunteer to search for him?’ So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, and some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, got up and followed them. Abu Sufyan was informed that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was searching for him, so he met a caravan of merchants and said: ‘Return Muhammad and you will have such and such a reward, and tell them that I have gathered a group for them and that I will return to them.’ So the merchants came and informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of that, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.’” So God revealed this verse, and this is what Ikrimah, Qatada and others said: This context was revealed regarding Hamra al-Asad, and it was said: It was revealed regarding the Battle of Badr al-Maw'id, but the first is correct. And the Almighty's saying: Those to whom the people said, 'The people have gathered against you, so fear them,' but it only increased them in faith, the verse, meaning those whom the people threatened with crowds and frightened them with the large number of enemies, but they did not care about that, rather they put their trust in God and sought His help, and said, 'God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.' Al-Bukhari said: Ahmad bin Yunus told us, he said: I think he said: Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said it when he was thrown into the fire, and Muhammad, peace be upon him, said it when the people said to them, 'The people have gathered against you, so fear them,' but it only increased their faith, and they said, 'God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.'" Al-Nasa'i narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Ibrahim and Harun ibn Abdullah, both on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Bakr, on the authority of Abu Bakr, who is Ibn Ayyash, on his authority. It is surprising that Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Yunus, then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it. Then Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Abu Ghassan Malik ibn Ismail, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Abu Ad-Dahha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The last words of Abraham, peace be upon him, when he was thrown into the fire were: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. And Abd Al-Razzaq said: Ibn Uyaynah said: Zakariya informed me on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: These are the words of Abraham, peace be upon him, when he was thrown into the fire. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Muammar told us, Ibrahim bin Musa al-Thawri told us, Abdul Rahim bin Muhammad bin Ziyad al-Sakari told us, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Hamid al-Tawil, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that it was said to him on the day of UHud 11:The people have gathered against you, so fear them. So God revealed this verse. He also narrated on his authority on the authority of Muhammad bin Ubayd God al-Rafi’i, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather Abu Rafi’: That the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Ali with a group of people with him in pursuit of Abu Sufyan, and a Bedouin from Khuza’ah met them and said: The people have gathered against you. They said: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. So this verse was revealed about them. Then Ibn Mardawayh said: “Dulaj bin Ahmad told us, Al-Hasan bin Sufyan told us, Abu Khaithama Mus’ab bin Sa’id told us, Musa bin A’yan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: ‘The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When you encounter a grave matter, say: ‘God is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs.’” This is a strange hadith from this source. Imam Ahmad said: Haywah bin Shuraih and Ibrahim bin Abi Al-Abbas told us, they said: Baqiyah told us, Buhair bin Sa’d told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Ma’dan, on the authority of Saif, on the authority of Awf bin Malik, that he told them: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, judged between two men, and when the one against whom the judgment was made turned away, he said: ‘God is sufficient for me, and He is the best disposer of affairs.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Bring me back to the man.’ He said: ‘What did you say?’ He said: ‘I said: God is sufficient for me, and He is the best disposer of affairs.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘God blames weakness, but you should be intelligent. If a matter overcomes you, say: God is sufficient for me.’” And what an excellent agent! And thus Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Baqiyyah from Buhayr from Khalid, from Sayf who is al-Shami, and it was not attributed from Awf ibn Malik from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. And Imam Ahmad said: Asbat told us, Mutraf told us from Atiyyah from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And when the trumpet is blown, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How can I enjoy myself while the companion of the trumpet has taken hold of the trumpet and bent his forehead, hearing when he is commanded to blow? The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What should we say? He said: Say: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. In God we trust. This has been narrated from more than one source, and it is a good hadith. We narrated from the Mother of the Believers, Zainab and Aisha, may God be pleased with them, that they boasted, and Zainab said: God married me and your families married you. Aisha said: My innocence was revealed from the heavens in the Qur’an, so Zainab submitted to her, then she said: What did you say when you rode the mount of Safwan bin Mu’attal? She said: I said: God is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. Zainab said: I said the word of the believers, and for this reason God the Almighty said: So they returned with favor from God and bounty, no harm had touched them, meaning when they put their trust in God, He sufficed them with what concerned them and repelled from them the harm of those who wanted to plot against them, so they returned to their country with favor from God and bounty, no harm had touched them from what their enemy had planned for them, and they pursued the pleasure of God, and God is the possessor of great bounty. Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah al-Hafiz narrated to us, Abu Bakr bin Dawud al-Zahid narrated to us, Muhammad bin Na’im narrated to us, Bishr bin al-Hakam narrated to us. Mubashar bin Abdullah bin Razeen told us, Sufyan bin Husayn told us, on the authority of Ya`la bin Muslim, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God Almighty: So they returned with favor and bounty from God, he said: The favor was that they were safe, and the bounty was that a caravan passed by during the season, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, bought it and made a profit on it, which he divided among his companions. Ibn Abi Nujayh said, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty: Those to whom the people said, ‘Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them,’ he said: This is Abu Sufyan, he said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, your meeting place is at Badr, where you killed our companions. Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Perhaps. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out for his appointment until he reached Badr. They found the market there, and they bought. This is what God Almighty said: “So they returned with favor and bounty from God. No harm had touched them.” The verse. He said: This was the minor Battle of Badr. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir. He also narrated on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Al-Husayn, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made an appointment with Abu Sufyan, they began to meet the polytheists and ask them about the Quraysh. They would say: They have gathered against you. They were plotting against them with that, wanting to frighten them. The believers would say: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. Until they reached Badr, and they found its markets healthy and no one had disputed with them in it. He said: A man from the polytheists informed the people of Mecca about Muhammad’s cavalry, and he said about that: My camels were frightened by Muhammad's horses, and dates were scattered like the Anjd. I took dried water as my appointment Ibn Jarir said: This is how Al-Qasim recited to us, but it is a mistake. Rather, it is: I have been repelled by the company of Muhammad and Ajwa from Yathrib like the Anjad She is following the religion of her father, the Atlad, and has made the water of Qadeed my appointment. And the water of Djnan is poured for her at noon tomorrow Then God the Almighty said: It is only Satan who frightens you with his allies, meaning he frightens you with his allies, and makes you think that they are powerful and strong. God the Almighty said: So fear them not, but fear Me, if you are believers, meaning if he tempts you and makes you think, then rely on Me and take refuge in Me, for I am sufficient for you and your supporter against them, as God the Almighty said: Is not God sufficient for His servant? And they frighten you with those besides Him, until His saying: “Say, ‘God is sufficient for me. Upon Him do those who rely rely.’” And God the Almighty said: “So fight the allies of Satan. Indeed, the plot of Satan has ever been weak.” And God the Almighty said: “Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan - they are the losers.” And God the Almighty said: “God has decreed, ‘I will surely prevail, I and My messengers. Indeed, God is Powerful and Exalted in Might.’” And He said: And God will surely support those who support Him. And God the Almighty said: O you who have believed, if you support God, He will support you. And God the Almighty said: “Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand. The Day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse, and they will have evil.” The house.
3:170: God the Almighty tells us about the martyrs that even if they are killed in this world, their souls are alive and provided for in the eternal home. Muhammad bin Jarir said: Muhammad bin Marzuq told us, Amr bin Yunus told us on the authority of Ikrimah, Ibn Ishaq bin Abi Talhah told us, Anas bin Malik told me about the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, whom the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to the people of Bir Ma'unah. He said: I do not know, forty or seventy, and at that water was Amir bin At-Tufayl Al-Ja'fari. So those people from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out until they came to a cave overlooking the water and sat in it. Then some of them said to one another: Who among you will deliver the message of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the people of this water? He said - I think he was Ibn Milhan Al-Ansari -: I am delivering the message of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he went out until he came to a group of them and hid in front of the houses. Then he said: “O people of Bir Ma’una, I am the Messenger of God to you. I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. So believe in God and His Messenger.” Then a man came out to him from the house with a spear and struck him in the side until he came out from the other side. He said: God is Great, I have won, by the Lord of the Kaaba. So they followed his tracks until they reached his companions in the cave. Amir bin At-Tufayl killed them all. Ishaq said: Anas bin Malik told me that God revealed a Qur’an about them: Convey from us to our people that we have met our Lord, and He is pleased with us and we are pleased with Him. Then it was abrogated and lifted after we had read it for a while. Then God Almighty revealed: “And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.” Muslim said in his Sahih:: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, Abu Muawiyah narrated to us, Al-A’mash narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Murrah, on the authority of Masruq, who said: We asked Abdullah about this verse: “And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead.
