Narrated by Ibn Jarir. The first is correct, although this is included in its meaning. It may be said that this is more appropriate to be included, and God Almighty knows best. God Almighty’s statement, And to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth, means, And spend from that in which He has made you successors, for all matters are referred back to God Almighty. So present from your wealth what will benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. And God is Acquainted with what you do, meaning your intentions and your consciences.
3:177: God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you. This is due to His intense concern for people. He was grieved by the infidels' haste to disobey, be stubborn, and dissent. So God Almighty said: Let not that grieve you. "Indeed, they will never harm God at all. God intends not to grant them any share in the Hereafter." That is, His wisdom in them is that He intends, by His will and power, not to grant them any share in the Hereafter. "And for them is a great punishment." Then God Almighty said, informing about that with a decisive statement: "Indeed, those who have purchased disbelief in exchange for faith." He was grieved by the infidels' haste to disobey, be stubborn, and dissent. So God Almighty said: Let not that grieve you. "Indeed, they will never harm God at all. God intends not to grant them any share in the Hereafter." That is, His wisdom in them is that He intends, by His will and power, not to grant them any share in the Hereafter. "And for them is a great punishment." Then God Almighty said, informing about that with a decisive statement: "Indeed, those who have purchased disbelief in exchange for faith." That is, they exchanged this for that. "They will never harm God at all." That is, they will harm themselves. "And for them is a painful punishment. Then God Almighty said, And let not those who disbelieve think that Our granting them respite is better for themselves. We only grant them respite so that they may increase in sin. And for them is a humiliating punishment." Like His statement: "Do they think that what We provide them with of wealth and children * We hasten for them in good things? Rather, they do not perceive." And like His saying: “So leave Me and he who denies this statement. We will lead them on gradually from where they do not know.” And like His saying: “And do not let their wealth and their children impress you. God only wants to punish them with them in this world and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers.” Then the Most High said: God would not leave the believers in that state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good. That is, He must establish a cause of trial, in which He reveals His friend and exposes His enemy, in which He knows the patient believer and the wicked hypocrite. He means by that the Day of Uhud, in which God tested the believers, and in which their faith, patience, endurance, steadfastness, and obedience to God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, became apparent, and in which He exposed the veil of the hypocrites. Their opposition, their refusal to fight, and their betrayal of God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, became apparent. For this reason, God the Almighty said: God would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good. Mujahid said: He distinguished between them on the day of Uhud. Qatadah said: He distinguished between them through jihad and migration. Al-Suddi said: They said: If Muhammad is truthful, then let him tell us who among us believes in him and who disbelieves. So God the Almighty revealed: God would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good. That is, until the believer emerges from the disbeliever. All of this was narrated by Ibn Jarir. Then God the Almighty said: And God would not inform you of the unseen. That is, you do not know the unseen of God in His creation until He distinguishes for you the believer from the hypocrite, were it not for the reasons He establishes that reveal that. Then the Almighty said: But God chooses from among His messengers whom He wills as in His saying: “He is the Knower of the unseen, and He reveals His secret to none * Except to a messenger with whom He is pleased. Then He makes a guard march before him and behind him.” Then the Almighty said: So believe in God and His messengers meaning obey God and His Messenger and follow him in what He has prescribed for you And if you believe and fear God, then for you is a great reward. And His saying: “And let not those who withhold what God has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them. Rather, it is bad for them.” That is, the miser should not think that his accumulation of money will benefit him, rather it is harmful to him in his religion, and perhaps in his worldly life. Then he told about the fate of his wealth on the Day of Resurrection, saying, They will be collared by what they were stingy with on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah bin Munir told us, he heard Abu al-Nadr, Abdul Rahman told us - he is the son of Abdullah bin Dinar - on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever God gives wealth and he does not pay its zakat, it will be like a bald-headed serpent with two tufts of hair, collaring him on the Day of Resurrection, taking hold of his two jaws - meaning his cheeks - and saying, ‘I am your wealth, I am your treasure.’” Then he recited this verse, “And let not those who are stingy with what God has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them. Rather, it is bad for them,” to the end of the verse. Al-Bukhari is the only one to narrate it from this source, not Muslim. Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih on the authority of al-Layth bin Sa’d on the authority of Muhammad bin Ajlan, on the authority of al-Qa’qa’ bin Hakim, on the authority of Abu Salih, on his authority. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Hajin bin Al-Muthanna told us, Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah bin Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Whoever does not pay the zakat on his wealth, God will present his wealth to him on the Day of Resurrection in the form of a bald-headed serpent with two tufts of hair, then he will hold it and say: I am your treasure, I am your treasure.” And this is how An-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Al-Fadl bin Sahl, on the authority of Abu An-Nadr Hashim bin Al-Qasim, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah bin Abi Salamah, on his authority. Then An-Nasa’i said: The narration of Abdul Aziz on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, is more authentic than the narration of Abdul Rahman on the authority of his father Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah. I said There is no contradiction between the two narrations, for it may be with Abdullah bin Dinar from both sources, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh narrated it from more than one source on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah. And from the hadith of Muhammad bin Abi Hamid on the authority of Ziyad Al-Khatmi on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on his authority. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us on the authority of Jami’, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “There is no servant who does not pay the zakat of his wealth except that a bald-headed serpent will be made to follow him, fleeing from him while he follows him, and he will say: I am your treasure.” Then Abdullah recited the proof of this from the Book of God, They will be collared with what they hoarded on the Day of Resurrection. This is how At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah on the authority of Jami’ ibn Abi Rashid. At-Tirmidhi added: And Abdul Malik ibn A’yan, both on the authority of Abu Wa’il Shaqiq ibn Salamah on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud on his authority. At-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan sahih. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash and Sufyan Ath-Thawri, both on the authority of Abu Ishaq As-Sabi’i, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud on his authority. Ibn Jarir narrated it through other chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud as a mursal. Another hadith Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Umayyah ibn Bastam told us, Yazid ibn Zari` told us, Sa`id told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, on the authority of Ma`dan ibn Abi Talhah, on the authority of Thawban, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He said: ‘Whoever leaves behind a treasure, it will appear to him on the Day of Resurrection as a bald-headed snake with two raisins, following him and saying: Who are you? Woe to you! It will say: I am your treasure that you left behind you. It will continue following him until it gives him his hand and he bites it, then it will follow the rest of his body.’” Its chain of transmission is good and strong, and they did not include it. It was narrated by Al-Tabarani on the authority of Jarir ibn Abdullah Al-Bajali, and it was narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh from the hadith of Bahz ibn Hakim on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “No man comes to his master and asks him for some of his surplus wealth, and he refuses it to him, except that a brave man will be summoned for him on the Day of Resurrection, licking the excess that he refused.” This is the wording of Ibn Jarir. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Abd Al-A’la told us, Dawud told us on the authority of Abu Qaz’ah, on the authority of a man, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “No relative comes to his relative and asks him for some of the excess that God has given him, and he is stingy with it, except that a brave man will be brought out for him from Hell, licking his excess until it encircles him.” Then he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Qaz’ah, whose name is Hujayr ibn Bayan, on the authority of Abu Malik Al-Abdi, with no chain of transmission ending with him. He narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Qaz’ah, with no chain of transmission ending with him. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It was revealed about the People of the Book who were stingy with what was in their hands of the revealed books, so that they would not explain them. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. The first is correct, although this is included in its meaning. It may be said that this is more appropriate to be included, and God Almighty knows best. God Almighty’s statement, And to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth, means, And spend from that in which He has made you successors, for all matters are referred back to God Almighty. So present from your wealth what will benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. And God is Acquainted with what you do, meaning your intentions and your consciences.
3:181: Said bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When the verse was revealed: Who is it that will loan God a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? The Jews said: O Muhammad, has your Lord become poor and asked His servants for a loan? So God revealed: God has certainly heard the statement of those who said, 'Indeed, God is poor, and we are rich.' The verse was narrated by Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Abi Hatim. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad told me on the authority of Ikrimah that he told him on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, entered the school and found many Jews gathered around a man from among them called Finhas, who was one of their scholars and rabbis, and with him was a rabbi called Ashya. Abu Bakr said to him: Woe to you, Finhas! Fear God and submit to Islam, for by God, you know that Muhammad, the Messenger of God, has brought you the truth from Him, and you will find it written with you in the Torah and the Gospel. Then Phinehas said: By God, O Abu Bakr, we have no need of God because of poverty, and He is indeed needy of us. We do not supplicate to Him as He supplicates to us, and we are rich from Him. If He were rich from us, He would not have borrowed from us as your companion claims. He forbids you from usury and gives to us, and if He were rich, He would not have given us usury. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, became angry and struck Phinehas’ face severely, and said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, were it not for the covenant between us and you, I would have struck your neck, O enemy of God. So lie to us as much as you can, if you are truthful. Then Phinehas went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, see what your companion did to me. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Bakr: What made you do what you did? He said: O Messenger of God, the enemy of God has said a terrible thing. He claimed that God is poor and that they are rich. When he said that, I became angry for God’s sake because of what he said, so I slapped him in the face. Phinehas denied that and said: I did not say that. Then God revealed what Phinehas said in response to him and in confirmation of what Abu Bakr had said: God has heard the statement of those who said, ‘God is poor and we are rich.’ The verse was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. And His saying, We will record what they said, is a threat and a warning, and for this reason the Almighty linked it with His saying, And their killing of the prophets without right, meaning this is what they said about God and this is their treatment of God’s messengers, and God will reward them for that with the worst reward, and for this reason the Almighty said, And We will say, ‘Taste the punishment of the burning fire.’ That is for what your hands have put forth, and because God is not unjust to His servants, meaning that this will be said to them as a rebuke, rebuke, humiliation, and belittlement. And the Almighty’s saying, Those who said, ‘Indeed, God has enjoined upon us that we should not believe in a messenger until he brings us an offering that is consumed by fire,’ the Almighty also says, as a lie to those who claimed that God has enjoined upon them in their books that they should not believe in a messenger until one of his miracles is that if a person from his nation gives charity and it is accepted from him, fire will come down from the sky to consume it, as Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, and others said. God the Almighty said: “Say: Messengers have come to you before me with clear proofs” meaning with arguments and evidence, and with what you said meaning with a fire that consumes the accepted sacrifices, so why did you kill them? meaning why did you confront them with denial, opposition and opposition and kill them if you should be truthful that you follow the truth and submit to the messengers. Then God the Almighty said, consoling His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: If they deny you, then messengers were denied before you who came with clear proofs and scriptures and the enlightening Book meaning do not let the denial of these people weaken you, for you have an example from the messengers before you who were denied despite what they brought of clear proofs, which are the decisive arguments and evidence, and scriptures which are the books received from heaven like the scrolls sent down to the messengers, and the enlightening Book meaning the clear, obvious and manifest.

3:185: The Almighty informs us in a general manner that includes all of creation that every soul will taste death, as He says: Everything on it will perish, but the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor, will remain. He, the Almighty, is the only Living One who does not die, and the jinn and mankind will die, as will the angels and the bearers of the Throne. The One, the Sovereign, is unique in perpetuity and survival, so He will be the last as He was the first. This verse contains consolation for all people, for no one will remain on the face of the earth until he dies. So when the period has passed and the sperm that God has decreed to exist in the loins of Adam is emptied and creation has come to an end, God will establish the Resurrection and reward the creatures for their deeds, great and small, many and few, great and small, and He will not wrong anyone by the weight of an atom. For this reason, the Almighty says: And you will only be given your wages in full on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdul Aziz Al-Awysi told us, Ali bin Abi Ali Al-Lahbi told us on the authority of Ja'far bin Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hussein, on the authority of his father, On the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, died and condolences came, a messenger came to them whose voice they could hear but not see. He said: Peace be upon you, O people of the House, and the mercy and blessings of God. Every soul will taste death, and you will only be given your full compensation on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, in God there is consolation for every calamity, a replacement for every lost one, and a catch-up for every missed opportunity. So trust in God and hope in Him, for the afflicted is he who is deprived of reward. Peace be upon you and the mercy and blessings of God. Ja`far ibn Muhammad said: My father told me that Ali ibn Abi Talib said: Do you know who this is? This is Al-Khidr, peace be upon him. And His statement: And whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained [his desire], meaning whoever is spared from the Fire, saved from it, and admitted to Paradise has attained complete attainment. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Ansari told us, Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Alqamah told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The place of a whip in Paradise is better than the world and everything in it. Read if you wish: “So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained [his desire].” This is an authentic hadith in the two Sahihs, from other chains of transmission without this addition. Abu Hatim, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak have narrated it without this addition, and from this hadith of Muhammad ibn Amr. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from another chain of transmission, and he said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim told us, Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, Humayd ibn Mas`adah told us, `Amr ibn `Ali told us, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa`d, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The place of a whip in Paradise is better than the world and everything in it.’ Then he recited this verse: ‘So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained [his desire].” It was mentioned earlier when God, the Most High, says: And do not die except as Muslims. Narrated by Imam Ahmad on the authority of Wakee’ ibn al-Jarrah on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Zaid ibn Wahb, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Rabb al-Ka’bah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-Aas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever would like to be saved from the Fire and enter Paradise, let death overtake him while he believes in God and the Last Day, and let him treat people as he would like to be treated.”’ And the Almighty’s saying: And what is the life of this world except the enjoyment of delusion is a belittling of the world, and a disparagement of its matter, and that it is lowly, transient, little and fleeting, as the Almighty said: Rather, you prefer the life of this world * While the Hereafter is better and more lasting. And the Almighty said: And whatever you are given is but the enjoyment of the life of this world and its adornment, and what is with God is better and more lasting. And in the hadith: By God, the world is in comparison to the Hereafter only as one of you dips his finger in the sea, so let him see what it brings back to him. And Qatada said about the Almighty’s saying: And what is the life of this world except the enjoyment of delusion, he said: “It is enjoyment, it is an abandoned enjoyment that is about to disappear from its people, by God, there is no god but Him, so take from this enjoyment the obedience of God if you are able, and there is no power except with God.” And the Almighty’s saying: You will surely be tested in your wealth and yourselves is like the Almighty’s saying: And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits to the end of the two verses, meaning that the believer will inevitably be tested in some of his wealth. Or himself or his children or his family, and the believer is tested according to the extent of his religion, if his religion is firm, the test will increase, And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with God much abuse. God Almighty says to the believers when they arrive in Medina before the Battle of Badr, comforting them for the harm that befell them from the People of the Book and the polytheists, and commanding them to forgive, be patient and pardon until God relieves, so God Almighty says, But if you are patient and fear God - indeed, that is of the matters [worthy] of determination. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib bin Abi Hamza told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Urwah bin Al-Zubayr told me that Usamah bin Zaid told him, he said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions used to forgive the polytheists and the People of the Book as God commanded them, and they used to be patient with the harm, God Almighty says, “And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with God much abuse.” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to interpret forgiveness as God commanded him until God permitted it for them.” This is how he mentioned it in brief, and Al-Bukhari mentioned it in detail when interpreting this verse, and he said: Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shu’ayb told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Urwah bin Al-Zubayr told me that Usamah bin Zaid told him that “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rode on a donkey with a Fadak cloak on it, and Usamah bin Zaid rode behind him, visiting Sa’d bin Ubadah in Banu Al-Harith bin Al-Khazraj before the Battle of Badr. He said: Until he passed by a gathering in which was Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, and that was before Abdullah bin Ubayy converted to Islam, and in the gathering were a mixture of Muslims and polytheists, idol worshippers, and People of the Book, Jews and Muslims, and in the gathering was Abdullah bin Rawahah. When the dust of the beast covered the gathering, Abdullah bin Ubayy covered his nose with his cloak and said: Do not dust us, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, greeted him, then he stood, got off, and called them to God Almighty and recited the Qur’an to them, and Abdullah bin Ubayy said: O man, there is nothing better than what you say. If it is true, then…” You harm us in our gatherings. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mounted his mount and rode until he entered upon Sa`d ibn `Ubadah. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him, “O Sa`d, did you not hear what Abu Hubab said, meaning `Abdullah ibn Ubayy? He said, ‘So-and-so.’ Sa`d said, ‘O Messenger of God, pardon him and forgive him, for by God who sent down the Book to you, God has come with the truth that He sent down to you. The people of this lake agreed to crown him and tie him with a headband. But when God refused that with the truth that God gave you, he was pleased with that. That is what happened to him, as you saw. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pardoned him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions used to pardon the polytheists and the People of the Book as God commanded them, and they were patient with them.’” Harm, God the Almighty said: And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with God much abuse 3:10. And God the Almighty said: “Many of the People of the Scripture wish they could turn you back to disbelief after you have believed, out of envy from themselves [i.e., the truth has become clear to them]. So pardon and overlook until God brings about His command” 3:10. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, interpreted the pardon as God had commanded him to do until He gave him permission to do so. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought Badr, and God killed the leaders of the disbelievers of Quraysh, Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul and those who were with him from the polytheists and idol worshippers said: This is a matter that has been decided, so pledge allegiance to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, on Islam and submit. So everyone who stands up for what is right or commands what is right or forbids what is wrong will inevitably be harmed, and there is no cure for him except patience in God, seeking help from God, and returning to God the Almighty.

The One, the Sovereign, is unique in perpetuity and survival, so He will be the last as He was the first. This verse contains consolation for all people, for no one will remain on the face of the earth until he dies. So when the period has passed and the sperm that God has decreed to exist in the loins of Adam is emptied and creation has come to an end, God will establish the Resurrection and reward the creatures for their deeds, great and small, many and few, great and small, and He will not wrong anyone by the weight of an atom. For this reason, the Almighty says: And you will only be given your wages in full on the Day of Resurrection. He said: Peace be upon you, O people of the House, and the mercy and blessings of God. Every soul will taste death, and you will only be given your full compensation on the Day of Resurrection. So trust in God and hope in Him, for the afflicted is he who is deprived of reward. Peace be upon you and the mercy and blessings of God. 3:187: This is a rebuke from God and a threat to the People of the Book from whom God took a covenant through the tongues of the prophets to believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to mention him among the people, so that they would be prepared for his command. Then, when God sent him, they followed him, but they concealed that and compensated for what they were promised of good in this world and the hereafter with insignificant and ridiculous worldly sins. So, their deal was a bad deal, and their pledge was a bad pledge. In this is a warning to the scholars not to follow their path, lest what happened to them befall them and their paths be taken with them. So, the scholars must give what they have in their hands of beneficial knowledge that indicates righteous deeds, and not conceal anything of it. It was reported in the hadith narrated through multiple chains of transmission from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Whoever is asked about knowledge and conceals it will be bridled with a bridle of fire on the Day of Resurrection. And the Almighty said: Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done will be bridled with fire. They do,” meaning by that the hypocrites who boast about what they have not been given, as it came in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever makes a false claim in order to gain more, God will only increase his poverty. And in the Sahih also: He who pretends to have what he has not been given is like one who wears two false garments. Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Abi Malekah told me that Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf told him that Marwan said: Go, O Rafi’, to his gatekeeper to Ibn Abbas and say: If every man among us who rejoices in what he has done and loves to be praised for what he has not done is to be punished, then we will all be punished. Ibn Abbas said: What do you have to do with this? This was only revealed about the People of the Book. Then Ibn Abbas recited: “And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture to make it clear to the people and not to conceal it, but they threw it behind their backs and exchanged for it a small price. Evil is that which they buy. Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done” verse. Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked them about something, but they concealed it from him and told him something else. They went out, showing him that they had told him what he had asked them about, and they praised him for that, and they were happy with what they had done in concealing what he had asked them about. This is how Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Tafsir, and Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, and Al-Nasa’i in their Tafsirs, and Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Jarir, Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, and Ibn Mardawayh, all of them from the hadith of Abd Al-Malik bin Jurayj in a similar manner. Al-Bukhari also narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj from Ibn Abi Malekah from Alqamah bin Waqqas, that Marwan said to his gatekeeper: Go, Rafi’, to Ibn Abbas, so he mentioned it. Al-Bukhari said: Saeed bin Abi Maryam told us, Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, Zaid bin Aslam told me from Ata’ bin Yasar, from Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him: That some men from the hypocrites during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to fight, they stayed behind and were happy. In their seat, they were against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from the battle, they would apologize to him and swear, and they would like to be praised for what they did not do. So the verse was revealed: Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done, and Muslim narrated it similarly from the hadith of Ibn Abi Maryam. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his interpretation from the hadith of Al-Layth bin Sa’d from Hisham bin Sa’d from Zaid bin Aslam, who said: Abu Sa’id, Rafi’ bin Khadij, and Zaid bin Thabit were with Marwan, and he said: O Abu Sa’id, have you seen the words of God, the Most High: Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done, and we rejoice in what we have done and love to be praised for what we have not done? Abu Saeed said: This is not like that. Rather, it is that some hypocrites used to stay behind when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent an expedition. If they suffered a calamity, they rejoiced in their staying behind, and if they had victory from God and conquest, they would swear to them in order to please them and praise them for their joy in victory and conquest. Marwan said: How does this compare to that? Abu Saeed said: And this one knows this? Marwan said: Is that so, O Zaid? He said: Yes, Abu Saeed spoke the truth. Then Abu Saeed said: And this one knows that - meaning Rafi’ ibn Khadij - but he fears that if he tells you, his camels will be taken away for charity. When they went out, Zaid said to Abu Saeed al-Khudri: Will you not praise me for what I have testified for you? Abu Saeed said: I have testified to the truth. Zaid said: Will you not praise me for what I have testified to? Then he narrated it from the hadith of Malik on the authority of Zaid ibn Aslam, on the authority of Rafi’ ibn Khadij: That he and Zaid ibn Thabit were with Marwan ibn al-Hakam, who was the governor of Medina, and Marwan said: O Rafi’, about what was this verse revealed? He mentioned it as mentioned above on the authority of Abu Saeed, may God be pleased with them, and Marwan used to send after that to ask Ibn Abbas as mentioned above, so he said to him what we mentioned and there is no contradiction between what Ibn Abbas mentioned and what these people said, because the verse is general in all that was mentioned, and God knows best. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from the hadith of Muhammad bin Abi Atiq and Musa bin Uqbah on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Muhammad bin Thabit Al-Ansari, that Thabit bin Qais Al-Ansari said: O Messenger of God, by God, I feared that I was ruined. He said: Why? He said: “God forbade a person from loving to be praised for what he did not do, and I find myself loving praise. God forbade arrogance, and I find myself loving beauty. God forbade us from raising our voices above your voice, and I am a man with a loud voice.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Are you not satisfied to live a praiseworthy life, be killed as a martyr, and enter Paradise? He said: Yes, O Messenger of God. So he lived a praiseworthy life and was killed as a martyr on the day of Musaylimah the Liar.” And God Almighty said: So do not think that they are safe from the punishment. It is read with the letter ta’ to address the singular, and with the letter ya’ to inform about them, meaning they do not think that they will be saved from the punishment, but rather it is inevitable for them. For this reason, the Most High said: And for them is a painful punishment. Then the Most High said: And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and God is over all things competent. Meaning, He is the Owner of all things, and the Able to do all things, so nothing is beyond His power, so fear Him and do not disobey Him, and beware of His anger and vengeance, for He is the Great, than whom there is none greater, and the Powerful, than whom there is none more powerful.
